nodes.d: The LORD tells Joshua not to fear and to ambush Ai; the city is drawn out, burned, and taken, and Israel may take its spoil.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Israel took Ai the second time?
ev: Retell the ambush plan and how it worked
Say how this differs from Jericho regarding spoil (8:2)

nodes.t: The law read at Mount Ebal
nodes.d: Joshua builds an altar on Mount Ebal as Moses commanded, writes a copy of the law on stones, and reads all its blessings and cursings to the whole assembly.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Israel did at Mount Ebal after Ai?
ev: Say what Joshua built and wrote on Mount Ebal
Explain who heard the law read (8:33-35)

nodes.t: The Gibeonite deception
nodes.d: The people of Gibeon pretend to come from a far country and trick Israel into a treaty without asking the LORD; when found out, they are made woodcutters and water carriers and spared because of the oath.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the Gibeonites tricked Joshua and what happened next?
ev: Retell how Gibeon deceived Israel
Say what Israel failed to do (9:14)
Explain why Israel did not destroy them (9:18-21)

nodes.t: The LORD fights at Gibeon
nodes.d: Five Amorite kings attack Gibeon; Joshua marches all night, the LORD sends hailstones, the sun stands still at Joshua's word, and the five kings are caught in a cave at Makkedah and put to death.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened when the five kings attacked Gibeon?
ev: Say why Israel went to help Gibeon
Describe what the LORD did in the battle (10:10-14)
Say what happened to the five kings (10:16-27)

nodes.t: The southern campaign
nodes.d: Joshua takes Makkedah, Libnah, Lachish, Eglon, Hebron and Debir and the surrounding country, because the LORD God of Israel fought for Israel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name some cities Joshua took in the south and say who gave the victory?
ev: List some of the southern cities Joshua took
Say who fought for Israel (10:42)

nodes.t: The northern campaign and the whole land taken
nodes.d: Jabin of Hazor gathers northern kings at the waters of Merom; the LORD delivers them to Israel, Hazor is burned, and the summary says Joshua took the land according to what the LORD told Moses and the land rested from war.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell about the battle at Merom and the summary of Joshua's conquest?
ev: Say who gathered at Merom and what the LORD told Joshua
Explain what chapter 11 says about Gibeon being the only city to make peace (11:19)
Say how the chapter says Joshua obeyed Moses' commands (11:15)

nodes.t: The list of defeated kings
nodes.d: Joshua 12 lists the two kings Moses defeated east of the Jordan and thirty-one kings Joshua defeated to the west.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the list in Joshua 12 shows?
ev: Name Sihon and Og as the kings on the east side (12:1-6)
Say how many kings are listed west of the Jordan (12:24)

nodes.t: Land still to be possessed and the eastern tribes
nodes.d: The LORD tells the aged Joshua that much land remains and orders it divided; the chapter recalls Moses' gifts east of the Jordan to Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh, and that the Levites' inheritance was the LORD himself.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Joshua 13 says remained and who already had land?
ev: Say what the LORD told old Joshua (13:1, 13:6-7)
Name the tribes that received land from Moses east of the Jordan
Say what the Levites' inheritance was (13:14, 13:33)

nodes.t: Caleb receives Hebron
nodes.d: Caleb recalls Moses' oath at Kadesh and, at eighty-five, asks for the hill country of Hebron; Joshua blesses him, Caleb drives out the sons of Anak, and Othniel wins Debir and Achsah.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell why Caleb received Hebron?
ev: Say why Caleb says he deserves Hebron (14:8-9)
Retell how Othniel won Achsah (15:16-17)

nodes.t: Judah's inheritance
nodes.d: The lot for Judah is described by its borders and cities, and the text notes that Judah could not drive out the Jebusites from Jerusalem.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Joshua 15 describes and what Judah failed to do?
ev: Say what chapter 15 says about the Jebusites in Jerusalem (15:63)

nodes.t: Ephraim and Manasseh's inheritance
nodes.d: The lots for Ephraim and Manasseh are described, the daughters of Zelophehad receive their inheritance, Canaanites in Gezer remain, and the house of Joseph complains of too little land and is told to clear the hill country.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Ephraim and Manasseh received and what they were told to do?
ev: Name the two tribes of the house of Joseph
Say what Zelophehad's daughters asked for (17:3-4)
Say what Joshua told the house of Joseph to do (17:14-18)

nodes.t: Shiloh and the seven remaining tribes
nodes.d: Israel sets up the tabernacle at Shiloh; Joshua rebukes the seven tribes for delaying, sends men to describe the land in seven parts, and casts lots for Benjamin, Simeon, Zebulun, Issachar, Asher, Naphtali and Dan before receiving his own city.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how the last seven tribes got their land?
ev: Say what Joshua told the seven tribes (18:3)
List the remaining tribes who received lots
Say what city Joshua received (19:49-50)

nodes.t: Cities of refuge
nodes.d: The LORD tells Joshua to appoint cities of refuge where someone who killed unwittingly can flee from the avenger of blood; six cities are named, three on each side of the Jordan.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what a city of refuge was for?
ev: Say who could flee to a city of refuge and who could not be handed over to the avenger (20:3-5)
Name some of the six cities (20:7-8)

nodes.t: Cities for the Levites and the promises kept
nodes.d: The Levites receive forty-eight cities from the tribes by lot, and the chapter ends by saying the LORD gave Israel all the land he swore to their fathers, gave them rest, and not one good word failed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Joshua 21:43-45 says about the LORD's promises?
ev: Say why the Levites got cities rather than a tribal territory (21:2)
Say what 21:43-45 says about the LORD's promises

nodes.t: The altar of witness
nodes.d: Joshua sends the eastern tribes home; they build a great altar by the Jordan, the western tribes prepare for war, and Phinehas and ten princes confront them, learning that the altar is a witness and not for sacrifice.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell the story of the altar by the Jordan and how Israel avoided war?
ev: Say why the western tribes were alarmed (22:11-20)
Explain what the eastern tribes said the altar was for (22:24-29)
Say how the dispute ended and what the altar was named (22:30-34)

nodes.t: Joshua's farewell charge
nodes.d: Old Joshua calls Israel to keep the law, cling to the LORD and avoid the remaining nations, warning that if they turn away and break the covenant, the LORD will bring evil on them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Joshua's warning in chapter 23?
ev: Say what Joshua told Israel to cling to
Say what Joshua warned would happen if they served other gods (23:12-16)

nodes.t: Choose this day: the covenant at Shechem
nodes.d: At Shechem Joshua recounts God's acts from Abraham to the conquest, urges Israel to choose whom to serve, makes a covenant with the people, and sets up a stone of witness before dying at 110.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened at Shechem and what Joshua said about choosing whom to serve?
ev: Say what Joshua and his house decided (24:15)
Retell the history Joshua recounted (24:2-13)
Say what Joshua did that day and where he was buried (24:25-30)

nodes.t: Judges: overview
nodes.d: Judges tells of Israel after Joshua's death, repeatedly falling into idolatry, being oppressed, crying out and being delivered by judges, and ends with the refrain that there was no king in Israel and everyone did what was right in his own eyes.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the cycle of sin, oppression, crying out and deliverance in Judges?
ev: Describe the repeating pattern in Judges 2:11-19
Name several judges and the enemies they faced
Say what 21:25 says about Israel at the end

nodes.t: Judah's victories and tribes that failed to drive out the Canaanites
nodes.d: After Joshua's death Judah and Simeon fight first, Othniel wins Achsah, and the chapter lists tribes that did not drive out the inhabitants; the angel of the LORD at Bochim says this disobedience will leave the nations as snares.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened after Joshua died and why the angel spoke at Bochim?
ev: Say who went up first against the Canaanites (1:1-2)
Name some tribes that did not drive out the inhabitants (1:27-33)
Say what the angel of the LORD said and how the people responded (2:1-5)

nodes.t: The cycle of the judges
nodes.d: After Joshua's generation a new generation forgets the LORD and serves Baal; he gives them to enemies, raises up judges to deliver them, and leaves nations to test Israel, who also intermarry and serve their gods.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the pattern that repeats through the book of Judges?
ev: Retell the pattern in 2:11-19
Say why the LORD left nations in the land (2:20-22, 3:1-4)

nodes.t: Othniel delivers Israel
nodes.d: Israel serves the king of Mesopotamia for eight years; when they cry out the LORD raises up Othniel, on whom the Spirit comes, and the land has rest forty years.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Othniel became Israel's first judge?
ev: Retell the first oppression and deliverance in Judges
Say what is said about the Spirit of the LORD and Othniel (3:10)

nodes.t: Ehud and Shamgar
nodes.d: Israel serves Eglon of Moab eighteen years; the left-handed Ehud kills Eglon with a hidden dagger, leads Israel to defeat Moab, and the land has rest eighty years; Shamgar also delivers Israel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell the story of Ehud and how Moab was subdued?
ev: Retell how Ehud killed Eglon
Say what Ehud did after escaping (3:27-30)
Say what Shamgar did (3:31)

nodes.t: Deborah, Barak and Jael
nodes.d: Under Jabin's oppression Deborah the prophetess calls Barak to fight Sisera; the LORD routs Sisera's chariots and Jael kills Sisera in her tent.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how God gave victory over Sisera through Deborah, Barak and Jael?
ev: Retell why Deborah summoned Barak (4:6-7)
Say how the LORD gave victory (4:14-16)
Say what Jael did (4:17-22)

nodes.t: The song of Deborah and Barak
nodes.d: Deborah and Barak sing praise to the LORD for the victory, honour the tribes that came and rebuke those that stayed away, bless Jael, and picture Sisera's mother waiting in vain.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the song of Deborah celebrates?
ev: Say who sings the song and whom it praises (5:1-3)
Name tribes praised or blamed (5:14-18, 5:23)
Say how long the land had rest (5:31)

nodes.t: The LORD calls Gideon
nodes.d: Midian oppresses Israel seven years and Israel cries out; the angel of the LORD calls Gideon, who tears down his father's altar of Baal by night, and then asks for a fleece sign.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how God called Gideon and what signs he asked for?
ev: Retell how the angel of the LORD found Gideon
Say what Gideon did to the altar of Baal (6:25-32)
Describe the fleece sign (6:36-40)

nodes.t: Gideon's three hundred
nodes.d: The LORD reduces Gideon's army to three hundred; after hearing a Midianite dream, Gideon surrounds the camp with trumpets, pitchers and lamps and the LORD sets the Midianites against each other.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Gideon defeated Midian with three hundred men?
ev: Say why the LORD reduced the army (7:2)
Describe how the three hundred attacked (7:16-22)

nodes.t: Gideon pursues Midian and refuses to rule
nodes.d: Gideon calms Ephraim, punishes Succoth and Penuel for refusing him bread, kills the kings Zebah and Zalmunna, declines Israel's offer to rule, but makes an ephod that becomes a snare; after his death Israel turns again to Baal.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Gideon did after the victory and what happened when he died?
ev: Say how Gideon answered the offer to rule (8:22-23)
Say what became a snare (8:27)
Say what Israel did after Gideon died (8:33-35)

nodes.t: Abimelech kills his brothers; Jotham's fable
nodes.d: Abimelech persuades Shechem to make him king and kills Gideon's seventy sons except Jotham, who tells a fable of the trees and the bramble and pronounces a curse.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Abimelech did and what Jotham said from Mount Gerizim?
ev: Say how Abimelech became king (9:1-6)
Retell Jotham's fable and the curse (9:7-21)

nodes.t: The fall of Abimelech
nodes.d: God sends an evil spirit between Abimelech and Shechem; Abimelech destroys Shechem and its tower, and at Thebez a woman drops a millstone on his head; the text says God repaid his wickedness and Jotham's curse came.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Jotham's curse came true for Abimelech and Shechem?
ev: Say what happened between Abimelech and Shechem
Describe how Abimelech died (9:50-54)
Say how the text explains these events (9:56-57)

nodes.t: Tola, Jair, Ibzan, Elon and Abdon
nodes.d: Short notices list judges who ruled after Abimelech and Jephthah, with their tribes, years and burial places.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name some of the judges mentioned briefly in Judges?
ev: Name two or more of these judges and say how long they judged

nodes.t: Israel cries to the LORD under the Philistines and Ammon
nodes.d: Israel again serves other gods and is oppressed by the Philistines and Ammon; the LORD tells them to cry to their chosen gods, but when they confess and put away the foreign gods, his soul is grieved for their misery.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Israel responded when the LORD refused at first to deliver them?
ev: Say what the LORD answered first (10:11-14)
Say what Israel did next (10:15-16)

nodes.t: Jephthah is made head of Gilead
nodes.d: Jephthah, driven out by his half-brothers, is asked back by the elders of Gilead to fight Ammon; he first sends messengers recounting how Israel came to the land.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Jephthah became leader of Gilead?
ev: Say why Jephthah was expelled and why he was recalled (11:1-8)
Summarise his message to the king of Ammon (11:12-27)

nodes.t: Jephthah's vow
nodes.d: The Spirit of the LORD comes on Jephthah, who vows to offer whatever first comes from his house if the LORD gives victory; the LORD delivers Ammon, and his only daughter comes out to meet him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jephthah vowed and what followed?
ev: Say what Jephthah vowed (11:30-31)
Say who met him and how she answered (11:34-36)

nodes.t: Jephthah and Ephraim
nodes.d: The men of Ephraim complain that Jephthah did not call them; Gilead fights them and uses the word Shibboleth at the Jordan fords; Jephthah judges six years.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the word Shibboleth was used for?
ev: Say why Ephraim was angry (12:1)
Say how the Gileadites identified Ephraimites (12:5-6)

nodes.t: The birth of Samson
nodes.d: The angel of the LORD tells Manoah's barren wife that she will bear a son who will be a Nazarite and begin to deliver Israel from the Philistines; Manoah offers a burnt offering and Samson is born.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the angel of the LORD promised Manoah's wife?
ev: Say what the son was to avoid (13:4-5, 13:7)
Say what Manoah and his wife saw at the offering (13:19-21)

nodes.t: Samson's wedding riddle
nodes.d: Samson wants a Philistine wife, kills a lion by the Spirit, and poses a riddle at his feast; his wife tells the answer, and he kills thirty men at Ashkelon and leaves; she is given to his companion.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell the story of Samson's riddle?
ev: Retell the riddle and how it was answered
Note that 14:4 says this was of the LORD, seeking occasion against the Philistines

nodes.t: Samson burns the fields and fights at Lehi
nodes.d: Samson burns the Philistines' grain with foxes carrying firebrands after his wife is given away; Judah binds him and hands him over, but the Spirit comes on him and he kills a thousand with a jawbone; God provides water.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened between Samson, the Philistines and Judah?
ev: Say why Samson burned the Philistine fields
Say what Judah did and what Samson did at Lehi (15:9-17)
Say how Samson's thirst was met (15:18-19)

nodes.t: Samson and Delilah
nodes.d: Samson carries off the gates of Gaza, then loves Delilah, who is bribed by the Philistine lords; after three false answers he reveals his Nazarite hair, it is cut, the LORD departs from him, and he is blinded and imprisoned.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Samson lost his strength?
ev: Say what Delilah asked and how Samson answered
Say what Samson told Delilah about his hair (16:17)
Say what happened when his hair was cut (16:19-21)

nodes.t: The death of Samson
nodes.d: At the Philistines' feast to Dagon, the blind Samson prays to the LORD and pulls down the pillars, killing more in his death than in his life.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Samson died?
ev: Say why the Philistines gathered (16:23-25)
Say what Samson prayed and did (16:28-30)

nodes.t: Micah's idols and his Levite priest
nodes.d: Micah of Ephraim returns stolen silver to his mother, makes images and an ephod, and hires a Levite from Bethlehem as his priest; the text notes there was no king and everyone did what was right in his own eyes.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what was wrong in Micah's house?
ev: Say what Micah made and whom he hired as priest
Say what 17:6 says about Israel then

nodes.t: The Danites take Micah's priest and settle Laish
nodes.d: The tribe of Dan sends spies who meet Micah's Levite; six hundred armed Danites take Micah's images and priest, capture the peaceful city of Laish and rename it Dan.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the Danites came to live in the city of Dan?
ev: Say what the Danites took from Micah
Say what they did to Laish (18:27-29)

nodes.t: The Levite and his concubine at Gibeah
nodes.d: A Levite and his concubine lodge at Gibeah of Benjamin; men of the city assault the house, she is abused through the night and found dead at the door, and he sends her divided body through Israel; the text says no such deed had been seen since Egypt.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what happened at Gibeah and what the Levite did?
ev: Say where the events took place
Say how Israel reacted to the sign sent to all the tribes (19:29-30)

nodes.t: Israel's war against Benjamin
nodes.d: Israel assembles at Mizpeh and demands the guilty men of Gibeah; Benjamin refuses and defeats Israel twice, but after Israel inquires of the LORD and uses an ambush, Benjamin is nearly destroyed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the war between Israel and Benjamin went?
ev: Say why Israel went to war with Benjamin
Say what happened in the first two battles and the third (20:21-25, 20:35)
Say how many Benjamite men escaped (20:47)

nodes.t: Wives for Benjamin
nodes.d: Israel grieves that a tribe is missing; having sworn not to give their daughters to Benjamin, they take wives from Jabesh-gilead and from the daughters of Shiloh; the book ends noting there was no king in Israel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Israel dealt with the tribe of Benjamin after the war?
ev: Say what oath Israel had sworn (21:1)
Say how the remaining Benjamites got wives (21:10-23)
Say how the book ends (21:25)

nodes.t: Ruth: overview
nodes.d: Ruth, set in the days when the judges ruled, follows Naomi and her Moabite daughter-in-law Ruth from loss in Moab to marriage with Boaz in Bethlehem and the birth of Obed, the grandfather of David.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} summarise the book of Ruth from Moab to the birth of Obed?
ev: Say where the story is set and when
Say how the book ends with David's line (4:17-22)

nodes.t: Naomi and Ruth return from Moab
nodes.d: A famine drives Elimelech's family to Moab, where he and his sons die; Naomi returns to Bethlehem, and Ruth refuses to leave her, pledging that Naomi's people and God will be hers.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Ruth said to Naomi and why Naomi returned to Bethlehem?
ev: Retell why Naomi's family went to Moab and what happened to them
Say what Ruth promised Naomi (1:16-17)
Say what Naomi asked to be called and why (1:20-21)

nodes.t: Ruth gleans in Boaz's field
nodes.d: Ruth gleans barley and lands in the field of Boaz, a kinsman of Elimelech, who shows her kindness and protection and tells her to stay with his young women; Naomi calls him one of their near kinsmen.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Boaz showed kindness to Ruth?
ev: Say how Boaz treated Ruth (2:8-16)
Say what Boaz said about the LORD's reward for Ruth (2:12)
Say what Naomi said about Boaz (2:20)

nodes.t: Ruth at the threshing floor
nodes.d: At Naomi's direction Ruth goes to Boaz at the threshing floor and asks him as a near kinsman to spread his skirt over her; he praises her character, says there is a nearer kinsman, and promises to act.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Ruth asked of Boaz and how he answered?
ev: Say what Naomi told Ruth to do
Say what Boaz said about the nearer kinsman (3:12-13)

nodes.t: Boaz redeems and marries Ruth
nodes.d: At the gate Boaz offers the nearer kinsman the right to redeem Elimelech's land and take Ruth; he declines, Boaz buys it and takes Ruth as his wife, and their son Obed is born, in the line leading to David.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Boaz redeemed Ruth and how the book links her to David?
ev: Describe what happened at the gate
Say what the people and women said (4:11-15)
Trace the line from Pharez to David (4:18-22)

nodes.t: 1 Samuel: overview
nodes.d: 1 Samuel runs from the birth of Samuel to Saul's death on Mount Gilboa: Samuel as prophet and judge, Israel's request for a king, Saul's reign and rejection, and David's rise and flight from Saul.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline 1 Samuel from Hannah's prayer to the death of Saul?
ev: Name the three main figures: Samuel, Saul and David
Say how the book begins and ends (1:1-20, 31:1-13)

nodes.t: Hannah prays for a son
nodes.d: Childless Hannah prays at Shiloh and vows to give a son to the LORD; Eli blesses her, Samuel is born, and after he is weaned she brings him to serve the LORD at Shiloh.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Hannah prayed for a child and what she did when God gave Samuel?
ev: Retell what Hannah asked and vowed (1:10-11)
Say what Hannah did when Samuel was weaned (1:24-28)

nodes.t: Hannah's song
nodes.d: Hannah praises the LORD as holy and a rock, who kills and makes alive, brings low and lifts up, raises the poor and breaks his adversaries, and gives strength to his king.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Hannah's song teaches about the LORD?
ev: Say what Hannah says about the LORD (2:2)
Name some reversals she describes (2:4-8)
Say what she says about the LORD's king and anointed (2:10)

nodes.t: Eli's wicked sons and the word against his house
nodes.d: Hophni and Phinehas abuse the sacrifices and the women at the tabernacle while Samuel grows in favour; a man of God tells Eli that the LORD will cut off his house, and that both sons will die in one day.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why God judged Eli's house?
ev: Say what Eli's sons did wrong (2:12-17, 2:22)
Say what sign was given to Eli (2:34)
Say what the LORD promises about a faithful priest (2:35)

nodes.t: The LORD calls Samuel
nodes.d: The LORD calls the boy Samuel three times before Eli tells him how to answer; the LORD tells him he will judge Eli's house, Samuel tells Eli everything, and all Israel knows he is a prophet.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how God called Samuel in the night?
ev: Retell how Samuel heard the LORD
Say what Samuel said when he finally answered (3:10)
Say what the LORD told Samuel and how Eli responded (3:11-18)

nodes.t: The ark is captured and Eli dies
nodes.d: Israel is defeated by the Philistines, brings the ark of the covenant from Shiloh to the camp, loses it as Hophni and Phinehas are killed, and Eli dies on hearing the news; Phinehas' wife names her son Ichabod.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the ark was lost and what happened to Eli?
ev: Say why Israel fetched the ark and what happened (4:3-11)
Say what happened to Eli and his sons (4:11-18)
Say what Ichabod means in the text (4:21-22)

nodes.t: The ark in Philistine cities
nodes.d: The Philistines set the ark beside Dagon in Ashdod, where Dagon falls before it; the LORD's hand strikes Ashdod, Gath and Ekron, and they want the ark sent away.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened when the Philistines kept the ark?
ev: Say what happened to Dagon (5:3-4)
Say what happened to the people of the cities that held the ark (5:6-12)

nodes.t: The ark comes back to Israel
nodes.d: The Philistines send the ark home on a cart pulled by two cows with a trespass offering; the cows go straight to Beth-shemesh, where seventy men are struck for looking into the ark, and the ark is taken to Kirjath-jearim.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the ark went back to Israel?
ev: Say what the Philistines sent with the ark (6:4-8)
Say what the cows did (6:12)
Say what happened at Beth-shemesh (6:19-21)

nodes.t: Samuel at Mizpeh and Ebenezer
nodes.d: After twenty years, Samuel calls Israel to put away foreign gods; at Mizpeh they fast and confess, the LORD thunders on the Philistines, and Samuel sets up the stone Ebenezer, saying the LORD has helped them so far.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened at Mizpeh and why Samuel set up the stone Ebenezer?
ev: Say what Samuel told Israel to do (7:3)
Explain what Ebenezer means (7:12)
Say how Samuel judged Israel (7:15-17)

nodes.t: Israel asks for a king
nodes.d: Samuel's sons take bribes, and the elders ask for a king like the nations; the LORD tells Samuel that they have rejected him, and Samuel warns what a king will take, but the people insist.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Israel asked for a king and what the LORD said about it?
ev: Say why the elders asked for a king (8:4-5, 8:19-20)
Say what the LORD said the request meant (8:7-8)
List things Samuel said a king would take (8:11-17)

nodes.t: Saul seeks his father's donkeys and meets Samuel
nodes.d: Saul searches for lost donkeys, goes with his servant to the seer Samuel, whom the LORD had told the day before that he would send a man to be captain over Israel; Samuel hosts him at a meal.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Saul came to meet Samuel?
ev: Say what Saul went to find
Say what the LORD told Samuel about Saul (9:15-17)

nodes.t: Samuel anoints Saul
nodes.d: Samuel pours oil on Saul as captain over the LORD's inheritance, gives him three signs, and God gives him another heart; Saul prophesies among the prophets but tells his uncle nothing of the kingdom.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Samuel anointed Saul?
ev: Say what Samuel did to Saul (10:1)
Name the signs that came to pass (10:2-10)
Say the proverb that arose (10:11-12)

nodes.t: Saul chosen king at Mizpeh
nodes.d: Samuel gathers Israel at Mizpeh, reminds them they rejected God by asking for a king, and Saul is chosen by lot, found hiding among the baggage, and acclaimed; some worthless men despise him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Saul was chosen as king in front of all the people?
ev: Say how Saul was chosen (10:20-21)
Say where Saul was found and what the people shouted (10:22-24)

nodes.t: Saul rescues Jabesh-gilead
nodes.d: Nahash the Ammonite threatens Jabesh-gilead; the Spirit of God comes on Saul, who summons Israel, defeats the Ammonites, spares those who had despised him, and is confirmed as king at Gilgal.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Saul saved Jabesh-gilead and what he said afterward?
ev: Say what Nahash demanded (11:2)
Say how Saul answered the call to spare his opponents (11:12-13)
Say who gets the credit Saul gives (11:13)

nodes.t: Samuel's farewell and warning
nodes.d: Samuel asks Israel to witness his honesty, recounts the LORD's righteous acts, says their request for a king was wrong, sends thunder and rain, and tells them to fear the LORD, promising not to stop praying for them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Samuel's farewell speech and the warning at its end?
ev: Say what Samuel asked the people to testify (12:3-5)
Say what sign confirmed his words (12:16-18)
Say what Samuel promised and what he told them to do (12:20-25)

nodes.t: Saul's unlawful offering at Gilgal
nodes.d: Facing the Philistines, Saul waits seven days for Samuel, then offers the burnt offering himself; Samuel says he acted foolishly and his kingdom will not continue, because the LORD has sought a man after his own heart.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Saul did wrong at Gilgal?
ev: Say what Saul did and why (13:8-12)
Say what Samuel said would happen (13:13-14)

nodes.t: Jonathan's victory and Saul's rash oath
nodes.d: Jonathan and his armour-bearer attack a Philistine garrison, saying the LORD may work for them, and the Philistines panic; Saul's oath forbidding food nearly costs Jonathan his life until the people rescue him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Jonathan did and what Saul's oath caused?
ev: Say what Jonathan said about the LORD saving by many or by few (14:6)
Explain Saul's oath and what Jonathan did (14:24-27)
Say how Jonathan was spared (14:43-45)

nodes.t: Saul rejected for sparing Amalek
nodes.d: Samuel tells Saul to destroy Amalek; Saul spares King Agag and the best livestock, Samuel says obedience is better than sacrifice and that the LORD has rejected Saul as king, and the LORD repents of making Saul king.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD rejected Saul as king?
ev: Say what the LORD commanded and what Saul did instead (15:3, 15:9)
Say what Samuel said about obedience and sacrifice (15:22-23)
Say what Samuel did to Agag (15:32-33)

nodes.t: Samuel anoints David
nodes.d: The LORD sends Samuel to Jesse of Bethlehem to anoint a new king; passing over the older sons because the LORD looks on the heart, Samuel anoints the youngest, David, and the Spirit comes on him while the Spirit leaves Saul.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how David was chosen and anointed?
ev: Say whom Samuel was sent to and why (16:1-3)
Say what the LORD said about outward appearance and the heart (16:7)
Say who was anointed and what followed (16:12-13)

nodes.t: David plays for Saul
nodes.d: An evil spirit from the LORD troubles Saul after the Spirit departs from him, and his servants bring David, who plays the harp, to ease him; Saul loves David and makes him his armour-bearer.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell why David came to serve Saul?
ev: Say why David was brought to Saul
Say what happened when David played (16:23)

nodes.t: David and Goliath
nodes.d: Goliath of Gath defies Israel for forty days; David, sent with food for his brothers, volunteers, refuses Saul's armour, and in the name of the LORD of hosts kills Goliath with a sling and stone, saying the battle is the LORD's.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell the story of David and Goliath and who David trusted?
ev: Retell how David came to fight Goliath
Say what David told Goliath about the LORD (17:45-47)
Say how David killed Goliath (17:48-51)

nodes.t: Jonathan's covenant and Saul's jealousy
nodes.d: After Goliath, Jonathan loves David and makes a covenant with him; the women's song makes Saul jealous, and he hurls a javelin at David and sets him dangerous tasks, but sees that the LORD is with David.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Saul grew jealous of David?
ev: Say what Jonathan gave David (18:3-4)
Say what the women sang and how Saul reacted (18:6-9)
Say why Saul was afraid of David (18:12, 18:28-29)

nodes.t: Saul tries to kill David
nodes.d: Saul orders David killed; Jonathan pleads for him and Saul swears an oath, but then throws his javelin again, Michal helps David escape through a window, and Saul himself prophesies when he follows David to Samuel at Ramah.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how David escaped from Saul?
ev: Say how Jonathan and Michal each helped David
Say what happened to Saul's messengers and to Saul at Naioth (19:20-24)

nodes.t: Jonathan warns David with arrows
nodes.d: David asks Jonathan to find out Saul's intent; Saul's anger at the new moon feast confirms he wants David dead, and Jonathan signals this with arrows, before the friends part in tears after renewing their oath.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Jonathan warned David with the arrows?
ev: Say how Jonathan and David planned to learn Saul's mind (20:5-23)
Say what Saul did to Jonathan at the feast (20:30-34)
Say what the two friends swore at parting (20:42)

nodes.t: David at Nob and Gath
nodes.d: David gets the holy bread and Goliath's sword from Ahimelech the priest at Nob, where Doeg the Edomite sees him, then flees to Achish king of Gath and pretends to be mad.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what David did at Nob and at Gath?
ev: Say what David received at Nob (21:6, 21:9)
Say who saw David there (21:7)
Say how David escaped from Gath (21:13-15)

nodes.t: Doeg kills the priests of Nob
nodes.d: David gathers distressed men at the cave of Adullam; Saul, told by Doeg that Ahimelech helped David, has Doeg kill the priests of Nob, and Abiathar escapes to David.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what happened to the priests at Nob?
ev: Say who joined David at Adullam (22:1-2)
Say what Doeg did and who escaped (22:18-20)

nodes.t: David saves Keilah and is hunted in the wilderness
nodes.d: David asks the LORD before rescuing Keilah and again about Saul, leaves before Saul arrives, and is pursued in the wilderness of Ziph and Maon until a Philistine raid recalls Saul; Jonathan strengthens David and they make a covenant.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how David escaped Saul in the wilderness and what he asked of the LORD?
ev: Say how David sought guidance from the LORD (23:2, 23:9-12)
Say what Jonathan told David (23:16-18)
Say how David escaped at Maon (23:26-28)

nodes.t: David spares Saul in the cave
nodes.d: Saul enters the cave at Engedi where David and his men are hiding; David cuts off a corner of Saul's robe but refuses to harm the LORD's anointed, and Saul weeps and acknowledges David will be king.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why David would not harm Saul?
ev: Say what David did and did not do in the cave (24:4-7)
Say what David told Saul afterward (24:9-15)
Say what Saul admitted (24:17-20)

nodes.t: Nabal, Abigail and David
nodes.d: Nabal insults David's men who had protected his flocks; David sets out to kill his household, but Abigail brings food and speaks to him, David is restrained from bloodshed, the LORD strikes Nabal dead, and Abigail becomes David's wife.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Abigail kept David from shedding blood?
ev: Say how Nabal treated David's men (25:10-11)
Say what Abigail did and what David said to her (25:18-33)
Say what happened to Nabal (25:36-38)

nodes.t: David spares Saul a second time
nodes.d: At Hachilah David and Abishai enter Saul's sleeping camp; David refuses Abishai's offer to kill Saul, takes his spear and water jar, and calls from a distance, and Saul admits he has sinned.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened when David found Saul sleeping at Hachilah?
ev: Say what David and Abishai found in Saul's camp (26:7)
Say why David would not let Abishai strike (26:9-11)
Say what David took and what Saul said (26:12, 26:21)

nodes.t: David among the Philistines at Ziklag
nodes.d: Fearing Saul, David goes with his six hundred men to Achish of Gath, is given Ziklag, and raids peoples in the south while making Achish think he is raiding Judah.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why David went to live among the Philistines?
ev: Say why David went to Gath (27:1)
Say what Achish gave David and what David told Achish about his raids (27:6-12)

nodes.t: Saul and the medium at Endor
nodes.d: With the Philistines camped against him, Saul gets no answer from the LORD and consults a medium at Endor, despite having banned them; the figure of Samuel tells him that the LORD has become his enemy and that he and his sons will die the next day.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why going to the medium at Endor was wrong for Saul and what he was told?
ev: Say why Saul went to the woman at Endor (28:5-7)
Say what Samuel told Saul (28:16-19)

nodes.t: The Philistine lords send David back
nodes.d: The Philistine lords refuse to let David fight with them against Israel, so Achish sends David and his men back from Aphek.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell why David did not fight with the Philistines against Israel?
ev: Say why the Philistine lords objected to David (29:3-5)
Say what Achish told David to do (29:7-11)

nodes.t: David recovers what was taken at Ziklag
nodes.d: Amalekites burn Ziklag and take the families captive; David strengthens himself in the LORD, inquires through the ephod, pursues and recovers everyone and everything, and rules that those who stayed behind share equally in the spoil.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how David got back the families taken from Ziklag?
ev: Say what David found at Ziklag and what he did first (30:3-8)
Say what David ruled about the spoil (30:23-25)

nodes.t: The death of Saul and his sons
nodes.d: Israel flees before the Philistines at Mount Gilboa; Jonathan and two brothers are killed, Saul takes his own life after being wounded, and the men of Jabesh-gilead recover and bury the bodies.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Saul and Jonathan died?
ev: Say who died at Gilboa
Say what the men of Jabesh-gilead did (31:11-13)

nodes.t: 2 Samuel: overview
nodes.d: 2 Samuel follows David from the news of Saul's death to his kingship over Judah and then all Israel, the LORD's promise of a lasting house, his sin with Bathsheba and its consequences in his own family, Absalom's and Sheba's revolts, and closing songs, warriors and a census.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline 2 Samuel from David's lament for Saul to the census at the end?
ev: Say how the book begins and what David did first
Name the promise in chapter 7
Name some consequences in David's family after chapter 11

nodes.t: David hears of Saul's death and laments
nodes.d: An Amalekite brings David news of Saul's death and claims to have killed him; David has him put to death for slaying the LORD's anointed, and composes a lament for Saul and Jonathan.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how David responded to the news that Saul was dead?
ev: Say what the Amalekite claimed and what David did (1:8-16)
Say what David said about Jonathan in his lament (1:26)

nodes.t: David made king of Judah; war with Ishbosheth
nodes.d: At Hebron the men of Judah anoint David king, while Abner makes Saul's son Ishbosheth king over the other tribes; a skirmish at Gibeon ends with Asahel killed by Abner.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Israel was divided between David and Ishbosheth?
ev: Say who anointed David at Hebron (2:4)
Say who Abner made king (2:8-9)
Say what happened to Asahel (2:18-23)

nodes.t: Abner joins David and is killed by Joab
nodes.d: Abner quarrels with Ishbosheth and offers to bring Israel to David; Joab kills Abner in revenge for Asahel, and David publicly mourns him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened to Abner and what David said about it?
ev: Say why Abner turned to David (3:7-12)
Say what Joab did and how David responded (3:27-39)

nodes.t: The murder of Ishbosheth
nodes.d: Two of Ishbosheth's captains kill him in his bed and bring his head to David, who has them put to death; Jonathan's lame son Mephibosheth is introduced.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what David did when Ishbosheth was murdered?
ev: Say what Rechab and Baanah did and how David responded (4:5-12)

nodes.t: David king over all Israel; Jerusalem and the Philistines
nodes.d: The tribes come to Hebron and anoint David king over Israel; he takes Zion and makes it the city of David, Hiram sends help for his house, and David defeats the Philistines twice after inquiring of the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how David became king over all Israel and took Jerusalem?
ev: Say who came to David at Hebron and what they said (5:1-3)
Say what city David took (5:6-9)
Say how David received guidance against the Philistines (5:19, 5:23-25)

nodes.t: David brings the ark to Jerusalem
nodes.d: Uzzah dies when he touches the ark on the cart, so David leaves it at Obed-edom's house; after three months he brings it into the city with sacrifices and dancing, and Michal despises him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the ark came to Jerusalem?
ev: Say what happened to Uzzah (6:6-7)
Say what happened to Obed-edom's house (6:11)
Say how David and Michal reacted when the ark came in (6:14-16, 6:20-23)

nodes.t: The LORD's promise to David
nodes.d: David wishes to build a house for the ark; the LORD sends Nathan to say that he will make David a house, set up his offspring after him, establish his throne for ever, and be a father to his son; David then prays in thanks.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD promised David through Nathan?
ev: Say what David wanted to do (7:2)
List what the LORD promised David (7:8-16)
Say how David responded (7:18-29)

nodes.t: David's victories and officers
nodes.d: David subdues the Philistines, Moab, Zobah, Syria and Edom, dedicates silver and gold to the LORD, and reigns over all Israel executing judgment and justice, with a list of officers.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name some of David's victories and say what he did with the silver and gold?
ev: Name some peoples David defeated (8:1-14)
Say what David did with the gifts and spoil (8:11)

nodes.t: David shows kindness to Mephibosheth
nodes.d: David asks if any of Saul's house remains to whom he can show kindness for Jonathan's sake, learns from Ziba of Mephibosheth, restores Saul's land to him, and has him eat at the king's table.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how David was kind to Mephibosheth and why?
ev: Say why David sought someone from Saul's house (9:1)
Say what David gave Mephibosheth (9:7, 9:10-13)

nodes.t: The war with Ammon and Syria
nodes.d: David's envoys to the new Ammonite king Hanun are humiliated, so Ammon hires Syrian troops; Joab and Abishai defeat Ammon's allies and David defeats the Syrians again.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell why David went to war with Ammon and the Syrians?
ev: Say how Hanun treated David's servants (10:4)
Say how the war ended (10:13-19)

nodes.t: David, Bathsheba and Uriah
nodes.d: While Israel fights at Rabbah, David takes Bathsheba, Uriah's wife, and when Uriah will not go home he has Joab place him where he will be killed, then marries Bathsheba; the text says this displeased the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what David did wrong and how the chapter judges it?
ev: Say what David did and then tried to cover up (11:4, 11:6-15)
Say what Uriah said about the ark and the army (11:11)
Say how the chapter ends (11:27)

nodes.t: Nathan rebukes David
nodes.d: Nathan tells David a parable of a rich man and a poor man's lamb and says "Thou art the man"; David confesses, the LORD puts away his sin, but the sword will not leave his house and the child born dies; Solomon is then born.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Nathan showed David his sin and what followed?
ev: Retell Nathan's parable and how David responded (12:1-7)
Say what David confessed and what Nathan answered (12:13)
Say what consequences were announced (12:10-14)
Say who was born to David and Bathsheba next (12:24-25)

nodes.t: Amnon, Tamar and Absalom's revenge
nodes.d: David's son Amnon forces his half-sister Tamar and then casts her out; David is angry but Absalom, after two years, has Amnon killed at a feast and flees to Geshur.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened among David's sons Amnon and Absalom?
ev: Say what Amnon did to Tamar (13:11-17)
Say what Absalom did two years later (13:23-29)
Say where Absalom went (13:37-38)

nodes.t: Absalom brought back to Jerusalem
nodes.d: Joab uses a wise woman of Tekoah with a parable to move David to bring Absalom back from Geshur; David lets him return but does not see him for two years, until Absalom forces Joab to arrange a meeting.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Absalom came back to Jerusalem?
ev: Say how Joab persuaded David (14:1-21)
Say how long Absalom did not see the king after returning (14:24-28)

nodes.t: Absalom's conspiracy and David's flight
nodes.d: Absalom wins the hearts of Israel, has himself proclaimed king at Hebron, and David flees Jerusalem with his servants, sends the ark back, and plants Hushai to oppose Ahithophel; Ziba and Shimei meet him, and Absalom takes David's concubines.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Absalom turned the people against David and how David responded?
ev: Describe how Absalom won the people (15:1-6)
Say what David did with the ark and with Hushai (15:25-37)
Say how David answered Shimei's cursing (16:10-12)

nodes.t: Hushai's counsel defeats Ahithophel's
nodes.d: Ahithophel advises Absalom to pursue David at once, but Hushai persuades him to wait and gather all Israel because the LORD had appointed to defeat Ahithophel's good counsel; messengers warn David, who crosses the Jordan, and Ahithophel hangs himself.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Hushai's advice saved David?
ev: Say what each counsellor advised (17:1-13)
Say why Absalom chose Hushai's advice (17:14)
Say what David received at Mahanaim (17:27-29)

nodes.t: The death of Absalom
nodes.d: David's army meets Absalom's in the wood of Ephraim; Absalom's head is caught in an oak and Joab kills him despite David's order to deal gently, and David weeps, "O my son Absalom".
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Absalom died and how David reacted?
ev: Say what David ordered about Absalom (18:5)
Say how Absalom died (18:9-15)
Say how David reacted to the news (18:33)

nodes.t: David returns to Jerusalem
nodes.d: Joab rebukes David's grief for Absalom; David returns toward Jerusalem, spares Shimei, hears Mephibosheth's account and divides the land between him and Ziba, honours Barzillai, and Israel and Judah quarrel over the king.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how David came back as king after Absalom's death?
ev: Say what Joab told David (19:5-7)
Say what David did to Shimei (19:23)
Say what Barzillai asked and what David did (19:31-39)

nodes.t: Sheba's revolt and Joab kills Amasa
nodes.d: Sheba the Benjamite calls Israel to leave David; Joab kills Amasa and pursues Sheba to Abel, where a wise woman persuades the city to throw out Sheba's head.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Sheba's revolt ended?
ev: Say what Sheba proclaimed (20:1)
Say what happened to Amasa (20:8-10)
Say what the wise woman of Abel did (20:16-22)

nodes.t: The famine and the Gibeonites
nodes.d: A three-year famine comes, and the LORD says it is because Saul put the Gibeonites to death; at the Gibeonites' request seven of Saul's sons are hanged, Mephibosheth is spared for the sake of the oath with Jonathan, and Saul's and Jonathan's bones are buried in Kish's tomb.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the famine came and what David did about it?
ev: Say what the LORD said was the cause of the famine (21:1)
Say why Mephibosheth was spared (21:7)
Say what David did with the bones of Saul and Jonathan (21:12-14)

nodes.t: Philistine giants defeated
nodes.d: Several descendants of the giant, including a brother of Goliath, are slain in battles at Gob and Gath by David's men after David grows faint.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name some of David's men who defeated the Philistine giants?
ev: Say who rescued David when he grew faint (21:15-17)
Say who killed the brother of Goliath (21:19)

nodes.t: David's song of deliverance
nodes.d: David praises the LORD as rock, fortress and deliverer who answered his cry, rescued him from his enemies and Saul, and shows mercy to his anointed, to David and his seed for evermore.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what David praises the LORD for in this song?
ev: Say the titles David gives the LORD (22:2-3)
Describe how the LORD answered David's cry (22:7-20)
Say what the song says about David's seed (22:51)

nodes.t: David's last words and the everlasting covenant
nodes.d: In his last words David says the Spirit of the LORD spoke by him that a ruler must be just and rule in the fear of God, and that although his house is not so with God, the LORD has made with him an everlasting covenant.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what David says about God's covenant with him in his last words?
ev: Say what David says a ruler must be (23:3)
Say how David describes his covenant with God (23:5)

nodes.t: David's mighty men
nodes.d: The chapter lists David's mighty men and their deeds, including the three who fetched water from the well of Bethlehem, which David poured out to the LORD instead of drinking.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what David did with the water from Bethlehem's well?
ev: Say what the three mighty men did for David (23:15-16)
Say what David did with the water (23:16-17)

nodes.t: David's census and the threshing floor
nodes.d: David has Joab count Israel despite Joab's protest and afterward confesses he has sinned; the LORD gives him a choice of three punishments, a plague strikes Israel, and David buys Araunah's threshing floor and builds an altar, whereupon the plague is stayed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what David did wrong in chapter 24 and how it ended?
ev: Say what David did and how he felt afterward (24:2, 24:10)
Say which punishment David chose (24:14)
Say what David did at Araunah's threshing floor (24:24-25)

nodes.t: Leviticus: overview
nodes.d: Leviticus gives the LORD's instructions from the tabernacle: the offerings, the consecration of the priests, clean and unclean, the day of atonement, holy living, the feasts, the jubilee, and the blessings and curses of obedience.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} give a one-sentence summary of what Leviticus is about?
ev: Name the main sections of Leviticus (offerings, priests, clean and unclean, atonement, holiness, feasts, jubilee, blessings and curses).

nodes.t: The burnt offering
nodes.d: Leviticus 1 describes the burnt offering from the herd, flock or birds: an unblemished male brought to the tabernacle door, a hand laid on its head so that it is accepted to make atonement, and all of it burned on the altar.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the burnt offering was and why the animal had to be without blemish?
ev: Describe what the worshipper and the priests each did with the burnt offering.
Say what verse 4 says the laid-on hand and the offering accomplish.

nodes.t: The grain offering
nodes.d: Leviticus 2 describes the grain (meat) offering of fine flour with oil and frankincense, a memorial portion burned and the rest given to the priests, with no leaven or honey and salt on every offering.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the grain offering and say what happened to the part that was not burned?
ev: List what went into a grain offering and what was kept out of it.
Say who received the part that was not burned.

nodes.t: The peace offering
nodes.d: Leviticus 3 describes the peace offering from herd or flock, male or female, without blemish: hand laid on the head, blood sprinkled, the fat burned on the altar, with a lasting rule against eating fat or blood.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how the peace offering differs from the burnt offering in what is burned?
ev: Say what part of the peace offering was burned and what was forbidden to eat (3:17).

nodes.t: The sin offering
nodes.d: Leviticus 4 gives the sin offering for sins done through ignorance, with different procedures for the anointed priest, the whole congregation, a ruler and a common person, each ending in atonement and forgiveness.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain who the sin offering was for and what the text says it achieves (for example 4:20, 26)?
ev: Name the four groups of people in chapter 4 and the animal each brings.
Say where the blood was put in the case of the priest and the congregation.

nodes.t: The trespass offering and restitution
nodes.d: Leviticus 5:1-6:7 lists wrongs needing a trespass offering (silence as a witness, uncleanness, rash oaths, trespass in holy things, deceit toward a neighbour), with confession, a graded offering by ability, and restitution plus a fifth.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why restitution is required alongside the trespass offering?
ev: State what the guilty person must do besides bringing an offering (confess, restore, add a fifth).
Describe how the offering changes if he cannot afford a lamb.

nodes.t: The priests' laws of the offerings
nodes.d: Leviticus 6:8-7:38 gives the priests' instructions for the burnt, grain, sin, trespass and peace offerings: the fire never to go out, which portions the priests eat, and the rules on fat, blood and the wave breast and heave shoulder.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the priests received from the offerings?
ev: Say what was to be kept burning continually on the altar.
Name which offerings the priests ate and which portion went to them from the peace offerings.

nodes.t: Aaron and his sons are consecrated
nodes.d: Leviticus 8 records Moses washing, clothing and anointing Aaron and his sons, anointing the tabernacle, and the sin, burnt and consecration offerings over seven days, as the LORD commanded.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Aaron and his sons were set apart as priests?
ev: Retell the order of events in the consecration of Aaron and his sons.
Find the phrase showing that they did as the LORD commanded (8:36).

nodes.t: The eighth day: glory and fire
nodes.d: Leviticus 9 tells how on the eighth day Aaron offered for himself and the people, blessed them, and the glory of the LORD appeared as fire came out and consumed the offering, so that the people shouted and fell on their faces.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened on the eighth day and how the people responded?
ev: Say what Aaron offered first and why, then what he offered for the people.
Describe what happened at the end of the chapter (9:23-24).

nodes.t: Nadab and Abihu
nodes.d: Leviticus 10 tells how Aaron's sons Nadab and Abihu offered fire before the LORD, fire came out and killed them, and Moses and Aaron respond; the chapter adds a rule about wine for priests and a question over the sin offering.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the death of Nadab and Abihu teaches about approaching the LORD?
ev: Tell what Nadab and Abihu did and what happened.
State what Moses said the LORD means by being sanctified in those who come near (10:3).

nodes.t: Clean and unclean animals
nodes.d: Leviticus 11 distinguishes animals that may and may not be eaten (land animals, water creatures, birds, insects) and what contact with carcasses makes one unclean, closing with the call to be holy because the LORD is holy.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the reason the chapter itself gives for the clean and unclean laws?
ev: Give the two marks of a land animal that may be eaten (11:3) and one animal that fails them.
Find the reason given in 11:44-45 for these laws.

nodes.t: Uncleanness after childbirth
nodes.d: Leviticus 12 sets the days of uncleanness after the birth of a son or daughter, circumcision on the eighth day, and the lamb and bird (or two birds if poor) offered for her cleansing.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what a woman did at the end of the days of purifying?
ev: State when a boy is to be circumcised according to 12:3.
Say what offerings she brings and what changes if she cannot afford a lamb.

nodes.t: Diseases of skin, clothing and houses
nodes.d: Leviticus 13 describes how the priest examines skin diseases, with seven-day confinement, pronouncing clean or unclean, the separation of the unclean person outside the camp, and a similar examination of diseased garments.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain who decided whether someone was clean and what happened to an unclean person?
ev: Say who judges whether a person is clean or unclean and what steps he takes.
Describe what the person with the disease must do (13:45-46).

nodes.t: Cleansing from disease and from mould
nodes.d: Leviticus 14 gives the rite for cleansing a healed person (two birds, cedar, scarlet, hyssop, washing, then offerings on the eighth day with blood and oil) and the examination and cleansing of a house with spreading plague.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how a healed person was declared clean again?
ev: Describe the two stages of the cleansing rite (day of cleansing and eighth day).
Say what the priest does to a house with a plague.

nodes.t: Bodily discharges
nodes.d: Leviticus 15 deals with uncleanness from bodily discharges of men and women, how it spreads to beds and things touched, washing and waiting seven days, and the sin and burnt offerings on the eighth day.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the text says Israel is to be kept separate from uncleanness (15:31)?
ev: Say what a person must do to be clean after a discharge ends (seven days, washing, two birds on the eighth day).
Find the reason given in 15:31 for these separations.

nodes.t: The day of atonement
nodes.d: Leviticus 16 sets out how, after Nadab and Abihu died, Aaron enters the holy place once a year with offerings for himself and the people, blood on the mercy seat, and a live goat that carries the people's iniquities into the wilderness.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what happened on the day of atonement and what the two goats show?
ev: Explain why Aaron must not come into the holy place at just any time (16:2).
Describe the two goats and what happens to each.
State the date and the people's duty on that day (16:29-31).

nodes.t: Sacrifices at the door and the sanctity of blood
nodes.d: Leviticus 17 requires that sacrifices be brought to the tabernacle door rather than offered in the open fields, and forbids eating blood, because the life of the flesh is in the blood which the LORD gave on the altar to make atonement.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why blood was treated as special according to Leviticus 17:11?
ev: State the reason given in 17:11 for the ban on eating blood.
Say what had to be done with blood from an animal taken in hunting (17:13).

nodes.t: Not like Egypt or Canaan: sexual boundaries
nodes.d: Leviticus 18 calls Israel not to follow the practices of Egypt or Canaan, listing forbidden sexual relations, Molech worship and other practices, and warns that the land vomits out nations that defile it.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the chapter says the LORD is giving these commands, using what verses 3 and 24-30 say?
ev: Say whose ways Israel is told not to follow (18:3).
State the consequence the chapter gives for defiling the land (18:24-28).
Find 18:5 and say what it promises to the person who does the LORD's statutes.

nodes.t: "Ye shall be holy": laws for neighbours
nodes.d: Leviticus 19 gathers commands under the call to be holy because the LORD is holy: honouring parents, sabbaths, leaving gleanings for the poor, honest dealing, no partiality, loving one's neighbour as oneself, care for the stranger and just weights.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list some ways Leviticus 19 says holiness shows up in daily life?
ev: Name at least five commands from the chapter that deal with how to treat other people.
Find the command to love the neighbour (19:18) and the command about the stranger (19:33-34).

nodes.t: Penalties for Molech worship, sorcery and sexual sin
nodes.d: Leviticus 20 repeats prohibitions on Molech worship, mediums, cursing parents and forbidden unions, attaching penalties to each, and ends by calling Israel to be holy and separate from the nations the LORD is casting out.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how chapter 20 relates to the commands of chapters 18 and 19?
ev: Name three sins in the chapter and the penalty the text attaches to each.
Find what the LORD says in 20:26 about why Israel is to be holy.

nodes.t: Holiness of the priests
nodes.d: Leviticus 21 lays down rules for the priests: limits on mourning, whom they may marry, higher standards for the high priest, and that a priest with a bodily blemish may eat the holy bread but may not approach the veil or altar.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the text says the priests must be holy (21:6, 8)?
ev: Say how the high priest's rules differ from other priests' in 21:10-15.
State what a blemished priest may and may not do (21:21-23).

nodes.t: Eating the holy things and acceptable gifts
nodes.d: Leviticus 22 says who may and may not eat the holy offerings (uncleanness bars a priest; strangers and hired servants may not), and that offerings to the LORD must be without blemish.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why animals with defects were not acceptable as offerings?
ev: Name who may not eat of the holy things and what bars a priest from eating (22:3-9).
Say what the text says about offering blemished animals (22:20-25).

nodes.t: The sabbath, Passover and firstfruits
nodes.d: Leviticus 23:1-22 lists the weekly sabbath and the feasts of the LORD in spring and early summer: Passover and Unleavened Bread, the wave sheaf of firstfruits, and the feast of weeks fifty days later, with a reminder to leave the corners of the field for the poor.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name the feasts in Leviticus 23:1-22 and when each was kept?
ev: Give the date and name of each feast in the first half of the chapter.
Say how the fifty days to the feast of weeks are counted (23:15-16).

nodes.t: Trumpets, atonement and booths
nodes.d: Leviticus 23:23-44 sets out the feasts of the seventh month: the day of trumpets, the day of atonement with its affliction of souls, and the feast of tabernacles in which Israel dwells in booths so their generations remember the exodus.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the feast of tabernacles was meant to remind Israel of?
ev: Give the date of each feast in the seventh month.
Say why Israel was to live in booths (23:43).

nodes.t: The lamps and the bread of the presence
nodes.d: Leviticus 24:1-9 commands pure olive oil for the lamps to burn continually before the LORD and twelve cakes of fine flour set in two rows each sabbath on the table with frankincense, for Aaron and his sons to eat.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the lamps and the twelve cakes in the tabernacle?
ev: Say what the lamps burn on and where the twelve cakes are set.
State who eats the cakes afterward.

nodes.t: The blasphemer and the law of equal justice
nodes.d: Leviticus 24:10-23 tells of a man, son of an Israelite woman and an Egyptian father, who blasphemed the name; the LORD tells Moses he is to be stoned, and gives the law of life for life, eye for eye, one law for stranger and native.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the law "eye for eye" (24:19-20) says is to be done, and who it applies to?
ev: Retell what the man did and what was decided.
Say what 24:22 says about the stranger and the native.

nodes.t: The sabbath year and the jubilee
nodes.d: Leviticus 25:1-22 commands a sabbath rest for the land every seventh year, and a jubilee after seven times seven years with trumpet, liberty and return to one's possession, with the LORD promising a blessing of enough produce in the sixth year.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the jubilee was and what it did for families and land?
ev: Describe what is not done to the land in the seventh year.
Say what happens in the fiftieth year (25:10-13) and how the LORD answers the question "what shall we eat?" (25:20-21).

nodes.t: Redeeming land and persons
nodes.d: Leviticus 25:23-55 teaches that the land is the LORD's and not to be sold permanently, provides for a kinsman to redeem land and a poor brother or sold person, forbids usury to a poor brother, and says Israel are the LORD's servants brought out of Egypt.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what a kinsman redeemer could do in Leviticus 25?
ev: Say who may redeem a poor man's land or person.
Find why the text says the land cannot be sold for ever (25:23) and why Israelites cannot be treated as slaves (25:42).

nodes.t: Blessings and curses of the covenant
nodes.d: Leviticus 26 sets before Israel blessings for walking in the statutes (rain, peace, God dwelling among them), and a graded series of punishments for disobedience ending in exile, with a promise to remember the covenant with Jacob, Isaac and Abraham when they confess.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the chapter says will happen if Israel obeys, if Israel disobeys, and if Israel confesses?
ev: Summarise the blessings in 26:3-13 and the stages of discipline from 26:14 on.
Find the verses where the LORD promises to remember his covenant (26:42-45).

nodes.t: Vows, devoted things and tithes
nodes.d: Leviticus 27 gives how a person, animal, house or field vowed to the LORD may be valued and redeemed (adding a fifth), what is devoted and cannot be redeemed, and that the tithe of land and herd is the LORD's.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the text says about vows and the tithe?
ev: Say how a vowed field or house could be redeemed.
Name what the chapter says belongs to the LORD without being redeemed (27:26, 28, 30-33).

nodes.t: Numbers: overview
nodes.d: Numbers follows Israel from Sinai through the wilderness: the census, camp and Levites, departure from Sinai, the rebellion at Kadesh and forty years of wandering, Balaam, a second census, and preparation on the plains of Moab for entering the land.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} give a short summary of where Israel starts and ends in Numbers?
ev: Describe the journey in Numbers in three stages: at Sinai, wandering, and on the plains of Moab.

nodes.t: The first census
nodes.d: Numbers 1 records the LORD telling Moses to number all men twenty years old and up able to go to war, with a leader from each tribe, giving a total of 603,550, while the Levites are not counted but appointed over the tabernacle.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain who was counted in the first census and who was left out?
ev: Say who was counted and who was not counted, and why the Levites were set apart (1:47-53).
Name the leader role given to one man from each tribe.

nodes.t: The order of the camp
nodes.d: Numbers 2 arranges the tribes in four groups around the tabernacle, each under its standard (Judah east, Reuben south, Ephraim west, Dan north), with the Levites' camp in the middle on the march.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Israel camped around the tabernacle?
ev: Say which tribe camped on each side of the tabernacle.
Say where the Levites' camp travelled (2:17).

nodes.t: The Levites take the place of the firstborn
nodes.d: Numbers 3 lists the sons of Aaron (noting Nadab and Abihu died) and the Levite families Gershon, Kohath and Merari with their camp positions, and says the LORD takes the Levites instead of Israel's firstborn, with redemption money for the extra firstborn.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the Levites are given to the LORD in place of the firstborn?
ev: Name the three Levite families and where each camped.
Explain why the LORD says the Levites are his (3:12-13).
Say how the 273 extra firstborn were redeemed (3:46-51).

nodes.t: The work of the Levite families
nodes.d: Numbers 4 counts the Levites aged thirty to fifty and assigns the work of carrying the tabernacle: the Kohathites the holy things after Aaron's sons cover them, the Gershonites the curtains, and the Merarites the boards and pillars.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what each of the Levite families carried when the camp moved?
ev: Say what each Levite family carried.
State the warning about the Kohathites seeing the holy things (4:15, 20).

nodes.t: Uncleanness and restitution in the camp
nodes.d: Numbers 5:1-10 commands that lepers and those with discharges or who touched the dead be put outside the camp, and that someone who wrongs another confesses and repays the wrong plus a fifth.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the camp had to be kept clean according to Numbers 5:3?
ev: Name who was sent outside the camp and the reason given in 5:3.
Say what a wrongdoer must do when guilty (5:6-8).

nodes.t: The law of jealousy
nodes.d: Numbers 5:11-31 prescribes what a husband who suspects his wife of unfaithfulness without witnesses does: bring her to the priest with an offering, have her swear an oath, and drink the water of bitterness, with the result left to the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the law of jealousy and say what it is meant to settle?
ev: Say who conducts the ritual and what the woman is made to drink.
Describe the two outcomes the text gives (5:27-28).

nodes.t: The Nazirite vow
nodes.d: Numbers 6:1-21 sets the rules for a man or woman who takes a vow of separation to the LORD: no wine or grape product, no razor, no contact with the dead, and offerings and shaving of the head when the days are ended.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what a Nazirite promised and how the vow ended?
ev: List the three things a Nazirite avoided.
Describe what happens when the vow period ends (6:13-20).

nodes.t: The priestly blessing
nodes.d: Numbers 6:22-27 gives the words with which Aaron and his sons are to bless Israel in the LORD's name: that the LORD bless and keep them, make his face shine on them and be gracious, and lift up his countenance and give peace.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the priestly blessing asks the LORD to do for his people?
ev: Say the three lines of the blessing in your own words.
Say what the LORD promises in 6:27 when the priests put his name on Israel.

nodes.t: The princes dedicate the altar
nodes.d: Numbers 7 records the twelve tribal princes giving wagons and oxen to the Levites and each bringing the same offering on his own day for the dedication of the altar, and ends with the LORD speaking to Moses from above the mercy seat.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the twelve princes did and what Moses heard at the end of chapter 7?
ev: Say who gave wagons and oxen and which Levite family received none (7:7-9).
Say what the same offering each prince brought included.
Find where the LORD spoke to Moses (7:89).

nodes.t: The lamps and the cleansing of the Levites
nodes.d: Numbers 8 has Aaron set up the seven lamps of the lampstand, then Moses cleanse the Levites by sprinkling, shaving and washing, and Aaron present them as a wave offering in place of the firstborn, with service limited to ages twenty-five to fifty.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the Levites were set apart for their work?
ev: Describe how the Levites were cleansed and presented.
Say the ages for active Levite service.

nodes.t: The Passover at Sinai and the second Passover
nodes.d: Numbers 9:1-14 records Israel keeping the Passover in the wilderness and the LORD granting those unclean through a dead body or on a journey a second Passover in the second month.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the provision for the second Passover?
ev: Say why some men could not keep the Passover on time (9:6-7).
Describe what the LORD allowed them to do.

nodes.t: The cloud over the tabernacle
nodes.d: Numbers 9:15-23 says that on the day the tabernacle was set up a cloud covered it, fire by night, and Israel camped or travelled at the LORD's command as the cloud stayed or lifted.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Israel knew when to move and when to stay?
ev: Say what Israel did when the cloud lifted and when it stayed.

nodes.t: The silver trumpets and leaving Sinai
nodes.d: Numbers 10 commands two silver trumpets for assembling and moving the camps, then records that on the twentieth day of the second month the cloud lifted and Israel set out from Sinai in the order of the tribes, with Moses asking Hobab to guide them and a prayer when the ark set out.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Israel set out from Sinai?
ev: List the uses of the silver trumpets.
Say which tribe went first and what Moses said when the ark set forward (10:35).

nodes.t: Complaining at Taberah and craving meat
nodes.d: Numbers 11:1-15 tells of the people complaining so that fire burns at the edge of the camp, then the mixed multitude craving the food of Egypt and weeping over the manna, and Moses crying to the LORD that the burden of the people is too heavy.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the people wanted and how Moses felt?
ev: Say what the people complained about and what Moses said to the LORD.

nodes.t: The seventy elders and the quail
nodes.d: Numbers 11:16-35 tells how the LORD has Moses gather seventy elders on whom he puts some of the Spirit, Eldad and Medad prophesy in the camp and Moses wishes all the LORD's people were prophets, then the LORD sends quail and a plague strikes those who lusted.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how the LORD answered Moses' complaint and the people's craving?
ev: Retell how the elders were chosen and what happened to them.
Say what happened while the meat was still between their teeth (11:33).

nodes.t: Miriam and Aaron speak against Moses
nodes.d: Numbers 12 tells how Miriam and Aaron criticize Moses, the LORD defends him as faithful in all his house and speaks to him mouth to mouth, Miriam becomes leprous, and Moses prays for her and she is shut out seven days.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD said about Moses in Numbers 12:6-8?
ev: Say what Miriam and Aaron said and how the LORD described Moses.
Describe the outcome for Miriam and how Moses responded.

nodes.t: The twelve spies
nodes.d: Numbers 13 tells how Moses sends one man from each tribe to search Canaan, they return after forty days with a cluster of grapes from Eshcol, and ten give a bad report while Caleb urges them to go up at once.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the report of the spies and the difference between Caleb and the ten?
ev: Say what the spies brought back and what Caleb said.
Tell how the ten described the people of the land.

nodes.t: Israel refuses to enter the land
nodes.d: Numbers 14:1-25 records the people weeping and wishing to return to Egypt, Joshua and Caleb urging faith, the glory of the LORD appearing, Moses interceding with appeal to the LORD's mercy, and the LORD pardoning yet declaring that those who tested him will not see the land.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the people responded to the spies' report and how Moses prayed?
ev: Say what Joshua and Caleb told the people (14:7-9).
Describe Moses' prayer and the LORD's answer (14:13-23).

nodes.t: Forty years in the wilderness
nodes.d: Numbers 14:26-45 records the LORD's sentence that the adults who murmured will die in the wilderness, their children will enter, the spies who gave a bad report die by plague, and the people who then presume to go up are beaten by the Amalekites and Canaanites.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Israel wandered forty years and who would enter the land?
ev: Say how long the wandering would last and why (14:33-34).
Describe what happened to those who went up anyway (14:44-45).

nodes.t: Offerings for the land and sins of ignorance
nodes.d: Numbers 15:1-31 gives offerings of flour, oil and wine for sacrifices in the land to come, the first of the dough as a heave offering, one law for native and stranger, atonement for sins of ignorance, and the cutting off of the person who sins presumptuously.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the difference the chapter draws between ignorance and presumption?
ev: Say what the section promises (it begins "when ye be come into the land").
Describe the difference between sin through ignorance and a presumptuous sin (15:27-31).

nodes.t: The man who gathered sticks on the sabbath
nodes.d: Numbers 15:32-36 tells of a man found gathering sticks on the sabbath, put in ward until the LORD says he is to be stoned outside the camp by the congregation.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened to the man who gathered sticks and why Moses first waited?
ev: Say what the man did and what the LORD told Moses to do.

nodes.t: Tassels as a reminder
nodes.d: Numbers 15:37-41 commands Israel to make fringes with a blue cord on the corners of garments, to look on them and remember all the LORD's commandments and be holy, since the LORD brought them out of Egypt.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Israelites wore fringes on their garments?
ev: Say what the fringes were for (15:39-40).

nodes.t: Korah's rebellion
nodes.d: Numbers 16:1-35 tells how Korah, Dathan, Abiram and 250 leaders oppose Moses and Aaron, Moses calls for a test with censers, and the earth swallows Korah's company while fire consumes the 250.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Korah's rebellion was about and what happened?
ev: Say what Korah's group claimed (16:3) and how Moses answered (16:5-11).
Describe how the LORD answered the challenge (16:31-35).

nodes.t: The plague stopped by incense
nodes.d: Numbers 16:36-50 records the censers beaten into a covering for the altar, the congregation murmuring against Moses and Aaron, a plague killing 14,700, and Aaron running with a censer between the dead and the living to make atonement.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Aaron stopped the plague?
ev: Say what was done with the censers and what Aaron did to stop the plague.

nodes.t: Aaron's rod that budded
nodes.d: Numbers 17 tells how each tribe's leader lays a rod before the LORD, Aaron's rod for Levi buds, blossoms and yields almonds, and it is kept before the testimony as a sign against rebels, while Israel cries that they will all perish.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the budding rod showed and why it was kept?
ev: Say how the rods were used to show whom the LORD had chosen.
Say where Aaron's rod was kept and why (17:10).

nodes.t: Duties and portions of priests and Levites
nodes.d: Numbers 18 charges Aaron and his sons to bear the sanctuary's guilt, assigns the Levites to help while no stranger may come near, gives the priests the offerings and firstborn, and gives the Levites the tithe as their inheritance, from which they give a tithe to the priests.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how the priests and Levites were supported?
ev: Say what the priests received and what the Levites received.
Find the reason the Levites have no land (18:20-24).

nodes.t: The red heifer and the water of separation
nodes.d: Numbers 19 prescribes a red heifer without blemish burned outside the camp with cedar, hyssop and scarlet, the ashes mixed with water to sprinkle on the third and seventh days those made unclean by a dead body.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the water of separation was for?
ev: Describe how the ashes were prepared and when they were sprinkled.
Say what uncleanness the water was for (19:11-13).

nodes.t: Water from the rock at Meribah
nodes.d: Numbers 20:1-13 tells how Miriam dies at Kadesh, the people quarrel with Moses for lack of water, and the LORD tells Moses to speak to the rock but Moses strikes it twice, and the LORD says Moses and Aaron did not believe him to sanctify him before Israel and will not bring the congregation in.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Moses did wrong at Meribah and what it cost him?
ev: Say what the LORD told Moses to do and what Moses did.
State the consequence given in 20:12.

nodes.t: Edom refuses Israel; Aaron dies
nodes.d: Numbers 20:14-29 records Israel asking the king of Edom to pass through and being refused, then Aaron's garments passing to Eleazar on mount Hor where Aaron dies and Israel mourns thirty days.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the priesthood passed from Aaron to Eleazar?
ev: Say what Moses asked of Edom and the answer.
Describe what happened to Aaron's garments and why (20:24-28).

nodes.t: Victory over Arad, Sihon and Og
nodes.d: Numbers 21:1-3 and 21:10-35 recount Israel's vow and victory over the Canaanite king of Arad, the journey to the plains of Moab, and defeats of Sihon king of the Amorites and Og king of Bashan, with Israel taking their lands.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name the kings Israel defeated and what the LORD said about Og?
ev: Say which two kings Israel defeated after Edom refused passage.
Say what the LORD told Moses about Og (21:34).

nodes.t: The fiery serpents and the bronze serpent
nodes.d: Numbers 21:4-9 tells how the people speak against God and Moses, the LORD sends fiery serpents, the people confess, and Moses makes a bronze serpent on a pole so that anyone bitten who looks at it lives.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the story of the bronze serpent and say what the people had to do to live?
ev: Say what the people said, what the LORD sent, and how those bitten were healed.

nodes.t: Balak sends for Balaam
