nodes.d: Numbers 22:1-21 tells how Israel camps on the plains of Moab, Balak king of Moab fears them and sends elders with rewards to Balaam to curse Israel, and God tells Balaam not to go and not to curse them, then permits him to go with the men if they call him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Balak sent for Balaam and what God told him?
ev: Say why Balak wanted Balaam and what God told Balaam first (22:12).

nodes.t: Balaam's donkey and the angel
nodes.d: Numbers 22:22-41 tells how the angel of the LORD stands in Balaam's way, the donkey turns aside three times, the LORD opens its mouth and then Balaam's eyes, and the angel tells him to go with the men but speak only what the LORD says; Balak then takes him up to the high places of Baal.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell Balaam's journey with the donkey and the angel?
ev: Say what the donkey saw that Balaam did not.
State what the angel told Balaam to speak (22:35).

nodes.t: Balaam's first two oracles
nodes.d: Numbers 23 records Balaam building seven altars and, with a word put in his mouth by the LORD, blessing Israel twice instead of cursing: how can he curse whom God has not cursed, and God is not a man that he should lie or repent.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Balaam blessed Israel and what Numbers 23:19 says about God?
ev: Say what Balak wanted and what Balaam said instead (23:8, 20).
Find what 23:19 says about God.

nodes.t: Balaam's third and fourth oracles: a star out of Jacob
nodes.d: Numbers 24 records Balaam blessing Israel a third time, Balak's anger, and a fourth oracle about what will happen in the latter days: a star out of Jacob and a sceptre out of Israel who will have dominion, then short sayings about Edom, Amalek, the Kenites and Asshur.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Balaam said would come out of Jacob in Numbers 24:17-19?
ev: Say what Balak did when Balaam kept blessing Israel (24:10).
Read 24:17-19 and say what is described coming from Jacob.

nodes.t: Baal of Peor and Phinehas
nodes.d: Numbers 25 tells how Israel at Shittim joins in the worship of Baal of Peor and sins with Moabite women, a plague kills 24,000 until Phinehas acts zealously, and the LORD gives him his covenant of peace and an everlasting priesthood and commands Israel to vex the Midianites.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what sin brought a plague at Peor and what Phinehas did?
ev: Say what Israel did at Shittim and how the plague stopped.
Say what the LORD gave Phinehas (25:11-13).

nodes.t: The second census
nodes.d: Numbers 26 records the LORD commanding a new numbering on the plains of Moab, giving the family lists and totals of the tribes (601,730 in all besides the Levites) and noting that apart from Caleb and Joshua none was left of those counted at Sinai, as the LORD had said they would die in the wilderness.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the second census showed about the LORD's word at Kadesh?
ev: Say why a second census was taken after the plague and how it was used (26:52-56).
Say who was left from the first census (26:64-65).

nodes.t: The daughters of Zelophehad
nodes.d: Numbers 27:1-11 tells how five daughters of Zelophehad ask Moses for their father's inheritance since he had no sons, and the LORD says they speak right and gives a law of inheritance for daughters, brothers and kinsmen.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the daughters of Zelophehad came to Moses and what the LORD decided?
ev: Say what the daughters asked and the LORD's answer.

nodes.t: Moses sees the land; Joshua is appointed
nodes.d: Numbers 27:12-23 tells how the LORD tells Moses to see the land from mount Abarim before he dies, Moses asks for a shepherd for the congregation, and the LORD tells him to lay his hand on Joshua, in whom is the Spirit, and set him before Eleazar and the people.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Joshua was chosen to lead after Moses?
ev: Say why Moses will not enter the land (27:14).
Describe how Joshua was commissioned.

nodes.t: The daily, sabbath, monthly and spring offerings
nodes.d: Numbers 28 specifies the offerings to be made: the continual burnt offering of two lambs daily, doubled on the sabbath, the monthly burnt offerings, and the offerings for Passover, Unleavened Bread and the day of firstfruits.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the continual burnt offering and when extra offerings were added?
ev: Say what was offered each morning and evening.
Name the feasts covered in the second half of the chapter.

nodes.t: The offerings of the seventh month
nodes.d: Numbers 29 specifies the offerings for the feast of trumpets, the day of atonement and the seven days of tabernacles, with a declining number of bullocks each day and a solemn assembly on the eighth.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list the feasts of the seventh month and what was offered at tabernacles?
ev: Name the three occasions in the seventh month listed here.
Say how the number of bullocks changes over the days of tabernacles.

nodes.t: Vows and oaths
nodes.d: Numbers 30 says a man must keep his vow, and sets out when a father or husband may allow or void the vow of a daughter or wife on the day he hears it, while the vow of a widow or divorced woman stands.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the chapter says about keeping vows to the LORD?
ev: Say how a man's vow differs from the vows in verses 3-15.
State when a father or husband could confirm or cancel a vow.

nodes.t: War against Midian
nodes.d: Numbers 31 records the LORD commanding vengeance on Midian, a thousand from each tribe going out with Phinehas, the kings and Balaam being killed, Moses' anger that the women who caused Israel to sin at Peor were spared, purification of the army and spoil, and the division of the plunder with a tribute to the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the reason the text gives for the war on Midian and how the spoil was divided?
ev: Say why the war against Midian was fought (31:2, 16).
Describe how the soldiers and the plunder were purified and divided.

nodes.t: Reuben and Gad ask for land east of the Jordan
nodes.d: Numbers 32 tells how Reuben and Gad, with great herds, ask to settle in Jazer and Gilead, Moses warns them with the example of the spies, and they agree to cross armed with Israel until the land is taken, so Moses gives land to Gad, Reuben and half of Manasseh.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the deal Moses made with Reuben and Gad?
ev: Say what Reuben and Gad asked and the condition Moses set.
Say what Moses said would happen if they did not keep their promise (32:23).

nodes.t: The stages of the journey
nodes.d: Numbers 33:1-49 lists in order the places Israel camped from leaving Rameses to the plains of Moab by the Jordan, recorded by Moses at the LORD's command, with notes on the Passover night, the Red Sea, Aaron's death and king Arad.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the list of stages in Numbers 33 is and why it was written?
ev: Say where the list begins and ends.
Find the note on Aaron's death (33:38-39).

nodes.t: Driving out the nations and the borders of the land
nodes.d: Numbers 33:50-56 and chapter 34 tell Israel to drive out the inhabitants and destroy their idols or they will become thorns in their sides, divide the land by lot, and set the borders of Canaan and the names of the men who divide it.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the instructions for taking and dividing the land?
ev: Say what Israel was told to do to the inhabitants and the idols and the warning for not doing it (33:52-56).
Name who divides the land (34:17-19).

nodes.t: Cities for the Levites and cities of refuge
nodes.d: Numbers 35 commands that the Levites receive forty-eight cities with pasture lands, six of them cities of refuge where a person who kills unintentionally may flee from the avenger of blood, with rules for murder, witnesses and the high priest's death.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the purpose of cities of refuge?
ev: Say how many cities the Levites got and how many were refuge cities.
State how the text tells murder from accidental killing, and what 35:33-34 says about blood and the land.

nodes.t: Inheritance stays in the tribe
nodes.d: Numbers 36 tells how the heads of Gilead's families raise a concern that Zelophehad's daughters marrying outside the tribe would move land to another tribe, and the LORD commands that they marry within their father's tribe so that each tribe keeps its inheritance; the daughters do so.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD told Zelophehad's daughters to marry within their tribe?
ev: Say what concern the family heads raised.
Say what the LORD commanded for heiresses (36:6-9) and what the daughters did.

nodes.t: Deuteronomy: overview
nodes.d: Deuteronomy records Moses' words to Israel on the plains of Moab in the fortieth year: a review of the journey, the ten commandments and the call to love the LORD, the laws for life in the land, the covenant renewal with its blessings and curses, Moses' song and blessing, and his death.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain where Israel is and what Moses is doing throughout Deuteronomy?
ev: Describe Deuteronomy as Moses' speeches before Israel enters the land and name its main parts.

nodes.t: Leave Horeb; leaders and judges appointed
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 1:1-18 opens Moses' words in the fortieth year: the LORD tells Israel to leave Horeb and take the land promised to the fathers, and Moses recalls appointing wise men as heads and judges who hear small and great alike without partiality.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell where and when Moses gave these speeches and what he told the judges?
ev: Say when and where Moses speaks (1:1-5).
Say what Moses charged the judges (1:16-17).

nodes.t: Moses recalls the spies and the refusal
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 1:19-46 has Moses recall the sending of twelve spies from Kadesh-barnea, Israel's refusal to go up despite the good fruit, the LORD's oath that that generation would not see the land except Caleb, and the failed attack when they presumed to go up.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Moses reminded the new generation of the spies?
ev: Compare this retelling with Numbers 13-14 and name one thing Moses emphasizes (for example the LORD going before them, 1:30-33).

nodes.t: Passing Edom, Moab and Ammon
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 2:1-23 recalls how the LORD told Israel not to fight Edom, Moab or Ammon because he had given them their land, how the generation of fighting men died during the thirty-eight years, and how the LORD had earlier given those lands to Esau's and Lot's descendants.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Israel left Edom, Moab and Ammon alone?
ev: Say whose land Israel was told not to take and the reason given.
Say how long it took from Kadesh-barnea to the brook Zered (2:14).

nodes.t: Sihon and Og defeated
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 2:24-3:22 recalls the defeat of Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan, the LORD hardening Sihon's spirit, the land east of the Jordan given to Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh, and Moses' command that they cross armed with their brothers.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how Israel took the land east of the Jordan?
ev: Say who the two kings were and what happened to them.
Say what Reuben, Gad and half Manasseh must do before settling (3:18-20).

nodes.t: Moses may only see the land
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 3:23-29 records Moses pleading with the LORD to let him cross the Jordan, the LORD refusing for the people's sake and telling him to view the land from Pisgah and to charge and encourage Joshua.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Moses asked the LORD and the answer he received?
ev: Say what Moses asked and what the LORD answered.
Say what Moses was told to do for Joshua.

nodes.t: Hear the statutes: no images, remember Horeb
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 4:1-40 urges Israel to keep the statutes without adding or taking away, to remember the day at Horeb when they heard the voice from the fire and saw no form, to make no image, to beware of forgetting the covenant, and warns of exile yet promises that the LORD, merciful, will be found when sought.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Moses told Israel to make no image of God?
ev: Say what Israel saw and did not see at Horeb and why that rules out images (4:12, 15-19).
Find the promise about seeking the LORD from exile (4:29-31).

nodes.t: Three cities of refuge east of the Jordan
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 4:41-49 records Moses setting apart Bezer, Ramoth and Golan east of the Jordan for a slayer who killed without hatred to flee to, and introduces the law Moses sets before Israel in the valley opposite Beth-peor.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the three cities east of the Jordan were for?
ev: Name the three cities and say who could flee there (4:42).

nodes.t: The ten commandments at Horeb
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 5 has Moses remind Israel that the LORD made a covenant with them at Horeb, repeats the ten commandments given from the fire, and recounts the people's fear and Moses standing between them and the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list the ten commandments and explain who gave them and to whom?
ev: Say the ten commandments in order.
Say what 5:2-3 says about whom the covenant was made with.
Find the reason attached to the sabbath commandment here (5:15).

nodes.t: Hear, O Israel: love the LORD
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 6 gives the great command to love the LORD with all heart, soul and might because he is one LORD, to teach the words to children throughout the day, to remember him when blessed in the land, and to answer a child's question with the story of the exodus.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what it means to love the LORD with all one's heart, soul and might?
ev: Say the command of 6:4-5 in your own words.
List the ways 6:6-9 says to keep the words before oneself and the children.

nodes.t: A holy people chosen in love
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 7 tells Israel to make no treaties or marriages with the nations of the land and to destroy their altars, because the LORD chose Israel not because they were many but because he loved them and keeps covenant with those who love him, and Israel is not to fear them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD chose Israel according to Deuteronomy 7:7-9?
ev: Say the reason 7:7-8 gives for why the LORD chose Israel.
Find the description of the LORD in 7:9.

nodes.t: Remember the wilderness; do not forget
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 8 calls Israel to remember how the LORD humbled and fed them with manna for forty years so they would learn that man lives by every word from the LORD's mouth, and warns against pride and forgetting him in the good land.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Moses told Israel to remember the wilderness before they entered the land?
ev: Say what the manna was meant to teach (8:3).
Say what danger Moses warns about in 8:11-18.

nodes.t: Not for your righteousness: the calf recalled
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 9:1-10:11 has Moses tell Israel they will take the land not for their righteousness but for the nations' wickedness, recalling the golden calf, his breaking the tables and fasting forty days, his prayer for the people, and the second tables placed in the ark.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Moses used the golden calf to show Israel it did not earn the land?
ev: Say why Moses says Israel is not given the land for its righteousness (9:4-6).
Describe what Moses did after the calf and what the LORD wrote on the new tables (10:1-5).

nodes.t: What the LORD requires
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 10:12-22 asks what the LORD requires: to fear him, walk in his ways, love and serve him with all the heart and keep his commandments; Israel is to circumcise the heart because the LORD of lords loves the stranger, orphan and widow.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what it means to circumcise the heart (10:16) in the context of this passage?
ev: List the things the LORD requires in 10:12-13.
Say what the LORD does for the fatherless, widow and stranger and what Israel is told in response (10:18-19).

nodes.t: Obey and be blessed; a blessing and a curse
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 11 calls Israel to love the LORD and remember his acts in Egypt and the wilderness, tells them the land is watered by the LORD's care, to bind his words upon them, and sets before them a blessing and a curse with mount Gerizim and mount Ebal.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the choice that Moses set before Israel in Deuteronomy 11:26-28?
ev: Say how the land of promise differs from Egypt in its water (11:10-12).
Say what blessing and curse are set before Israel (11:26-28).

nodes.t: Worship at the place the LORD chooses
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 12 tells Israel to destroy the pagan places of worship and to bring offerings, tithes and firstfruits to the one place the LORD will choose, rejoicing there with households and the Levite, while allowing ordinary meat to be eaten at home but not blood.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why chapter 12 sets worship at one place the LORD chooses?
ev: Say what Israel was to destroy and where they were to offer sacrifices.
Say what is allowed at home and what is still forbidden (12:15-16, 23-25).

nodes.t: Testing prophets and loyalty to the LORD
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 13 warns that a prophet or dreamer, a family member or a city that urges Israel to follow other gods must not be obeyed even if a sign comes true, because the LORD is testing Israel's love, and gives the penalties.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why a prophet whose sign came true was still not to be followed?
ev: Say how a prophet can give a sign and still be rejected (13:1-3).
Say what the chapter says to do with a city led astray (13:12-16).

nodes.t: Holy people: food and tithes
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 14 says Israel are children of the LORD and a holy people, so they are not to mutilate themselves for the dead, lists the clean and unclean animals, birds and fish, and gives the tithe to be eaten before the LORD, with a third-year tithe for the Levite, stranger, fatherless and widow.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the third-year tithe was for?
ev: Say how this list compares with Leviticus 11 (the same kinds of marks).
Say who received the tithe of the third year (14:28-29).

nodes.t: The year of release and care for the poor
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 15 commands debts to be released every seventh year, tells Israel to lend freely to the poor and open the hand, to free Hebrew servants in the seventh year with a generous gift remembering Egypt, and to dedicate firstling animals to the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Israel had to do for the poor and for a servant who had served six years?
ev: Say what happens every seventh year for debts and for servants.
Find the reason Moses gives for generosity (15:15).

nodes.t: Three feasts; judges and officers
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 16 commands Passover, the feast of weeks and the feast of tabernacles at the place the LORD chooses, with all males appearing three times a year and giving as they are able, and appoints just judges who take no bribes and forbids setting up images near the altar.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list the three feasts of Deuteronomy 16 and what judges had to avoid?
ev: Name the three feasts and the number of times males appear each year.
Say what the judges must not do (16:19).

nodes.t: Witnesses and the central court
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 17:1-13 requires sacrifices without blemish, trial with at least two or three witnesses before a penalty for idolatry, and a place of final decision by priests and judge where hard cases are brought and whose sentence must be obeyed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why two or three witnesses were needed before a person was put to death?
ev: Say how many witnesses were required (17:6).
Say where hard cases were to be taken.

nodes.t: The law of the king
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 17:14-20 anticipates Israel asking for a king and says he must be one the LORD chooses from among their brothers, must not multiply horses, wives or silver, and must write a copy of the law and read it all his life.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the king was to do with the law and what he was to avoid?
ev: List what the king must not multiply.
Say what the king must write and do with the law (17:18-19).

nodes.t: The Levites' portion
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 18:1-8 says the Levites have no inheritance among their brothers because the LORD is their inheritance, lists the portions of sacrifices and firstfruits that are the priests' due, and allows a Levite from any town to serve at the chosen place.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how the Levites were provided for?
ev: Say what the Levites have instead of land.
Say what portions the priests were due.

nodes.t: No divination or sorcery
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 18:9-14 forbids Israel to learn the abominable practices of the nations: passing children through fire, divination, sorcery, charms, mediums and consulting the dead, which the LORD calls an abomination.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list practices Deuteronomy 18 forbids and say why?
ev: Name some of the practices forbidden here.
Say why the LORD is driving out the nations (18:12).

nodes.t: A prophet like Moses
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 18:15-22 promises that the LORD will raise up a prophet like Moses from among his brothers, recalls Israel's request at Horeb not to hear the LORD's voice directly, puts the LORD's words in the prophet's mouth, and gives a test for false prophets.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD promised in Deuteronomy 18:15-19 and how to tell a false prophet?
ev: Say what the LORD promises in 18:15 and 18:18.
Give the test of 18:22 for a prophet who speaks in the LORD's name.

nodes.t: Cities of refuge and honest witnesses
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 19 commands three cities of refuge in the land for accidental killers while the murderer who lies in wait is to be handed over, forbids moving a neighbour's landmark, and requires two or three witnesses, with the penalty of the false witness being what he intended for his brother.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why a false witness received the punishment he planned for another?
ev: Say how an accidental killing differs from murder in this chapter.
Say what happens to a false witness (19:16-21).

nodes.t: Laws of war
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 20 instructs that when Israel goes to battle the priest tells them not to fear since the LORD goes with them, certain men are excused from fighting, a distant city is offered peace first, the cities of the nations in the land are to be destroyed so Israel will not learn their abominations, and fruit trees are not to be cut down in a siege.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Israel was to do before attacking a far-off city and why the Canaanite cities were treated differently?
ev: Say what the priest says before battle (20:3-4).
Describe the offer of peace and the rule for trees.
Say the reason given for destroying the Canaanite cities (20:18).

nodes.t: The unsolved murder
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 21:1-9 gives the rite when a slain man is found and the killer is unknown: the nearest city's elders break a heifer's neck in an unworked valley, wash their hands, declare innocence and ask the LORD not to lay innocent blood on Israel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the elders carried out the rite for an unsolved murder?
ev: Describe what the elders do and say.
Say why the rite is needed (21:8-9).

nodes.t: Laws for the family
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 21:10-23 gives rules about a captive woman taken as a wife, the firstborn right of the son of an unloved wife, the stubborn and rebellious son brought to the elders, and the burial before nightfall of a man hanged on a tree, who is accursed of God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the rule about the firstborn of an unloved wife and the rule for a hanged man?
ev: Name the four situations in this section.
Say when a hanged man's body was to be buried and why (21:22-23).

nodes.t: Caring for a neighbour's property and the creation order
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 22:1-12 commands returning a brother's lost animals, helping a fallen ox, sparing the mother bird, putting a battlement on the roof, and various mixing laws (seeds, ox and ass, wool and linen) and tassels on garments.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the text tells Israel to return a neighbour's lost animal and put a battlement on a roof?
ev: Give two commands in the section about helping a neighbour.
Say what the battlement was for (22:8).

nodes.t: Marriage, charge and sexual purity laws
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 22:13-30 treats a husband's false charge against his bride, adultery, a betrothed woman assaulted in the city or the field, a woman not betrothed, and a man's taking his father's wife, with penalties set out for each case.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how these laws protected a woman from false charges and from guilt for an assault she could not prevent?
ev: Say what the elders do in the case of a false charge (22:18-19).
Say how the text distinguishes the betrothed woman in the city from the field (22:23-27).

nodes.t: The congregation, the camp and a holy LORD among them
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 23:1-14 says who may not enter the congregation of the LORD (certain persons, Ammonites and Moabites to the tenth generation, with the Edomite and Egyptian treated differently), and commands the camp to be kept clean because the LORD walks in the midst of it.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD wanted the camp kept clean (23:14)?
ev: Say why Ammonites and Moabites were excluded (23:3-5).
Say why the camp must be kept clean (23:14).

nodes.t: Fugitive slaves, usury, vows and gleaning
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 23:15-25 forbids returning an escaped slave to his master, forbids prostitution in Israel and offering its wages, forbids interest on loans to a brother, calls for vows to be paid, and allows a neighbour to eat from a vineyard or field but not carry away.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the text says about keeping a vow?
ev: Say what to do about an escaped servant (23:15-16).
Say what is allowed when passing a neighbour's vineyard.

nodes.t: Divorce, pledges and the poor
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 24:1-5 says a man who divorces his wife by a bill may not take her again after she has married another, and a newly married man is free from war for a year; 24:6-22 commands fair treatment of pledges, wages paid on the day, personal responsibility for sin, justice for stranger and orphan, and gleanings left for the poor.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Moses tells Israel to remember Egypt when treating the poor and stranger?
ev: Say what the law of 24:1-4 forbids.
Say how Israel was to treat a poor man's pledge and wages (24:10-15).
Find the reason repeated in 24:18, 22.

nodes.t: Punishment limits, the ox and the brother's widow
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 25:1-12 limits a beating to forty stripes, forbids muzzling an ox that treads out the corn, gives the duty of a brother to raise up a name for a dead brother and the shoe-loosing ceremony if he refuses, and a rule about a wife seizing a man in a fight.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the purpose of the law of the brother's widow in 25:5-10?
ev: Say the limit on flogging and the reason (25:3).
Describe the duty of a living brother to a dead brother's childless widow.

nodes.t: Honest weights and remembering Amalek
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 25:13-19 requires accurate weights and measures, calls dishonest dealing an abomination, and commands Israel to remember what Amalek did on the way from Egypt, attacking the weary, and blot out his memory when the LORD gives rest.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why honest weights and measures mattered to the LORD?
ev: Say what the LORD calls dishonest weights (25:16).
Say what Amalek did and what Israel is to do about it (25:17-19).

nodes.t: Firstfruits and the tithe confession
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 26 commands a basket of firstfruits brought to the priest with a confession that tells Israel's story from a wandering Aramean father through Egypt to the gift of the land, a third-year tithe declaration, and a mutual avowal that the LORD is Israel's God and Israel his people.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell Israel's story as the firstfruits confession tells it?
ev: Summarize the confession said with the firstfruits (26:5-10).
Say what Israel and the LORD each avouch in 26:17-19.

nodes.t: Stones, altar and the curses from Ebal
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 27 commands that on crossing the Jordan Israel set up stones with the law written on them and an altar on mount Ebal, and that tribes stand on Gerizim to bless and Ebal to curse, with Levites declaring twelve curses to each of which all the people say Amen.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Israel was to do at Gerizim and Ebal?
ev: Say which tribes stood on which mount.
Name several of the sins cursed and what the people answer (27:15-26).

nodes.t: Blessings of obedience
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 28:1-14 promises that if Israel hearkens diligently to the LORD, blessings will overtake them in city and field, in children, crops and herds, victory over enemies, plenty of rain and being the head not the tail, if they do not turn aside.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD promised Israel if they obeyed?
ev: List areas of life that are blessed (28:3-6).
State the condition repeated in 28:1, 9, 13-14.

nodes.t: Curses of disobedience
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 28:15-68 sets out the curses that will come if Israel does not obey: sickness, drought, defeat, siege, exile among the nations and a return to Egypt, because they did not serve the LORD joyfully for all he gave.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} compare the blessings of verses 1-14 with the curses that follow?
ev: Say why the text says these curses come (28:47).
Describe the final picture of exile in 28:64-68.

nodes.t: The covenant in the land of Moab
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 29 calls Israel, including children and strangers, to enter the LORD's covenant and oath that day, warns that anyone who turns to idols will bear the curses of this covenant, and says the nations will ask why the land is ruined, to be answered that they forsook the covenant; the secret things belong to the LORD and the revealed things to Israel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what covenant Israel enters in Deuteronomy 29 and what happens if they forsake it?
ev: Say who stands in the covenant ceremony (29:10-15).
Say what the nations will be told about a ruined land (29:24-28).
Find 29:29 and say what it says belongs to the LORD and what to Israel.

nodes.t: Return to the LORD; the word is near; choose life
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 30 says that when blessing and curse have come and Israel returns and obeys, the LORD will gather them, bring them to the land, and circumcise their hearts; the commandment is not hidden or far off but very near, and Moses sets life and death before them and calls them to choose life.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the choice set before Israel in Deuteronomy 30:15-20?
ev: Say what the LORD promises when Israel returns (30:1-6).
Say what 30:11-14 says about where the word is.
Say the choice in 30:19.

nodes.t: Joshua commissioned; the law read every seven years
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 31 records Moses at 120 years old encouraging Israel and Joshua that the LORD goes before them and will not fail them, writing the law and giving it to the priests to read every seventh year, the LORD predicting Israel's turning away, and the book of the law placed beside the ark.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Moses told Israel to do with the law after his death?
ev: Say what Moses told Joshua (31:7-8).
Say when and to whom the law is to be read (31:10-13).

nodes.t: The song of Moses
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 32:1-43 is a song that praises the LORD as the Rock whose work is perfect, recalls his care for Jacob in the wilderness, accuses Israel of forgetting him and worshipping other gods, tells of judgment, yet says vengeance is the LORD's and he will judge his people and be merciful to his land.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} summarize the song in three parts: the LORD's faithfulness, Israel's unfaithfulness and the LORD's judgment and mercy?
ev: Describe the picture of the LORD as the Rock in 32:3-4.
Summarize what Israel did in return for his care (32:15-18).

nodes.t: Moses is told to go up Nebo
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 32:44-52 records Moses speaking the song with Joshua, telling Israel to set their hearts on the words because they are their life, and the LORD telling him to go up mount Nebo to see the land and die because of the trespass at Meribah.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD told Moses to go up Nebo?
ev: Say why Moses is told he will not enter the land (32:51).
Say what Moses tells Israel about the words of the law (32:46-47).

nodes.t: Moses' blessing of the tribes
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 33 records Moses' blessing of Israel before his death: the LORD coming from Sinai, a blessing in turn on Reuben, Judah, Levi, Benjamin, Joseph, Zebulun, Issachar, Gad, Dan, Naphtali and Asher, and a close praising the LORD as Israel's refuge and shield.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say something Moses blessed about two of the tribes and how the chapter ends?
ev: Name the tribes blessed.
Find the closing description of the LORD in 33:26-29.

nodes.t: The death of Moses
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 34 tells how Moses goes up Nebo and sees the whole land the LORD swore to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, dies at 120 and is buried by the LORD in Moab, Israel mourns thirty days, Joshua is filled with the spirit of wisdom, and no prophet since has been like Moses.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Moses' life ended and who led Israel next?
ev: Say what the LORD showed Moses and said to him (34:1-4).
Say how the chapter describes Moses and who takes his place (34:9-12).

nodes.t: Acts: overview
nodes.d: Acts continues Luke's account from the ascension of Jesus (1:9) to Paul preaching at Rome (28:31): the Holy Ghost at Pentecost, the church in Jerusalem, the witness spreading to Judaea, Samaria and the Gentiles, and Paul's journeys, arrest and voyage to Rome.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline how the gospel spreads in Acts from Jerusalem to Rome?
ev: Say how Acts 1:8 gives the shape of the book (Jerusalem, Judaea, Samaria, the uttermost part)
Name the major sections: Peter in Jerusalem, Stephen and Philip, Saul's conversion, Cornelius, Paul's journeys, Paul's arrest and Rome

nodes.t: Jesus is taken up and the apostles wait
nodes.d: Luke begins by recalling Jesus teaching the apostles for forty days, promising the Holy Ghost, and being taken up in a cloud. Two men in white say he will return in the same way, and the disciples return to Jerusalem to pray.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Jesus said before he went up into heaven and what the apostles did next?
ev: Retell what Jesus told the apostles to wait for and be witnesses of (1:4-8)
Say what the two men told the disciples about Jesus coming back (1:11)

nodes.t: Matthias takes the place of Judas
nodes.d: Peter says the scripture about Judas had to be fulfilled and that a witness of the resurrection must replace him. The group prays and the lot falls on Matthias, who is numbered with the eleven.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the believers chose a replacement for Judas and how they chose him?
ev: State the requirement Peter gives for the one to be chosen (1:21-22)
Explain how Matthias was chosen (1:23-26)

nodes.t: The Holy Ghost comes at Pentecost
nodes.d: On the day of Pentecost a sound like a rushing wind fills the house, tongues like fire rest on each of them, and they speak in other languages. Jews from many nations each hear the wonderful works of God in their own tongue, and some mock.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what happened at Pentecost and how the crowd responded?
ev: Describe the sound, the fire and the languages (2:2-4, 2:6-11)
Name the two reactions of the crowd (2:12-13)

nodes.t: Peter preaches at Pentecost
nodes.d: Peter says the outpouring is what Joel spoke of, declares that God raised the crucified Jesus and made him Lord and Christ, and calls on the hearers to repent and be baptized. About three thousand are added that day.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} summarise Peter's argument at Pentecost and what he told the people to do?
ev: Say how Peter uses Joel, and the Psalms of David, to explain Jesus (2:16-21, 2:25-35)
State what Peter tells the crowd to do and to whom the promise belongs (2:38-39)

nodes.t: The life of the first church
nodes.d: The new believers continue in the apostles' doctrine, fellowship, breaking of bread and prayers, share what they have with those in need, worship in the temple, and see the Lord add to the church daily.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list what the first believers did together and how the church grew?
ev: List the four things the believers continued in (2:42)
Describe how they treated their possessions and each other (2:44-46)

nodes.t: The lame man at the Beautiful gate
nodes.d: Peter and John meet a man lame from birth begging at the temple gate. Peter commands him in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth to rise and walk, and he enters the temple walking and praising God while the people look on in wonder.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the lame man was healed and in whose name it was done?
ev: Retell the healing, including what Peter said he did and did not have (3:6)
Describe how the people reacted (3:9-11)

nodes.t: Peter preaches in Solomon's porch
nodes.d: Peter tells the amazed crowd that the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob glorified his Son Jesus, whom they delivered up, and that faith in his name made the man strong. He calls them to repent so that their sins may be blotted out, and reminds them of God's covenant with the fathers and the blessing promised to Abraham's seed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Peter said made the man walk and what he urged the crowd to do?
ev: Say whom Peter credits for the healing (3:12-16)
Explain what Peter calls the people to do and why (3:18-19, 3:25-26)

nodes.t: Peter and John before the council
nodes.d: The priests, the captain of the temple and the Sadducees arrest Peter and John, and about five thousand have believed. Filled with the Holy Ghost, Peter tells the rulers there is salvation in no other name than Jesus, and when ordered to stop speaking they answer that they cannot but speak what they have seen and heard.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Peter said to the rulers and why he and John would not stop preaching?
ev: State what Peter says about the name of Jesus (4:10-12)
Explain how Peter and John answered the order to stop (4:19-20)

nodes.t: The church prays for boldness
nodes.d: Released, Peter and John report to their own company, and together they pray to God the maker of heaven and earth, recalling that rulers gathered against his Christ according to his counsel. They ask for boldness, the place is shaken, and they are filled with the Holy Ghost.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the church prayed for after the threats and what happened next?
ev: Say what the believers asked God for (4:29-30)
Describe how God answered (4:31)

nodes.t: One heart and one soul: sharing with the needy
nodes.d: The multitude of believers are of one heart and soul, and owners of lands and houses sell them and lay the money at the apostles' feet for distribution to those in need. Joses, called Barnabas, is named as one who sold land and gave the money.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how the early believers shared and who Barnabas was?
ev: Describe how the believers met one another's needs (4:34-35)
Name the man given as an example and what he did (4:36-37)

nodes.t: Ananias and Sapphira
nodes.d: Ananias and Sapphira sell a possession and keep back part of the price while laying the rest at the apostles' feet. Peter says they lied to the Holy Ghost and to God; both fall down dead and great fear comes on the church.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Ananias and Sapphira did wrong and what happened?
ev: Say what the couple did and what Peter said it really was (5:2-4, 5:9)
Describe the effect on the church (5:11)

nodes.t: The apostles freed and brought before the council
nodes.d: Many signs are done and multitudes are healed, so the high priest and Sadducees imprison the apostles. An angel of the Lord opens the prison and sends them back to teach in the temple; before the council they say they must obey God rather than men, Gamaliel advises caution, and they leave rejoicing and keep teaching Jesus Christ.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the apostles escaped prison and why they kept preaching after being beaten?
ev: Describe how the apostles were freed and what the angel told them (5:19-20)
Summarise Gamaliel's advice and the apostles' response (5:29, 5:38-42)

nodes.t: Seven men are chosen to serve
nodes.d: When Grecian widows are neglected in the daily distribution, the twelve ask the disciples to choose seven men of good report, full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom, so that the apostles can give themselves to prayer and the word. Stephen and six others are chosen and prayed for, and the word of God increases.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the seven were chosen and what the apostles kept doing?
ev: Say what problem arose and what the apostles proposed (6:1-4)
Name the first of the seven chosen (6:5)

nodes.t: Stephen is seized and accused
nodes.d: Stephen, full of faith and power, does wonders among the people; men from several synagogues dispute with him and cannot resist his wisdom. They bring false witnesses before the council who say he spoke against the temple and Moses' customs, and the council sees his face like the face of an angel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Stephen was accused of and who accused him?
ev: State the charges brought against Stephen (6:11-14)
Describe how the council saw Stephen (6:15)

nodes.t: Stephen's speech: Abraham, the patriarchs and Joseph
nodes.d: Asked by the high priest if the charges are true, Stephen begins with the God of glory appearing to Abraham, the promise of the land, the covenant of circumcision and the sons of Jacob. He tells how the patriarchs sold Joseph in envy, yet God was with him and raised him up in Egypt, and how Jacob and his family came down there.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline how Stephen begins his speech from Abraham to Joseph?
ev: Say what God promised Abraham and how long his seed would be in a strange land (7:3-7)
Retell what Stephen says about Joseph and his brothers (7:9-14)

nodes.t: Stephen's speech: Moses and the people's refusal
nodes.d: Stephen recounts Israel's growth in Egypt, the birth and upbringing of Moses, his first attempt to help his brethren and their rejection, and God's call from the burning bush. He says the people refused Moses, turned back in their hearts to Egypt, and made a calf.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Stephen says Israel treated Moses, whom God sent as ruler and deliverer?
ev: Retell the stages of Moses' life Stephen names (7:20-36)
Say how Stephen says the fathers treated Moses (7:35, 7:39-41)

nodes.t: Stephen's speech: tabernacle, temple and stiffnecked people
nodes.d: Stephen recalls the tabernacle in the wilderness and David and Solomon's house, then says the Most High does not dwell in temples made with hands. He charges the council with resisting the Holy Ghost like their fathers, who persecuted the prophets and now betrayed and murdered the Just One.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Stephen answers the charge about the temple and what he accuses the council of?
ev: Say what Stephen says about where God dwells (7:48-50)
State the charge Stephen makes against the council (7:51-53)

nodes.t: Stephen sees Jesus and is stoned
nodes.d: The council is cut to the heart, but Stephen, full of the Holy Ghost, sees the glory of God and Jesus standing at God's right hand. They stone him outside the city, with the witnesses laying their clothes at the feet of a young man named Saul, and Stephen prays that the Lord Jesus receive his spirit and that this sin not be laid to their charge.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Stephen saw, how he died, and what he asked for his killers?
ev: Say what Stephen saw and said before he died (7:55-56)
Give his two prayers as he was stoned (7:59-60)

nodes.t: Persecution scatters the church
nodes.d: Saul consents to Stephen's death and a great persecution scatters the church in Jerusalem throughout Judaea and Samaria, except the apostles. Saul ravages the church, entering houses and imprisoning men and women, while the scattered believers go everywhere preaching the word.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how the persecution after Stephen spread the word?
ev: Say what Saul did to the church (8:3)
Explain what the scattered believers did (8:4)

nodes.t: Philip in Samaria and Simon the sorcerer
nodes.d: Philip preaches Christ in Samaria with miracles, and many believe and are baptized, including Simon who had practised sorcery. Peter and John come, pray, and lay hands on them so they receive the Holy Ghost; when Simon offers money for this power, Peter rebukes him and tells him to repent.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Philip did in Samaria and why Peter rebuked Simon?
ev: Describe what happened in Samaria through Philip (8:5-8, 8:12)
Explain why Peter rebuked Simon (8:18-23)

nodes.t: Philip and the Ethiopian eunuch
nodes.d: An angel and the Spirit send Philip to a chariot on the road to Gaza, where an Ethiopian officer is reading Isaiah. Philip begins at that scripture and preaches Jesus; the man believes, is baptized, and goes on his way rejoicing.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how Philip explained the scripture to the Ethiopian and what happened afterward?
ev: Say what the eunuch was reading and what Philip did with it (8:28-35)
Describe the baptism and what happened to Philip (8:36-40)

nodes.t: Saul meets Jesus on the road to Damascus
nodes.d: Saul, breathing threats against the disciples, is stopped near Damascus by a light from heaven and the voice of Jesus asking why he persecutes him. Struck blind, he is led into the city, and Ananias, sent by the Lord, lays hands on him; he receives sight, is filled with the Holy Ghost, and is baptized.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened to Saul on the Damascus road and how Ananias helped him?
ev: Say what Jesus said to Saul and what Saul asked (9:4-6)
Explain what the Lord told Ananias about Saul (9:15-16)

nodes.t: Saul preaches and escapes from Damascus
nodes.d: Saul immediately preaches in the synagogues that Jesus is the Son of God, and the Jews plot to kill him, so the disciples let him down the wall in a basket. In Jerusalem Barnabas brings him to the apostles, and when the Grecians try to kill him he is sent to Tarsus while the churches have rest.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Saul was accepted by the disciples in Jerusalem?
ev: Describe how Saul escaped Damascus (9:23-25)
Say what Barnabas did for Saul (9:26-27)

nodes.t: Peter heals Aeneas and raises Dorcas
nodes.d: Peter heals the paralysed Aeneas at Lydda in the name of Jesus Christ and many turn to the Lord. At Joppa he kneels, prays, and says "Tabitha, arise" to the disciple Dorcas, who is presented alive, and many believe.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell the stories of Aeneas and Dorcas and what people did afterward?
ev: Describe the two miracles Peter did (9:34, 9:40)
Say what Dorcas was known for (9:36, 9:39)

nodes.t: Cornelius and Peter see visions
nodes.d: Cornelius, a devout centurion at Caesarea, is told by an angel to send for Simon Peter at Joppa. Meanwhile Peter sees a sheet of animals let down from heaven and is told what God has cleansed not to call common, and the Spirit tells him to go with the three men.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the two visions and how they brought Peter and Cornelius together?
ev: Describe Cornelius' vision and what he did (10:3-8)
Say what the voice told Peter and what it meant for his actions (10:13-20)

nodes.t: Peter preaches to Cornelius and the Gentiles receive the Spirit
nodes.d: Peter tells Cornelius' household that God is no respecter of persons and that everyone who believes in Jesus receives remission of sins. While he is speaking the Holy Ghost falls on the Gentiles, and Peter commands them to be baptized.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Peter preached to Cornelius and why he baptized the Gentiles?
ev: State what Peter says about God and every nation (10:34-35)
Explain why Peter orders the Gentiles to be baptized (10:44-48)

nodes.t: Peter explains himself in Jerusalem
nodes.d: Believers in Judaea criticise Peter for eating with uncircumcised men, so he retells the vision and the Spirit falling on the Gentiles. Hearing it, they glorify God and say he has granted repentance unto life to the Gentiles also.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Peter answered those who criticised him about the Gentiles?
ev: Say what the believers objected to (11:2-3)
State the conclusion the church reached (11:17-18)

nodes.t: The church at Antioch and the first Christians
nodes.d: Scattered believers preach the Lord Jesus to Greeks at Antioch and a great number believe; Barnabas is sent, finds Saul at Tarsus, and they teach there a year, where the disciples are first called Christians. The Antioch disciples send relief to Judaea after Agabus foretells a famine.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the Antioch church began and what it did for the brethren in Judaea?
ev: Say where the disciples were first called Christians (11:26)
Describe what the Antioch church did when famine was foretold (11:27-30)

nodes.t: James killed and Peter freed from prison
nodes.d: Herod kills James and imprisons Peter, but the church prays unceasingly. An angel leads Peter out past the guards at night, and he comes to the house of Mary, where Rhoda is so glad she forgets to open the gate and the astonished believers at last let him in.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how God rescued Peter and what the church was doing at the time?
ev: Describe how Peter was brought out of prison (12:6-10)
Say what the church was doing and how they reacted (12:5, 12:12-16)

nodes.t: Herod's death and the word of God grows
nodes.d: Herod, in royal apparel, receives the people's shout that he speaks as a god; the angel of the Lord strikes him because he gave not God the glory. The word of God grows and multiplies, and Barnabas and Saul return with John Mark.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Herod died and what happened to the word of God?
ev: Say why Herod was struck down (12:22-23)
Contrast Herod's end with what happened to the word of God (12:24)

nodes.t: Barnabas and Saul are sent out from Antioch
nodes.d: The Holy Ghost tells the Antioch prophets and teachers to separate Barnabas and Saul for the work, and the church fasts, prays and sends them. On Cyprus, Saul (also called Paul) strikes the sorcerer Elymas blind and the deputy Sergius Paulus believes.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain who sent Barnabas and Saul out and what happened on Cyprus?
ev: Say how Barnabas and Saul were sent (13:2-4)
Describe what happened to Elymas and the deputy (13:8-12)

nodes.t: Paul preaches in the synagogue at Pisidian Antioch
nodes.d: Invited to speak after the reading of the law and prophets, Paul traces Israel's story from Egypt through the judges and David to Jesus, whom God raised from the dead. He declares forgiveness of sins and that by Jesus all who believe are justified from what the law of Moses could not justify.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} summarise Paul's sermon from Israel's history to forgiveness through Jesus?
ev: Outline the history Paul recounts to reach Jesus (13:17-23)
State what Paul says is preached through Jesus (13:38-39)

nodes.t: Paul and Barnabas turn to the Gentiles
nodes.d: Gentiles ask to hear more, and the next sabbath almost the whole city gathers; the envious Jews contradict, so Paul and Barnabas say they turn to the Gentiles, citing the Lord's command to be a light to them. The Gentiles rejoice, those ordained to eternal life believe, and the apostles are expelled.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul and Barnabas turned to the Gentiles at Antioch?
ev: Say why Paul and Barnabas turned to the Gentiles (13:45-47)
Describe how the Gentiles and the disciples responded (13:48, 13:52)

nodes.t: Iconium and Lystra: healing, worship refused, stoning
nodes.d: At Iconium many believe but the city is divided and the apostles flee. At Lystra Paul heals a man lame from birth and the crowd calls them gods; the apostles stop the sacrifice and preach the living God who made heaven and earth, but Jews from Antioch and Iconium turn the people and stone Paul, who rises up and goes on.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened at Lystra and what the apostles said to the crowd?
ev: Say how Paul and Barnabas responded when the people wanted to sacrifice to them (14:14-18)
Describe what happened to Paul after the healing (14:19-20)

nodes.t: The return to Antioch: elders appointed
nodes.d: Paul and Barnabas return through the cities, confirming the disciples, warning that entering the kingdom is through much tribulation, and ordaining elders in every church with prayer and fasting. Back at Antioch they report that God had opened the door of faith to the Gentiles.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul and Barnabas did on their way back and what they reported?
ev: Say what the apostles told the disciples about tribulation (14:22)
Describe the report given at Antioch (14:26-27)

nodes.t: The Jerusalem council on circumcision
nodes.d: Men from Judaea teach that Gentiles must be circumcised to be saved, so Paul and Barnabas go to Jerusalem. Peter recalls God giving the Gentiles the Holy Ghost and says salvation is through the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ; James cites the prophets and judges that Gentile believers should not be troubled, only asked to abstain from idols, fornication, strangled things and blood.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the question the Jerusalem council settled and how they answered it?
ev: State the question that began the dispute (15:1, 15:5)
Say what Peter and James each concluded (15:7-11, 15:13-19)

nodes.t: The letter to the Gentile churches
nodes.d: The apostles and elders send Judas Barsabas and Silas with Paul and Barnabas, carrying a letter saying that it seemed good to the Holy Ghost and to them to lay no greater burden than the necessary things. The Antioch believers read it and rejoice.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the letter from Jerusalem said and how Antioch responded?
ev: Say who delivered the letter and what it asked of Gentile believers (15:22-29)
Describe how Antioch received it (15:30-32)

nodes.t: Paul and Barnabas part ways
nodes.d: Paul proposes revisiting the churches, and Barnabas wants to take John Mark, whom Paul will not take since he left them in Pamphylia. The contention is so sharp that they separate; Barnabas takes Mark to Cyprus and Paul takes Silas through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the churches.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell why Paul and Barnabas separated and who went with each?
ev: Say what the disagreement was about (15:37-38)
Describe where each pair went (15:39-41)

nodes.t: Timothy joins and the call to Macedonia
nodes.d: At Lystra Paul takes Timothy, whose mother is a believing Jewess and whose father is Greek, and circumcises him because of the Jews there, while delivering the Jerusalem decrees. Forbidden by the Spirit to go to Asia or Bithynia, Paul sees a vision of a man of Macedonia and concludes the Lord has called them to preach there.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Paul was led to go to Macedonia?
ev: Say why Paul circumcised Timothy (16:3)
Describe how the Spirit directed the journey (16:6-10)

nodes.t: Lydia's heart is opened at Philippi
nodes.d: At Philippi on the sabbath Paul speaks to women by the river, and the Lord opens the heart of Lydia, a seller of purple who worshipped God. She and her household are baptized, and she constrains the missionaries to stay in her house.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Lydia came to believe at Philippi?
ev: Say who Lydia was and how she came to believe (16:14)
Describe what she did after being baptized (16:15)

nodes.t: Paul and Silas in the Philippian jail
nodes.d: After Paul casts a spirit out of a slave girl, her owners have Paul and Silas beaten and jailed. At midnight they pray and sing, an earthquake opens the doors, and the jailer asks what he must do to be saved; they tell him to believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and he and his household are baptized.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened in the Philippian jail and how the jailer was saved?
ev: Describe what Paul and Silas did in the prison at midnight (16:25)
Give the jailer's question and the answer (16:30-31)

nodes.t: Paul insists on his rights as a Roman
nodes.d: The magistrates send word to let Paul and Silas go, but Paul says they were beaten openly uncondemned, being Romans, and demands that the magistrates come themselves. The magistrates fear and ask them to leave, and the pair visit Lydia's house and encourage the brethren before departing.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul would not leave the Philippian prison quietly?
ev: Say what Paul demanded and why (16:37)
Describe the magistrates' reaction (16:38-39)

nodes.t: Thessalonica and Berea: reasoning from the scriptures
nodes.d: At Thessalonica Paul reasons from the scriptures for three sabbaths that Christ must suffer and rise again; some believe but jealous Jews raise an uproar against Jason's house. At Berea the Jews receive the word readily and search the scriptures daily to see whether these things are so, but opponents from Thessalonica follow.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the Bereans did with Paul's message?
ev: Say what Paul argued from the scriptures (17:2-3)
Explain what made the Bereans noble (17:11)

nodes.t: Paul at the Areopagus in Athens
nodes.d: Distressed by the idols of Athens, Paul is brought to the Areopagus, where he speaks of the altar to the unknown God. He says God who made the world does not dwell in temples, gave life and breath to all, made all nations of one blood, commands all men to repent, and will judge the world by the man he raised from the dead; some mock, and some believe.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} summarise what Paul said to the Athenians about God, repentance and judgment?
ev: Say what Paul tells the Athenians about the God who made the world (17:24-28)
State the command and the warning in 17:30-31

nodes.t: Paul at Corinth
nodes.d: At Corinth Paul works with Aquila and Priscilla and reasons in the synagogue; when the Jews oppose, he goes to the Gentiles, and Crispus the synagogue ruler believes. The Lord tells him in a night vision not to be afraid, for he has much people in the city, and Gallio dismisses the Jews' charge against him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened to Paul at Corinth and what the Lord told him?
ev: Say what the Lord told Paul in the night (18:9-10)
Describe how Gallio handled the accusation (18:14-16)

nodes.t: Apollos is taught more perfectly
nodes.d: Paul sails to Ephesus, Caesarea and Antioch and then strengthens the disciples in Galatia and Phrygia. Apollos, an eloquent man mighty in the scriptures who knows only the baptism of John, is taken aside by Aquila and Priscilla, who expound the way of God to him more perfectly, and he helps the believers in Achaia.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Apollos was helped by Priscilla and Aquila?
ev: Say what Apollos knew and lacked (18:24-25)
Describe what Aquila and Priscilla did for him (18:26)

nodes.t: Paul at Ephesus: the twelve disciples and the school of Tyrannus
nodes.d: Paul finds about twelve disciples at Ephesus who know only John's baptism; they are baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus, and when Paul lays hands on them the Holy Ghost comes and they speak with tongues and prophesy. Paul then reasons for two years, so that all in Asia hear the word of the Lord Jesus.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened to the twelve disciples at Ephesus?
ev: Say what the disciples had and had not received (19:2-5)
Describe where and how long Paul taught after leaving the synagogue (19:9-10)

nodes.t: Miracles at Ephesus and the burning of the books
nodes.d: God works special miracles through Paul, and the seven sons of Sceva who try to use the name of Jesus over an evil spirit are overpowered. Fear falls on Ephesus, the name of the Lord Jesus is magnified, and believers burn their magic books worth fifty thousand pieces of silver.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened to the sons of Sceva and what the believers did with their books?
ev: Say what happened to the sons of Sceva (19:13-16)
Describe how the believers responded (19:17-19)

nodes.t: The riot of the silversmiths at Ephesus
nodes.d: Demetrius the silversmith, whose trade in shrines for Diana is threatened by Paul's teaching that gods made with hands are no gods, stirs up the craftsmen. The whole city rushes into the theatre shouting "Great is Diana", until the town clerk quiets the crowd and says that disputes belong to the law courts and a lawful assembly.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the craftsmen at Ephesus were angry and how the riot ended?
ev: Say what Demetrius said was at stake (19:24-27)
Explain how the town clerk calmed the crowd (19:35-41)

nodes.t: Eutychus falls from the window at Troas
nodes.d: Paul travels through Macedonia and Greece to Troas, where the disciples meet on the first day of the week to break bread. Paul speaks until midnight, young Eutychus falls from a third-floor window and is taken up dead, and Paul embraces him and tells them his life is in him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell what happened to Eutychus while Paul was preaching?
ev: Describe what happened to Eutychus (20:9-10)
Say what the disciples were doing when Paul preached (20:7)

nodes.t: Paul's farewell to the Ephesian elders
nodes.d: At Miletus Paul calls the Ephesian elders and recalls his service and teaching in Asia, telling them he goes bound in the Spirit to Jerusalem. He charges them to feed the church of God, warns of grievous wolves arising even from among them, commends them to God and the word of his grace, and recalls that it is more blessed to give than to receive.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Paul's charge to the Ephesian elders and the warnings he gave?
ev: Say what Paul told the elders to do and why (20:28-31)
Describe how the elders and Paul parted (20:36-38)

nodes.t: Warnings along the road to Jerusalem
nodes.d: Paul sails to Tyre, where disciples tell him through the Spirit not to go up to Jerusalem, and stays at Caesarea with Philip the evangelist. The prophet Agabus binds his own hands and feet with Paul's girdle and says the Jews will bind him; Paul replies that he is ready to die for the name of the Lord Jesus, and they say the will of the Lord be done.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the warnings Paul received on his way to Jerusalem and how he answered?
ev: Say what Agabus did and said (21:10-11)
Explain Paul's answer to those who begged him not to go (21:13-14)

nodes.t: Paul and the vow in the temple
nodes.d: At Jerusalem James and the elders glorify God for Paul's report, but tell him that thousands of Jews zealous for the law have heard he teaches against Moses. They advise him to join four men with a vow, and restate that Gentile believers need keep only the things in the earlier letter; Paul does so in the temple.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why James and the elders advised Paul to take part in the vow?
ev: Say what rumour the elders mention and what they advised (21:20-24)
Restate the instruction about Gentile believers (21:25)

nodes.t: Paul is seized in the temple and arrested
nodes.d: Jews from Asia stir up the people against Paul, saying he teaches against the people, the law and the place and has brought Greeks into the temple. They drag him out to kill him, the chief captain rescues him and binds him with chains, and Paul asks leave to speak to the people.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell why Paul was seized in the temple and how he was rescued?
ev: Describe the charges of the Asian Jews (21:28-29)
Say how Paul was saved from the mob (21:31-33)

nodes.t: Paul tells his story to the crowd
nodes.d: Speaking in Hebrew from the stairs, Paul tells of his upbringing under Gamaliel, his persecution of the Way, the vision on the Damascus road, and Ananias' words. He says that in the temple the Lord told him to depart because he would be sent far to the Gentiles, and at that word the crowd cries out for his death.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell Paul's own account of how he came to follow Jesus and why the crowd shouted?
ev: Summarise the parts of his life Paul describes (22:3-5, 22:6-16)
Say which word made the crowd shout (22:21-22)

nodes.t: Paul declares he is a Roman
nodes.d: As the chief captain orders Paul to be examined by scourging, Paul asks the centurion whether it is lawful to scourge a Roman uncondemned. The chief captain is afraid on learning that Paul is a Roman, freeborn, and next day sets him before the chief priests and council.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Paul's Roman citizenship affected his treatment?
ev: Say what Paul asked the centurion (22:25)
Describe how the chief captain reacted (22:26-29)

nodes.t: Paul before the council: the resurrection
nodes.d: Paul tells the council he has lived in all good conscience, and when the high priest orders him struck, he rebukes him and then says he did not know he was the high priest. Perceiving Sadducees and Pharisees, he says he is called in question for the hope of the resurrection, the council divides, and the Lord stands by him that night to say he must bear witness at Rome.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Paul used the question of the resurrection before the council?
ev: Say how Paul divided the council (23:6-9)
State what the Lord told Paul that night (23:11)

nodes.t: The plot against Paul and his transfer to Caesarea
nodes.d: More than forty Jews bind themselves by a curse to neither eat nor drink till they have killed Paul. Paul's sister's son tells the chief captain, who sends Paul by night with a large escort and a letter to Felix at Caesarea.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the plot against Paul was discovered and how he was kept safe?
ev: Describe the plot and who uncovered it (23:12-16)
Say what the chief captain's letter reports (23:26-30)

nodes.t: Paul before Felix
nodes.d: The high priest and the orator Tertullus accuse Paul before Felix; Paul answers that he worships the God of his fathers, believes the law and the prophets, and hopes for a resurrection of the just and unjust. Felix trembles when Paul reasons of righteousness, temperance and judgment to come, but defers him and leaves him bound for two years.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Paul defended himself before Felix and how Felix responded?
ev: Say what Paul confessed about the way he worships (24:14-16)
Describe Felix's response and how long Paul stayed bound (24:25-27)

nodes.t: Paul appeals to Caesar
nodes.d: Festus succeeds Felix and the Jews ask that Paul be sent to Jerusalem, intending an ambush. Paul says he has not offended against the law, the temple or Caesar, refuses to be handed over, and appeals to Caesar; Festus answers that he will go to Caesar.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul appealed to Caesar?
ev: Say what Paul said when Festus proposed a trial at Jerusalem (25:9-11)
Give Festus' decision (25:12)

nodes.t: Festus lays Paul's case before King Agrippa
nodes.d: King Agrippa and Bernice visit Festus, who explains that the accusers brought no charge he expected, only questions about their religion and about one Jesus who was dead whom Paul affirmed to be alive. Agrippa wishes to hear Paul and Festus brings him forth, saying he has no certain thing to write to Caesar.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Festus told Agrippa about Paul's case?
ev: Say how Festus summarised the case (25:18-19)
State why Festus brought Paul before Agrippa (25:26-27)

nodes.t: Paul's defence before Agrippa
nodes.d: Paul tells Agrippa of his life as a Pharisee, his persecution of the saints and the vision on the road to Damascus, where Jesus sends him to open eyes and turn Gentiles from darkness to light. He says he says nothing beyond what Moses and the prophets said, that Christ should suffer and rise first, and Agrippa answers "Almost thou persuadest me to be a Christian".
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell Paul's speech to Agrippa and how Agrippa replied?
ev: State the commission Jesus gave Paul (26:16-18)
Say what Paul says the prophets and Moses foretold (26:22-23)

nodes.t: The voyage to Rome and the storm
nodes.d: Paul and other prisoners are delivered to the centurion Julius and sail for Italy; Paul warns of danger but the centurion trusts the master of the ship. A tempest drives the ship for many days until all hope is lost, then an angel tells Paul he must stand before Caesar and that God has given him all who sail with him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the storm began and what God told Paul in it?
ev: Say what Paul warned and who was believed (27:9-11)
Give the angel's message to Paul (27:23-25)

nodes.t: The shipwreck and the escape to land
nodes.d: On the fourteenth night the sailors try to flee and Paul tells the centurion they must stay in the ship; Paul urges all to eat and gives thanks to God before them. The ship runs aground and breaks up, the centurion stops the soldiers from killing the prisoners, and all 276 reach land safe.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how everyone on the ship came safely to land?
ev: Describe what Paul urged before the wreck (27:31, 27:33-36)
Say what happened to the people on board (27:42-44)

nodes.t: Paul on Malta
nodes.d: The islanders show kindness; when a viper fastens on Paul's hand he shakes it off unharmed, and they change their minds and say he is a god. Paul prays for and heals the father of Publius and others on the island.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened to Paul on Malta?
ev: Describe the viper and the islanders' two opinions (28:3-6)
Say what Paul did for Publius' father (28:8)

nodes.t: Paul arrives at Rome
nodes.d: After three months the party sails in a ship of Alexandria and lands at Puteoli, where they find brethren. Believers from Rome come to meet Paul on the road, and he thanks God and takes courage; at Rome he is allowed to dwell by himself with a soldier.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Paul arrived at Rome and who welcomed him?
ev: Say how the Roman brethren met Paul (28:15)
Describe the conditions of his stay at Rome (28:16)

nodes.t: Paul preaches in Rome
nodes.d: Paul tells the Jewish leaders at Rome that he is bound for the hope of Israel and expounds the kingdom of God from Moses and the prophets, with some believing and others not. He quotes Isaiah on hardened hearts, says salvation is sent to the Gentiles, and for two years receives all who come, preaching with all confidence, no man forbidding him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul did and said at Rome and how Acts ends?
ev: Say how the Jews divided in response (28:24-25)
Describe how the book ends (28:30-31)

nodes.t: James: overview
nodes.d: James is a letter from James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes scattered abroad, with practical teaching on trials, living faith, the tongue, humility, wealth and patience.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what James tells believers to do with trials, words and wealth?
ev: Name the main themes of James in order
Say who the letter is from and to whom it is written

nodes.t: Trials, wisdom and the crown of life
nodes.d: James says to count trials as joy because tested faith produces patience, to ask God for wisdom without wavering, and promises the crown of life to the one who endures.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why James says to count it all joy when trials come?
ev: Explain what testing of faith produces
Say how James tells believers to ask for wisdom

nodes.t: Temptation, the word and doing it
nodes.d: James says God does not tempt anyone; desire gives birth to sin and sin to death, while every good gift comes from the Father of lights who gave new birth by the word of truth, and believers must be doers of the word.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the difference between hearing the word and doing it?
ev: Describe the path from desire to death in 1:14-15
Contrast hearing the word with doing it
State what James calls pure religion

nodes.t: No partiality: the royal law
nodes.d: James rebukes giving the rich seats of honour and shaming the poor in the assembly, reminds them God chose the poor rich in faith, and calls loving your neighbour the royal law.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what James says is wrong with favouring the rich over the poor?
ev: Describe the example of partiality in the assembly
Say what James calls the royal law
Explain why partiality is sin according to 2:9

nodes.t: Faith and works
nodes.d: James argues that faith without works is dead, using the demons who believe, Abraham offering Isaac, and Rahab, and concludes a man is justified by works and not by faith only.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what James is arguing about the kind of faith that is dead?
ev: Explain what James means by faith that is alone and dead
Retell how Abraham and Rahab are used as examples
Compare the wording of James 2:24 with Romans 3:28 and 4:2-3

nodes.t: The tongue
nodes.d: James warns that few should be teachers, compares the tongue to a bit, a rudder and a fire, and says it cannot be tamed by man yet is used both to bless God and curse people.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say why James calls the tongue a fire?
ev: Name the three pictures James uses for the tongue
Say what inconsistency James points out in 3:9-10

nodes.t: Wisdom from above and earthly wisdom
nodes.d: James contrasts envy and strife, which he calls earthly, sensual and devilish wisdom, with wisdom from above, which is pure, peaceable, gentle and full of mercy and good fruits.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how to tell wisdom from above from earthly wisdom?
ev: List the marks of wisdom from above
Describe what comes with bitter envying and strife

nodes.t: Conflicts, the world and humbling before God
nodes.d: James traces fightings to desires within, calls friendship with the world enmity with God, and says God gives grace to the humble, so believers must submit, resist the devil and draw near to God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what James says to do instead of fighting and loving the world?
ev: Say where James says wars and fightings come from
List the commands in 4:7-10
Explain what God does with the proud and the humble

nodes.t: Judging others and boasting about tomorrow
nodes.d: James forbids speaking evil of a brother and judging him since there is one lawgiver, and rebukes plans made without saying if the Lord will, since life is a vapour.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why James says to say, If the Lord will?
ev: Say why James says there is one lawgiver
Explain what James says we should say about our plans
State the point of 4:17

nodes.t: Warning to the rich who defraud
nodes.d: James tells rich men to weep for coming miseries: their riches are corrupted, wages withheld from labourers cry out to the Lord of sabaoth, and they have lived in luxury and condemned the just.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the rich are accused of in James 5:1-6?
ev: Name the charges James brings against the rich in 5:1-6
Say who hears the cries of the harvest labourers

nodes.t: Patience until the coming of the Lord
nodes.d: James urges patience like the farmer waiting for rain, points to the prophets and Job as examples, says the Lord is pitiful and merciful, and tells them not to swear oaths.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why James says to be patient until the coming of the Lord?
ev: Describe the farmer picture of patience
Name the examples of endurance James gives
Say what James tells them about oaths

nodes.t: Prayer, healing and restoring the wanderer
nodes.d: James tells the afflicted to pray, the sick to call the elders, believers to confess faults and pray for one another, cites Elijah as a man like us whose prayer was answered, and ends by urging restoring one who strays from the truth.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what James says to do when someone is sick, sinning or wandering?
ev: Describe what the sick are told to do in 5:14-15
Say how James uses Elijah
Explain what happens when someone turns a sinner from error

nodes.t: 1 Peter: overview
nodes.d: 1 Peter is a letter from the apostle Peter to scattered strangers in Asia Minor, written to encourage them in suffering with the living hope, the example of Christ, holy conduct and humility under God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say how 1 Peter encourages believers who suffer?
ev: Say who wrote 1 Peter and to whom
Name the main themes: hope, holiness, suffering and humility

nodes.t: Born again to a living hope
nodes.d: Peter blesses God who by the resurrection of Jesus has given new birth to a living hope and an inheritance kept in heaven, while faith is tested like gold and the prophets searched out this salvation.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what living hope Peter says believers have and why they can rejoice in trials?
ev: Describe the inheritance in 1:4
Explain why trials test faith in 1:6-7
Say what the prophets searched into in 1:10-11

nodes.t: Be holy: redeemed by precious blood
nodes.d: Peter calls believers to be holy as God is holy, reminds them they were redeemed by the precious blood of Christ the lamb without blemish, and says they were born again by the abiding word.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Peter says paid the price for believers, and how they should live because of it?
ev: Say what Peter says redeemed them and what it was not
Explain the call to be holy in 1:15-16
Describe what the word of the Lord does according to 1:23-25

nodes.t: The living stone and the holy priesthood
nodes.d: Peter calls Christ the living stone chosen by God, says believers are built up as a spiritual house and royal priesthood, and says they were once not a people but are now the people of God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name three things Peter calls believers in 1 Peter 2:9?
ev: Explain the stone picture in 2:4-8
List the names Peter gives believers in 2:9
Say what 2:10 says changed for them

nodes.t: Strangers and pilgrims: honourable conduct and submission
nodes.d: Peter tells believers living as pilgrims among Gentiles to keep honest conduct, submit to rulers and honour all, and servants to be subject to masters even when treated wrongly.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say how Peter says believers should behave under authorities?
ev: Say why Peter tells them to keep honest conduct among the Gentiles
Describe how Peter says to treat the king and all men

nodes.t: Christ suffered for us, an example
nodes.d: Peter says believers are called to follow the steps of Christ, who did not sin, did not revile in return, bore our sins on the tree, and brings the strayed sheep back to the Shepherd.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain both what Christ did for us and what example he left in 1 Peter 2:21-25?
ev: Describe how Christ responded when reviled
Say what Christ did on the tree in 2:24
Explain the sheep and Shepherd picture

nodes.t: Wives, husbands and the hidden person of the heart
nodes.d: Peter addresses wives with the example of Sarah and holy women, stressing a meek and quiet spirit as precious to God, and tells husbands to live with their wives with understanding and honour as fellow heirs of the grace of life.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Peter tells husbands and wives in 1 Peter 3:1-7?
ev: Say what Peter calls the adorning of great price
Describe what husbands are told in 3:7

nodes.t: Blessing, good conscience and suffering for doing good
nodes.d: Peter tells all to be of one mind and repay evil with blessing, says suffering for righteousness is blessed, and that believers should always be ready to give a reason for their hope with meekness and a good conscience.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Peter says to respond when others speak evil of us?
ev: Say how Peter tells believers to answer evil
Explain what being ready to answer for hope looks like in 3:15
