nodes.t: Christ suffered once, the days of Noah and baptism
nodes.d: Peter says Christ suffered once for sins, the just for the unjust, to bring us to God, and was made alive; he mentions the spirits who were disobedient in the days of Noah, the eight saved by water, and says baptism saves by the resurrection of Jesus, who is now at God's right hand.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what 1 Peter 3:18-22 says about Christ and about Noah?
ev: Say why Christ suffered once according to 3:18
Retell what 3:20 says about Noah and the eight saved through water
State where Christ is now according to 3:22

nodes.t: Living to the will of God
nodes.d: Peter says believers who have the mind of Christ in suffering should end the old life of Gentile excess, live to God, and prepare for the end by prayer, fervent love, hospitality and using gifts for God's glory.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list how Peter says to live because the end of all things is at hand?
ev: Describe the old life Peter says to leave behind
List the commands in 4:7-11
Explain why gifts are to be used for God's glory

nodes.t: The fiery trial and suffering as a Christian
nodes.d: Peter says not to be surprised by fiery trial but to rejoice in sharing Christ's sufferings, not to suffer as an evildoer, and to entrust the soul to a faithful Creator while judgment begins at the house of God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Peter says not to be surprised by a fiery trial?
ev: Say how Peter tells believers to view fiery trials
Distinguish suffering as a Christian from suffering as an evildoer
Say whom believers entrust their souls to in 4:19

nodes.t: Shepherd the flock, humility and the roaring lion
nodes.d: Peter exhorts elders to shepherd willingly as examples with the chief Shepherd coming, tells all to be clothed with humility, cast cares on God, resist the devil who prowls like a roaring lion, and ends with greetings from Babylon.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Peter tells elders and everyone else to do in chapter 5?
ev: Describe how elders are to lead in 5:2-3
Say what Peter tells believers to do with their cares
Say how Peter describes the devil and how to resist him

nodes.t: 2 Peter: overview
nodes.d: 2 Peter is a letter from Simon Peter urging growth in the knowledge of Christ, warning against false teachers and scoffers, and pointing to the certain day of the Lord and new heavens and a new earth.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what 2 Peter warns about and what it tells believers to do?
ev: Name the three sections: growth, false teachers, the day of the Lord
Say what Peter wants believers to remember

nodes.t: Precious promises and growing in godliness
nodes.d: Peter says God has given all that pertains to life and godliness and great promises, and tells believers to add virtue, knowledge, temperance, patience, godliness, brotherly kindness and charity to faith so they are fruitful and make their calling sure.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list the qualities Peter says to add to faith?
ev: List the qualities to add to faith in 1:5-7
Say what Peter says God has given in 1:3-4
Explain what lacking these things means in 1:9

nodes.t: Eyewitnesses and the sure word of prophecy
nodes.d: Peter says he will remind believers before his death, that the apostles were eyewitnesses of Christ's majesty when the Father's voice spoke on the holy mount, and that prophecy of scripture came from men moved by the Holy Ghost.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Peter says the apostles did not follow cunningly devised fables?
ev: Say what the apostles saw and heard on the holy mount
Explain where Peter says prophecy of scripture came from

nodes.t: False teachers and the examples of judgment
nodes.d: Peter warns that false teachers will bring in destructive heresies out of covetousness, and shows that God judged sinning angels, the old world in Noah's day, and Sodom and Gomorrah while delivering Noah and Lot.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what examples Peter uses to show God judges the ungodly and rescues the godly?
ev: Describe what the false teachers do and why
List the three examples of judgment in 2:4-6
Say who God delivered in 2:5-9

nodes.t: The character and end of the false teachers
nodes.d: Peter describes the false teachers as presumptuous, greedy and following Balaam, promising freedom while enslaved to corruption, and says to return to the way of righteousness after knowing it is worse than never knowing it.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Peter portrays the false teachers and why turning back is so serious?
ev: Name the charges in 2:13-15
Explain the saying about the dog and the sow in 2:22
Say who Peter compares them to in 2:15-16

nodes.t: Scoffers and the longsuffering of the Lord
nodes.d: Peter says scoffers will ask where the promised coming is, recalls that the world once perished by water and the present heavens and earth are kept for fire, and says the Lord delays because he is longsuffering, not willing that any perish.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Peter says the Lord seems slow to keep his promise?
ev: Say what the scoffers claim in 3:4
Explain what Peter says they forget in 3:5-7
Say why the Lord has not yet come, according to 3:9

nodes.t: The day of the Lord and new heavens and earth
nodes.d: Peter says the day of the Lord will come like a thief with fire dissolving the heavens and the elements, so believers should live in holiness and look for new heavens and a new earth where righteousness dwells, and grow in grace.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say how Peter tells believers to live while they wait for the day of the Lord?
ev: Describe how the day of the Lord comes
Say what kind of people Peter says we ought to be in 3:11
Say what new thing believers look for in 3:13

nodes.t: 1 John: overview
nodes.d: 1 John is a letter written so that believers may have fellowship with the Father and the Son, know they have eternal life, walk in the light, love one another, and hold to the truth that Jesus is the Christ come in the flesh.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what 1 John wants believers to know?
ev: Name the main themes: light, love, truth about Jesus, assurance
Say what John says he wrote so that in 5:13

nodes.t: Fellowship, walking in the light and confessing sin
nodes.d: John declares the Word of life that he has heard, seen and touched, says God is light, and teaches that walking in the light brings cleansing by the blood of Jesus and that confessed sins are forgiven.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what John says to do when we sin?
ev: Say what John says he saw and heard
Explain what God is according to 1:5
Describe what happens when we confess sins in 1:9

nodes.t: Our advocate and keeping his commandments
nodes.d: John writes that we may not sin, but if anyone sins we have an advocate, Jesus Christ the righteous, the propitiation for our sins and the whole world, and that knowing him is shown by keeping his commandments.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say who our advocate is and how we know we know him?
ev: Name what Jesus is called in 2:1-2
Say how we know that we know him

nodes.t: The old and new commandment: light and hatred
nodes.d: John says the commandment to love is old and yet new because the true light shines, and that hating a brother means walking in darkness while loving a brother abides in the light.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how John connects loving a brother with being in the light?
ev: Contrast loving and hating a brother in light and darkness
Say who John addresses in 2:12-14

nodes.t: Not loving the world, and antichrists
nodes.d: John tells believers not to love the world, since its lust of the flesh, lust of the eyes and pride of life pass away, and warns of many antichrists who went out from them, while the anointing from the Holy One teaches them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what John says about the world and about those who deny the Son?
ev: List what John says is in the world
Say who John calls antichrist in 2:22
Describe what he says about those who left in 2:19

nodes.t: Abiding in him and being children of God
nodes.d: John urges abiding in Christ with confidence at his appearing, says we are now sons of God and shall be like him, and that Christ appeared to take away sins and destroy the works of the devil.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what John says about being God's children now and later?
ev: Say what we shall be when he appears
Explain why the Son of God was manifested according to 3:8
Contrast the children of God with the children of the devil

nodes.t: Love in deed and truth, assurance and the commandment
nodes.d: John says love is the message from the beginning, unlike Cain who killed his brother, that Christ laid down his life for us so we ought to love in deed and truth, and that God is greater than a condemning heart.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what John means by loving not in word only but in deed and in truth?
ev: Say how John contrasts Cain with the love Christ showed
Explain what loving in deed and truth means in 3:17-18
State the commandment in 3:23

nodes.t: Testing the spirits
nodes.d: John tells believers to test every spirit, says the spirit of God confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh, and says those in them have overcome because greater is he that is in them than he that is in the world.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say how John tells us to test what teachers say?
ev: Say how to test a spirit according to 4:2-3
Explain why believers have overcome in 4:4

nodes.t: God is love
nodes.d: John says love is of God and God is love, shown when God sent his only Son as propitiation, that we love because he first loved us, and that perfect love casts out fear and one who hates a brother cannot love God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how John says we know that God is love?
ev: Say how God showed his love in 4:9-10
Explain 4:19
Describe what John says about loving God and hating a brother

nodes.t: Born of God, overcoming and the witness to the Son
nodes.d: John says everyone who believes Jesus is the Christ is born of God and overcomes the world through faith, and the witness of God about his Son is that God gave eternal life in the Son.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what John says is the witness God gave about his Son?
ev: Say what overcomes the world in 5:4
State the record God gave in 5:11
Say what 5:12 says about having the Son

nodes.t: Assurance, prayer and keeping from idols
nodes.d: John says he wrote so believers may know they have eternal life, that God hears prayer according to his will, mentions sin not unto death and sin unto death, and ends by telling them to keep from idols.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what John wants his readers to know about eternal life and prayer?
ev: Say why John wrote this letter according to 5:13
Describe the confidence in prayer in 5:14-15
State John's last command

nodes.t: 2 John: overview
nodes.d: 2 John is a short letter from the elder to an elect lady and her children, about walking in truth and love and not receiving those who do not bring the doctrine of Christ.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what 2 John tells believers about truth and love?
ev: Say who writes and who receives 2 John
Name its two concerns: love and truth

nodes.t: Walk in truth and love; beware of deceivers
nodes.d: The elder rejoices that the children walk in truth, repeats the commandment to love, warns of deceivers who deny Jesus Christ has come in the flesh, and says not to receive those who bring no such doctrine.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why 2 John says to love and also to be careful about false teachers?
ev: Say what the commandment from the beginning is in 2JN 1:5-6
Describe the deceivers in 2JN 1:7
Say what the elder says to do about visitors without the doctrine

nodes.t: 3 John: overview
nodes.d: 3 John is a short letter from the elder to Gaius commending his hospitality to travelling brothers, naming Diotrephes who refuses them and Demetrius who has a good report.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say who Gaius, Diotrephes and Demetrius are in 3 John?
ev: Name the three people the elder mentions
Say what 3 John praises

nodes.t: Gaius, Diotrephes and Demetrius: hospitality and truth
nodes.d: The elder commends Gaius for faithfully helping brothers and strangers who went out for Christ's name, contrasts Diotrephes who loves preeminence and rejects them, and says to imitate good and not evil, with Demetrius well reported.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} contrast what Gaius does with what Diotrephes does?
ev: Say what Gaius does that the elder praises
Describe what Diotrephes does
Say why the elder says we should receive such travellers

nodes.t: Jude: overview
nodes.d: Jude, a servant of Jesus Christ and brother of James, urges believers to contend for the faith once delivered, warns of ungodly men who crept in, recalls examples of judgment, and ends with a call to keep in God's love and a doxology.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jude asks believers to contend for?
ev: Say who wrote Jude
Say what Jude urges in verse 3

nodes.t: Contend for the faith once delivered
nodes.d: Jude says he had to urge believers to contend earnestly for the faith once delivered to the saints because ungodly men had crept in who turn grace into licence and deny the Lord.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Jude says he had to write about contending for the faith?
ev: Say who Jude addresses in verse 1
Describe the men in verse 4

nodes.t: Examples of judgment: unbelievers, angels and Sodom
nodes.d: Jude recalls that the Lord destroyed those who did not believe after saving a people out of Egypt, that angels who left their place are kept in chains until judgment, and that Sodom and Gomorrha suffer the vengeance of eternal fire.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name the three examples of judgment Jude gives?
ev: List the three examples in verses 5-7
Say what Sodom and Gomorrha are set forth as

nodes.t: The ungodly men described: Cain, Balaam, Core and Enoch's prophecy
nodes.d: Jude says these dreamers despise authority, have gone in the way of Cain, the error of Balaam and the rebellion of Core, are like waterless clouds and fruitless trees, and that Enoch prophesied the Lord comes to judge the ungodly.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the false men in Jude using the examples and pictures Jude gives?
ev: Say what Jude says about Michael in verse 9
Name the three figures in verse 11
Describe the pictures from nature in verses 12-13
Say what Enoch prophesied in verses 14-15

nodes.t: Keep yourselves in the love of God and the doxology
nodes.d: Jude reminds believers of the apostles' warning about mockers, tells them to build themselves up in faith, pray in the Holy Ghost, keep in God's love and show mercy to doubters, and ends praising him who is able to keep them from falling.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say how Jude tells believers to keep themselves and whom he praises?
ev: List Jude's commands in verses 20-23
Say who is able to keep them from falling

nodes.t: Revelation: overview
nodes.d: Revelation is the revelation of Jesus Christ given to John on Patmos: letters to seven churches, a vision of the throne in heaven, the Lamb, series of seals, trumpets and bowls, and the end in the new Jerusalem.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline the main parts of Revelation as the book itself presents them?
ev: Say who gave the revelation and to whom
Name the main parts: churches, throne, Lamb, judgments, new heaven and earth
Say what is promised to the one who reads and keeps it in 1:3

nodes.t: Prologue: the revelation of Jesus Christ
nodes.d: John introduces the revelation Jesus Christ gave, blesses those who read, hear and keep it, greets the seven churches from the God who is, was and is to come and from Jesus Christ, and announces that he cometh with clouds.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say how Revelation introduces itself and who Jesus is in these verses?
ev: Say who is the source of the revelation in 1:1
Name what Jesus is called in 1:5
Describe what 1:7 says about his coming

nodes.t: John's vision of Christ among the lampstands
nodes.d: John on Patmos hears a voice and sees one like the Son of man among seven golden candlesticks, with eyes like fire and a two-edged sword from his mouth, who says he is first and last, alive for evermore, holding the keys of death and hell.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the vision of Christ in Revelation 1 and what he says to John?
ev: Describe what John saw
Say what Christ says about himself in 1:17-18
Say what the seven stars and seven candlesticks are in 1:20

nodes.t: Letter to Ephesus: leaving the first love
nodes.d: Christ commends Ephesus for works, patience and testing false apostles, but says they have left their first love and must repent; to the one who overcomes he promises the tree of life.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Christ praises and corrects in the church at Ephesus?
ev: Say what Christ commends and what he has against Ephesus
State the promise to the one who overcomes

nodes.t: Letter to Smyrna: faithful unto death
nodes.d: Christ, who was dead and is alive, tells poor but rich Smyrna not to fear coming suffering, to be faithful unto death, and promises the crown of life and no hurt from the second death.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Christ promises to the faithful at Smyrna?
ev: Say what Christ says not to fear
State the promise in 2:10-11

nodes.t: Letter to Pergamos: holding fast, yet holding false teaching
nodes.d: Christ commends Pergamos for holding his name even where Satan dwells and where Antipas was killed, but rebukes them for holding the teaching of Balaam and of the Nicolaitanes, and calls them to repent.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Christ commends and rebukes at Pergamos?
ev: Say what Pergamos did well
Name the wrong teachings Christ names
State the promise in 2:17

nodes.t: Letter to Thyatira: Jezebel and holding fast
nodes.d: Christ commends Thyatira's love, service, faith and patience, rebukes them for tolerating Jezebel who teaches fornication and idol food, and tells the rest to hold fast until he comes, promising power over nations and the morning star.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Christ says about Jezebel and about those who did not follow her?
ev: Say what Christ commends in 2:19
Describe the charge in 2:20
State the promise in 2:26-28

nodes.t: Letter to Sardis: a name that thou livest, and art dead
nodes.d: Christ tells Sardis that they have a name for being alive but are dead, calls them to watch and repent, notes a few who have not defiled their garments, and promises white raiment and his confession of the name of the one who overcomes.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Christ says to the church at Sardis and what he promises to the few?
ev: Say what Christ says about Sardis' reputation
Describe the promise in 3:4-5

nodes.t: Letter to Philadelphia: the open door
nodes.d: Christ, holy and true, holding the key of David, tells Philadelphia he has set before them an open door, they kept his word, he will keep them from the hour of temptation, and the overcomer will be a pillar in his temple with the name of the new Jerusalem.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Christ commends and promises to the church at Philadelphia?
ev: Describe what Christ has set before Philadelphia
State the promise to the one who overcomes in 3:12

nodes.t: Letter to Laodicea: lukewarm, and Christ at the door
nodes.d: Christ rebukes Laodicea for being neither cold nor hot and for saying they are rich while they are wretched, counsels them to buy gold, white raiment and eyesalve from him, and says he stands at the door and knocks.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Christ says to Laodicea and the invitation in 3:20?
ev: Describe what Laodicea thinks of itself and what Christ says they are
Explain the picture in 3:20
State the promise to the overcomer in 3:21

nodes.t: The throne in heaven
nodes.d: John is called up through an open door and sees a throne with one sitting on it, a rainbow, twenty-four elders in white with crowns, four living creatures crying holy, holy, holy, and all worship God as Creator.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the throne room scene and what the worshippers say?
ev: Describe what surrounds the throne
Say what the four beasts and the elders say and do
Say why God is worthy according to 4:11

nodes.t: The sealed scroll and the Lamb
nodes.d: John weeps that no one can open the sealed scroll until the Lion of the tribe of Juda appears as a Lamb as though slain, takes the scroll, and heaven and every creature worship him as worthy because he redeemed people from every nation by his blood.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain who is worthy to open the scroll and why?
ev: Say why John wept and what was announced
Describe the Lamb and what he does
Say what the new song says about why he is worthy

nodes.t: The first six seals
nodes.d: The Lamb opens six seals: four horsemen, the souls under the altar crying how long, and a great earthquake with the sun black and the moon as blood, so that people hide from the wrath of the Lamb.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the six seals in order as John sees them?
ev: List the four horses and what each rider holds or does
Describe the cry of the souls under the altar and the answer they receive
Say how the people respond to the sixth seal

nodes.t: The sealed servants and the great multitude
nodes.d: Before the winds are released, 144,000 servants from the tribes of Israel are sealed, and John then sees a countless multitude from all nations in white robes before the throne and the Lamb, who came out of great tribulation.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the two groups in Revelation 7 and what the text says about the multitude?
ev: Describe the sealing in 7:1-8
Say who the great multitude is according to 7:13-14
State what God and the Lamb do for them in 7:15-17

nodes.t: The seventh seal and the first four trumpets
nodes.d: The seventh seal brings silence in heaven, seven angels receive trumpets, an angel offers incense with the prayers of the saints, and the first four trumpets strike a third of the earth, sea, rivers and lights, ending with a cry of woe.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the first four trumpets as they are given in chapter 8?
ev: Say what happens at the seventh seal
Describe what the first four trumpets strike
Say what the flying angel announces in 8:13

nodes.t: The fifth and sixth trumpets
nodes.d: At the fifth trumpet the bottomless pit is opened and locusts torment people who lack the seal of God, and at the sixth four angels at the Euphrates are loosed with a great army, yet the rest do not repent.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what happens at the fifth and sixth trumpets and how people respond?
ev: Describe the fifth trumpet and who is harmed
Say what the sixth trumpet looses
Say what the surviving people fail to do in 9:20-21

nodes.t: The mighty angel and the little book
nodes.d: A mighty angel stands on sea and land and swears by the Creator that there will be no more delay, and John is told to take and eat the little book, sweet in his mouth and bitter in his belly, and to prophesy again.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell what John is told and shown in Revelation 10?
ev: Describe the angel and what he swears
Say what John does with the little book
Say what John is told to do afterward

nodes.t: The temple measured and the two witnesses
nodes.d: John is told to measure the temple while the court is given to the Gentiles, and two witnesses prophesy in sackcloth, are killed by the beast from the pit, lie in the great city three and a half days, and are raised and called up to heaven.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell what the two witnesses do and what happens to them in Revelation 11?
ev: Describe what John is told to measure and not measure
Describe the two witnesses and what happens to them
Say how the survivors respond in 11:13

nodes.t: The seventh trumpet: the kingdoms become the Lord's
nodes.d: At the seventh trumpet loud voices in heaven say the kingdoms of this world have become those of the Lord and his Christ, the elders worship, and the temple in heaven opens to show the ark of his testament.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what is announced when the seventh angel sounds?
ev: Say what the voices announce in 11:15
Say what the elders thank God for in 11:17-18
Describe what is seen in the temple in 11:19

nodes.t: The woman, the dragon and the man child
nodes.d: John sees a woman clothed with the sun who bears a man child who is caught up to God, a great red dragon who tries to devour the child, war in heaven in which the dragon is cast down, and the dragon's pursuit of the woman and her seed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the main figures of Revelation 12 and what the text says each does?
ev: Describe the woman, the dragon and the child
Say who the dragon is named in 12:9
Say how the saints overcome him in 12:11
Describe what the dragon does after he is cast down

nodes.t: The beast from the sea and the beast from the earth
nodes.d: John sees a beast rise out of the sea receiving authority from the dragon and making war on the saints, and a second beast from the earth that makes people worship the first, speaks as a dragon, and imposes a mark and the number 666.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe both beasts in Revelation 13 and what they cause people to do?
ev: Describe the first beast and what it is given
Describe what the second beast does
Say whose names are not written in the book of life in 13:8

nodes.t: The Lamb on Zion, three angels and the harvest
nodes.d: John sees the Lamb on mount Sion with 144,000 redeemed, three angels announcing the everlasting gospel, Babylon's fall and a warning about the beast's mark, a blessing on the dead in the Lord, and the harvest and winepress of God's wrath.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list the sights and the three angels' messages in Revelation 14?
ev: Describe the 144,000 and their song
List the messages of the three angels
Describe the two images of harvest and winepress

nodes.t: The song of Moses and the Lamb; seven angels with bowls
nodes.d: John sees seven angels with the seven last plagues and those who conquered the beast singing the song of Moses and of the Lamb on a sea of glass, after which the angels receive golden bowls of God's wrath and the temple fills with smoke.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the scene before the seven bowls are poured out?
ev: Say who sings and what they sing about
Describe what the seven angels are given

nodes.t: The seven bowls of wrath
nodes.d: The seven angels pour out bowls on the earth, sea, rivers, sun, the beast's throne, Euphrates and air, with a call to watch, gathering at Armageddon, a great earthquake and Babylon remembered before God, while people curse God and do not repent.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list the seven bowls and how people respond?
ev: List what each of the seven bowls is poured on
Say what the angel of the waters says about God in 16:5-7
Say how people respond in 16:9, 11 and 21

nodes.t: The woman on the scarlet beast
nodes.d: An angel shows John the judgment of the great whore, Babylon the great, seated on a scarlet beast with seven heads and ten horns and drunk with the blood of the saints; the angel explains the mystery and says the Lamb will overcome the beast's allies.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what John sees in Revelation 17 and what the angel explains?
ev: Describe the woman and the beast
Say what the angel says the waters and the woman are in 17:15, 18
Say what 17:14 says about the Lamb

nodes.t: The fall of Babylon
nodes.d: An angel announces that Babylon the great has fallen, a voice calls God's people to come out of her, and kings, merchants and sailors mourn her sudden ruin while heaven is told to rejoice.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what happens to Babylon in Revelation 18 and who mourns?
ev: Say what the voice tells God's people in 18:4
Describe who mourns and why in 18:9-19
Say what heaven is told in 18:20

nodes.t: Hallelujah and the marriage supper of the Lamb
nodes.d: A great multitude in heaven praises God for judging the great whore, announces that the Lord God omnipotent reigns and that the marriage of the Lamb has come, and John is told that those called to the marriage supper are blessed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what is celebrated in heaven in Revelation 19:1-10?
ev: Say why the multitude rejoices in 19:1-2
Describe the bride and her clothing in 19:7-8
Say what the angel tells John when he falls to worship

nodes.t: The rider on the white horse and the defeat of the beast
nodes.d: Heaven opens and one called Faithful and True, The Word of God and King of kings, rides a white horse with a sharp sword from his mouth, and the beast and the false prophet are taken and cast into the lake of fire.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the rider on the white horse and what happens to the beast?
ev: Describe the rider and the names written on him
Say what happens to the beast and the false prophet

nodes.t: The binding of Satan and the thousand years
nodes.d: An angel binds the dragon, that old serpent, for a thousand years; John sees thrones and those who lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years, called the first resurrection, and the text says the rest of the dead lived not again until the thousand years ended.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Revelation 20:1-6 describes without adding more than the text says?
ev: Describe what happens to Satan in 20:1-3
Say what John sees about those on the thrones in 20:4-6
Say what is called the first resurrection

nodes.t: Satan loosed, the great white throne and the lake of fire
nodes.d: After the thousand years Satan is loosed and gathers Gog and Magog, fire from God devours them, the devil is cast into the lake of fire, and the dead are judged before a great white throne by their works, with death and hell cast into the lake of fire and those not in the book of life.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the great white throne judgment as Revelation 20:11-15 shows it?
ev: Describe what Satan does when loosed and what happens to him
Say what is judged and by what in 20:12-13
Say what is cast into the lake of fire in 20:14-15

nodes.t: A new heaven and a new earth
nodes.d: John sees a new heaven and new earth and the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God as a bride; God dwells with his people, wipes away every tear, and says he makes all things new, while the unbelieving have their part in the lake of fire.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what God promises in Revelation 21:1-8?
ev: Say what the voice says about God dwelling with men
List what is gone in 21:4
Say what God says in 21:5-7

nodes.t: The holy city, new Jerusalem
nodes.d: An angel shows John the bride, the Lamb's wife, as a city with the glory of God, twelve gates named for the tribes of Israel and twelve foundations named for the apostles, no temple because God and the Lamb are its temple, and only those written in the Lamb's book of life entering.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the city John sees and what is said about its light and temple?
ev: Describe the walls, gates and foundations
Say why there is no temple and no need of sun
Say who enters according to 21:27

nodes.t: The river of life and the tree of life
nodes.d: John sees the river of the water of life from the throne of God and of the Lamb, with the tree of life on either side bearing twelve fruits and healing the nations, no more curse, and the servants seeing God's face and reigning for ever.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Revelation 22:1-5 says is in the city?
ev: Describe the river and the tree
Say what 22:3 says about the curse
Say what God's servants do according to 22:3-5

nodes.t: Epilogue: I come quickly, the invitation and the warning
nodes.d: The angel and Jesus confirm the words are faithful and true, Jesus says he comes quickly with his reward and is the Alpha and Omega and the bright and morning star, the Spirit and the bride say Come and invite the thirsty, a warning is given about adding to or taking from the book, and the book ends with the grace of the Lord Jesus.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say how Revelation ends and what invitation it gives?
ev: Say what Jesus says about himself in 22:12-16
Quote the invitation of 22:17 in your own words
Say what the warning in 22:18-19 is about

nodes.t: Faith, love and hope in Thessalonica
nodes.d: Paul thanks God for the Thessalonians' work of faith, labour of love and patience of hope, and recalls how they received the gospel and turned from idols to serve the living God and wait for his Son.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what it means that the Thessalonians turned from idols to serve the living God and wait for his Son (1:9-10)?
ev: Name the three things Paul remembers in 1:3
Describe how 1:9-10 sums up their conversion

nodes.t: Paul's ministry among them
nodes.d: Paul reminds them how he and his companions brought the gospel despite suffering at Philippi, working night and day, and treating them like a nurse and a father; the Thessalonians received it as the word of God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Paul says he behaved among the Thessalonians and how they received the word (2:13)?
ev: Say why Paul did not flatter or seek glory (2:4-6)
Point out the nurse and father pictures (2:7, 2:11)

nodes.t: Longing to see them, and Timothy's report
nodes.d: Hindered from returning, Paul sent Timothy from Athens to strengthen them, and Timothy's good news of their faith and love comforted Paul and led to his prayer for their love and holiness at Christ's coming.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul sent Timothy and what news he brought back (3:5-6)?
ev: Tell why Paul sent Timothy (3:2, 3:5)
Summarise the prayer in 3:11-13

nodes.t: Sanctification and brotherly love
nodes.d: God's will is their sanctification: sexual purity, not wronging a brother, brotherly love, quiet living and honest work.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul means by saying God has called us unto holiness, not uncleanness (4:7)?
ev: State what 4:3 says is the will of God
List the practical commands of 4:11-12

nodes.t: Those who sleep in Jesus and the Lord's coming
nodes.d: Paul comforts the Thessalonians about believers who have died: God will bring them with Jesus, the dead in Christ rise first, and all believers will be with the Lord for ever.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Paul says will happen to believers who have died when the Lord comes (4:16)?
ev: Explain why believers need not sorrow as those without hope (4:13-14)
Order the events of 4:16-17

nodes.t: The day of the Lord and living as children of the day
nodes.d: The day of the Lord comes as a thief in the night on those who say peace and safety, but believers, children of light, are to be watchful and sober, since God appointed them to salvation.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul says believers are not in darkness that the day should overtake them as a thief (5:4-5)?
ev: Contrast night and day in 5:4-8
Name the armour in 5:8

nodes.t: Closing exhortations and prayer
nodes.d: Paul urges respect for leaders, care for the unruly and weak, joy, prayer and thanksgiving, testing everything, and prays that God sanctify them wholly and keep them blameless until Christ's coming.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name three of the short commands in 5:16-22 and say why they matter?
ev: Recite 5:16-18
Describe how they are to treat the unruly, the feebleminded and the weak (5:14)

nodes.t: 1 Thessalonians: overview
nodes.d: Paul's first letter to the Thessalonian church, from thanksgiving for their faith (ch. 1) through his ministry and concern for them (2-3), to holy living, the Lord's coming and closing exhortations (4-5).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what 1 Thessalonians is about?
ev: Describe the movement: thanksgiving (1), ministry and Timothy (2-3), holy living and the Lord's coming (4-5)

nodes.t: Persecution, God's righteous judgment and Christ revealed
nodes.d: Paul thanks God for their growing faith under persecution and says God will repay those who trouble them and give rest to believers when the Lord Jesus is revealed from heaven.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul says will happen when the Lord Jesus is revealed from heaven (1:7-10)?
ev: State what 1:6-7 says God will do for the troubled and for those who trouble them
Describe how Christ is revealed in 1:7-10

nodes.t: The day of Christ and the man of sin
nodes.d: Paul tells them not to be shaken as if the day of Christ had come, because a falling away and the revealing of the man of sin come first, whom the Lord will destroy at his coming.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul says the Thessalonians should not be troubled that the day of Christ is at hand (2:1-3)?
ev: Say what must come before that day (2:3)
State what happens to the Wicked when the Lord comes (2:8)

nodes.t: Chosen to salvation: stand fast
nodes.d: Paul gives thanks that God chose them from the beginning to salvation through sanctification and belief of the truth, and tells them to hold the teachings they received and prays for their comfort.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul says God has done for the Thessalonians in 2:13-14?
ev: Name the means of salvation in 2:13
Tell what Paul tells them to hold in 2:15

nodes.t: Pray for us; the Lord is faithful
nodes.d: Paul asks prayer that the word of the Lord run freely and that they be delivered from wicked men, and affirms that the Lord is faithful to establish and keep them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Paul asks the Thessalonians to pray for, and who he says is faithful (3:1-3)?
ev: State the two requests of 3:1-2
Find who is faithful in 3:3

nodes.t: Work, and dealing with the disorderly
nodes.d: Paul commands them to withdraw from brothers who live disorderly and will not work, pointing to his own example of labour, and says to admonish such a person as a brother, not treat him as an enemy.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what example Paul set about work and what he told them to do about those who would not work (3:7-12)?
ev: Quote or paraphrase 3:10 and say who it addresses
Explain how the disorderly are to be treated (3:14-15)

nodes.t: 2 Thessalonians: overview
nodes.d: Paul's second letter to the Thessalonians on persecution and God's judgment (ch. 1), the day of Christ and the man of sin (ch. 2), and prayer, work and discipline (ch. 3).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what 2 Thessalonians is about?
ev: Describe the three movements: judgment and relief (1), the day of Christ (2), prayer and work (3)

nodes.t: Timothy charged at Ephesus: sound teaching and the law
nodes.d: Paul left Timothy at Ephesus to charge some not to teach other doctrine or follow fables and endless genealogies; the aim of the commandment is love, and the law is good when used lawfully.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul left Timothy at Ephesus (1:3-5)?
ev: State the aim of the charge (1:5)
Explain how 1:8-11 says the law is used lawfully

nodes.t: Christ came to save sinners
nodes.d: Paul thanks Christ for putting him into the ministry though he was a blasphemer and persecutor; Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, and Paul charges Timothy to hold faith and a good conscience.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul says about himself and about why Christ Jesus came into the world (1:13-16)?
ev: Recite or paraphrase 1:15
Say what Paul says his case shows about Christ (1:16)

nodes.t: Prayer for all, one God, one mediator
nodes.d: Prayer is to be made for all men, including kings; God our Saviour wills all to be saved, and there is one God and one mediator, the man Christ Jesus, who gave himself a ransom for all.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what 2:5-6 teaches about Jesus as mediator?
ev: List the kinds of prayer in 2:1
State who the one mediator is (2:5)

nodes.t: Conduct in the church: men, women and teaching
nodes.d: Paul gives instruction on men praying and on women's modesty and good works, and says he does not permit a woman to teach or have authority over a man, grounding this in the order of Adam and Eve's creation and the deception.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what reasons Paul gives from Genesis in 2:13-14 for his instruction in 2:12?
ev: Describe what the text says about men praying and women adorning themselves (2:8-10)
State the reasons Paul gives in 2:13-14

nodes.t: Qualifications for overseers and deacons
nodes.d: Paul lists the character required of a bishop (overseer) and of deacons and their wives, including a well-ordered household, a good report and tested blamelessness.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list some qualities of an overseer in 3:2-7 and say why household management matters (3:5)?
ev: Name several qualifications in 3:2-7
Say how deacons are to be proved (3:10)

nodes.t: The church and the mystery of godliness
nodes.d: Paul writes so Timothy may know how to behave in the house of God, the church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth, and states the mystery of godliness: God manifest in the flesh, received up into glory.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name what Paul says about Christ in 1 Timothy 3:16?
ev: Say how 3:15 describes the church
List the six statements about Christ in 3:16

nodes.t: Departing from the faith: good creation received with thanks
nodes.d: The Spirit says some will depart from the faith, forbidding marriage and certain foods; Paul says every creature of God is good and sanctified by the word of God and prayer.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul says nothing is to be refused if received with thanksgiving (4:4-5)?
ev: State what the false teachers forbid (4:3)
Explain why 4:4-5 says food is not to be refused

nodes.t: A good minister of Jesus Christ
nodes.d: Timothy is to refuse profane fables, train himself in godliness, set an example in word, conduct, love, faith and purity, devote himself to reading, exhortation and doctrine, and not neglect his gift.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul tells Timothy to do so that no one despises his youth (4:12-16)?
ev: Recite or paraphrase 4:12
List the three things in 4:13

nodes.t: Honouring widows and caring for family
nodes.d: Timothy is to treat people of every age with respect, honour widows who are truly widows, expect families to care for their own, and set guidelines for enrolling widows and for younger widows.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain who is to care for widows according to 5:4 and 5:16?
ev: State what 5:8 says about providing for one's own
Describe the tasks of a widow indeed (5:5, 5:10)

nodes.t: Elders: honour, accusation and impartiality
nodes.d: Elders who rule well are worthy of double honour; an accusation against an elder needs two or three witnesses; Timothy is to rebuke sin openly, act without partiality, and not lay hands hastily.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Paul says an accusation against an elder should be handled (5:19-21)?
ev: Say how 5:18 supports honouring elders
State the rule about accusations in 5:19

nodes.t: Servants, false gain, and godliness with contentment
nodes.d: Servants are to honour their masters; those who teach otherwise and suppose gain is godliness are to be avoided; godliness with contentment is great gain, and the love of money is a root of all evil.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul says about godliness with contentment and the love of money (6:6-10)?
ev: Recite 6:6-8
Explain what 6:10 says about the love of money

nodes.t: Fight the good fight; charge to the rich
nodes.d: Timothy, a man of God, is to flee these things, pursue righteousness and godliness, fight the good fight of faith and keep the commandment until Christ's appearing; the rich are to trust the living God and do good.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul charges Timothy to do in 6:11-14?
ev: List what Timothy flees and follows (6:11)
State what the rich are told in 6:17-19

nodes.t: 1 Timothy: overview
nodes.d: Paul's letter to Timothy at Ephesus about sound doctrine, prayer, order in the church, qualified leaders, and a minister's conduct and charge.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what 1 Timothy is about (see 3:14-15)?
ev: Describe how 3:15 states the letter's purpose
Name the main sections: false teaching, prayer and conduct, leaders, Timothy's ministry, groups in the church, closing charge

nodes.t: Stir up the gift; do not be ashamed of the gospel
nodes.d: Paul remembers Timothy's sincere faith and tells him to stir up God's gift, not be ashamed of the testimony, and share in the afflictions of the gospel, since God saved and called us by his own purpose and grace and Christ brought life and immortality to light.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul tells Timothy to do in 1:6-8 and why (1:9-10)?
ev: Say whose faith dwelt in Timothy first (1:5)
Explain how 1:9-10 describes salvation

nodes.t: Those who turned away and Onesiphorus who refreshed Paul
nodes.d: Paul notes that all in Asia have turned away from him, including Phygellus and Hermogenes, while Onesiphorus often refreshed him and sought him out in Rome.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Onesiphorus did for Paul and why Paul prays for him (1:16-18)?
ev: Contrast the two groups in 1:15-16
Tell what Onesiphorus did in Rome (1:17)

nodes.t: Strong in grace: soldier, athlete, farmer
nodes.d: Timothy is to pass on what he heard to faithful men, endure hardness as a good soldier, strive lawfully like an athlete and labour like a farmer; Paul endures for the elect, and the faithful saying says if we die with him we shall live with him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the soldier, athlete and farmer pictures in 2:3-6 and what they teach?
ev: Name the three pictures in 2:3-6
Recite the faithful saying of 2:11-13

nodes.t: A workman approved by God
nodes.d: Timothy is to avoid wrangling about words and profane babblings, rightly handle the word of truth, and flee youthful lusts; the Lord's servant must be gentle and patient, instructing opponents in hope that God grants repentance.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what it means to be a workman who rightly divides the word of truth (2:15)?
ev: State the goal of 2:15
Describe how the Lord's servant treats opponents (2:24-26)

nodes.t: Perilous times in the last days
nodes.d: Paul describes men in the last days with a form of godliness but denying its power, compares them to Jannes and Jambres who withstood Moses, and says they will not progress further.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Paul says about people in the last days and what Timothy should do about them (3:1-5)?
ev: List several marks of the men in 3:2-4
Say who Jannes and Jambres are compared to (3:8)

nodes.t: Continue in Scripture, inspired by God
nodes.d: Timothy is to continue in what he learned, having known the holy scriptures from childhood; all scripture is given by inspiration of God and is profitable for teaching, reproof, correction and training in righteousness, so the man of God is thoroughly furnished.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what 3:16-17 says about Scripture and what it is for?
ev: Say what the scriptures are able to do (3:15)
List the four uses in 3:16

nodes.t: Preach the word: Paul's charge and finished course
nodes.d: Paul charges Timothy before God and Christ to preach the word in season and out, warns of those who will not endure sound doctrine, and says he is ready to be offered, having fought the good fight and awaiting a crown of righteousness.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul charges Timothy to do and what Paul says awaits him (4:2, 4:7-8)?
ev: Recite 4:2
Describe what Paul says of his own course in 4:6-8

nodes.t: Paul's last requests and greetings
nodes.d: Paul asks Timothy to come, names companions who left or remain, recounts that none stood with him at his first answer but the Lord stood with him, and sends greetings.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say who stood with Paul at his first defence and what he asks Timothy to bring (4:11-17)?
ev: Say who is with Paul in 4:11
Tell who stood with Paul at his first answer (4:16-17)

nodes.t: 2 Timothy: overview
nodes.d: Paul's last letter in this collection, written as a prisoner to Timothy, urging faithfulness, endurance, trust in Scripture and preaching the word until the end.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what 2 Timothy is about?
ev: Describe the four chapters: not ashamed (1), endure and handle the word (2), Scripture in the last days (3), the charge and Paul's last words (4)

nodes.t: Elders in every city of Crete
nodes.d: Paul greets Titus, mentions the hope of eternal life promised before the world began, and tells him he left him in Crete to appoint elders who are blameless and hold fast the faithful word.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul left Titus in Crete and what kind of men were to be elders (1:5-9)?
ev: State why Paul left Titus in Crete (1:5)
List some qualities of an elder in 1:6-9

nodes.t: Rebuking the unruly teachers
nodes.d: Many unruly talkers, especially of the circumcision, subvert households for gain; Titus is to rebuke them sharply, since they profess to know God but deny him by their works.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul says about those who profess to know God but deny him by works (1:16)?
ev: Say what these teachers do (1:11)
Explain 1:16

nodes.t: Sound doctrine in every household
nodes.d: Titus is to teach what fits sound doctrine to older men and women, younger women and men, and servants, and to be a pattern of good works himself.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Paul wants the different groups to live and why (2:5, 2:8, 2:10)?
ev: Name the groups in 2:2-10
State why Titus must be an example (2:7-8)

nodes.t: The grace of God has appeared
nodes.d: The grace of God that brings salvation has appeared to all men, teaching us to deny ungodliness and live soberly while looking for the glorious appearing of our great God and Saviour Jesus Christ, who gave himself to redeem and purify a people for himself.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Titus 2:11-14 says grace teaches us and what Christ did for us?
ev: Say what grace teaches in 2:12
State what Christ gave himself to do in 2:14

nodes.t: Saved by mercy, not by works
nodes.d: Believers once lived in folly and malice, but God our Saviour saved them according to his mercy, not works, through the washing of regeneration and renewing of the Holy Ghost, that they might be justified by grace and be heirs; they are to be careful to maintain good works.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Titus 3:4-7 says about how God saved us?
ev: Say what 3:5 says saved us and what it says did not
Describe how believers are to treat others (3:1-2)

nodes.t: Avoiding division, and final instructions
nodes.d: Titus is to avoid foolish questions and genealogies, reject a divisive man after two admonitions, and Paul closes with travel instructions, names of helpers and greetings.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Paul says to avoid and what to do after admonishing a divisive person twice (3:9-10)?
ev: State what to do with a divisive man (3:10)
Name people mentioned in 3:12-13

nodes.t: Titus: overview
nodes.d: Paul's letter to Titus in Crete about appointing elders, opposing unruly teachers, sound doctrine in daily life, and salvation by grace that leads to good works.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what Titus is about?
ev: Describe the three chapters: order and elders (1), sound doctrine and grace (2), mercy and good works (3)

nodes.t: Greeting and thanks for Philemon's love
nodes.d: Paul and Timothy greet Philemon, Apphia, Archippus and the church in his house, and Paul thanks God for Philemon's love and faith toward the Lord Jesus and all saints.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Paul thanks God for about Philemon (1:4-7)?
ev: Name the people greeted in 1:1-2
Say what Paul has heard of Philemon (1:5)

nodes.t: Paul appeals for Onesimus
nodes.d: Paul, an aged prisoner, urges Philemon out of love to receive Onesimus, whom he begot in his bonds, no longer as a servant but as a beloved brother.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul asks Philemon to do about Onesimus and why he asks by love rather than command (1:8-16)?
ev: State how Paul describes Onesimus in 1:10-11
Say how Paul wants Philemon to receive him (1:16)

nodes.t: Receive him as myself
nodes.d: Paul asks Philemon to receive Onesimus as he would receive Paul, offers to repay anything Onesimus owes, expresses confidence in Philemon, and sends greetings from his companions.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul offers to do if Onesimus has wronged Philemon (1:17-19)?
ev: Say what Paul offers in 1:18-19
Name the fellow workers who send greetings (1:23-24)

nodes.t: Philemon: overview
nodes.d: Paul's short personal letter to Philemon, appealing on behalf of Onesimus.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what Philemon is about?
ev: Summarise the letter's one request in 1:10-17

nodes.t: God has spoken by his Son
nodes.d: God who spoke by the prophets has in these last days spoken by his Son, heir of all things, maker of the worlds, radiance of his glory, who purged sins and sat at God's right hand, better than the angels.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Hebrews 1:1-4 says about how God has spoken and who the Son is?
ev: List what 1:2-3 says about the Son
Say how 1:4-14 compares him with angels

nodes.t: Do not neglect so great salvation
nodes.d: Because the word spoken through angels was steadfast, the readers must give heed to the salvation first spoken by the Lord and confirmed by those who heard him, with God bearing witness by signs and wonders.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the warning of 2:1-3 and why it is serious?
ev: State the question of 2:3
Say how the message was confirmed (2:3-4)

nodes.t: Jesus made like his brothers
nodes.d: Jesus, made a little lower than the angels, tasted death for everyone, shared flesh and blood to destroy the devil and free those enslaved by fear of death, and became a merciful and faithful high priest able to help the tempted.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Jesus became like his brothers according to Hebrews 2:14-18?
ev: Say why he shared flesh and blood (2:14-15)
State what kind of high priest he is (2:17)

nodes.t: Christ greater than Moses
nodes.d: Moses was faithful as a servant in God's house, but Christ is faithful as a Son over his own house, and believers are that house if they hold fast.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how the text says Christ is greater than Moses (3:3-6)?
ev: Compare servant and son in 3:5-6
Say what condition 3:6 states

nodes.t: Do not harden your hearts as in the wilderness
nodes.d: Quoting the warning that God swore the generation that provoked him in the wilderness would not enter his rest, the writer urges them to beware an evil heart of unbelief and to exhort one another daily.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what happened to those who came out of Egypt and what warning the writer draws (3:16-19)?
ev: Say why that generation could not enter (3:19)
Describe what 3:12-13 tells the readers to do

nodes.t: A rest remains for the people of God
nodes.d: The promise of entering God's rest still stands: the gospel preached to them did not profit those without faith, God rested on the seventh day, and a Sabbath rest remains for God's people, so they must labour to enter it.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the rest is that remains for God's people, and what warning goes with it (4:9-11)?
ev: Cite the creation rest mentioned in 4:4
State what remains for the people of God (4:9)
Say what the word of God does in 4:12

nodes.t: A great high priest who sympathises
nodes.d: We have a great high priest, Jesus the Son of God, who passed into the heavens and was tempted in all points like us yet without sin, so we may come boldly to the throne of grace.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why we may come boldly to the throne of grace (4:14-16)?
ev: Say how Jesus is like and unlike us (4:15)
State where we may come (4:16)

nodes.t: Called as high priest after Melchizedek's order
nodes.d: Every high priest is taken from men to offer gifts and sacrifices and is called of God as Aaron was; Christ was so called, learned obedience through suffering, and became the source of eternal salvation, a priest after the order of Melchizedek.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how the text says Christ was called to be high priest (5:4-10)?
ev: List what a high priest does (5:1-3)
Say how Christ became a high priest (5:5-6, 5:10)

nodes.t: From milk to solid food: a warning and encouragement
nodes.d: The writer says the readers are dull of hearing and need milk, urges them to go on to maturity, warns about falling away after being enlightened, and is persuaded of better things, praising their work of love and urging diligence and patience.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the writer asks the readers to do in 6:1 and why (5:11-14)?
ev: Contrast milk and strong meat (5:12-14)
Describe the two earth pictures of 6:7-8
Say what the writer is persuaded of (6:9-10)

nodes.t: God's oath to Abraham: an anchor of the soul
nodes.d: God promised Abraham and confirmed it by an oath, swearing by himself; by two unchangeable things the heirs of promise have strong comfort, a hope like an anchor that enters within the veil where Jesus has gone as forerunner, a high priest after Melchizedek's order.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the text says about God's promise and oath to Abraham, and why it gives us hope (6:13-19)?
ev: State why God swore by himself (6:13)
Describe the anchor picture of 6:19-20

nodes.t: Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest
nodes.d: Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of the most high God, met Abraham, blessed him and received tithes; this shows he is greater than Abraham and the Levites, and is made like the Son of God, abiding a priest continually.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Hebrews 7:1-10 says about Melchizedek and why he is called greater than Abraham?
ev: Retell how 7:1-2 summarises Genesis 14
Explain the argument that the lesser is blessed by the greater (7:7)

nodes.t: Another priest, a change of law, an unchangeable priesthood
nodes.d: Because perfection did not come through the Levitical priesthood, another priest arose from Judah after the order of Melchizedek, by an oath and the power of an endless life; Jesus is surety of a better testament and lives to save to the uttermost and intercede.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the writer says the priesthood had to change and what Jesus' priesthood is like (7:11-25)?
ev: State why another priest was needed (7:11)
Explain how Jesus differs from the many priests (7:23-27)

nodes.t: A better covenant: the new covenant promised
nodes.d: Jesus ministers in the true tabernacle as mediator of a better covenant on better promises; the writer cites the promise of a new covenant, in which God will write his laws on hearts, be their God, and remember their sins no more, making the first old.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what the writer says God promised in the new covenant (8:8-12)?
ev: State what is better about the covenant (8:6)
List the promises of 8:10-12
Say what 8:13 says about the first covenant

nodes.t: The first covenant's tabernacle and ordinances
nodes.d: The first covenant had a worldly sanctuary with a first tent and Most Holy Place containing the ark, and only the high priest entered once a year with blood; the writer says the Holy Spirit signified this could not perfect the conscience until a time of reformation.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the tabernacle arrangements and what they could not do (9:1-10)?
ev: Name items in the Holiest of all (9:3-4)
Say what the Holy Spirit showed by the arrangement (9:8)

nodes.t: Christ's own blood and the mediator of the new testament
nodes.d: Christ entered the heavenly sanctuary once by his own blood, obtained eternal redemption, and is the mediator of the new testament; the first was dedicated with blood, without shedding of blood there is no remission, and he will appear a second time without sin for salvation.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the writer says Christ's blood does what the blood of bulls and goats could not (9:12-14)?
ev: Contrast animal blood and Christ's blood (9:12-14)
State what 9:22 says about blood and remission
Describe the two appearings in 9:26-28

nodes.t: One sacrifice for sins for ever
nodes.d: The law's repeated sacrifices could not take away sins, but Christ came to do God's will and by one offering of his body perfected for ever those who are sanctified; the writer again cites the covenant promise that sins will be remembered no more.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Christ's single offering is enough according to Hebrews 10:10-18?
ev: Say why the old sacrifices were repeated (10:1-4)
State what Christ did and where he sat down (10:10-14)

nodes.t: Draw near with full assurance
nodes.d: Because of boldness to enter the holiest by the blood of Jesus, through the veil of his flesh, and with a great priest over God's house, believers are to draw near with a true heart, hold fast their hope, provoke one another to love and good works, and not stop meeting together.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the writer says believers should do because of Jesus' blood and high priesthood (10:19-25)?
ev: List the three "let us" calls in 10:22-24
Say what 10:25 warns against

nodes.t: Warning against wilful sin; endure and live by faith
nodes.d: The writer warns that no sacrifice remains for wilful sin after receiving the truth, reminds readers of their earlier endurance, and urges patience, since the just shall live by faith and they are not of those who draw back.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the writer asks the readers to remember and do in 10:32-39?
ev: Describe the warning of 10:26-29
State what the just shall do (10:38)
Tell what the readers endured before (10:32-34)

nodes.t: What faith is: Abel, Enoch and Noah
nodes.d: Faith is the substance of things hoped for and evidence of things unseen; by faith Abel offered a better sacrifice, Enoch was translated, and Noah built the ark; without faith it is impossible to please God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what faith is (11:1) and give the example of Noah (11:7)?
ev: Recite or paraphrase 11:1
Say what 11:6 requires of one who comes to God
Name what each of Abel, Enoch and Noah did by faith

nodes.t: By faith Abraham, Sarah and the patriarchs
nodes.d: By faith Abraham went out not knowing where, sojourned as a stranger seeking a city built by God, Sara received strength to bear a child, Abraham offered Isaac, and Isaac, Jacob and Joseph acted in faith about things to come.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Abraham did by faith and what the patriarchs were looking for (11:8-16)?
ev: Say what Abraham did by faith in 11:8-10 and 11:17-19
Name what Isaac, Jacob and Joseph did in 11:20-22
State what 11:13-16 says these people sought

nodes.t: By faith Moses, Israel and Rahab
nodes.d: By faith Moses' parents hid him, Moses chose affliction with God's people over Egypt's pleasures, kept the Passover, Israel crossed the Red Sea and the walls of Jericho fell, and Rahab was not destroyed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Moses chose by faith and why (11:24-27)?
ev: List what Moses did by faith (11:24-28)
Name the two events of 11:29-30

nodes.t: The rest of the cloud: triumph and suffering by faith
nodes.d: The writer lists Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel and the prophets, and describes those who conquered and those who suffered, none of whom received the promise without us.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the writer says about those who by faith suffered and had not yet received the promise (11:35-40)?
ev: Name some people in 11:32
Contrast the two kinds of experience in 11:33-38

nodes.t: Looking to Jesus, the author and finisher of faith
nodes.d: Surrounded by a cloud of witnesses, believers lay aside every weight and sin and run with patience, looking to Jesus, who endured the cross for the joy set before him and sat down at God's right hand.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what 12:1-2 tells believers to do and why they should look to Jesus?
ev: State what we lay aside and what we run (12:1)
Say what Jesus endured and where he is (12:2)

nodes.t: The Lord's discipline of his sons
nodes.d: The writer reminds readers that the Lord chastens those he loves as a father disciplines sons, for their profit and holiness, and that discipline afterwards yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the writer says God's discipline is a sign of sonship (12:5-11)?
ev: State why God chastens (12:6, 12:10)
Describe the result in 12:11

nodes.t: Pursue peace and holiness; the example of Esau
nodes.d: The readers are to follow peace and holiness, watch against a root of bitterness, and not be like Esau, who sold his birthright for one meal and later found no place of repentance though he sought the blessing with tears.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the writer says about Esau as a warning (12:15-17)?
ev: Say what we are to follow (12:14)
Tell what Esau did and what happened afterward (12:16-17)

nodes.t: Not Mount Sinai but Mount Zion
nodes.d: Believers have not come to the fearful mountain of Sinai but to mount Zion, the heavenly Jerusalem, to God, to Jesus the mediator of the new covenant and to the blood of sprinkling; they must not refuse the one who speaks, and receive a kingdom that cannot be shaken.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Hebrews 12:18-24 contrasts Sinai with Zion and names Jesus there?
ev: Contrast the two mountains (12:18-24)
State what is said of the kingdom and of God (12:28-29)

nodes.t: Brotherly love, marriage and contentment
nodes.d: The writer calls for brotherly love and hospitality to strangers, remembering prisoners, honour in marriage, and a life free from covetousness because God has said he will never leave or forsake.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name some practical commands in 13:1-5 and the promise that supports them?
ev: List the commands of 13:1-5
Say what promise supports contentment (13:5)

nodes.t: Leaders, Jesus outside the camp, and sacrifices of praise
nodes.d: Readers are to remember their leaders, avoid strange doctrines, go out to Jesus outside the camp bearing his reproach, seeking the city to come, and offer sacrifices of praise and doing good.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what it means to go to Jesus outside the camp and what sacrifices God is pleased with (13:12-16)?
ev: Recite 13:8
Say where Jesus suffered and what believers are to do (13:12-13)
List the sacrifices of 13:15-16

nodes.t: Obey leaders; blessing and farewell
nodes.d: The writer asks them to obey their leaders and pray for him, prays that the God of peace who raised Jesus through the blood of the everlasting covenant would equip them, and closes with news of Timothy and greetings.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the prayer of 13:20-21 and what it says about Jesus?
ev: Say what the benediction asks of God (13:20-21)
Note the greeting from those of Italy (13:24)

nodes.t: Hebrews: overview
nodes.d: The letter to the Hebrews presents Jesus as God's Son, greater than angels and Moses, our great high priest after Melchizedek who mediates a better covenant by one sacrifice, and calls readers to faith and endurance.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what Hebrews teaches about Jesus and what the readers are told to do?
ev: Describe the main parts: the Son (1-2), Moses and rest (3-4), the high priest (4-7), the new covenant and sacrifice (8-10), faith (11), endurance and exhortations (12-13)

nodes.t: 1 Corinthians: overview
nodes.d: Paul writes to the church at Corinth about divisions, sin in the church, questions they asked him, worship, the resurrection and the collection (1:1-16:24).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} give a short outline of 1 Corinthians and name three problems Paul corrects in the Corinthian church?
ev: Name the main problems Paul addresses: divisions, immorality, lawsuits, marriage, food offered to idols, the Lord's supper, gifts, the resurrection
Say who the letter is addressed to from 1:2

nodes.t: Greeting and the call to unity
nodes.d: Paul thanks God for the grace given to the Corinthians, then appeals to them to end their divisions over which leader they follow.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why following one teacher against another is wrong, using 1 Corinthians 1:10-13?
ev: Quote the slogans the Corinthians were using (1:12)
Explain why Paul says Christ is not divided (1:13)

nodes.t: The cross: God's wisdom and power
nodes.d: Paul says the preaching of the cross looks foolish to those perishing but is the power of God to those being saved, and that God chose the weak and low so that no one may boast.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul says the cross is God's wisdom and power, using 1 Corinthians 1:18-31?
ev: Contrast how the cross is seen by those perishing and by those saved (1:18)
List who God chose according to 1:26-29 and why (1:29)
Name what Christ is made to us (1:30)

nodes.t: The Spirit reveals God's hidden wisdom
nodes.d: Paul preached Christ crucified in weakness, and says the wisdom of God, hidden from this world's rulers, is revealed by the Spirit and understood only spiritually.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain, using 1 Corinthians 2, how a person comes to understand the things of God?
ev: State what Paul determined to know among the Corinthians (2:2)
Explain who knows the things of God and how we receive them (2:10-12)
Contrast the natural man and the spiritual person (2:14-15)

nodes.t: Servants, builders and God's temple
nodes.d: Paul tells the divided Corinthians that he and Apollos are only servants, that God gives the increase, that Jesus Christ is the one foundation, and that the church is God's temple.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain who gives growth in the church and what the foundation is, using 1 Corinthians 3?
ev: Explain the picture of planting and watering (3:6-7)
Say what the one foundation is (3:11)
Explain what happens to each builder's work (3:12-15)
Say why the church is called God's temple (3:16-17)

nodes.t: Faithful stewards and the apostles as fathers
nodes.d: Paul says ministers are stewards who must be found faithful, whom the Lord will judge; he contrasts the Corinthians' pride with the apostles' sufferings and warns that he will come.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul says it is a small thing to be judged by men, using 1 Corinthians 4:1-7?
ev: Say what is required of stewards (4:2)
Explain who is to judge and when (4:4-5)
Answer Paul's question in 4:7 about what we have that we did not receive

nodes.t: Dealing with sin in the church
nodes.d: Paul rebukes the church for tolerating a case of sexual immorality, tells them to put the person out, and explains that they must judge those inside the church while God judges those outside.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul tells the Corinthians to put away the wicked person, using 1 Corinthians 5?
ev: Describe the sin reported in 5:1 and the church's attitude (5:2)
Explain the picture of leaven (5:6-8)
Explain the difference between those within and those without (5:9-13)

nodes.t: Lawsuits among believers
nodes.d: Paul asks why Christians take each other to law before unbelievers, reminds them that the saints will judge the world, and warns that the unrighteous will not inherit the kingdom.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain 1 Corinthians 6:11 and why it matters for how believers treat each other?
ev: Say where Paul wants disputes settled and why (6:1-5)
List the kinds of people who will not inherit the kingdom (6:9-10)
Quote the three things Paul says happened to the Corinthians in 6:11

nodes.t: Your body is the Lord's temple
nodes.d: Paul teaches that the body is for the Lord, not for sexual immorality, that believers are members of Christ and the Spirit's temple, and that they were bought with a price.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul says our bodies belong to God, using 1 Corinthians 6:19-20?
ev: Explain why the body is not for fornication (6:13-15)
Say what Paul tells them to do about fornication (6:18)
Explain what it means that believers are bought with a price (6:19-20)

nodes.t: Marriage, singleness and calling
nodes.d: Answering the Corinthians' letter, Paul teaches about the duties of husband and wife, the unmarried and widows, believers married to unbelievers, and living in the calling in which one was called.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} summarize what Paul says in 1 Corinthians 7:1-24 about marriage and about staying in the calling in which we were called?
ev: Describe the mutual duty of husband and wife (7:3-4)
Say what Paul teaches about a believer with an unbelieving spouse (7:12-16)
Explain the rule of 7:17, 7:20 and 7:24

nodes.t: The unmarried, widows and the shortness of time
nodes.d: Paul gives his judgment about virgins and the unmarried in view of the present distress, says the time is short, and explains that the unmarried can attend upon the Lord without distraction.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul says in 1 Corinthians 7:35 that he writes these things, and what he does not mean to do?
ev: Say whether Paul calls marriage a sin (7:28)
Explain why he says the time is short (7:29-31)
State the condition for a widow's remarriage (7:39)

nodes.t: Knowledge, love and food offered to idols
nodes.d: Paul says an idol is nothing and there is one God and one Lord, but that knowledge puffs up while love builds up, so believers must not cause a weak brother to stumble.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul would give up eating meat rather than make a brother stumble, using 1 Corinthians 8:13?
ev: State the confession of 8:6
Explain the difference between knowledge and love in 8:1
Explain how a believer can wound a weak conscience (8:9-12)

nodes.t: Paul's rights given up for the gospel
nodes.d: Paul defends his apostleship and his right to be supported, but says he has not used that right, becoming all things to all people so that he might save some.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul gave up his rights, using 1 Corinthians 9:19-23?
ev: List the rights Paul says he has (9:4-6)
Explain why he did not use them (9:12, 9:18)
Explain what Paul means by becoming all things to all men (9:19-22)

nodes.t: Running the race with discipline
nodes.d: Paul compares the Christian life to a race and to a fight that requires self-control, so that he is not disqualified after preaching to others.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul means by running to obtain an incorruptible crown (1 Corinthians 9:24-27)?
ev: Describe the two pictures Paul uses (race and fight)
Explain what Paul does to his body and why (9:27)

nodes.t: Warnings from Israel in the wilderness
nodes.d: Paul reminds the Corinthians that Israel passed through the sea and ate and drank spiritual food, yet many fell; he says these things were examples to us, and that God provides a way of escape from temptation.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul uses Israel's failures as a warning, and what God promises in 1 Corinthians 10:13?
ev: List the privileges of Israel in 10:1-4 and the sins in 10:7-10
Explain why Paul says these things were written (10:11)
State the promise of 10:13

nodes.t: The Lord's table and the table of demons
nodes.d: Paul tells believers to flee idolatry, explaining that the cup and bread are communion in Christ's blood and body, and that they cannot share both the Lord's table and the table of demons.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul says we cannot drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of devils (1 Corinthians 10:21)?
ev: Explain what the cup and the bread are called in 10:16
Say why believers cannot partake of both tables (10:20-21)

nodes.t: Liberty, conscience and the glory of God
nodes.d: Paul gives practical rules for eating what is sold in the market or served at a feast, tells believers to seek the good of others, and sums up: do all to the glory of God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} apply 1 Corinthians 10:31 to an everyday choice and explain how seeking another's good fits with it?
ev: State the rule of 10:31
Explain what to do when someone says the food was offered to idols (10:28-29)
Say whom Paul asks them to follow (11:1)

nodes.t: Order in worship: headship and head coverings
nodes.d: Paul praises the Corinthians for keeping the traditions, teaches about headship and about men and women praying or prophesying, and says the churches have no other custom.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul says about headship in 1 Corinthians 11:3 and 11:11-12 without leaving out either passage?
ev: State the order of headship in 11:3
Say what practices Paul addresses for men and women in 11:4-7
Note that Paul says man and woman are not independent of each other in the Lord (11:11-12)

nodes.t: The Lord's supper
nodes.d: Paul rebukes the Corinthians for how they ate together, then recounts what he received from the Lord about the bread and the cup, calls the cup the new testament in Christ's blood, and tells them to examine themselves.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell what Paul says about the bread and the cup in 1 Corinthians 11:23-26 and explain what it means to examine oneself?
ev: Describe the abuses in 11:20-22
Retell the institution of the supper from 11:23-25
Explain what the supper shows until the Lord comes (11:26)
Say what Paul tells each person to do before eating (11:28)

nodes.t: One Spirit, many gifts
nodes.d: Paul says that no one confesses Jesus as Lord except by the Holy Ghost and that the one Spirit gives different gifts to each person for the common good.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the gifts differ but come from the same Spirit, using 1 Corinthians 12:4-11?
ev: State the test of 12:3
List some gifts named in 12:8-10
Explain who decides how gifts are distributed (12:11)

nodes.t: One body, many members
nodes.d: Paul compares the church to a body with many members that need one another, naming various roles God has set in the church.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} use the picture of the body in 1 Corinthians 12 to explain why every church member matters?
ev: Explain how we all became one body (12:13)
Explain why no member can say it has no need of another (12:21)
Say what happens when one member suffers (12:26)

nodes.t: The more excellent way: love
nodes.d: Paul says that gifts, knowledge and sacrifice are nothing without love, describes what love is and does, and says that faith, hope and love remain, the greatest being love.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why love is greater than gifts, using 1 Corinthians 13?
ev: List things love does and does not do (13:4-7)
Say what will cease and what never fails (13:8)
Name the three that abide (13:13)

nodes.t: Tongues, prophecy and order in the assembly
nodes.d: Paul urges them to seek gifts that build up the church, especially prophecy, requires tongues to be interpreted, regulates speaking in turn, and ends by saying all things should be done decently and in order.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the purpose Paul gives for all speaking in church (14:26) and the rules in 1 Corinthians 14:27-33?
ev: Explain why Paul prefers prophecy in church (14:3-5)
State the rules for tongues and prophets (14:27-32)
Say why God is not the author of confusion (14:33)
Read 14:34-35 carefully and say what it commands about speaking in the churches

nodes.t: The gospel: Christ died and rose
nodes.d: Paul reminds the Corinthians of the gospel he received and preached, that Christ died for our sins, was buried and rose the third day according to the scriptures, and was seen by many witnesses.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} state the gospel in the words of 1 Corinthians 15:3-4 and name some who saw the risen Christ?
ev: Recite the gospel summary from 15:3-4
List the witnesses named in 15:5-8
Explain what Paul says about himself in 15:9-10

nodes.t: If Christ is not raised: the firstfruits
nodes.d: Paul argues that if there is no resurrection of the dead then Christ is not risen and faith is vain, but Christ is risen as the firstfruits, as Adam brought death and Christ brings life, until death is destroyed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the resurrection of Christ matters for the believer, using 1 Corinthians 15:12-22?
ev: List the consequences if Christ is not risen (15:14-19)
