Explain Adam and Christ in 15:21-22
Say what the last enemy is (15:26)

nodes.t: The resurrection body and the victory over death
nodes.d: Paul answers how the dead are raised, with the picture of a seed, contrasts the natural and spiritual body and the first and last Adam, and describes believers being changed at the last trumpet with death swallowed up in victory.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Paul says will happen to the dead in Christ and to the living, using 1 Corinthians 15:42-58?
ev: Explain the seed picture (15:36-38)
Contrast sown and raised in 15:42-44
Explain how believers will be changed (15:51-53)
State the closing exhortation of 15:58

nodes.t: The collection, plans and closing greetings
nodes.d: Paul gives orders for the collection for the saints, his travel plans, advice about Timothy, Apollos and Stephanas, and ends with greetings and a blessing.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul asks the Corinthians to do about the collection and how the letter closes (1 Corinthians 16)?
ev: Describe how the collection was to be given (16:1-2)
Name the co-workers Paul mentions
Quote the closing words of 16:13-14

nodes.t: 2 Corinthians: overview
nodes.d: Paul's second letter to the Corinthians: comfort in affliction, the ministry of the new covenant and reconciliation, the collection for the saints, and a defence of his apostleship (1:1-13:14).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} give a short outline of 2 Corinthians and say what its three main parts are about?
ev: Name the main sections: comfort and ministry (1-7), the collection (8-9), Paul's defence of his apostleship (10-13)
Say what Paul tells the Corinthians about his sufferings

nodes.t: The God of all comfort
nodes.d: Paul blesses God as the Father of mercies, who comforts us in trouble so that we can comfort others, and tells of a deadly trouble in Asia that taught him to trust in God who raises the dead.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why God comforts us, using 2 Corinthians 1:3-4?
ev: Say who God is called in 1:3
Explain why we are comforted (1:4)
Explain what Paul learned from the trouble in Asia (1:8-10)

nodes.t: All God's promises are yes in Christ
nodes.d: Paul defends changing his travel plans, saying his word is not yes and no, because God is true and in Christ all the promises of God are yes; God has established, anointed and sealed believers and given the Spirit as a guarantee.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what it means that all the promises of God are yes in Christ (2 Corinthians 1:20)?
ev: Explain what Paul says about God's promises in 1:20
List what God has done for believers in 1:21-22
Say why Paul had not yet come to Corinth (1:23)

nodes.t: Forgiving the offender
nodes.d: Paul says he wrote with many tears, that the punishment the majority inflicted on the offender is enough, and urges the church to forgive and comfort him so that Satan gets no advantage.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul urges the Corinthians to forgive and comfort the man who had been punished (2 Corinthians 2:5-11)?
ev: Say why Paul wrote with tears (2:4)
Explain what Paul asks the church to do for the punished man (2:7-8)
Say why forgiving matters (2:11)

nodes.t: Led in triumph: the fragrance of Christ
nodes.d: After telling of his restlessness at Troas, Paul thanks God who leads us in triumph in Christ and spreads the knowledge of him, which is a fragrance of life to some and of death to others.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul means by being a sweet savour of Christ, using 2 Corinthians 2:14-17?
ev: Explain the two kinds of aroma in 2:15-16
Contrast Paul's speaking with those who corrupt the word of God (2:17)

nodes.t: Ministers of the new covenant
nodes.d: Paul says the Corinthians are Christ's letter written by the Spirit on hearts, calls himself a minister of the new testament, and contrasts the ministry of death carved on stone, with its fading glory, with the ministry of the Spirit and righteousness.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Paul contrasts the ministry written on stone with the ministry of the Spirit in 2 Corinthians 3:3-11?
ev: Say what the Corinthians are called in 3:2-3
Explain the difference between the letter and the Spirit (3:6)
Compare the two ministrations in 3:7-11

nodes.t: Unveiled face: from glory to glory
nodes.d: Paul says Moses put a veil over his face, a veil that remains in the reading of the old testament but is done away in Christ, and that believers with open face behold the glory of the Lord and are changed into his image.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what happens to a person who turns to the Lord, using 2 Corinthians 3:16-18?
ev: Explain the veil of Moses (3:13-15)
Say when the veil is taken away (3:16)
Explain what happens to those who behold the Lord's glory (3:18)

nodes.t: Treasure in jars of clay
nodes.d: Paul says the gospel is the light of the knowledge of God's glory in the face of Christ, hidden to those blinded by the god of this world, and that believers carry it in weak earthen vessels so that the power is God's.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul says we have this treasure in earthen vessels (2 Corinthians 4:7)?
ev: Explain who blinds unbelievers and why (4:4)
Say where the light of the knowledge of God's glory is seen (4:6)
Explain why we have the treasure in earthen vessels (4:7)
Describe the four contrasts in 4:8-9

nodes.t: The inward man is renewed
nodes.d: Paul says that although the outward man perishes, the inward man is renewed day by day, and that light affliction produces an eternal weight of glory for those who look at the unseen.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul does not lose heart, using 2 Corinthians 4:16-18?
ev: Contrast the outward and inward man (4:16)
Contrast the seen and the unseen (4:18)

nodes.t: The heavenly house and the judgment seat
nodes.d: Paul says that if the earthly tent is destroyed, believers have an eternal house from God, are confident to be present with the Lord, walk by faith, and must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul says about being at home with the Lord and about the judgment seat in 2 Corinthians 5:1-10?
ev: Say what Paul expects after the tent is dissolved (5:1)
Explain what Paul says about walking by faith (5:7)
Say who must appear before Christ's judgment seat (5:10)

nodes.t: New creation and the ministry of reconciliation
nodes.d: Paul says the love of Christ constrains us because he died for all, that anyone in Christ is a new creature, that God reconciled us in Christ and gave us the message of reconciliation, and that Christ was made sin for us so that we might become the righteousness of God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what it means to be reconciled to God, using 2 Corinthians 5:18-21?
ev: Explain why Christ died for all (5:15)
Say what is true of anyone in Christ (5:17)
Explain reconciliation in 5:18-19
Explain the exchange described in 5:21

nodes.t: Now is the day of salvation: marks of true ministry
nodes.d: Paul urges the Corinthians not to receive God's grace in vain, says now is the day of salvation, and lists the hardships and virtues by which he commends himself as a minister of God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul means by "now is the day of salvation" in 2 Corinthians 6:2?
ev: Quote the point of 6:2
List some hardships in 6:4-5 and some virtues in 6:6-7
Explain the paradoxes in 6:8-10

nodes.t: Separation and the temple of the living God
nodes.d: Paul warns against being unequally yoked with unbelievers, says believers are the temple of the living God, and gives promises that God will be their Father and they his sons and daughters, calling them to cleanse themselves.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul says believers should not be unequally yoked with unbelievers, using 2 Corinthians 6:14-18?
ev: Name the contrasts Paul draws in 6:14-16
Say what promises are given in 6:16-18
Explain the conclusion of 7:1

nodes.t: Godly sorrow and Titus's report
nodes.d: Paul tells how Titus comforted him in Macedonia with news of the Corinthians' repentance, and distinguishes godly sorrow, which leads to repentance and salvation, from the sorrow of the world which brings death.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the difference between godly sorrow and worldly sorrow, using 2 Corinthians 7:9-11?
ev: State the difference between godly sorrow and the sorrow of the world (7:10)
Say who brought comfort and what he reported (7:6-7)
List fruits of the Corinthians' sorrow (7:11)

nodes.t: The grace of giving: the churches of Macedonia
nodes.d: Paul tells of the Macedonians' generous gift out of deep poverty, urges the Corinthians to complete their part, points to Christ who became poor so that we might be rich, and says the aim is fairness.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Christ's example motivates giving, using 2 Corinthians 8:9?
ev: Describe the Macedonians' giving (8:2-5)
Explain Christ's example in 8:9
Say what Paul means by equality in 8:13-15

nodes.t: Titus and the brothers: honesty with the offering
nodes.d: Paul commends Titus and two brothers sent to administer the gift, so that no one could blame him and everything would be honest before the Lord and men.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul arranged for several trusted men to handle the offering (2 Corinthians 8:20-21)?
ev: Name who is sent to Corinth (8:16-23)
Explain why Paul takes care to be honest about the gift (8:20-21)

nodes.t: God loves a cheerful giver
nodes.d: Paul urges the Corinthians to be ready with the gift, saying that he who sows bountifully will reap bountifully, that each should give as he has decided in his heart, and that God supplies all they need and receives thanks.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how God wants us to give, using 2 Corinthians 9:6-8?
ev: Say how each person should give (9:7)
Explain the sowing and reaping picture (9:6)
Say what the gift produces according to 9:12-13

nodes.t: Spiritual weapons and true authority
nodes.d: Paul says he does not war according to the flesh, that his weapons are mighty to pull down strongholds and bring every thought captive to Christ, and answers those who say his presence is weak.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul says about the weapons of our warfare in 2 Corinthians 10:3-5?
ev: Explain what the weapons of Paul's warfare do (10:4-5)
Say what critics said about Paul (10:10)
Say what authority the Lord gave him for (10:8)

nodes.t: Boasting only in the Lord
nodes.d: Paul says he will not compare himself with those who commend themselves or boast of others' work; his boasting stays within the limit God assigned, and the one approved is the one the Lord commends.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain who is truly approved, using 2 Corinthians 10:17-18?
ev: Explain the limit Paul keeps in his boasting (10:13-16)
Quote the principle of 10:17-18

nodes.t: False apostles and Paul's foolish boasting
nodes.d: Paul fears the Corinthians will be led astray from Christ as the serpent deceived Eve, warns of false apostles disguised as servants of righteousness, and, speaking as a fool, lists his sufferings as a servant of Christ.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul warns about false apostles in 2 Corinthians 11:13-15 and why he lists his sufferings?
ev: Say what Paul fears in 11:3
Explain how false apostles disguise themselves (11:13-15)
List some sufferings Paul names in 11:23-27
Describe the escape at Damascus (11:32-33)

nodes.t: The thorn in the flesh: power in weakness
nodes.d: Paul tells of being caught up to paradise, then of a thorn in the flesh given to keep him humble; the Lord answered his prayer by saying his grace is sufficient and his strength is made perfect in weakness.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul says "when I am weak, then am I strong," using 2 Corinthians 12:7-10?
ev: Say what Paul asked the Lord three times (12:8)
Quote the Lord's answer (12:9)
Explain why Paul can say he is strong when weak (12:10)

nodes.t: Paul's signs, his love and his fears
nodes.d: Paul says the signs of an apostle were done among the Corinthians, that he will not burden them but gladly spend himself for them, and that he fears finding sin and disorder when he comes a third time.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul would not burden the Corinthians, using 2 Corinthians 12:14-15?
ev: Say how Paul describes his care for them (12:14-15)
List the sins Paul fears finding (12:20-21)

nodes.t: Examine yourselves: final warnings and blessing
nodes.d: Paul warns that he will not spare those who have sinned, tells the Corinthians to examine themselves whether they are in the faith, and closes with an exhortation and a trinitarian blessing.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul asks the Corinthians to do in 2 Corinthians 13:5 and name the three persons in 13:14?
ev: Quote the command of 13:5
Name the three persons in the blessing of 13:14
List the closing exhortations in 13:11

nodes.t: Galatians: overview
nodes.d: Paul writes to the churches of Galatia, who were turning to another gospel, to defend justification by faith, the freedom of the sons of God and life by the Spirit (1:1-6:18).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul wrote to the Galatians and what he says the true gospel is?
ev: Say what problem prompted the letter (1:6-9)
Name the three parts: Paul's defence (1-2), justification by faith (3-4), living by the Spirit (5-6)

nodes.t: There is only one gospel
nodes.d: Paul greets the Galatians, is amazed that they are turning to another gospel, and pronounces a curse on anyone, even an angel, who preaches a different gospel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul says there is no other gospel, using Galatians 1:6-9?
ev: Say what Christ gave himself for (1:4)
State what Paul says of anyone who preaches another gospel (1:8-9)

nodes.t: Paul's gospel and call by revelation
nodes.d: Paul says he received the gospel by the revelation of Jesus Christ, not from men, and tells of his former persecution of the church, God's call, his time in Arabia and his first visit to Jerusalem.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Paul says he came to preach the gospel, using Galatians 1:11-24?
ev: Say how Paul received his gospel (1:11-12)
Describe what Paul was like before his call (1:13-14)
Say what the churches of Judaea said about him (1:23-24)

nodes.t: Paul and the apostles at Jerusalem
nodes.d: Fourteen years later Paul went to Jerusalem with Barnabas and Titus, refused to give in to false brothers who wanted Titus circumcised, and was given the right hand of fellowship by James, Cephas and John.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what happened at Jerusalem in Galatians 2:1-10 and why Paul would not give way?
ev: Say why Titus was not circumcised (2:3-5)
Describe the agreement about preaching to the Gentiles and the circumcised (2:7-9)
Name what they asked Paul to remember (2:10)

nodes.t: Paul opposes Peter at Antioch
nodes.d: Paul tells how he opposed Peter to his face at Antioch for withdrawing from eating with Gentiles out of fear, since this was not in step with the truth of the gospel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul confronted Peter, using Galatians 2:11-14?
ev: Describe what Peter did and why (2:12)
Say why Paul rebuked him (2:14)

nodes.t: Justified by faith in Christ, crucified with Christ
nodes.d: Paul says a person is not justified by works of the law but by faith in Jesus Christ, and that he has been crucified with Christ and now lives by faith in the Son of God who loved him and gave himself for him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Paul says a person is justified, using Galatians 2:16 and 2:20?
ev: Quote the main claim of 2:16
Explain what Paul means by being crucified with Christ (2:20)
Say what would follow if righteousness came by the law (2:21)

nodes.t: Received the Spirit by hearing with faith
nodes.d: Paul asks the foolish Galatians whether they received the Spirit and saw miracles by works of the law or by hearing with faith, since they began in the Spirit.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Paul argues from the Galatians' own experience of the Spirit in Galatians 3:1-5?
ev: Say what question Paul asks in 3:2
Explain why he calls the Galatians foolish (3:1, 3:3)

nodes.t: Abraham, faith and the blessing for the nations
nodes.d: Paul argues that Abraham believed God and it was counted to him for righteousness, so those of faith are Abraham's children, and that Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law so that the blessing of Abraham might come to the Gentiles.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Galatians 3:6-9 connects Abraham's faith to the Gentiles?
ev: Quote what Paul says Abraham did (3:6)
Explain who are the children of Abraham (3:7)
Say what the scripture foresaw (3:8)
Explain how Christ redeemed us from the curse (3:13-14)

nodes.t: The promise and the law
nodes.d: Paul argues that the promise to Abraham and his seed, who is Christ, cannot be cancelled by the law that came 430 years later, and that the law was added because of transgressions until the seed should come.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Paul says the law relates to the promise made to Abraham in Galatians 3:15-22?
ev: Explain why the law does not cancel the promise (3:15-18)
Say who the seed is (3:16)
Say why the law was added (3:19)
Say what the scripture has concluded about all (3:22)

nodes.t: Sons of God in Christ: neither Jew nor Greek
nodes.d: Paul says the law was a schoolmaster to bring us to Christ, that all who are baptized into Christ and have faith are children of God, one in Christ, and Abraham's seed and heirs according to the promise.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how someone becomes a child of God and heir of the promise, using Galatians 3:26-29?
ev: Explain the picture of the schoolmaster (3:24-25)
List the distinctions Paul says are gone in Christ (3:28)
Say what believers are in Christ (3:29)

nodes.t: Redeemed to be sons and heirs
nodes.d: Paul compares the heir under guardians to people under the elements of the world, and says that when the time was full God sent his Son under the law to redeem those under the law so that we receive adoption, and God sent the Spirit of his Son crying Abba, Father.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what God did "in the fulness of time" and what it means to be a son, using Galatians 4:4-7?
ev: Describe the heir who is still a child (4:1-2)
Say what God did when the fulness of time came (4:4-5)
Say what the Spirit cries (4:6)

nodes.t: Paul's plea: do not turn back
nodes.d: Paul asks why the Galatians, now known by God, are turning back to weak and beggarly elements and observing days and seasons, recalls their warmth toward him, and pleads with them as a mother in labour until Christ is formed in them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Paul's pleading with the Galatians in Galatians 4:8-20?
ev: Say what Paul fears (4:11)
Describe how the Galatians first received Paul (4:13-15)
Say what Paul wants formed in them (4:19)

nodes.t: Two sons, two covenants: Hagar and Sarah
nodes.d: Paul uses Abraham's two sons, one by the bondwoman and one by the free woman, as an allegory of two covenants, and says believers are children of promise like Isaac and not children of the bondwoman.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Paul reads the story of Hagar and Sarah in Galatians 4:21-31?
ev: Say who the two sons and their mothers are (4:22-23)
Explain the two covenants named in 4:24-26
Say who Paul says we are like (4:28, 4:31)
Quote the scripture Paul cites in 4:30

nodes.t: Stand fast in the liberty of Christ
nodes.d: Paul tells the Galatians to stand fast in the liberty with which Christ has made them free, warns that anyone who accepts circumcision as a way to be justified falls from grace, and says what counts is faith working through love.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul says Christ is of no effect to those who seek justification by the law (Galatians 5:4)?
ev: Say what Paul warns happens if they are circumcised (5:2-4)
Say what avails in Christ Jesus (5:6)
Explain the picture of leaven (5:9)

nodes.t: Walking by the Spirit: works of the flesh and fruit of the Spirit
nodes.d: Paul says freedom is for serving one another in love, that the whole law is fulfilled in loving your neighbour, and contrasts the works of the flesh with the fruit of the Spirit for those who walk in the Spirit.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name the fruit of the Spirit from Galatians 5:22-23 and explain the difference between flesh and Spirit?
ev: Say how liberty is to be used (5:13)
List some works of the flesh (5:19-21) and the fruit of the Spirit (5:22-23)
Say what belongs to those who are Christ's (5:24)

nodes.t: Bearing burdens, sowing and reaping
nodes.d: Paul teaches restoring a person overtaken in a fault gently, bearing one another's burdens, and sowing to the Spirit rather than to the flesh, and not growing weary in doing good.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul means by "whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap" in Galatians 6:7-9?
ev: Say how to restore someone who has fallen (6:1)
Explain the sowing and reaping principle (6:7-8)
Say who we should do good to (6:10)

nodes.t: Boasting only in the cross
nodes.d: Paul closes in his own hand, says those who press circumcision want to avoid persecution for the cross, that he glories only in the cross of Christ, and that what counts is a new creature, and he bears the marks of Jesus.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul glories only in the cross of Christ (Galatians 6:14)?
ev: Say what Paul glories in (6:14)
Say what counts instead of circumcision or uncircumcision (6:15)

nodes.t: Ephesians: overview
nodes.d: Paul's letter to the saints at Ephesus: God's blessings in Christ, salvation by grace, the unity of Jew and Gentile in one body, and how to walk worthy in the church, home and spiritual battle (1:1-6:24).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} give a short outline of Ephesians and say what its two halves are about?
ev: Describe the two halves: what God has done in Christ (1-3) and how to walk worthy (4-6)

nodes.t: Blessed in Christ: chosen, adopted, redeemed, sealed
nodes.d: Paul blesses God, who in Christ chose us before the foundation of the world, adopted us, redeemed us through his blood, made known the mystery of his will, and sealed believers with the Holy Spirit as the pledge of the inheritance.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list what God has done for believers in Christ, using Ephesians 1:3-14?
ev: List the blessings Paul names in 1:3-14
Say when God chose us and for what purpose (1:4)
Say what the Holy Spirit is for believers (1:13-14)

nodes.t: Paul's prayer: Christ above all, head of the church
nodes.d: Paul gives thanks and prays that the Ephesians may know the hope of God's calling and the greatness of his power, which raised Christ and set him far above every power as head over all things to the church, his body.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul says about Christ's position and the church in Ephesians 1:20-23?
ev: Say what Paul prays that they may know (1:17-19)
Describe where God has set Christ (1:20-22)
Say what the church is to Christ (1:22-23)

nodes.t: Dead in sin, saved by grace through faith
nodes.d: Paul says that Christians were dead in trespasses and followed the world, the devil and the flesh, but God, rich in mercy, made them alive with Christ; salvation is by grace through faith, not by works, and believers are created for good works.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Ephesians 2:8-10 says a person is saved and what follows from it?
ev: Describe the condition before salvation (2:1-3)
Explain 2:8-9
Say what we were created in Christ for (2:10)

nodes.t: One new man: Jew and Gentile reconciled
nodes.d: Paul says Gentiles were once far from Israel and the covenants of promise, but are brought near by the blood of Christ, who broke down the dividing wall, made both one and gave both access to the Father; together they are built into a holy temple.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Christ made Jew and Gentile one, using Ephesians 2:13-18?
ev: Describe the Gentiles' former state (2:11-12)
Say what Christ did to the dividing wall (2:14-16)
Explain the picture of the household and temple (2:19-22)

nodes.t: The mystery of Christ and Paul's second prayer
nodes.d: Paul explains the mystery made known to him, that Gentiles are fellow heirs of the same body and of the promise in Christ, that the church shows God's wisdom to the powers, and prays that they know the love of Christ and be filled with the fulness of God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} state the mystery Paul describes in Ephesians 3:6 and what he prays for in 3:16-19?
ev: State the mystery of 3:6
Say what the church makes known (3:10)
Summarise Paul's prayer in 3:16-19
Say who receives glory in 3:20-21

nodes.t: Unity of the body and gifts for building up
nodes.d: Paul urges the Ephesians to walk worthy and keep the unity of the Spirit, lists the "one" things of the faith, and says the ascended Christ gave apostles, prophets, evangelists, pastors and teachers to equip the saints and build up the body until it is mature.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Christ gave pastors and teachers to the church, using Ephesians 4:11-16?
ev: List the sevenfold unity of 4:4-6
Name the gifts given in 4:11
Say what the gifts are for (4:12-16)

nodes.t: Put off the old man, put on the new
nodes.d: Paul tells the Ephesians not to live as the Gentiles do but to put off the old man and put on the new, created in righteousness and holiness, with specific commands about truth, anger, work, speech and forgiveness.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what it means to put off the old man and put on the new, using Ephesians 4:22-24 and one example from 4:25-32?
ev: Contrast the old and new man (4:22-24)
List specific commands in 4:25-32
Say what we are told not to grieve (4:30)

nodes.t: Walk in love, light and wisdom
nodes.d: Paul tells the Ephesians to walk in love as Christ loved us, to avoid immorality and covetousness, to walk as children of light and not be drunk with wine but filled with the Spirit, and to submit to one another.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what walking as a child of light means, using Ephesians 5:8-11?
ev: Say how we are to walk (5:2, 5:8, 5:15)
Contrast drunkenness and being filled with the Spirit (5:18)
Say what follows from being filled (5:19-21)

nodes.t: Marriage and Christ and the church
nodes.d: Paul instructs wives and husbands, grounding the husband's love and the wife's submission in the relation of Christ to the church, quotes the scripture about two becoming one flesh, and calls this a great mystery concerning Christ and the church.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Paul connects marriage with Christ and the church in Ephesians 5:22-33?
ev: Say what Paul commands wives and husbands (5:22, 5:25)
Describe what Christ did for the church (5:25-27)
Say what Paul says the "great mystery" is about (5:32)

nodes.t: Children, parents, servants and masters
nodes.d: Paul tells children to obey their parents in the Lord, quotes the commandment to honour father and mother, tells fathers to bring children up in the Lord, and gives instructions to servants and masters who both answer to a Master in heaven.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul tells children and parents in Ephesians 6:1-4?
ev: Quote the commandment Paul cites (6:2)
Say what fathers are told (6:4)
Say what masters are reminded of (6:9)

nodes.t: The whole armour of God
nodes.d: Paul calls believers to be strong in the Lord and put on the armour of God to stand against the devil and spiritual powers, listing truth, righteousness, the gospel of peace, faith, salvation and the word of God, with prayer, and asks for prayer for himself.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list the armour of God in Ephesians 6:14-17 and say what each piece stands for in the text?
ev: Say who we wrestle against (6:12)
List the pieces of armour (6:14-17)
Explain the role of prayer (6:18-20)

nodes.t: Philippians: overview
nodes.d: Paul writes from prison to the church at Philippi about joy, the humility of Christ, pressing toward the goal, and contentment (1:1-4:23).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} give a short outline of Philippians and say what Paul says about joy?
ev: Say where Paul was when he wrote (1:7, 1:13)
Name the theme that recurs, rejoicing (e.g. 3:1, 4:4)

nodes.t: Thanksgiving and prayer for the Philippians
nodes.d: Paul thanks God for the Philippians' partnership in the gospel, is confident that God will complete the good work begun in them, and prays that their love will grow in knowledge and they be filled with the fruits of righteousness.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul is confident that God will do, using Philippians 1:6?
ev: Quote the confidence of 1:6
Say what Paul prays for in 1:9-11

nodes.t: Paul in chains: Christ is preached
nodes.d: Paul says his imprisonment has advanced the gospel, that Christ is preached whether from envy or love, and that he rejoices in this.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul rejoices in prison, using Philippians 1:12-18?
ev: Say what happened because of Paul's bonds (1:12-14)
Contrast the two kinds of preachers (1:15-17)

nodes.t: To live is Christ, to die is gain
nodes.d: Paul says Christ will be magnified in his body whether by life or death, that to live is Christ and to die is gain, and urges the Philippians to live worthy of the gospel, standing firm together and not afraid of opponents.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul means by "to live is Christ, and to die is gain" in Philippians 1:21?
ev: Quote 1:21
Explain Paul's dilemma (1:22-25)
Say what Paul asks of the Philippians (1:27-28)
Say what has been granted to them (1:29)

nodes.t: The mind of Christ: humbled and exalted
nodes.d: Paul urges unity and humility, pointing to Christ, who being in the form of God took the form of a servant, humbled himself to death on a cross, and was highly exalted so that every knee will bow and every tongue confess that Jesus Christ is Lord.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the path of Christ in Philippians 2:6-11 and say how it applies to us in 2:3-5?
ev: Describe the steps of Christ's humbling (2:6-8)
Say what God did in response (2:9-11)
Say what attitude Paul asks of the Philippians (2:3-5)

nodes.t: Work out your salvation: shining as lights
nodes.d: Paul tells the Philippians to work out their own salvation with fear and trembling because God works in them, to do all things without grumbling, and to shine as lights holding forth the word of life.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul says "work out your own salvation" and then adds that God works in you (Philippians 2:12-13)?
ev: Explain 2:12-13 together
Say what the Philippians are to do among a crooked generation (2:14-16)

nodes.t: Timothy and Epaphroditus
nodes.d: Paul commends Timothy, who cares for the Philippians like a son serving with his father, and Epaphroditus, who nearly died serving the work of Christ and whom Paul sends back to them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul says about Timothy and Epaphroditus in Philippians 2:19-30?
ev: Say what Paul says of Timothy (2:20-22)
Describe what happened to Epaphroditus (2:25-30)

nodes.t: Counting all things loss for Christ
nodes.d: Paul warns against those who trust the flesh, lists his own credentials, and says he counts them loss for the knowledge of Christ, wanting the righteousness that comes through faith in Christ rather than his own righteousness from the law.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul gave up and what he gained, using Philippians 3:7-9?
ev: List Paul's credentials (3:5-6)
State what Paul wants instead (3:8-10)
Explain which righteousness Paul wants (3:9)

nodes.t: Pressing toward the goal and our citizenship in heaven
nodes.d: Paul says he has not yet attained but presses toward the prize of the upward call, urges the Philippians to follow his example and not live as enemies of the cross, and says our citizenship is in heaven, from where we await the Saviour who will transform our bodies.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Paul's "one thing I do" in Philippians 3:13-14 and what believers await in 3:20-21?
ev: Describe what Paul does (3:13-14)
Contrast the enemies of the cross with believers (3:18-20)
Say what the Saviour will do (3:21)

nodes.t: Rejoice, do not be anxious, think on these things
nodes.d: Paul urges unity between two women, tells the Philippians to rejoice in the Lord always, to pray with thanksgiving instead of being anxious so that the peace of God guards them, and to think on what is true, honest, just and pure.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul says to do instead of being anxious, using Philippians 4:6-7?
ev: Quote the commands of 4:4 and 4:6
Say what the peace of God does (4:7)
List some things to think on (4:8)

nodes.t: Content in every state and God's supply
nodes.d: Paul thanks the Philippians for their gift, says he has learned to be content whether abased or abounding, that he can do all things through Christ who strengthens him, and that God will supply all their need; he closes with greetings.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul says about contentment in Philippians 4:11-13?
ev: Say what Paul learned (4:11-12)
Quote 4:13 and 4:19
Describe how Paul treats the Philippians' gift (4:17-18)

nodes.t: Colossians: overview
nodes.d: Paul writes to the church at Colosse about the supremacy of Christ, warns against empty philosophy and rules, and calls believers raised with Christ to a new life (1:1-4:18).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} give a short outline of Colossians and say who Paul says Christ is?
ev: Describe the main sections: the supremacy of Christ (1), warnings (2), the new life (3-4)

nodes.t: Thanksgiving, prayer and rescue into the kingdom
nodes.d: Paul gives thanks for the Colossians' faith, love and hope, prays that they will be filled with the knowledge of God's will and walk worthily, and thanks the Father who delivered us from the power of darkness into the kingdom of his Son.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Colossians 1:13-14 says God has done for believers?
ev: Say what Paul prays for (1:9-11)
Say what the Father has done (1:12-14)

nodes.t: The supremacy of Christ
nodes.d: Paul says Christ is the image of the invisible God, firstborn of creation, by whom and for whom all things were created, head of the church and firstborn from the dead, in whom all fulness dwells and through whose cross God reconciles all things.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list what Colossians 1:15-20 says about who Christ is?
ev: List what Paul says Christ is and has done in 1:15-20
Explain how the Colossians were reconciled (1:21-22)
Say the condition stated in 1:23

nodes.t: Paul's ministry and the mystery: Christ in you
nodes.d: Paul rejoices in his sufferings for the church, says he is a minister to make known the mystery once hidden and now revealed, which is Christ in you the hope of glory, and that he labours to present everyone perfect in Christ.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul says the mystery is in Colossians 1:26-27?
ev: State the mystery of 1:27
Say what Paul does and why (1:28-29)

nodes.t: Rooted in Christ: complete in him
nodes.d: Paul says all the treasures of wisdom are hidden in Christ, warns against being taken captive by philosophy and the traditions of men, and says believers are complete in him, circumcised, buried and raised with him, forgiven, with the written record against them nailed to the cross.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why believers are complete in Christ, using Colossians 2:9-15?
ev: Say where wisdom and knowledge are found (2:3)
Say what Paul warns against (2:8)
Explain what God did with the record of debt (2:14)
Say what Christ did to the powers (2:15)

nodes.t: Shadow and substance: against rules and false humility
nodes.d: Paul tells the Colossians not to let anyone judge them about food, festivals or the sabbath, which are a shadow of things to come while the body belongs to Christ, and warns against false humility and man-made rules that cannot restrain the flesh.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul means by saying these things are a shadow and the substance is of Christ (Colossians 2:16-17)?
ev: Say what the shadow and the body are (2:17)
Explain why rules like "touch not, taste not" fail (2:20-23)

nodes.t: Raised with Christ: seek things above
nodes.d: Paul says that because believers are raised with Christ they should seek and set their minds on things above, for their life is hid with Christ in God; they must put to death sins such as fornication and covetousness, and put off anger and lies.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul tells believers to seek things above, using Colossians 3:1-4?
ev: Say what believers are to seek (3:1-2)
List sins to put off (3:5-9)
Say what is true in the new man (3:10-11)

nodes.t: Put on love: the new life in the church
nodes.d: Paul tells the elect of God to put on mercy, kindness, humility and patience, to forgive as Christ forgave, to put on love above all, to let the peace of God rule, the word of Christ dwell richly, and to do everything in the name of the Lord Jesus.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Colossians 3:12-17 describes a Christian community?
ev: List what to put on (3:12-14)
Say how we forgive (3:13)
Quote the rule of 3:17

nodes.t: Households, prayer and walking in wisdom
nodes.d: Paul instructs wives, husbands, children, fathers, servants and masters, urges constant prayer, asks for prayer for opportunities to speak the mystery of Christ, and calls the Colossians to walk in wisdom toward outsiders with gracious speech.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Colossians 3:23 says about how we should work and for whom?
ev: Say what each household member is told (3:18-4:1)
Say what Paul asks the Colossians to pray for (4:3-4)
Describe how they should speak to outsiders (4:5-6)

nodes.t: Messengers, fellow workers and greetings
nodes.d: Paul names Tychicus, Onesimus, Aristarchus, Mark, Epaphras, Luke and others, sends greetings to Laodicea, asks that the letter be read there too, and closes in his own hand.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name some of Paul's co-workers in Colossians 4 and say what Paul asks about the letter (4:16)?
ev: Name some of Paul's co-workers in 4:7-14
Say what is to be done with the letter (4:16)

nodes.t: Hosea: overview
nodes.d: Hosea's word to Israel in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash and Judah's kings: a prophet's marriage to an unfaithful wife pictures the LORD's love for faithless Israel, followed by charges, judgment and a call to return.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences how Hosea's marriage pictures the LORD's relationship with Israel?
ev: Say that Hosea's marriage (chs 1-3) is an acted picture of the LORD and Israel
Outline the book as marriage (1-3), charges and judgment (4-13) and a closing call to return (14)

nodes.t: Hosea's wife and children
nodes.d: The LORD tells Hosea to take a wife of whoredoms; their three children are named Jezreel, Loruhamah and Loammi as signs, yet the chapter ends with a promise that Israel will be called sons of the living God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the names of Hosea's three children meant and what hope the LORD adds at the end of chapter 1?
ev: Name the three children and what each name signals
Point out the promise in 1:10-11 that reverses 'not my people'

nodes.t: The LORD pleads and allures his wife
nodes.d: The LORD charges Israel with going after her lovers and forgetting him, announces discipline, then promises to allure her into the wilderness and betroth her to himself for ever in faithfulness.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how chapter 2 moves from judgment on Israel to the LORD betrothing her again?
ev: Describe the charge (2:5, 2:8, 2:13) and the discipline (2:6-13)
Describe the promise to betroth Israel for ever (2:19-20) and to say 'Thou art my people' (2:23)

nodes.t: Hosea buys back his wife
nodes.d: The LORD tells Hosea to love a woman who is an adulteress, as he loves Israel; Hosea buys her and tells her to wait for him, and Israel is said to wait many days before returning to seek the LORD and David their king.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell Hosea 3 and say what it shows about the LORD's love for Israel?
ev: Retell what Hosea did and what he said to the woman
Say what the action pictures about Israel in 3:4-5

nodes.t: The LORD's controversy with the land
nodes.d: The LORD charges the people and priests with no truth, mercy or knowledge of God, with violence, idolatry and sexual sin at the high places, and declares that his people are destroyed for lack of knowledge.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say why the LORD has a controversy with the land in Hosea 4?
ev: List the sins named in 4:1-2 and 4:12-14
Explain 4:6 in plain words

nodes.t: Priests, house of Israel and Judah judged
nodes.d: Priests, people and king are warned that judgment is coming; Ephraim and Judah turn to Assyria for healing but cannot be healed, and the LORD says he will withdraw until they acknowledge their offence and seek his face.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Ephraim's help from Assyria fails in Hosea 5 and what the LORD waits for?
ev: Say whom the LORD addresses in 5:1
Explain why turning to the Assyrian could not heal them (5:13)
Say what the LORD waits for in 5:15

nodes.t: Return to the LORD; mercy, not sacrifice
nodes.d: The people speak of returning to the LORD who has torn and will heal, but the LORD answers that their goodness is like morning dew, that he desires mercy and the knowledge of God more than offerings, and that they have transgressed the covenant.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD means in Hosea 6:6 when he says he desires mercy, not sacrifice?
ev: Read the call to return in 6:1-3 and the LORD's reply in 6:4-6
Explain 6:6 in plain words
Notice the reference to transgressing the covenant in 6:7

nodes.t: Ephraim: a cake not turned
nodes.d: The LORD would heal Israel but finds falsehood and treachery, from the king and princes down; Ephraim is like a half-baked cake and a silly dove that calls to Egypt and goes to Assyria rather than crying to the LORD with the heart.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD compares Ephraim to a silly dove in Hosea 7?
ev: Describe two pictures used for Ephraim (7:8, 7:11)
Say what Ephraim does instead of turning to the LORD (7:11, 7:14)

nodes.t: Sowing the wind, reaping the whirlwind
nodes.d: The trumpet sounds because Israel transgressed the covenant, set up kings and idols of their own making and the calf of Samaria; they sow the wind and reap the whirlwind, and will return to Egypt.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what it means that Israel sows the wind and reaps the whirlwind?
ev: Name the charges in 8:1, 8:4 and 8:12
Explain the saying in 8:7

nodes.t: No rejoicing: days of recompence
nodes.d: Israel is told not to rejoice, since the land will not feed them and they will go into Assyria and Egypt; the LORD recalls finding Israel like grapes in the wilderness before they went to Baalpeor and Gilgal, and Ephraim's fruit is cut off.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how the LORD first found Israel in Hosea 9:10 and what the people did next?
ev: Say where the LORD says Israel will go (9:3, 9:6, 9:17)
Describe the picture of 9:10 and what went wrong

nodes.t: Israel an empty vine
nodes.d: Israel the vine bears fruit for himself and multiplies altars and images; calves and king will be carried off, yet the LORD calls them to sow righteousness and seek him until he rains righteousness on them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the call to sow in righteousness in Hosea 10:12 and what Israel had sown instead?
ev: Explain why Israel is called an empty vine (10:1)
Read the call in 10:12 and say how it contrasts with 10:13

nodes.t: Out of Egypt: the LORD's fatherly love
nodes.d: The LORD remembers calling his son out of Egypt, teaching Ephraim to walk and drawing them with bands of love, yet they turned to Baalim; he declares he will not carry out the fierceness of his anger, for he is God and not man.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how the LORD speaks about Israel as his child in Hosea 11:1-4 and 11:8-9?
ev: Retell 11:1-4 in your own words
Explain what 11:8-9 says about the LORD's heart and character

nodes.t: Ephraim's lies; Jacob recalled
nodes.d: The LORD has a controversy with Judah and Israel; he recalls Jacob taking his brother's heel, wrestling and finding God at Bethel, then calls Ephraim to turn, since the people trade by deceit and trust in wealth.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say which parts of Jacob's life Hosea 12 recalls and why?
ev: Say which events of Jacob's life are recalled (12:3-4, 12:12)
Read the call of 12:6 and the sin of 12:7-8

nodes.t: No saviour beside the LORD
nodes.d: Ephraim's idol worship brings him to vanish like morning cloud; the LORD alone is God and Saviour from Egypt, yet he will come as a lion and bear, though he also promises to ransom them from the grave and death.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Hosea 13:4 says there is no saviour but the LORD?
ev: Summarise 13:4 and 13:9 in your own words
Describe the judgment pictures of 13:7-8
Point to the ransom promise of 13:14

nodes.t: Return, and the LORD will heal
nodes.d: The book ends with a call to take words and return to the LORD, who promises to heal backsliding, love freely and be like dew so that Israel flourishes, with a closing note that the ways of the LORD are right.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Hosea ends, with what Israel is told to do and what the LORD promises?
ev: Say what Israel is told to say and renounce (14:2-3)
Describe the LORD's promises in 14:4-7
Read the closing line (14:9)

nodes.t: Joel: overview
nodes.d: The word of the LORD to Joel: a locust plague and the near day of the LORD, a call to return with all the heart, the LORD's promise of restoration and of his Spirit poured out, and judgment on the nations.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} give a short summary of Joel and say where the 'day of the LORD' appears?
ev: Outline the book: plague (1), call and promise (2), nations judged (3)
Say what the phrase 'day of the LORD' is used for in 1:15 and 2:1

nodes.t: The locust plague and call to mourn
nodes.d: A devastating swarm strips the land's vines, fields and trees, and the offerings are cut off from the house of the LORD; old men, drunkards, farmers and priests are told to mourn and to fast and cry to the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the plague in Joel 1 and what the people were told to do?
ev: Describe what was destroyed (1:4-12)
Say whom Joel tells to mourn and what they are to do (1:13-14)

nodes.t: The army and the call to return
nodes.d: Joel pictures a great army and the day of the LORD as darkness, then the LORD calls the people to turn to him with all the heart, since he is gracious, slow to anger and may leave a blessing; priests are to plead for sparing.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Joel 2:12-13 asks of the people and why the LORD may be turned to?
ev: Describe the day of the LORD in 2:1-11
Explain 2:12-13 in your own words

nodes.t: Restoration and the Spirit poured out
nodes.d: The LORD pities his people, drives off the northern army, restores the years the locust has eaten, and promises afterward to pour out his Spirit on all flesh, with wonders before the day of the LORD and deliverance for all who call on his name.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the promise of 2:28-29 and the promise to whoever calls on the name of the LORD?
ev: List the restoration promises of 2:19-27
Say who receives the Spirit in 2:28-29
Read the promise of 2:32

nodes.t: The nations judged; Judah dwells for ever
nodes.d: When the LORD restores Judah he gathers the nations to the valley of Jehoshaphat to judge them for what they did to his people; the day of the LORD is near, and the book closes with Judah dwelling for ever and the LORD dwelling in Zion.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the nations are gathered in Joel 3 and how the book ends?
ev: Say why the nations are judged (3:2-6)
Describe the picture of harvest in 3:13
Describe the closing promise of 3:17-21

nodes.t: Amos: overview
nodes.d: Amos, a herdman of Tekoa, sees words concerning Israel in the days of Uzziah and Jeroboam: judgment on the nations and on Israel, five visions, and a closing promise to raise David's fallen tabernacle and restore Israel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain who Amos was and what his book says about Israel in a few sentences?
ev: Outline: nations (1-2), sermons on Israel (3-6), visions (7-9)
Say what Amos was before the LORD sent him (1:1, 7:14-15)

nodes.t: Judgment on the surrounding nations
nodes.d: Amos announces for each of Damascus, Gaza, Tyre, Edom, Ammon, Moab and Judah that for three transgressions, and for four, the LORD will not turn away punishment, naming the crime and sending fire.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name some nations in Amos 1-2 and say what pattern each oracle follows?
ev: Name some of the nations and a crime named for each
Notice that Judah is included (2:4-5)

nodes.t: Judgment on Israel's oppression and ingratitude
nodes.d: The LORD charges Israel with selling the righteous and the poor, profaning his name and silencing prophets, after he destroyed the Amorite and brought them out of Egypt; no strong or swift man will escape.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Israel is charged with in Amos 2:6-16 and what the LORD had done for them?
ev: List the sins in 2:6-8 and 2:12
Recall the LORD's acts for them in 2:9-11

nodes.t: You only have I known
nodes.d: Because the LORD knew Israel alone of all the families of the earth, he will punish them for their iniquities; the prophet speaks because the LORD has spoken, and the palaces and altars of Bethel will fall.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Amos 3:2 connects the LORD's knowing of Israel with punishment?
ev: Read 3:2 and say why it comes before punishment
Explain 3:7 in your own words
Describe the coming judgment in 3:11-15

nodes.t: Kine of Bashan; yet ye have not returned
nodes.d: Amos rebukes the kine of Bashan in Samaria who oppress the poor and mocks empty worship at Bethel and Gilgal; the LORD lists famine, drought, blight, plague and overthrow after which they have not returned, and calls Israel to prepare to meet God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the refrain of Amos 4:6-11 and what the LORD calls Israel to do in 4:12?
ev: List the disasters of 4:6-11 and the refrain
Say what Israel is told in 4:12

nodes.t: Seek the LORD and live
nodes.d: Amos laments for fallen Israel, tells them to seek the LORD and not Bethel, condemns those who trample the poor and pervert justice, warns that the day of the LORD is darkness, and says the LORD hates their feasts but wants justice to roll like water.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD says about Israel's feasts and songs and what he wants instead in Amos 5:21-24?
ev: Explain why the day of the LORD is darkness in 5:18-20
Describe what the LORD wants in 5:21-24

nodes.t: Woe to those at ease
nodes.d: Amos pronounces woe on the comfortable leaders of Zion and Samaria who lie on ivory beds and feast but are not grieved for Joseph's affliction; they will go into captivity first, since they have turned justice into gall.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how the people in Amos 6 lived and what the LORD says will happen to them?
ev: Describe how the leaders live in 6:4-6
Say what will happen to them in 6:7 and 6:14

nodes.t: Locusts, fire and the plumbline
nodes.d: Amos is shown locusts and a fire and pleads for Jacob, and the LORD relents; then he is shown a plumbline set in the midst of Israel with the high places and Jeroboam's house to fall.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the three visions of Amos 7:1-9 and how the LORD responds to Amos' prayers?
ev: Say what Amos asks in 7:2 and 7:5 and how the LORD answers
Describe the third vision (7:7-9)

nodes.t: Amaziah tells Amos to go
nodes.d: Amaziah priest of Bethel reports Amos to Jeroboam and tells him to flee to Judah; Amos answers that he was a herdman and fig gatherer whom the LORD took and sent, and announces judgment on Amaziah and exile for Israel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Amaziah said to Amos and how Amos answered?
ev: Retell the exchange
Say how Amos describes his own calling (7:14-15)

nodes.t: Basket of summer fruit; famine of the word
nodes.d: The LORD shows Amos a basket of summer fruit and says the end has come for Israel; Amos charges merchants with cheating and buying the poor, and the LORD announces mourning and a famine of hearing his words.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the famine described in Amos 8:11-12?
ev: Describe the vision and the LORD's explanation (8:1-3)
Name the merchants' sins (8:4-6)
Explain the famine in 8:11-12

nodes.t: No escape from the LORD
nodes.d: The LORD stands by the altar and says none can escape, though they dig to hell or climb to heaven; he will sift Israel among all nations yet not utterly destroy the house of Jacob, and sinners who deny the evil will die.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say how Amos 9:1-10 shows both the certainty of judgment and a limit placed on it?
ev: Describe how far the LORD's hand reaches in 9:2-4
Read the limit on judgment in 9:8-9

nodes.t: David's fallen tabernacle raised
nodes.d: The LORD promises to raise up the fallen tabernacle of David, so that Israel possess the remnant of Edom and the heathen called by his name, with abundant harvests and a restored land from which they will not be uprooted.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the promises that end the book of Amos?
ev: Say what the LORD will raise up (9:11)
Describe the promises of 9:13-15

nodes.t: Obadiah: overview
nodes.d: The one-chapter vision of Obadiah against Edom: Edom's pride is brought down, its violence against brother Jacob is condemned, and the day of the LORD brings deliverance on Zion and a kingdom that is the LORD's.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say who Obadiah's vision is about and give its three parts?
ev: Say who the vision is against (1:1)
Outline in three parts: pride (1-9), violence against Jacob (10-14), the day of the LORD (15-21)

nodes.t: Edom's pride brought down
nodes.d: The LORD says he will make Edom small, bringing down the one who dwells in the clefts of the rock and says in his heart that none can bring him down; his allies deceive him and the wise men of Esau's mount are destroyed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Edom feels safe in Obadiah 1:3-4 and what the LORD says about it?
ev: Say what deceived Edom (1:3)
Describe how far the LORD says he will bring Edom down (1:4)

nodes.t: Edom's violence against his brother
nodes.d: Edom is condemned for standing aloof while strangers took Jerusalem, and for rejoicing, entering the gate, looting and cutting off fugitives in the day of his brother Jacob's calamity.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list what Edom did in his brother's day of calamity according to Obadiah 1:10-14?
ev: List what Edom should not have done (1:12-14)
Say what relationship the text names between Edom and Jacob (1:10)

nodes.t: The day of the LORD and the kingdom
nodes.d: The day of the LORD is near on all the nations, and as Edom has done it will be done to him; on Mount Zion there will be deliverance, the house of Jacob will possess their possessions, and the kingdom will be the LORD's.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Obadiah 1:15-21 says will happen to Edom and to the house of Jacob?
ev: Read the principle of 1:15
Contrast the end of Esau with Zion in 1:17-18
Read the closing line (1:21)

nodes.t: Jonah: overview
nodes.d: A narrative of the prophet Jonah son of Amittai, sent to Nineveh: he flees, is caught in a storm and swallowed by a great fish, then preaches, Nineveh repents, and the LORD answers Jonah's anger with a question about pity for the city.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the book of Jonah in a few sentences and say how it ends?
ev: Retell the four chapters in order
Say what question the book ends on (4:11)

nodes.t: Jonah flees and the storm
nodes.d: Told to go to Nineveh, Jonah goes the other way toward Tarshish; the LORD sends a great storm, the sailors cast lots and Jonah is thrown into the sea, whereupon the sea calms and the men fear the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell why the storm came in Jonah 1 and how it stopped?
ev: Say what the LORD told Jonah to do and what he did
Tell what Jonah said about himself in 1:9 and 1:12
Say how the sailors responded in 1:14-16

nodes.t: Jonah in the fish
nodes.d: The LORD prepares a great fish that swallows Jonah for three days and three nights; from its belly Jonah prays, remembers the LORD and declares that salvation is of the LORD, and the fish casts him on dry land.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened to Jonah after he was thrown into the sea and what he prayed?
ev: Tell how long Jonah was in the fish
Describe what Jonah says in his prayer (2:2, 2:9)

nodes.t: Nineveh believes and God spares
nodes.d: The word comes to Jonah a second time; he cries that Nineveh will be overthrown in forty days, the people and their king fast, wear sackcloth and turn from their evil way, and God sees their works and does not do the harm he said.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how Nineveh responded to Jonah's preaching and what God did?
ev: Retell Jonah's message and the response of Nineveh
Say what God did in 3:10

nodes.t: Jonah's anger and the gourd
nodes.d: Jonah is angry and says he fled because he knew the LORD is gracious and slow to anger; the LORD prepares a gourd and then a worm and wind, and asks whether he should not spare Nineveh with its many people and cattle.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD teaches Jonah with the gourd in Jonah 4?
ev: Explain why Jonah was angry (4:2)
Describe the gourd, the worm and the question in 4:10-11

nodes.t: Micah: overview
nodes.d: Micah the Morasthite sees the word of the LORD concerning Samaria and Jerusalem in the days of Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah: three cycles of judgment and hope, with the ruler from Bethlehem, what the LORD requires, and pardon for the remnant.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline Micah as judgment followed by hope in each section?
ev: Notice the three 'Hear' sections (1:2, 3:1, 6:1)
Name two hope passages (4:1-5, 5:2, 7:18-20)

nodes.t: The LORD comes against Samaria and Judah
nodes.d: The LORD comes down from his temple as witness against the people; Samaria will become a heap and its idols be broken, and the wound reaches Judah to the gate of Jerusalem, with a lament naming towns of Judah.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD comes against Samaria and Jerusalem in Micah 1?
ev: Say what the LORD says is the transgression of Jacob (1:5)
Describe what happens to Samaria (1:6-7) and how far the wound comes (1:9)

nodes.t: Woe to those who covet; the remnant gathered
nodes.d: Micah pronounces woe on those who plot evil and seize fields and houses, and on those who silence prophets; the chapter ends with the LORD promising to gather the remnant of Israel like sheep with their king before them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the wicked did in Micah 2:1-2 and what the LORD promises in 2:12?
ev: Describe the sins in 2:1-2 and 2:8-9
Describe the promise of 2:12-13

nodes.t: Heads, prophets and priests judged
nodes.d: Micah charges Israel's heads with hating good, their prophets with crying peace for pay, and rulers, priests and prophets with judging, teaching and divining for reward while claiming the LORD is among them; Zion will be plowed as a field.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Micah says is wrong with Israel's leaders in chapter 3?
ev: List who is charged and with what (3:1-3, 3:5, 3:9-11)
Read what Micah says he is full of (3:8)
Say what happens to Zion (3:12)

nodes.t: The mountain of the LORD in the last days
nodes.d: In the last days the mountain of the LORD's house is exalted, nations come to be taught his ways, swords become plowshares and each sits under his vine and fig tree.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Micah says will happen in the last days to the mountain of the LORD?
ev: Describe what the nations say and do (4:2-3)
Describe the picture of 4:4

nodes.t: Zion in travail and delivered
nodes.d: The LORD will gather the lame and outcast as a remnant and reign in Zion; Zion must go to Babylon, where she will be delivered, and the nations gathered against her will be gathered like sheaves for her to thresh.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Micah 4:6-13 says about the remnant and Zion's trouble and deliverance?
ev: Say where Zion goes and where she is delivered (4:10)
Explain 4:12 in plain words

nodes.t: The ruler out of Bethlehem
nodes.d: A siege strikes the judge of Israel, yet from little Bethlehem Ephratah comes one to be ruler in Israel whose goings forth are from of old; he stands and feeds in the LORD's strength, is the peace against Assyria, and the LORD purges idols and horses.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Micah 5:2 promises and what the ruler will do?
ev: Read 5:2 and say where the ruler comes from
Describe what he does in 5:4-5
Describe the purifying in 5:10-14

nodes.t: The LORD's controversy: what he requires
nodes.d: The LORD pleads with his people, recalling Egypt, Moses, Aaron and Miriam and Balaam; asked what offerings please him, Micah answers that he requires justice, mercy and a humble walk, and the LORD condemns false weights and the ways of Omri and Ahab.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} state what the LORD requires according to Micah 6:8 and what question it answers?
ev: Retell what the LORD recalls in 6:3-5
Read 6:8 and state its three requirements
Name the sins in 6:10-12 and 6:16

nodes.t: Lament and waiting for the God of salvation
nodes.d: The prophet laments that the upright are gone and trust fails even in the home; he resolves to look to the LORD, bear the LORD's indignation for his sin, and expect to be brought to the light.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how the speaker of Micah 7:7-9 responds to a world of betrayal?
ev: Describe the lament of 7:1-6
Read 7:7-9 and say what the speaker resolves

nodes.t: Who is a God like thee
nodes.d: Micah prays that the LORD feed his flock and show wonders as at the coming out of Egypt; the book ends asking who is a God who pardons iniquity, delights in mercy, casts sins into the sea and keeps his oath to Jacob and Abraham.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Micah ends and what it says about the LORD pardoning sin?
ev: Read 7:18-19 and list what the LORD does with sin
Say whose oath is recalled in 7:20

nodes.t: Nahum: overview
nodes.d: The burden of Nineveh, the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite: the LORD is both a jealous avenger and a stronghold to those who trust him, and Nineveh's fall is described and explained.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Nahum is about and describe the LORD as he is shown in chapter 1?
ev: Say what the book's heading names (1:1)
Outline: the LORD's character (1), the city's fall (2), the reasons and a final lament (3)

nodes.t: The LORD: jealous, slow to anger, a stronghold
nodes.d: Nahum describes the LORD as jealous and avenging yet slow to anger, who will not acquit the wicked, before whom mountains quake, and who is a strong hold to those who trust him; he promises to break the yoke from Judah and cut off Nineveh's idols.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Nahum 1 shows the LORD as both a judge and a stronghold?
ev: Read 1:2-3 and 1:7 and describe what they say about the LORD
Describe the good news to Judah in 1:12-15

nodes.t: The attack on Nineveh
nodes.d: Nahum describes the assault on the city, with chariots, flooded gates and fleeing defenders, and its plunder, until the LORD of hosts declares himself against Nineveh and its lion's den.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Nahum 2 pictures the fall of Nineveh and who is said to be against her?
ev: Describe the attack scenes in 2:3-10
Read the LORD's declaration in 2:13

nodes.t: Woe to the bloody city
nodes.d: Nahum pronounces woe on a city full of lies and blood and compares it with No, which also fell; its strongholds, merchants and captains will fail, and no healing remains for a wound that all who hear of her applaud.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Nahum 3 compares Nineveh with No and how the book ends?
ev: Name the sins of the city in 3:1 and 3:4
Say what happened to No and why it is mentioned (3:8-10)
Read how the book ends (3:19)

nodes.t: Habakkuk: overview
nodes.d: The burden Habakkuk saw: his complaints about violence in Judah and the LORD's answers, the vision to wait for in which the just live by faith, woes on the proud, and a prayer ending in rejoicing in the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Habakkuk moves from complaint to rejoicing?
ev: Describe the pattern of complaint and answer in chapters 1-2
Say how the book ends (3:17-19)

nodes.t: How long? The LORD raises up the Chaldeans
nodes.d: Habakkuk cries to the LORD about violence and perverted justice, and the LORD answers that he is raising up the fierce Chaldeans to sweep through the land.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Habakkuk complains about and how the LORD answers?
ev: State Habakkuk's complaint (1:2-4)
Describe the LORD's answer (1:5-11)

nodes.t: Why dost thou look on the treacherous?
nodes.d: Habakkuk affirms that the LORD is everlasting and holy and has ordained the Chaldeans for judgment, but asks how a God of purer eyes than to see evil can look on the treacherous while they net the nations.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} state Habakkuk's second question and what he says about the LORD's character before asking it?
ev: Say what Habakkuk affirms about the LORD (1:12-13)
Describe the question he asks (1:13) and the picture of the net (1:14-17)

nodes.t: The vision to wait for; the just live by faith
nodes.d: Habakkuk stands on his watch; the LORD tells him to write the vision, which will surely come though it tarries, and contrasts the proud, whose soul is not upright, with the just, who shall live by his faith.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the contrast of Habakkuk 2:4 and say what the LORD tells Habakkuk to do with the vision?
ev: Say what Habakkuk does and what the LORD tells him to do (2:1-3)
Read 2:4 and state the contrast
Find where Paul cites it (Romans 1:17)

nodes.t: Woes on the plunderer and idolater
nodes.d: The LORD pronounces a series of woes on the one who increases what is not his, builds a town with blood, shames his neighbour and trusts speechless idols, and says the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the LORD's glory while he is in his holy temple.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name some of the woes of Habakkuk 2 and the hope of 2:14?
ev: List the woes by their beginning words (2:6, 2:9, 2:12, 2:15, 2:19)
Read 2:14 and 2:20

nodes.t: Habakkuk's prayer: the LORD marches forth
nodes.d: Habakkuk prays that the LORD in wrath remember mercy, then recalls the LORD coming in glory with the nations driven apart, the sea and mountains shaken, and the LORD going forth for the salvation of his people with his anointed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Habakkuk asks in 3:2 and what he recalls about the LORD in this prayer?
ev: Read the request of 3:2
Describe the LORD's appearing (3:3-6, 3:10-11) and its purpose (3:13)

nodes.t: Yet I will rejoice in the LORD
nodes.d: Habakkuk trembles at what he has heard, yet resolves that though fig tree, vine, olive, field and flock fail he will rejoice in the God of his salvation, who is his strength.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Habakkuk chooses to do in Habakkuk 3:17-18 even when everything fails?
ev: List what fails in 3:17
Read the response in 3:18-19

nodes.t: Zephaniah: overview
nodes.d: The word of the LORD to Zephaniah in the days of Josiah: the great day of the LORD on Judah and the earth, a call to seek the LORD, judgment on nations and Jerusalem, and promised joy for a humble remnant.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline Zephaniah and say what the 'day of the LORD' is in this book?
ev: Say when the word came (1:1)
Outline: judgment (1), call and nations (2), Jerusalem and remnant (3)

nodes.t: The great day of the LORD on Judah
nodes.d: The LORD says he will sweep away everything, stretching his hand against Judah and Jerusalem for Baal worship, mixed oaths and indifference; the day is near, a day of wrath and darkness that silver and gold cannot buy off.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the day of the LORD in Zephaniah 1 and why it comes on Judah?
ev: List the sins named in 1:4-6 and 1:12
Describe the day in 1:14-18

nodes.t: Seek the LORD; the nations judged
nodes.d: Zephaniah calls the meek of the earth to seek the LORD, righteousness and meekness, perhaps to be hidden in the day of anger; he announces judgment on Philistia, Moab, Ammon, Ethiopia and Assyria's Nineveh, with a place left for Judah's remnant.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Zephaniah 2:3 tells the meek to do and which nations are judged in the chapter?
ev: Read 2:3
List the nations and what is said of each
Say who gains the coast in 2:7

nodes.t: The oppressing city and the LORD within
nodes.d: Jerusalem is condemned as filthy and oppressing: she did not listen or trust the LORD, and her princes, judges, prophets and priests are corrupt, though the just LORD in her midst does no iniquity, and the LORD tells them to wait until he gathers the nations.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Zephaniah 3:1-8 describes Jerusalem's leaders and the LORD in her midst?
ev: List who is charged in 3:3-4
Say what the LORD hoped for in 3:7

nodes.t: The remnant restored; the LORD sings over you
nodes.d: The LORD promises to purify the speech of the peoples, leave a humble remnant who trust in him, and cause Zion to sing, for the LORD their king is in her midst, mighty to save, rejoicing over her with singing, and gathering the outcast.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Zephaniah 3:17 says the LORD does over his people?
ev: Describe the remnant in 3:12-13
Read 3:17 and say what the LORD does for his people

nodes.t: Haggai: overview
nodes.d: Haggai's four messages in the second year of Darius to Zerubbabel and Joshua and the remnant: build the LORD's house, take courage for its glory, receive blessing from this day, and the LORD's choice of Zerubbabel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Haggai calls the people to do and name two of the messages?
ev: Name the four dated messages (1:1, 2:1, 2:10, 2:20)
Say what the first message asks (1:8)

nodes.t: Consider your ways: build the house
nodes.d: Haggai tells Zerubbabel, Joshua and the people that it is not time to live in panelled houses while the LORD's house lies waste; they sow much and gain little, and when they obey the LORD says he is with them and stirs them to work.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell what the people were told in Haggai 1 and what they did?
ev: Say what the LORD says is wrong in 1:4 and 1:9
Describe how the people responded (1:12-14)

nodes.t: The glory of the latter house
nodes.d: The LORD tells the builders to be strong, for his Spirit remains among them according to the word covenanted when they came out of Egypt; he will shake the nations and fill the house with glory, greater than the former, and give peace in this place.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how the LORD encourages the builders in Haggai 2:1-9?
ev: Read 2:3-5 and say how the LORD encourages them
Describe the promise of 2:6-9

nodes.t: Holy and unclean; blessing from this day
nodes.d: Haggai asks the priests whether holiness or uncleanness spreads by touch and applies the answer to the people and their offerings, recalls their failed harvests, and says that from the day the temple foundation was laid the LORD will bless them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the questions Haggai asked the priests and the promise that ends the section?
ev: Retell the two questions to the priests (2:12-13)
Say what changes 'from this day' (2:18-19)

nodes.t: Zerubbabel the signet
nodes.d: On the same day as the blessing the LORD says he will shake the heavens and earth and overthrow the thrones of kingdoms, and promises to take Zerubbabel his servant and make him as a signet, for he has chosen him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the LORD promises Zerubbabel in Haggai 2:23?
ev: Say what the LORD says he will do to kingdoms (2:22)
Say what he promises Zerubbabel (2:23)

nodes.t: Zechariah: overview
nodes.d: Zechariah, prophet in the second year of Darius, receives a call to return, eight night visions about Jerusalem, Joshua and Zerubbabel, answers about fasting and promises for Zion, and two later burdens about the shepherd, the pierced one and the day of the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline Zechariah as visions, a question about fasting and two later burdens?
ev: Say that chapters 1-6 are visions and 7-8 answer a question about fasting
Name the two 'burdens' of 9-11 and 12-14 (9:1, 12:1)

nodes.t: Turn unto me, and I will turn unto you
nodes.d: In the second year of Darius the LORD tells Zechariah to say that he was sore displeased with the fathers, who did not heed the former prophets, and calls the people to turn to him so that he will turn to them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the invitation in Zechariah 1:3 and why the fathers are mentioned?
ev: Read the call of 1:3
Say what the fathers did when the prophets spoke (1:4-6)

nodes.t: The riders among the myrtle trees
nodes.d: Zechariah sees a night vision of riders sent through the earth; the angel of the LORD asks how long the LORD will withhold mercy from Jerusalem, and the LORD answers with comfort that he is jealous for Zion, will return with mercies, and his house will be built.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the angel of the LORD asks in Zechariah 1:12 and how the LORD replies?
ev: Describe the vision and the angel's question (1:8-12)
Describe the LORD's answer (1:13-17)

nodes.t: Four horns and four carpenters
nodes.d: Zechariah sees four horns that scattered Judah, Israel and Jerusalem, and four carpenters who come to terrify them and cast out the horns of the Gentiles.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the vision of the four horns and the four carpenters?
ev: Say what the horns are explained to be (1:19, 1:21)
Say what the carpenters come to do (1:21)

nodes.t: The man with the measuring line
nodes.d: A man goes to measure Jerusalem, but an angel says it will be inhabited like towns without walls, for the LORD will be a wall of fire and the glory in her midst; exiles are called to flee Babylon, and many nations will be joined to the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD says about Jerusalem's walls in Zechariah 2:4-5?
ev: Describe the vision and the message about walls (2:1-5)
Say what the LORD promises in 2:10-11

nodes.t: Joshua the high priest cleansed
nodes.d: Joshua the high priest stands in filthy garments before the angel of the LORD with Satan accusing; the LORD rebukes Satan, has the filthy clothes removed, says he has caused Joshua's iniquity to pass, and promises his servant the Branch and the removal of the land's iniquity in one day.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the vision of Joshua in filthy garments and what the LORD does for him?
ev: Retell what happens to Joshua's clothing (3:3-5)
Say what the LORD says about the Branch and 'one day' (3:8-9)

nodes.t: The lampstand and the two olive trees
nodes.d: Zechariah sees a gold lampstand with two olive trees; the LORD tells Zerubbabel that it is not by might nor power but by his spirit, that Zerubbabel who laid the foundation will finish the house, and that none should despise the day of small things.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD tells Zerubbabel in Zechariah 4:6 and 4:9-10?
ev: Read 4:6 and say whom it is spoken to
Say what Zerubbabel's hands do (4:9)
Describe the two olive trees (4:14)

nodes.t: The flying roll and the woman in the ephah
nodes.d: Zechariah sees a flying scroll that is a curse on thieves and false swearers, and an ephah in which a woman called wickedness is shut with lead and carried by two women with wings to the land of Shinar.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the two visions of Zechariah 5 and what each is said to mean?
ev: Say what the flying roll is and whom it enters (5:3-4)
Say what the woman in the ephah is called and where the ephah goes (5:8, 5:11)

nodes.t: Four chariots; crowns for Joshua; the Branch
nodes.d: Four chariots come out from between two bronze mountains as spirits of the heavens going throughout the earth; then Zechariah is told to make crowns and set them on Joshua the high priest, speaking of a man called the Branch who will build the temple and rule.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Zechariah is told to do with the crown and what is said about the Branch?
ev: Describe the vision of the chariots (6:1-8)
Describe the crown action and what it says of the Branch (6:11-13)

nodes.t: Fasting question: did ye fast unto me?
nodes.d: Messengers ask whether the people should continue the fast of the fifth month; the LORD asks whether they fasted for him and tells them to render true judgment and mercy, since the fathers hardened their hearts against the law and were scattered.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD says in Zechariah 7:9-10 in answer to the question about fasting?
ev: State the question that is asked (7:3)
Read the commands of 7:9-10
Say what happened because the fathers would not hear (7:11-14)

nodes.t: The LORD returns to dwell in Jerusalem
nodes.d: The LORD says he has returned to Zion and Jerusalem will be a city of truth with old people and playing children in her streets; he will save his people, make them a blessing, and tells them to speak truth and judge truly.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Zechariah 8:1-17 pictures Jerusalem when the LORD returns?
ev: Describe the picture of 8:4-5
Read the promise of 8:8
List the commands of 8:16-17

nodes.t: Fasts become feasts; nations seek the LORD
nodes.d: The LORD says the fasts of the fourth, fifth, seventh and tenth months will become joy and cheerful feasts, and many peoples and strong nations will come to Jerusalem to seek the LORD, with ten men from all languages taking hold of a Jew.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say how the LORD answers the fasting question and what the nations will do?
ev: Name the fasts that become feasts (8:19)
Describe what the peoples say and do (8:20-23)

nodes.t: Thy King cometh, lowly and riding on an ass
nodes.d: A burden against Hadrach, Damascus, Tyre and Philistia is followed by a call for Zion to rejoice because her just and saving King comes lowly on an ass; he cuts off chariot and bow, speaks peace to the nations, and the LORD saves his people.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the King of Zechariah 9:9-10 and what he does?
ev: Say what is said of the King in 9:9
Describe his rule in 9:10
Read the promise to prisoners in 9:11-12

nodes.t: The LORD visits his flock
nodes.d: The LORD tells his people to ask him for rain, rejects idols and false shepherds, and promises to strengthen Judah and Joseph, gather and bring them back, and make them strong in him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD promises his flock in Zechariah 10 and what he says about idols and shepherds?
ev: Say what Israel is told to ask (10:1)
Say what the LORD says of the shepherds and flock (10:2-3)
Describe the regathering (10:8-10)

nodes.t: Two staves and thirty pieces of silver
nodes.d: Zechariah is told to shepherd the flock of the slaughter and takes two staves called Beauty and Bands; the flock rejects him, he breaks the staves, is paid thirty pieces of silver which the LORD tells him to cast to the potter, and a foolish shepherd is announced.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell what Zechariah does with the two staves and the thirty pieces of silver?
ev: Name the two staves and what breaking each means (11:10, 11:14)
Retell what happens to the thirty pieces of silver (11:12-13)

nodes.t: Jerusalem a burdensome stone; they look on the pierced
nodes.d: The LORD will make Jerusalem a cup of trembling and a burdensome stone to the nations that gather against her, and will pour on David's house and Jerusalem the spirit of grace and supplications, so that they look on him whom they have pierced and mourn.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Zechariah 12:10 says the LORD will pour out and what the people do?
ev: Describe what happens to nations that attack Jerusalem (12:2-3, 12:9)
Read 12:10 and describe the mourning that follows (12:10-14)
