nodes.t: A fountain opened; the shepherd smitten
nodes.d: In that day a fountain is opened for sin and uncleanness and idols and false prophets are cut off; the LORD calls the sword against his shepherd, the sheep are scattered, and a third part is refined as silver and calls on his name.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the fountain of Zechariah 13:1 and what the LORD says about the shepherd and the refined third in 13:7-9?
ev: Read 13:1
Say what the LORD calls the sword to do (13:7)
Describe the refining of the third part (13:9)

nodes.t: The day of the LORD: king over all the earth
nodes.d: The LORD gathers all nations against Jerusalem, then goes forth to fight, standing on the mount of Olives; living waters flow, he is king over all the earth, the survivors keep the feast of tabernacles, and everything is holiness to the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Zechariah 14:9 says about the LORD and how the book ends?
ev: Describe the siege and the LORD's coming (14:2-5)
Read 14:9 and describe the closing picture (14:16-21)

nodes.t: Malachi: overview
nodes.d: The burden of the word of the LORD to Israel by Malachi: a series of disputes in which the LORD states a charge, the people ask how, and he answers, ending with the coming day of the LORD and the promise to send Elijah.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Malachi's disputes work and how the book ends?
ev: Notice the pattern of 'Wherein?' questions (1:2, 1:6, 2:17, 3:7-8)
Say how the book ends (4:5-6)

nodes.t: I have loved you
nodes.d: The LORD says he loved Israel, and when they ask how, he points to Jacob and Esau, saying he loved Jacob and hated Esau and laid waste Esau's mountains; he promises that he will be magnified from the border of Israel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the LORD answers the question 'Wherein hast thou loved us?' in Malachi 1:2-3?
ev: Read the exchange of 1:2
Say what happens to Edom's plans (1:4)

nodes.t: Polluted offerings and a great name
nodes.d: The LORD rebukes priests who despise his name by bringing blind, lame and sick animals as offerings and call his table contemptible; he says he has no pleasure in them and that his name will be great among the Gentiles everywhere.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what was wrong with the offerings in Malachi 1 and what the LORD says about his name?
ev: Describe the offerings and the priests' attitude (1:7-8, 1:12-13)
Read the promise of 1:11

nodes.t: The covenant with Levi corrupted
nodes.d: The LORD sends a commandment to the priests: his covenant with Levi was of life and peace, and Levi feared him and turned many from iniquity, but the priests have departed from the way, caused many to stumble and been partial in the law.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} contrast Levi and the priests of Malachi's day in chapter 2?
ev: Describe what Levi was like (2:5-6)
Say what the priests did (2:8-9)

nodes.t: Treachery against brother and wife
nodes.d: Malachi charges Judah with profaning the covenant of the fathers and marrying the daughter of a strange god, and with dealing treacherously with the wife of their youth, since the LORD hates putting away; they also weary him by saying evildoers please him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the LORD condemns in Malachi 2:10-16?
ev: Say what wearies the LORD in 2:17

nodes.t: The messenger and the refiner
nodes.d: The LORD announces a messenger to prepare the way before him and the LORD coming suddenly to his temple, like a refiner's fire who purifies the sons of Levi; he will be a swift witness against sinners, for he does not change.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe who is coming in Malachi 3:1 and what he does in 3:2-3?
ev: Say what is promised in 3:1
Describe the refiner (3:2-3)
Read 3:6

nodes.t: Return to me: tithes and offerings
nodes.d: The LORD tells the people to return, and when they ask how, says they have robbed him in tithes and offerings; he calls them to bring the whole tithe into the storehouse and promises to open the windows of heaven and rebuke the devourer.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD says about tithes and offerings in Malachi 3:7-12?
ev: Read the charge of 3:8-9
Describe the promises of 3:10-12

nodes.t: Is it vain to serve God?
nodes.d: The people say it is vain to serve God and call the proud happy; those who fear the LORD speak together and he writes a book of remembrance, and says they will be his jewels on the day he makes, spared as a son.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the book of remembrance in Malachi 3:16-17?
ev: Describe what the people complained (3:14-15)
Describe what the LORD does for those who fear him (3:16-17)

nodes.t: The day that burns; the Sun of righteousness; Elijah
nodes.d: The coming day burns the wicked like stubble, but for those who fear the LORD the Sun of righteousness arises with healing; the people are told to remember the law of Moses, and the LORD will send Elijah the prophet before the great day to turn hearts of fathers and children.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the two outcomes on the day of the LORD in Malachi 4 and what the LORD promises to send?
ev: Contrast the two outcomes of 4:1-3
Read the closing command and promise (4:4-6)

nodes.t: Luke: The Gospel Orderly Told
nodes.d: Luke writes an orderly account for Theophilus so he may know the certainty of what he was taught, from the births of John and Jesus to the resurrection, ascension and the apostles' commission.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Luke wrote his Gospel and where it begins and ends?
ev: Say who Luke addresses, why he wrote, and how the book begins and ends.

nodes.t: Luke's Purpose and Eyewitnesses
nodes.d: Luke says many have set out an account, that eyewitnesses and ministers of the word handed it down, and that he writes in order so Theophilus may know the certainty of what he was taught.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say why Luke wrote and who he says handed the story down?
ev: Name the reason Luke gives for writing and the sources he mentions.

nodes.t: Gabriel Promises a Son to Zacharias
nodes.d: While Zacharias serves in the temple at the hour of incense, the angel Gabriel says Elisabeth will bear a son, John; Zacharias doubts, is struck dumb, and Elisabeth conceives.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell what Gabriel told Zacharias and what happened to him because he doubted?
ev: Retell the angel's message, Zacharias's question and its result.

nodes.t: Gabriel Announces Jesus to Mary
nodes.d: In the sixth month Gabriel tells the virgin Mary, betrothed to Joseph of David's house, that she will bear Jesus, who will receive David's throne and be called Son of the Highest; Mary submits.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Gabriel told Mary about her son and how she responded?
ev: Say what the angel promised about Jesus and how Mary answered.

nodes.t: Mary Visits Elisabeth and Sings
nodes.d: Mary hurries to Elisabeth's house; the child leaps in Elisabeth's womb, Elisabeth blesses Mary, and Mary praises God for mercy, for scattering the proud and lifting the lowly, and for remembering Abraham.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell Mary's visit to Elisabeth and name things Mary praises God for?
ev: Retell the meeting and name two things Mary praises God for in her song.

nodes.t: John Is Born; Zacharias Prophesies
nodes.d: Elisabeth bears a son, the family insists on the name John, Zacharias's tongue is loosed, and he blesses God for the horn of salvation, the oath to Abraham, and his son who will go before the Lord.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Zacharias spoke again and what he said about John and God's promise?
ev: Describe how Zacharias regained speech and what he said about God's covenant and about John.

nodes.t: The Birth of Jesus and the Shepherds
nodes.d: A decree brings Joseph and Mary to Bethlehem, where Jesus is born and laid in a manger; angels announce a Saviour, Christ the Lord, to shepherds, who go and tell what they saw.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the birth of Jesus and the shepherds' part in it?
ev: Retell the birth, the angel's announcement and what the shepherds did.

nodes.t: Simeon and Anna in the Temple
nodes.d: Jesus is named and presented at the temple; Simeon, to whom the Spirit promised he would see the Lord's Christ, blesses God for salvation for all peoples, and Anna the prophetess speaks of him to those awaiting redemption.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Simeon and Anna said when they saw the child Jesus?
ev: Say what Simeon was waiting for and what he and Anna said.

nodes.t: The Boy Jesus in the Temple
nodes.d: At twelve, Jesus stays in Jerusalem after the Passover and is found after three days among the teachers; he tells his parents he must be about his Father's business and then returns home subject to them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the story of Jesus at twelve in the temple?
ev: Retell where Jesus was found and what he said, and how he lived afterwards.

nodes.t: John the Baptist Prepares the Way
nodes.d: In the fifteenth year of Tiberius the word comes to John, who preaches a baptism of repentance, calls for fruits worthy of repentance, answers the crowds, tax collectors and soldiers, points to one mightier, and is imprisoned by Herod.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain John's message of repentance and what he said about the one coming after him?
ev: List what John told the crowds, tax collectors and soldiers to do and what he said about the coming one.

nodes.t: The Baptism of Jesus
nodes.d: When the people were baptized, Jesus is baptized and prays; heaven opens, the Holy Ghost descends like a dove, and a voice from heaven calls him beloved Son.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what happened when Jesus was baptized?
ev: Say what happened at Jesus' baptism and what the voice said.

nodes.t: The Genealogy of Jesus
nodes.d: Luke lists Jesus' descent, as was supposed from Joseph, back through David, Abraham, Noe and Seth to Adam, who was the son of God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say who the genealogy in Luke 3 ends with and name some people on the list?
ev: Say where the list begins, which famous names it passes, and where it ends.

nodes.t: The Temptation in the Wilderness
nodes.d: Full of the Spirit, Jesus is tempted forty days by the devil and answers each of three temptations with 'It is written' and a word of Scripture; the devil departs for a season.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the three temptations and how Jesus answered them?
ev: Name the three temptations and how Jesus answered each.

nodes.t: Jesus Reads Isaiah at Nazareth
nodes.d: In the Nazareth synagogue Jesus reads the passage about the anointed preacher of good news and says it is fulfilled in their hearing; he points to Elias and Eliseus helping outsiders, and the crowd tries to throw him down.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus read in Nazareth and why the people were angry?
ev: Say what Jesus read, what he said about it, and why the people turned on him.

nodes.t: Teaching and Healing in Capernaum
nodes.d: Jesus teaches with authority in the Capernaum synagogue, casts out an unclean spirit, heals Simon's wife's mother and many at sunset, and tells the crowds he must preach the kingdom to other cities.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list what Jesus did in Capernaum and say why he went on to other cities?
ev: Name what Jesus did in Capernaum and why he moved on.

nodes.t: The Great Catch and the First Disciples
nodes.d: After teaching from Simon's boat, Jesus tells him to let down the nets; a huge catch breaks them, Peter confesses he is a sinful man, and Simon, James and John leave all to follow Jesus.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the great catch of fish and the call of Simon, James and John?
ev: Retell the catch and what Jesus said to Simon and what the fishermen did.

nodes.t: Jesus Cleanses a Leper
nodes.d: A man full of leprosy asks Jesus, if he is willing, to make him clean; Jesus touches him and he is cleansed, and is told to show himself to the priest as Moses commanded.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the healing of the leper?
ev: Say what the leper asked and what Jesus did and told him.

nodes.t: The Paralytic Let Down Through the Roof
nodes.d: Friends lower a paralysed man through the tiles; Jesus forgives his sins, answers the scribes' charge of blasphemy by showing the Son of man has power to forgive sins, and tells the man to rise and walk.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say why Jesus both forgave the man's sins and healed him?
ev: Explain why Jesus healed him after forgiving his sins.

nodes.t: Levi's Feast and the Question of Fasting
nodes.d: Jesus calls the tax collector Levi, who gives a feast; asked why he eats with sinners, Jesus says he came to call sinners to repentance, and he speaks of the bridegroom and of new wine and old wineskins.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain whom Jesus came to call and what his sayings about the bridegroom and new wine mean in the passage?
ev: Say who Jesus came to call, and what he said about the bridegroom and new wine.

nodes.t: Lord of the Sabbath
nodes.d: The disciples pluck grain on the sabbath, and Jesus cites David eating the shewbread and says the Son of man is Lord of the sabbath; on another sabbath he heals a withered hand, asking whether it is lawful to do good or evil.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe both sabbath conflicts and what Jesus claimed?
ev: Describe the two sabbath conflicts and what Jesus said in each.

nodes.t: Jesus Chooses the Twelve
nodes.d: After a night in prayer on a mountain, Jesus calls his disciples and names twelve apostles, including Simon Peter, Matthew and Judas Iscariot the traitor.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name several of the twelve and say how Jesus prepared for choosing them?
ev: Say what Jesus did before choosing the twelve and name some of them.

nodes.t: Blessings and Woes on the Plain
nodes.d: Jesus blesses the poor, hungry, weeping and hated for his sake, and pronounces woe on the rich, full, laughing and well-spoken-of.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} contrast the blessings and woes Jesus gives in Luke 6?
ev: Compare who Jesus calls blessed with who he calls woe.

nodes.t: Love Your Enemies; Be Merciful
nodes.d: Jesus tells his hearers to love enemies, bless those who curse them, do to others as they would have done to them, lend without hope of return, be merciful as the Father is, and not judge or condemn but forgive and give.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list what Jesus commands about enemies and judging others?
ev: Say what Jesus commands about enemies, mercy and judging.

nodes.t: The Blind Guide, the Tree, and Two Builders
nodes.d: Jesus uses sayings about blind guides, a log and a speck, trees known by fruit, and a good treasure of the heart, and ends with the builder on rock who hears and does his words versus the builder with no foundation.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the two builders and why hearing without doing is not enough?
ev: Explain what Jesus says separates the wise builder from the foolish one.

nodes.t: The Centurion's Servant
nodes.d: A centurion sends elders and friends to ask Jesus to heal his servant, saying a word is enough since he himself is under authority; Jesus marvels at such faith and the servant is found well.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the centurion's request and Jesus' response?
ev: Say what the centurion believed about Jesus' word and how Jesus responded.

nodes.t: Jesus Raises the Widow's Son at Nain
nodes.d: Seeing a widow carrying out her only son, Jesus has compassion, touches the bier and tells the young man to arise; he sits up and speaks, and the people say God has visited his people.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the raising of the widow's son at Nain?
ev: Retell what Jesus did at Nain and what the crowd said.

nodes.t: John's Question and Jesus' Answer
nodes.d: John in prison sends two disciples to ask whether Jesus is the one to come; Jesus points to the healings and the gospel preached to the poor, then calls John more than a prophet, the messenger sent before him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Jesus answered John's question and what he said about John?
ev: Say how Jesus answered John's disciples and what he said about John.

nodes.t: The Woman Who Anointed Jesus' Feet
nodes.d: At Simon the Pharisee's house a sinful woman washes Jesus' feet with tears and anoints them; Jesus tells of two debtors forgiven and says her many sins are forgiven for she loved much.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the story of the two debtors and how Jesus applied it?
ev: Explain the parable of two debtors and how it applies to Simon and the woman.

nodes.t: The Parable of the Sower
nodes.d: Jesus tours with the twelve and women who minister to him, and tells of a sower whose seed falls on four soils; he explains the seed is the word of God and the soils are ways of hearing, and tells them to take heed how they hear.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name the four soils in the parable of the sower and say what Jesus says each means?
ev: Name the four soils and what each stands for according to Jesus.

nodes.t: Jesus' Mother and Brothers
nodes.d: When his mother and brothers cannot reach him for the crowd, Jesus says those who hear the word of God and do it are his mother and brothers.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say who Jesus calls his family and why?
ev: Say whom Jesus calls his mother and brothers.

nodes.t: Jesus Calms the Storm
nodes.d: Crossing the lake, Jesus sleeps as a storm fills the boat; the disciples wake him, he rebukes wind and waves, and they marvel and wonder who he is.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the calming of the storm?
ev: Retell the storm and what the disciples asked afterwards.

nodes.t: The Man Among the Tombs
nodes.d: In the country of the Gadarenes Jesus frees a man possessed by a legion of demons; they enter swine that rush into the lake, and the healed man is told to return home and tell what God has done.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the healing of the man called Legion?
ev: Retell what happened to the man and the swine and what Jesus told the man to do.

nodes.t: Jairus' Daughter and the Woman with the Issue
nodes.d: Jairus asks Jesus to heal his dying daughter; on the way a woman with twelve years of bleeding touches his garment and is healed, and then Jesus raises the girl from death.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the healing of the woman and the raising of Jairus' daughter?
ev: Say what happened to the woman and to Jairus' daughter and what Jesus told Jairus.

nodes.t: The Twelve Are Sent Out; Herod Is Perplexed
nodes.d: Jesus gives the twelve power and sends them to preach and heal, taking nothing for the journey; Herod hears of him and is perplexed, saying he beheaded John.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jesus told the twelve and why Herod was perplexed?
ev: Say what the twelve were told to bring and do, and what Herod said.

nodes.t: Feeding the Five Thousand
nodes.d: When the crowd follows Jesus to a desert place, he tells the twelve to give them food; five loaves and two fishes are blessed and broken, all are filled, and twelve baskets of fragments remain.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the feeding of the five thousand?
ev: Retell what Jesus did with the loaves and fishes and how much was left.

nodes.t: Peter Confesses the Christ; Take Up the Cross
nodes.d: Jesus asks who people say he is; Peter answers 'The Christ of God', and Jesus says the Son of man must suffer, be killed and rise, and that his followers must deny themselves and take up their cross daily.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Peter's confession and what Jesus said discipleship costs?
ev: Say what Peter confessed, what Jesus foretold, and what he asked of followers.

nodes.t: The Transfiguration
nodes.d: About eight days later Jesus takes Peter, John and James up a mountain to pray; his appearance changes, Moses and Elias speak with him of his decease at Jerusalem, and a voice from the cloud says 'hear him'.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the transfiguration and what the voice from the cloud said?
ev: Say who appeared with Jesus, what they talked about, and what the voice said.

nodes.t: The Boy with the Spirit; Who Is Greatest
nodes.d: Coming down the mountain, Jesus heals a boy the disciples could not help, again tells them he will be delivered into men's hands, and answers their argument about greatness by setting a child beside him and telling John not to forbid one who casts out demons in his name.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus taught the disciples about greatness using the child?
ev: Say how Jesus answered the dispute about who is greatest.

nodes.t: Setting His Face to Jerusalem
nodes.d: As the time comes for him to be received up, Jesus sets his face toward Jerusalem; a Samaritan village refuses him and he rebukes James and John for wanting fire, then answers three would-be followers about the cost of following.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe Jesus turning toward Jerusalem and what he said to those who wanted to follow?
ev: Say what happened in Samaria and what Jesus told the three would-be followers.

nodes.t: The Seventy Sent Out
nodes.d: Jesus sends seventy others two by two ahead of him with instructions like those given the twelve, pronounces woe on unrepentant towns, and when they return rejoicing tells them rather to rejoice that their names are written in heaven.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jesus told the seventy and what he said to rejoice about?
ev: Say what the seventy were told to do and what Jesus said they should rejoice in.

nodes.t: The Good Samaritan
nodes.d: Asked by a lawyer what he must do to inherit eternal life, Jesus draws out love of God and neighbour; to the question 'who is my neighbour' he tells of a Samaritan who helps a man left by robbers after a priest and a Levite pass by.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the parable of the good Samaritan and say what Jesus told the lawyer to do?
ev: Retell the parable and say what Jesus told the lawyer to do.

nodes.t: Martha and Mary
nodes.d: Martha is distracted by serving and asks Jesus to tell Mary to help; Jesus says Martha is troubled about many things but one thing is needful and Mary has chosen it.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jesus said to Martha about Mary?
ev: Say what Jesus told Martha about Mary's choice.

nodes.t: Teach Us to Pray
nodes.d: Asked by a disciple how to pray, Jesus gives a prayer to the Father about his name, kingdom, bread, forgiveness and temptation, and teaches persistence with the friend at midnight and the Father who gives the Holy Spirit to those who ask.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jesus taught about how to pray?
ev: Say what the prayer asks for and what Jesus says about asking and seeking.

nodes.t: Casting Out Demons: Beelzebub and the Sign of Jonas
nodes.d: After Jesus casts out a mute spirit, some say he does it by Beelzebub; he answers that a divided kingdom falls, that he casts out by the finger of God, refuses a sign except the sign of Jonas, and speaks of light and the eye.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the charge about Beelzebub and Jesus' answer?
ev: Say the charge made against Jesus and how he answered it.

nodes.t: Woes on the Pharisees and Lawyers
nodes.d: At a Pharisee's table Jesus rebukes the Pharisees for cleaning the outside while inside is full of wickedness and tithing herbs while neglecting judgment and the love of God, and the lawyers for burdening men and building the prophets' tombs; the scribes begin to lie in wait for him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list the faults Jesus names in the Pharisees and lawyers?
ev: List some things Jesus faults the Pharisees and lawyers for.

nodes.t: Fear God, Not Men; Confess Christ
nodes.d: Jesus warns against the leaven of the Pharisees, says nothing hidden will stay hidden, tells his friends to fear the One who has power after death, assures them God knows every sparrow and hair, and promises the Holy Ghost will teach them what to say.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain who Jesus says to fear and what he says about sparrows?
ev: Say who Jesus tells his friends to fear and why they need not be afraid.

nodes.t: The Parable of the Rich Fool
nodes.d: Asked to settle an inheritance, Jesus warns against covetousness and tells of a rich man who plans bigger barns and is told 'thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee'.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the parable of the rich fool and what it warns against?
ev: Say what the rich man planned and what God said to him.

nodes.t: Do Not Be Anxious; Treasure in Heaven
nodes.d: Jesus tells the disciples not to be anxious for food or clothing, pointing to ravens and lilies, to seek the kingdom, and to give alms, for where treasure is, the heart will be also.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus teaches about worry using ravens and lilies?
ev: Say what Jesus points to about God's care and what he says to seek first.

nodes.t: Watchful and Faithful Servants
nodes.d: Jesus teaches being ready like servants awaiting their master's return, with the thief and the faithful steward as examples, and says to whom much is given much will be required.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus teaches about being ready for the Son of man?
ev: Say what Jesus says about readiness and about the faithful and unfaithful servant.

nodes.t: Fire, Division and Reading the Times
nodes.d: Jesus says he came to send fire and has a baptism to undergo, that his coming will bring division even in households, rebukes the crowd for reading the sky but not the time, and urges settling with an adversary.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Jesus says about division and what the crowd failed to discern?
ev: Say what Jesus says about division and about discerning the time.

nodes.t: Repent or Perish; The Barren Fig Tree
nodes.d: Told about Galileans killed by Pilate and eighteen killed by a tower, Jesus says those victims were not worse sinners and everyone must repent or perish, then tells of a fig tree given one more year to bear fruit.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus said about the Galileans and the tower and the fig tree?
ev: Say what Jesus says about those who died and what the fig-tree parable shows.

nodes.t: The Woman Bent Eighteen Years
nodes.d: Jesus heals a woman bound by a spirit for eighteen years in a synagogue on the sabbath; he answers the ruler's indignation by pointing to loosing an ox on the sabbath and calls her a daughter of Abraham.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the healing of the bent woman and Jesus' reply?
ev: Retell the healing and Jesus' answer to the ruler of the synagogue.

nodes.t: Mustard Seed and Leaven
nodes.d: Jesus compares the kingdom of God to a grain of mustard seed that grows into a tree and to leaven hidden in three measures of meal.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the mustard seed and leaven parables?
ev: Describe the two kingdom pictures Jesus gives.

nodes.t: The Narrow Door and Lament over Jerusalem
nodes.d: Journeying toward Jerusalem, Jesus tells those asking if few are saved to strive to enter the narrow gate before the master shuts the door, says people will come from every direction to the kingdom, calls Herod a fox, and laments over Jerusalem.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus says about the narrow door and his lament over Jerusalem?
ev: Say what Jesus says about the narrow gate and what he laments over Jerusalem.

nodes.t: Healing on the Sabbath and Humility at the Table
nodes.d: At a chief Pharisee's house Jesus heals a man with dropsy, and tells guests not to seek the highest seats and hosts to invite the poor, since the humble will be exalted.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jesus taught about humility at the Pharisee's meal?
ev: Say what Jesus did for the man with dropsy and what he taught about seats and invitations.

nodes.t: The Parable of the Great Supper
nodes.d: A man gives a great supper and invited guests make excuses about land, oxen and marriage, so the master sends servants to bring in the poor, maimed, lame and blind, and then those in the highways, and none of the first invited will taste it.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the parable of the great supper and who was brought in?
ev: Say what excuses were given and who was invited instead.

nodes.t: The Cost of Discipleship
nodes.d: To the great crowds Jesus says a disciple must put him before family and his own life, bear his cross, count the cost like a tower-builder or king going to war, and forsake all; salt that loses its savour is thrown out.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the tower builder and king illustrations about counting the cost?
ev: List what Jesus says a disciple must be ready to give up and the two cost-counting pictures.

nodes.t: The Lost Sheep and the Lost Coin
nodes.d: When Pharisees murmur that Jesus receives sinners, he tells of a shepherd seeking one lost sheep and a woman seeking one lost coin, and says there is joy in heaven over one sinner who repents.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the two parables of the lost sheep and coin and what they show about heaven?
ev: Say why Jesus told these parables and what the joy in heaven is over.

nodes.t: The Parable of the Prodigal Son
nodes.d: A younger son takes his inheritance, wastes it, feeds swine, and returns repenting; the father runs to welcome him with robe, ring and feast, while the elder brother angrily refuses to join and the father pleads with him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the parable of the prodigal son and name what the father does for each son?
ev: Retell the parable and say what the father says to each son.

nodes.t: The Unjust Steward and Serving Two Masters
nodes.d: Jesus tells his disciples of a steward who reduces his master's debtors' bills and is commended for shrewdness, then teaches faithfulness in little and says no one can serve God and mammon.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus teaches about money and faithfulness after the steward parable?
ev: Say what Jesus draws from the steward and what he says about two masters.

nodes.t: The Pharisees' Pride and the Law Stands
nodes.d: The covetous Pharisees deride Jesus, who says God knows their hearts and what men esteem is abomination to him, that the law and prophets were until John, and that not a tittle of the law will fail.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jesus tells the Pharisees about their hearts and the law?
ev: Say how Jesus answers the Pharisees who mocked him.

nodes.t: The Rich Man and Lazarus
nodes.d: Jesus tells of a rich man and a beggar named Lazarus who both die; Lazarus is carried to Abraham's bosom and the rich man is in torment, where Abraham says a great gulf is fixed and that his brothers have Moses and the prophets.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the story of the rich man and Lazarus and what Abraham said about Moses and the prophets?
ev: Retell the parable and what Abraham says about Moses and the prophets.

nodes.t: Offences, Forgiveness, Faith and Duty
nodes.d: Jesus warns against causing little ones to stumble, tells his disciples to rebuke and forgive a repenting brother even seven times a day, and answers a request for more faith with the mustard seed and the servant who does his duty.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jesus taught about offences, forgiveness and faith?
ev: Say what Jesus teaches about forgiving and about faith as a mustard seed.

nodes.t: Ten Lepers Cleansed
nodes.d: Ten lepers cry for mercy and Jesus sends them to the priests; as they go they are cleansed, and only one, a Samaritan, returns to give thanks.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the healing of the ten lepers and who came back to give thanks?
ev: Retell what happened to the ten and what Jesus said about the one who returned.

nodes.t: The Kingdom's Coming and the Days of the Son of Man
nodes.d: Asked when the kingdom comes, Jesus says it does not come with observation and is in the midst of them, then tells the disciples the Son of man will be revealed suddenly like lightning, as in the days of Noe and Lot, after he first suffers and is rejected.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Jesus compares his coming to the days of Noe and Lot?
ev: Say how Jesus describes the coming of the Son of man and what examples he uses.

nodes.t: The Persistent Widow
nodes.d: Jesus tells a parable that men ought always to pray and not faint: a widow keeps asking an unjust judge until he avenges her, and God will avenge his elect speedily.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the parable of the widow and the judge and what it teaches about prayer?
ev: Say what the parable teaches about prayer.

nodes.t: The Pharisee and the Publican
nodes.d: Two men pray in the temple: a Pharisee thanking God he is not like others, and a tax collector beating his breast and asking mercy; Jesus says the publican went home justified and that the self-exalted will be humbled.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} contrast the two prayers and say who went home justified and why?
ev: Contrast the two prayers and say who went home justified.

nodes.t: Jesus Receives Little Children
nodes.d: When people bring infants to Jesus and the disciples rebuke them, Jesus calls the children to him and says the kingdom belongs to such and must be received as a little child.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jesus said when children were brought to him?
ev: Say what Jesus said about the children and receiving the kingdom.

nodes.t: The Rich Ruler
nodes.d: A ruler asks what to do to inherit eternal life, says he has kept the commandments, and is told to sell all and follow; he goes away sorrowful, and Jesus says it is hard for the rich to enter the kingdom but possible with God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the story of the rich ruler and Jesus' words about what is impossible and possible?
ev: Retell what the ruler asked, what Jesus told him and what Jesus said is possible with God.

nodes.t: Jesus Foretells His Suffering Again
nodes.d: Jesus tells the twelve they go up to Jerusalem where things written by the prophets will be accomplished: he will be delivered to the Gentiles, mocked, scourged, killed, and rise the third day, but they understand none of it.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jesus told the twelve about Jerusalem and what they understood?
ev: List what Jesus says will happen and how the disciples responded.

nodes.t: The Blind Man near Jericho
nodes.d: A blind beggar near Jericho calls Jesus 'thou son of David', persists when rebuked, asks to receive his sight, and is healed; he follows Jesus glorifying God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the healing of the blind man near Jericho?
ev: Say what the blind man called Jesus and what happened.

nodes.t: Zacchaeus
nodes.d: Zacchaeus, a rich chief tax collector, climbs a sycomore tree to see Jesus; Jesus invites himself to his house, Zacchaeus promises half his goods to the poor and fourfold restitution, and Jesus says the Son of man came to seek and save the lost.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the story of Zacchaeus and what Jesus said about seeking the lost?
ev: Say what Zacchaeus did and what Jesus said he came to do.

nodes.t: The Parable of the Pounds
nodes.d: Because he is near Jerusalem and people expect the kingdom to appear, Jesus tells of a nobleman who gives ten servants a pound each before going away to receive a kingdom; on his return he rewards the faithful, rebukes the servant who hid his pound, and deals with the citizens who refused him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the parable of the pounds?
ev: Say what each servant did with the pound and what the nobleman did on his return.

nodes.t: The Entry into Jerusalem
nodes.d: Jesus sends two disciples for a colt, rides it toward Jerusalem as the disciples spread clothes and praise God, saying 'Blessed be the King that cometh', and weeps over the city that does not know the things of its peace.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell Jesus' entry to Jerusalem and why he wept?
ev: Retell the entry and say why Jesus wept over Jerusalem.

nodes.t: Jesus Drives Out the Traders
nodes.d: Jesus enters the temple and drives out those selling, saying his house is a house of prayer but they made it a den of thieves, and teaches there daily while the chief priests seek to destroy him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell what Jesus did in the temple and what he said about it?
ev: Say what Jesus did in the temple and what he said.

nodes.t: By What Authority?
nodes.d: In the temple the chief priests, scribes and elders ask by what authority Jesus acts; he asks them whether John's baptism was from heaven or men, they will not answer, and so he will not tell them either.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Jesus' question about John's baptism and why the leaders were trapped?
ev: Say what Jesus asked and why the leaders would not answer.

nodes.t: The Parable of the Wicked Tenants
nodes.d: Jesus tells of a vineyard owner whose servants are beaten and sent away and whose beloved son is killed by the tenants; he says the owner will destroy them and give the vineyard to others, and cites the rejected stone that becomes the head of the corner.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the parable of the tenants and say what Jesus said about the rejected stone?
ev: Say what the tenants did to the servants and the son and what Jesus said about the stone.

nodes.t: Tribute to Caesar
nodes.d: Spies sent by the scribes and chief priests ask whether it is lawful to pay tribute to Caesar; Jesus asks for a coin, asks whose image it bears, and says to render to Caesar what is Caesar's and to God what is God's.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the tribute question and Jesus' answer?
ev: Say how Jesus answered and why they could not trap him.

nodes.t: The Sadducees Ask About the Resurrection
nodes.d: The Sadducees, who deny the resurrection, ask whose wife a woman married to seven brothers would be; Jesus says those counted worthy of that world neither marry nor die, and the dead are raised, as Moses called the Lord the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Jesus' answer to the Sadducees about the resurrection?
ev: Say what Jesus said about the resurrection and how he used Moses.

nodes.t: David's Lord and Beware the Scribes
nodes.d: Jesus asks how Christ can be David's son when David calls him Lord in the Psalms, and warns the disciples about scribes who love long robes and best seats and devour widows' houses.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Jesus' question about David calling Christ Lord and his warning about scribes?
ev: Say the question Jesus asks about David and what he warns about the scribes.

nodes.t: The Widow's Two Mites
nodes.d: Jesus sees rich men giving gifts and a poor widow giving two mites, and says she gave more than all of them because she gave all she had.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the widow's offering and why Jesus praised it?
ev: Say why Jesus said the widow gave more than the rich.

nodes.t: The Temple Foretold to Fall; Signs and Persecution
nodes.d: As some admire the temple's stones, Jesus says none will be left on another; asked when, he warns about deceivers, wars and signs, and tells the disciples they will be brought before rulers, given words and wisdom, and not lose a hair of their heads.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} summarize what Jesus foretold about the temple and about persecution?
ev: Say what Jesus says will happen to the temple and what he tells disciples about persecution.

nodes.t: Jerusalem Surrounded and the Son of Man Coming
nodes.d: Jesus says when Jerusalem is surrounded by armies the disciples should flee, that days of vengeance will come, that they will see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power, and tells them to watch and pray; he gives the fig tree parable and says his words will not pass away.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus says about Jerusalem, his coming, and watching and praying?
ev: Say what the disciples are told to do and what they are told to watch for.

nodes.t: The Plot and Judas' Offer
nodes.d: As Passover approaches, the chief priests and scribes seek to kill Jesus; Satan enters Judas Iscariot, who agrees with them to betray Jesus for money.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how Judas came to offer to betray Jesus?
ev: Say who plotted, what Judas agreed to, and what the text says entered Judas.

nodes.t: The Last Supper
nodes.d: Jesus prepares and eats the Passover with the twelve, saying he desired to eat it before he suffers, and gives bread as his body and the cup as 'the new testament in my blood, which is shed for you'; he says one at the table will betray him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Jesus did and said at the Passover meal in Luke 22?
ev: Say what Jesus said over the bread and the cup and what he said about the betrayer.

nodes.t: Who Is Greatest: One Who Serves
nodes.d: The disciples dispute who is greatest; Jesus contrasts Gentile kings with himself as one who serves, promises them a kingdom, tells Simon that Satan desired to sift him but he prayed for his faith, and foretells Peter's three denials.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Jesus' teaching on greatness and his words to Peter?
ev: Say what Jesus said about greatness and what he told Peter.

nodes.t: Prayer on the Mount of Olives
nodes.d: On the Mount of Olives Jesus prays 'Father, if thou be willing, remove this cup... not my will, but thine be done'; an angel strengthens him, he prays in agony, and he finds the disciples asleep.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell Jesus' prayer on the Mount of Olives?
ev: Say what Jesus prayed and what he told the disciples.

nodes.t: Betrayal and Arrest
nodes.d: Judas comes with a crowd and betrays Jesus with a kiss; a disciple cuts off the high priest's servant's ear, Jesus heals it, and says to the leaders that this is their hour and the power of darkness.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the arrest of Jesus and what he did for the wounded servant?
ev: Say how Judas betrayed Jesus and what Jesus did for the servant.

nodes.t: Peter Denies Jesus
nodes.d: Jesus is taken to the high priest's house; Peter follows afar and three times denies knowing him, the cock crows, the Lord looks at him, and Peter weeps bitterly; Jesus is mocked and struck.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell Peter's denials and what he did after the cock crowed?
ev: Retell Peter's three denials and what happened after the third.

nodes.t: Jesus Before the Council
nodes.d: At day the elders, chief priests and scribes bring Jesus before their council and ask if he is the Christ and the Son of God; he says the Son of man will sit at God's right hand and answers 'Ye say that I am'.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the council asked Jesus and how he answered?
ev: Say what the council asked and how Jesus answered.

nodes.t: Jesus Before Pilate and Herod
nodes.d: The crowd accuses Jesus before Pilate, who three times finds no fault; he is sent to Herod, who mocks him, and Pilate at last releases Barabbas and delivers Jesus to be crucified.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the trial before Pilate and Herod and who was released?
ev: Say what Pilate repeatedly said and who was released.

nodes.t: The Crucifixion and the Thief
nodes.d: Jesus is led to Calvary with Simon of Cyrene carrying the cross, prays 'Father, forgive them', is mocked, and tells the repentant criminal beside him that today he will be with him in paradise.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jesus said on the cross to the Father and to the criminal?
ev: Say what Jesus said for those crucifying him and to the repentant criminal.

nodes.t: Jesus Dies and Is Buried
nodes.d: Darkness falls, the temple veil is torn, Jesus cries 'Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit' and dies; the centurion glorifies God, and Joseph of Arimathaea lays the body in a new rock tomb as the women watch.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the death of Jesus and his burial?
ev: Say what signs and words marked Jesus' death and who buried him.

nodes.t: The Empty Tomb
nodes.d: On the first day of the week the women find the stone rolled away and are told by two men in shining garments that Jesus is risen; the apostles think it idle talk, but Peter runs to the tomb and sees the linen clothes.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell what the women found at the tomb and what they were told?
ev: Say what the women found and were told and how the apostles reacted.

nodes.t: The Road to Emmaus
nodes.d: Two disciples walk to Emmaus when Jesus joins them unrecognised; he explains from Moses and all the prophets the things concerning himself, and their eyes are opened when he breaks bread; they return to Jerusalem to tell the eleven.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the Emmaus road and how Jesus opened the Scriptures?
ev: Say how the two disciples recognised Jesus and what he explained to them.

nodes.t: Jesus Appears and Ascends
nodes.d: Jesus appears to the disciples, shows his hands and feet and eats fish, opens their minds to the Scriptures, tells them repentance and remission of sins will be preached to all nations beginning at Jerusalem, and is carried up to heaven as he blesses them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus said to the disciples before ascending and how he left them?
ev: Say what Jesus showed them, what he told them to preach, and how he left.

nodes.t: John: Believe That Jesus Is the Christ
nodes.d: John presents Jesus as the Word made flesh through signs, 'I am' sayings, a farewell discourse, the cross and resurrection, and states that these things are written so readers believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and have life in his name.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why John wrote his Gospel and how it begins and ends?
ev: State why John says he wrote the book and name some signs or 'I am' sayings.

nodes.t: The Word Became Flesh
nodes.d: John opens with the Word, who was in the beginning with God and was God, through whom all things were made, who is life and light, and who became flesh and dwelt among us full of grace and truth; John the Baptist is sent to witness to the light.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what John 1 teaches about who the Word is and what he did?
ev: Say what John says about the Word before creation, in creation and in becoming flesh.

nodes.t: John the Baptist's Witness
nodes.d: Priests and Levites ask John who he is; he says he is not the Christ but a voice crying in the wilderness, and next day he sees Jesus and calls him the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world and the Son of God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say how John described himself and what he called Jesus?
ev: Say who John said he was and what he called Jesus.

nodes.t: The First Disciples
nodes.d: Andrew and another follow Jesus, Andrew brings Simon who is named Cephas, Philip finds Nathanael, who confesses Jesus the Son of God and King of Israel, and Jesus says they will see angels ascending and descending on the Son of man.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name the first disciples Jesus gathered and what Nathanael said about him?
ev: Name the first disciples called and what Nathanael confessed.

nodes.t: Water Made Wine at Cana
nodes.d: At a wedding in Cana of Galilee the wine runs out; Jesus has the stone waterpots filled and the water becomes wine, which John calls the beginning of his signs, manifesting his glory so that his disciples believed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the water becoming wine and what it revealed?
ev: Retell the miracle and what John says it showed.

nodes.t: Jesus Cleanses the Temple
nodes.d: At Passover Jesus drives the sellers and money-changers out of the temple; asked for a sign, he says 'Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up', which John says he spoke of the temple of his body.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus did in the temple and what he meant by raising the temple in three days?
ev: Say what Jesus did, what sign he named and what John says it meant.

nodes.t: Born Again: Nicodemus
nodes.d: Nicodemus comes to Jesus by night and is told that no one can see the kingdom of God without being born of water and the Spirit; Jesus compares the Spirit to wind and says the Son of man must be lifted up like the serpent Moses lifted so that believers have eternal life.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus told Nicodemus about being born again?
ev: Say what Jesus told Nicodemus about new birth and being lifted up.

nodes.t: God So Loved the World
nodes.d: The discourse continues: God gave his only begotten Son so that whoever believes should not perish but have eternal life; the Son came not to condemn but to save, and men loved darkness rather than light.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what John 3:16-21 says about God's love, belief and the light?
ev: Say what God gave, who receives life, and why people reject the light.

nodes.t: John: He Must Increase
nodes.d: John the Baptist, still baptizing, is told that Jesus baptizes and many come; he says he is only the bridegroom's friend and that Jesus must increase while he decreases, because the one who comes from above is above all.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain John the Baptist's words about Jesus increasing?
ev: Say how John responds to Jesus' growing following and what he says about the Son.

nodes.t: The Woman at the Well
nodes.d: At Jacob's well in Samaria, Jesus asks a woman for water, offers living water, shows he knows her life, and tells her that true worshippers worship the Father in spirit and truth, and when she speaks of Messiah he says he is he.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jesus offered the Samaritan woman and what he taught about worship?
ev: Say what Jesus offered the woman and what he said about worship.

nodes.t: The Harvest in Samaria
nodes.d: The woman tells the town, Jesus tells his disciples that his food is to do the will of him who sent him and to finish his work, and many Samaritans believe, some because of the woman and more because they heard him themselves.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Jesus' words about food and the harvest and how Samaritans believed?
ev: Say what Jesus said was his food and how the Samaritans came to believe.

nodes.t: The Nobleman's Son Healed
nodes.d: A nobleman at Cana asks Jesus to come heal his dying son; Jesus says 'Thy son liveth', the man believes and finds his son recovered at the same hour, and John calls this the second sign in Galilee.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the healing of the nobleman's son?
ev: Say what Jesus said, how the father acted and what he learned.

nodes.t: Healing at Bethesda on the Sabbath
nodes.d: At a feast in Jerusalem Jesus heals a man who had been ill thirty-eight years by the pool of Bethesda and tells him to take up his bed; because it is the sabbath the Jews persecute Jesus, and when he says his Father works they seek to kill him for making himself equal with God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the healing at Bethesda and why the Jews opposed Jesus?
ev: Say what Jesus did and why the leaders wanted to kill him.

nodes.t: The Son's Work and Authority
nodes.d: Jesus says the Son does only what he sees the Father do, gives life as the Father does, has been given all judgment, and that those who hear his word and believe have eternal life; the dead will hear his voice and come out of the graves to life or judgment.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus says about the Son's work, life and judgment?
ev: Say what Jesus says the Son does with the Father and what he says about life and judgment.

nodes.t: Witnesses to Jesus
nodes.d: Jesus names the witnesses to him: John, his works, the Father, and the Scriptures, which testify of him, and says Moses wrote of him and accuses those who will not come to him for life.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list the witnesses Jesus gives for himself and what he says about Moses?
ev: List the witnesses Jesus names and what he says about Moses.

nodes.t: The Feeding of the Five Thousand
nodes.d: Near Passover a large crowd follows Jesus; he tests Philip, takes a boy's five barley loaves and two fishes, gives thanks and distributes, all are filled and twelve baskets are gathered; the people want to take him by force to make him king.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the feeding of the five thousand in John 6?
ev: Retell the miracle and what the crowd wanted to do after.

nodes.t: Jesus Walks on the Sea
nodes.d: At night, with a wind blowing, the disciples row across the sea and see Jesus walking on the water; he says 'It is I; be not afraid', and the boat is immediately at land.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell Jesus walking on the sea?
ev: Say what the disciples saw and what Jesus said.

nodes.t: I Am the Bread of Life
nodes.d: The crowd seeks Jesus for the loaves; he says to labour for food that endures, that believing is the work of God, that Moses did not give the true bread from heaven, and that he is the bread of life; all the Father gives him will come and he will raise them at the last day.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus means by 'I am the bread of life' in this passage?
ev: Say what Jesus says he is and what he promises those who come to him.

nodes.t: Eat My Flesh, Drink My Blood
nodes.d: The Jews murmur that Jesus said he came down from heaven; he says no man comes unless the Father draws him, and that unless they eat his flesh and drink his blood they have no life; he contrasts himself with the manna their fathers ate.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus says in John 6 about the Father drawing and about eating his flesh?
ev: Say what Jesus says about the Father's drawing and about eating his flesh and drinking his blood.

nodes.t: Many Disciples Turn Back; Peter's Confession
nodes.d: Many disciples find the teaching hard and leave; Jesus asks the twelve if they will go too, and Peter answers 'to whom shall we go? thou hast the words of eternal life' and confesses him as the Christ, the Son of the living God; Jesus says one of them is a devil.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say why many disciples left and what Peter confessed?
ev: Say why many left and what Peter said.

nodes.t: Jesus and His Brothers: Going Up to the Feast
nodes.d: Near the feast of tabernacles, Jesus' brothers, who do not believe in him, tell him to show himself in Judaea; he says his time has not come and goes up later privately, while people murmur about him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what happened between Jesus and his brothers before the feast of tabernacles?
ev: Say what his brothers said, what he answered, and how the people reacted.

nodes.t: Teaching in the Temple at the Feast
nodes.d: In the middle of the feast Jesus teaches in the temple, saying his doctrine is from the one who sent him; he answers the charge about healing on the sabbath, the crowd debates whether he is the Christ, and officers sent to seize him do not.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jesus claimed about his teaching and how people responded?
ev: Say where Jesus said his doctrine came from and how the crowd divided.

nodes.t: Rivers of Living Water
nodes.d: On the last great day of the feast Jesus cries out that anyone who thirsts should come to him and drink and rivers of living water will flow from the believer, which John says refers to the Spirit to be given after Jesus is glorified; the crowd, officers and Pharisees divide, and Nicodemus speaks for a fair hearing.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus offered on the last day of the feast and what John says it means?
ev: Say what Jesus invited people to do and what John says the living water means.

nodes.t: The Woman Taken in Adultery
nodes.d: Scribes and Pharisees bring a woman caught in adultery to Jesus to test him; he says the one without sin may cast the first stone, they leave one by one, and Jesus tells her he does not condemn her and to go and sin no more.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the story of the woman taken in adultery and what Jesus said?
ev: Say what Jesus said to the accusers and to the woman.

nodes.t: I Am the Light of the World
nodes.d: Jesus says 'I am the light of the world', that whoever follows him will not walk in darkness, and defends his testimony as true because the Father who sent him also bears witness; he says those who do not believe that he is he will die in their sins.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain 'I am the light of the world' and what Jesus warns those who do not believe?
ev: Say what Jesus says about himself as light and what he says to those who do not believe.

nodes.t: The Truth Will Set You Free
nodes.d: To Jews who believed him, Jesus says continuing in his word means being his disciples and knowing the truth that makes free; he says whoever commits sin is sin's servant, and the Son sets free indeed, and denies that those seeking to kill him are doing Abraham's works.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus means by the truth making free and who he says is a servant of sin?
ev: Say what Jesus says sets people free and what he says about who is a servant of sin.

nodes.t: Before Abraham Was, I Am
nodes.d: The Jews accuse Jesus of a devil; he says Abraham rejoiced to see his day, and when they say he is not fifty and has seen Abraham, Jesus says 'Before Abraham was, I am', and they take up stones.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus said about Abraham and how his hearers responded?
ev: Say what Jesus said about Abraham and how the Jews reacted.

nodes.t: A Man Born Blind Is Healed
nodes.d: Jesus sees a man blind from birth, says the blindness is so God's works may be shown, declares himself the light of the world, anoints his eyes with clay and sends him to wash in Siloam, and the man sees.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how Jesus healed the man born blind?
ev: Say why the man was blind according to Jesus and how he was healed.

nodes.t: The Healed Man Before the Pharisees
nodes.d: The Pharisees question the healed man and his parents, divide over the sabbath, and cast the man out when he says Jesus must be from God; Jesus finds him, the man believes and worships, and Jesus says those who say 'we see' remain in sin.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell what happened when the healed man was questioned and what Jesus said to him afterwards?
ev: Say how the healed man answered the Pharisees and what happened when Jesus found him.

nodes.t: I Am the Door and the Good Shepherd
nodes.d: Jesus says he is the door of the sheep and the good shepherd who knows his sheep, lays down his life for them, has other sheep not of this fold, and has power to lay down his life and take it again.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the good shepherd teaching and what it says about Jesus' life and death?
ev: Say what Jesus says the good shepherd does and what he says about his life.

nodes.t: I and My Father Are One
nodes.d: At the feast of dedication the Jews ask Jesus to say plainly if he is the Christ; he says his sheep hear his voice and no one can pluck them from his hand and 'I and my Father are one', and they take up stones, but he escapes beyond Jordan.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus says about his sheep and his oneness with the Father?
ev: Say what Jesus says about his sheep and about himself and the Father.

nodes.t: Lazarus Is Sick and Dies
nodes.d: Mary and Martha send word that Lazarus is sick; Jesus says the sickness is for the glory of God, stays two days, then tells the disciples Lazarus sleeps and is dead, and Thomas says they may go and die with him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jesus said about Lazarus's illness and why he waited?
ev: Say what Jesus said about Lazarus's sickness and what he did.

nodes.t: I Am the Resurrection and the Life
nodes.d: Martha meets Jesus, who tells her that her brother will rise again and says 'I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live'; Martha confesses him the Christ, the Son of God, and Mary and the mourners weep and Jesus weeps.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jesus says to Martha about the resurrection and life?
ev: Say what Jesus said to Martha and what she answered.

nodes.t: Jesus Raises Lazarus
nodes.d: At the tomb Jesus has the stone taken away, prays to the Father, and cries 'Lazarus, come forth'; the dead man comes out bound in graveclothes.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the raising of Lazarus?
ev: Retell the raising of Lazarus.

nodes.t: The Council Plots to Kill Jesus
nodes.d: Many believe after the raising of Lazarus, but others tell the Pharisees; the chief priests and Pharisees hold a council, and Caiaphas says one man should die for the people, which John says was prophecy, and from that day they plan to put Jesus to death.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the council plotted against Jesus and what Caiaphas said?
ev: Say what the council feared, what Caiaphas said and what John says it meant.

nodes.t: Mary Anoints Jesus at Bethany
nodes.d: Six days before Passover a supper is made at Bethany; Mary anoints Jesus' feet with costly ointment, Judas objects but John says he was a thief, and Jesus says she kept it for the day of his burying.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell Mary's anointing of Jesus and Judas's objection?
ev: Say what Mary did, what Judas said and how Jesus answered.

nodes.t: The Entry into Jerusalem
nodes.d: The crowd takes palm branches and cries 'Hosanna', Jesus rides a young donkey as written, the disciples later remember this after he is glorified, and the Pharisees say the world has gone after him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell Jesus' entry into Jerusalem in John?
ev: Say how the crowd greeted Jesus and what John says the disciples understood later.

nodes.t: The Hour Has Come: A Grain of Wheat
nodes.d: Greeks ask to see Jesus; he says the hour has come for the Son of man to be glorified, that a grain of wheat must fall and die to bear fruit, that when he is lifted up he will draw all men, and a voice from heaven answers his prayer.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the grain of wheat saying and what Jesus says about being lifted up?
ev: Say what Jesus says about the grain of wheat and about being lifted up.

nodes.t: Unbelief and Jesus' Final Public Words
nodes.d: Despite many signs the people do not believe, which John says fulfils Isaiah, and many rulers believe but fear confessing him; Jesus cries that believing in him is believing in the one who sent him and that he came as light, not to judge but to save.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what John says about unbelief and what Jesus says about his words and judgment?
ev: Say why John says the people did not believe and what Jesus says about those who hear and reject his words.

nodes.t: Jesus Washes the Disciples' Feet
nodes.d: Before the Passover, knowing his hour has come, Jesus rises from supper and washes his disciples' feet; he says Peter will know later and that those he washes are clean, then tells them to wash one another's feet as he did.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the foot washing and what Jesus said it was for?
ev: Say what Jesus did, what Peter said and what Jesus told the disciples to do.

nodes.t: Jesus Identifies the Betrayer
nodes.d: Troubled in spirit, Jesus says one of the twelve will betray him; he gives a sop to Judas, Satan enters Judas, Jesus tells him to do quickly what he does, and Judas goes out into the night.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how Judas was identified and what he did?
ev: Say how Jesus pointed to the betrayer and what Judas did.

nodes.t: A New Commandment
nodes.d: After Judas leaves, Jesus says the Son of man is now glorified and gives a new commandment to love one another as he loved them, by which all men will know they are his disciples; he tells Peter he will deny him thrice before the cock crows.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jesus' new commandment is and what he foretold about Peter?
ev: Say what the new commandment is and what Jesus told Peter.

nodes.t: I Am the Way, the Truth and the Life
nodes.d: Jesus tells the disciples not to be troubled, that he goes to prepare a place in his Father's house and will come again; to Thomas he says 'I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me', and to Philip that seeing him is seeing the Father.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus says about the way to the Father and the place he prepares?
ev: Say what Jesus promised about the Father's house and what he said about the way to the Father.

nodes.t: The Promise of the Comforter
nodes.d: Jesus promises to ask the Father to give another Comforter, the Spirit of truth, who will abide with them and teach and remind them of all he said; he leaves his peace and says that those who love him keep his word.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jesus promises about the Comforter and the Holy Ghost in John 14?
ev: Say what Jesus promises about the Spirit and what he says about loving him.

nodes.t: I Am the True Vine
nodes.d: Jesus says he is the true vine, the Father the husbandman and the disciples the branches; they must abide in him to bear fruit, keep his commandments, love one another, and are called friends whom he chose.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the vine and branches picture and what abiding means?
ev: Say what Jesus says branches must do and what he says about love and friends.

nodes.t: The World's Hatred and the Witness of the Spirit
nodes.d: Jesus warns the disciples that the world hated him first and will hate them and persecute them, that the Comforter, the Spirit of truth, will testify of him, and that they will also bear witness.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the world hates the disciples and who will bear witness according to Jesus?
ev: Say why Jesus says the world will hate his disciples and who will testify.

nodes.t: The Work of the Spirit
nodes.d: Jesus says it is expedient that he goes away so the Comforter will come, who will reprove the world of sin, righteousness and judgment, guide the disciples into all truth and glorify Jesus.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jesus says the Spirit will do for the world and for the disciples?
ev: Say what the Spirit will do when he comes.

nodes.t: Sorrow Turned to Joy; I Have Overcome the World
nodes.d: Jesus says the disciples will weep but their sorrow will become joy, like a woman after travail, promises that the Father will give what they ask in his name, and says that though they will be scattered he has overcome the world.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Jesus' words on sorrow turning to joy and 'I have overcome the world'?
ev: Say what Jesus says about their sorrow and his last words about peace and the world.

nodes.t: Jesus' Prayer for Glory and for His Disciples
nodes.d: Jesus looks to heaven and prays for the Father to glorify the Son, says eternal life is knowing the only true God and Jesus Christ, and prays for the disciples he has kept, that the Father would keep them, sanctify them by truth, and not take them out of the world.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jesus prays for himself and his disciples in John 17?
ev: Say what Jesus asks for himself and for the disciples.

nodes.t: Jesus' Prayer for All Believers
nodes.d: Jesus prays for those who will believe through the disciples' word, that they may all be one as the Father is in him and he in the Father so the world may believe, and that they be with him to see his glory.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say who Jesus prays for in John 17:20-26 and what he asks?
ev: Say who Jesus prays for here and what he asks.

nodes.t: Jesus Is Arrested in the Garden
nodes.d: Jesus crosses the brook Cedron to a garden; Judas comes with soldiers and officers, Jesus says 'I am he' and they fall backward, he asks that his disciples go free, rebukes Peter's sword-cutting and says he must drink the cup the Father gave him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the arrest of Jesus in John 18?
ev: Say what happened when Jesus said 'I am he' and what he told Peter.

nodes.t: Before Annas; Peter Denies
nodes.d: Jesus is taken to Annas and Caiaphas and is questioned about his disciples and doctrine; meanwhile Peter at the fire three times denies being his disciple, and a cock crows.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell Jesus before the high priest and Peter's denials?
ev: Say what Jesus said to the high priest and what Peter did.

nodes.t: Jesus Before Pilate: My Kingdom Is Not of This World
nodes.d: The Jews take Jesus to Pilate; Pilate asks if he is King of the Jews, Jesus says his kingdom is not of this world and that he came to bear witness to the truth, Pilate finds no fault, and the crowd asks for Barabbas.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus told Pilate about his kingdom?
ev: Say what Jesus told Pilate about his kingdom and who the crowd chose.

nodes.t: Scourged, Mocked and Sentenced
nodes.d: Pilate has Jesus scourged and mocked with a crown of thorns; the Jews say he made himself the Son of God and, when Pilate seeks to release him, cry 'Crucify him' and say 'We have no king but Caesar'; Pilate delivers Jesus to be crucified.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how Pilate handed Jesus over to be crucified?
ev: Say what the soldiers did, what the Jews cried and what Pilate finally did.

nodes.t: The Crucifixion
nodes.d: Jesus carries his cross to Golgotha and is crucified between two others under a title 'Jesus of Nazareth the King of the Jews'; soldiers cast lots for his coat, he commits his mother to the beloved disciple, says 'I thirst' and 'It is finished', bows his head and gives up the ghost.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the crucifixion in John and name Jesus' last words?
ev: Say what Jesus said from the cross and what the soldiers did with his clothes.

nodes.t: His Side Pierced and the Burial
nodes.d: The soldiers do not break Jesus' legs but pierce his side, and John says these things fulfil Scripture; Joseph of Arimathaea and Nicodemus wrap his body with spices and lay it in a new tomb in a garden.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what happened to Jesus' body after his death and who buried him?
ev: Say what the soldiers did and who buried Jesus.

nodes.t: The Empty Tomb
nodes.d: Mary Magdalene finds the stone taken away and tells Peter and the beloved disciple; they run to the tomb, find the linen clothes lying, and the other disciple sees and believes.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell what Peter and the other disciple found at the tomb?
ev: Say what the disciples found in the tomb.

nodes.t: Jesus Appears to Mary Magdalene
nodes.d: Mary weeps at the tomb, sees two angels, turns and takes Jesus for the gardener until he says her name; she tells the disciples she has seen the Lord.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how Mary Magdalene met the risen Jesus?
ev: Say how Mary recognised Jesus and what she told the disciples.

nodes.t: Jesus Appears to the Disciples
nodes.d: On the evening of the first day Jesus stands among the disciples behind shut doors, shows his hands and side, says 'Peace be unto you', sends them as the Father sent him, breathes on them and says 'Receive ye the Holy Ghost'.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jesus showed and told the disciples on the evening of the resurrection?
ev: Say what Jesus showed them and what he told them.

nodes.t: Thomas and the Purpose of John's Book
nodes.d: Thomas, absent the first time, says he will not believe unless he sees and touches; eight days later Jesus appears and Thomas says 'My Lord and my God'; John says the signs are written that readers may believe Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and have life.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the story of Thomas and say why John says he wrote?
ev: Say what Thomas said and why John says the book was written.

nodes.t: The Great Catch and Breakfast by the Sea
nodes.d: Seven disciples fish all night without a catch; Jesus on the shore tells them to cast on the right side and the net is full, the beloved disciple says 'It is the Lord', Peter swims ashore, and Jesus gives them bread and fish by a fire of coals.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell Jesus' appearance by the sea of Tiberias?
ev: Retell the catch and how the disciples recognised Jesus.

nodes.t: Peter Restored and the Last Words
nodes.d: Jesus asks Peter three times if he loves him and tells him to feed his sheep, foretells how Peter will die, tells him to follow him and not worry about the beloved disciple; John says this disciple wrote these things and that the world could not hold all that Jesus did.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell what Jesus asked Peter and told him after breakfast?
ev: Say what Jesus asked Peter and told him to do.

nodes.t: 1 Kings: overview
nodes.d: 1 Kings opens with David old and Solomon made king (1:1-53), moves through Solomon's wisdom, temple and decline, then the division of the kingdom and the prophets Elijah and Micaiah under Israel's kings, ending with Ahab's death and Jehoshaphat and Ahaziah (22:53).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline 1 Kings in order, from Solomon's accession to Ahab's death?
ev: Name the main phases: Solomon's accession, the temple, the divided kingdom, Elijah and Ahab
Say how the book begins (David's old age) and ends (Ahaziah of Israel)

nodes.t: Adonijah exalts himself and Solomon is anointed
nodes.d: Adonijah declares he will be king, but Nathan and Bathsheba remind David of his oath, and David has Zadok and Nathan anoint Solomon at Gihon. Adonijah flees to the altar and Solomon spares him on condition of good conduct.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Solomon became king instead of Adonijah?
ev: Retell how Adonijah's attempt failed and Solomon was anointed
Name the people who stood with Adonijah and the people who did not

nodes.t: David's charge to Solomon and his death
nodes.d: David, nearing death, tells Solomon to keep the LORD's commandments so the LORD will continue his word about David's house, and gives instructions about Joab, Barzillai's sons and Shimei. David dies after reigning forty years and Solomon sits on his throne.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what David charged Solomon with before he died?
ev: Say what David told Solomon to do in order to walk with the LORD (2:3-4)
State how long David reigned and where he was buried

nodes.t: Solomon establishes his kingdom
nodes.d: Solomon has Adonijah put to death after Adonijah asks for Abishag, removes Abiathar from the priesthood, has Joab killed at the altar, and puts Shimei to death when he leaves Jerusalem against his oath. The text concludes that the kingdom was established in Solomon's hand.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Solomon dealt with Adonijah, Abiathar, Joab and Shimei?
ev: List the four men dealt with in chapter 2 and why each was judged
Find the verse that says the kingdom was established (2:46)

nodes.t: Solomon asks for wisdom at Gibeon
nodes.d: At Gibeon the LORD appears to Solomon in a dream and says "Ask what I shall give thee"; Solomon asks for an understanding heart to judge the people, and God also gives him riches and honour with a call to walk in his ways.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Solomon asked God for at Gibeon, and what God gave him?
ev: Say what Solomon asked for and what God added
Explain why the LORD was pleased with the request (3:10-11)

nodes.t: Solomon judges between two mothers
nodes.d: Two women claim the same living child; Solomon orders the child divided, and the mother whose heart yearns for her son is revealed. All Israel sees the wisdom of God in him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the story of the two mothers and say what it shows about Solomon's wisdom?
ev: Retell how Solomon found the real mother
Say what Israel concluded about Solomon (3:28)

nodes.t: Solomon's officials, provisions and fame
nodes.d: Chapter 4 lists Solomon's officials and twelve district officers, describes Israel dwelling safely and his wide dominion, and records his wisdom, proverbs and songs and the visitors who came to hear him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how 1 Kings 4 shows God keeping his word to give Solomon wisdom?
ev: Name the picture of peace in 4:25
Give two ways the chapter shows Solomon's wisdom or fame (4:29-34)

nodes.t: Solomon and Hiram prepare to build the temple
nodes.d: Solomon tells Hiram of Tyre that David could not build the house because of his wars, but that the LORD has given rest; Hiram supplies cedar and fir for wheat and oil, and Solomon raises a levy of workers.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Solomon, not David, built the house of the LORD?
ev: Say why David had not built the house (5:3)
Describe the agreement between Solomon and Hiram

nodes.t: Solomon builds the temple
nodes.d: The house of the LORD is built in seven and a half years of work with stone, cedar and gold, with an inner oracle holding two cherubim. In the middle of the building the LORD tells Solomon that if he keeps the statutes, God will dwell among Israel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the temple Solomon built and what the LORD said to him about it?
ev: Say what was in the inner room (the oracle) and what covered the house
State the condition and promise in 6:12-13

nodes.t: Solomon's palace and the temple furnishings
nodes.d: Solomon builds his own house over thirteen years, and Hiram of Tyre casts the two bronze pillars, the molten sea, bases, lavers and other vessels for the temple.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name some furnishings made for the temple and who made them?
ev: Name some of the bronze items Hiram made
Say how long Solomon took to build his own house (7:1)

nodes.t: The ark is brought into the temple and the glory fills it
nodes.d: At the feast Solomon and the elders bring the ark of the covenant into the oracle; there is nothing in it but the two tables of stone, and a cloud fills the house so the priests cannot minister.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened when the ark was brought into the new temple?
ev: Say what the ark contained (8:9)
Describe what happened when the priests came out (8:10-11)

nodes.t: Solomon blesses Israel and recalls the LORD's word to David
nodes.d: Solomon blesses the LORD for keeping what he spoke to David his father, that David's son would build the house, and says the place is set for the ark with the covenant the LORD made with Israel's fathers.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Solomon says the LORD had spoken to David about building the house?
ev: Say what the LORD promised David about the house (8:18-19)
Explain how Solomon says the promise was kept (8:20)

nodes.t: Solomon's prayer of dedication
nodes.d: Standing before the altar, Solomon praises the LORD who keeps covenant and mercy, asks that the promise to David be confirmed, and prays that God will hear and forgive in specific situations of sin, defeat, famine, a stranger's prayer and exile.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} summarise Solomon's dedication prayer and what he asks for?
ev: Say what Solomon asks God to do when his people sin and then repent (8:33-34, 46-50)
Find where Solomon asks God to keep his word to David (8:25-26)

nodes.t: Solomon blesses the people and the feast ends
nodes.d: Solomon blesses the congregation, urges their hearts to be perfect with the LORD, and the king and all Israel offer great sacrifices and keep a feast before sending the people home joyful.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the dedication of the temple ended?
ev: Say what Solomon urged the people to do (8:61)
Describe how the people went home (8:66)

nodes.t: The LORD appears to Solomon a second time
nodes.d: The LORD says he has hallowed the house and promises to establish Solomon's throne for ever as he promised David if Solomon walks in integrity, but warns that if Israel and their children turn away he will cut Israel off and cast out the house.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the conditions the LORD set before Solomon after the temple was finished?
ev: State the promise and the warning (9:4-7)
Say what the nations would conclude if Israel forsook the LORD (9:8-9)

nodes.t: Solomon's cities, labour and ships
nodes.d: Solomon gives Hiram twenty cities, raises a levy to build the temple, his house and cities, puts the remaining Canaanite peoples to forced labour, offers sacrifices three times a year, and builds a fleet that brings gold from Ophir.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Solomon used his labour force and wealth after the temple was built?
ev: Name some things built with the levy (9:15-19)
Say where the fleet gold came from (9:26-28)

nodes.t: The queen of Sheba visits Solomon
nodes.d: The queen of Sheba comes to test Solomon with hard questions, sees his wisdom and house, and blesses the LORD who set him on the throne. The chapter also records Solomon's great gold, ivory throne, chariots and horses.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell why the queen of Sheba came and what she said about the LORD?
