ev: Say what the queen concluded after seeing Solomon (10:6-9)
Name some signs of Solomon's wealth in the chapter

nodes.t: Solomon's heart turns away
nodes.d: Solomon loves many foreign wives from nations the LORD had forbidden, his wives turn his heart to other gods, and he builds high places. The LORD tells him he will tear the kingdom away, though not in his days and not all of it, for David's sake.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD was angry with Solomon and what he said would follow?
ev: Say what turned Solomon's heart (11:3-4)
State what the LORD said would happen and what he would hold back (11:11-13)

nodes.t: Adversaries and Jeroboam's promise
nodes.d: The LORD raises up Hadad the Edomite and Rezon of Damascus against Solomon, and the prophet Ahijah tears his garment in twelve pieces and tells Jeroboam he will rule ten tribes if he walks in the LORD's ways. Solomon seeks to kill Jeroboam, who flees to Egypt, and Solomon dies after forty years.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe Ahijah's sign to Jeroboam and what it meant?
ev: Name the adversaries raised up against Solomon
Explain what the torn garment pictured (11:29-31)

nodes.t: The kingdom divides at Shechem
nodes.d: Rehoboam rejects the old men's counsel and answers Israel harshly; ten tribes break away and make Jeroboam king while Judah stays with Rehoboam. The text says the cause was from the LORD, and Shemaiah forbids war against their brethren.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how the kingdom of Israel was divided after Solomon?
ev: Compare the counsel of the old men and the young men (12:7, 10-11)
Say which tribes followed Rehoboam and which followed Jeroboam

nodes.t: Jeroboam makes golden calves at Bethel and Dan
nodes.d: Fearing his people will return to Rehoboam if they go to Jerusalem, Jeroboam makes two golden calves, sets them in Bethel and Dan, appoints priests who were not Levites and ordains a feast. The text says this thing became a sin.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jeroboam did at Bethel and Dan and why it was sin?
ev: Say why Jeroboam made the calves (12:26-27)
List the changes he made to Israel's worship

nodes.t: The man of God from Judah and the old prophet
nodes.d: A man of God from Judah cries against Jeroboam's altar at Bethel, naming a child Josiah, and the altar is rent. He is told not to eat or drink there, but is deceived by an old prophet and killed by a lion on the way home.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the story of the man of God who came from Judah to Bethel?
ev: Retell how the man of God disobeyed and what happened
Say what the sign at the altar was (13:3-5)

nodes.t: Ahijah announces judgment on Jeroboam's house
nodes.d: Jeroboam's wife, disguised, goes to Ahijah about her sick son; Ahijah tells her the LORD will cut off Jeroboam's house and root up Israel from the land because of his sins. The chapter then reports Jeroboam's death and Rehoboam's evil reign in Judah, including Shishak's raid on Jerusalem.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the LORD said through Ahijah about Jeroboam and about Israel?
ev: Say what Ahijah announced about Jeroboam's house (14:10-16)
Name what Shishak of Egypt took from Jerusalem (14:25-26)

nodes.t: Abijam and Asa reign in Judah
nodes.d: Abijam walks in his father's sins, yet for David's sake the LORD gives him a lamp in Jerusalem. Asa does right as David did, removes idols and his mother Maachah from being queen, but the high places stay; he pays Benhadad of Syria to break with Baasha of Israel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Asa served the LORD and where he fell short?
ev: Say what Asa removed and what he left (15:12-14)
Explain how Asa dealt with Baasha's building of Ramah (15:17-22)

nodes.t: Nadab and Baasha, kings of Israel
nodes.d: Nadab of Israel walks in Jeroboam's sin and Baasha kills him and all of Jeroboam's house. The LORD then speaks through Jehu son of Hanani against Baasha for walking in Jeroboam's way.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the house of Jeroboam ended, and why Baasha was judged too?
ev: Say how Jeroboam's house ended (15:29-30)
State the word of the LORD against Baasha (16:2-4)

nodes.t: Elah, Zimri and Omri
nodes.d: Zimri kills Elah and Baasha's house, reigns seven days and burns the palace when Omri besieges Tirzah; Israel divides between Tibni and Omri, and Omri prevails, buys the hill of Samaria and does worse than all before him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} follow the quick succession of Elah, Zimri and Omri in Israel?
ev: Say how Zimri's reign ended (16:15-19)
Name the city Omri built and what he did in the LORD's sight (16:24-26)

nodes.t: Ahab begins to reign
nodes.d: Ahab son of Omri does evil above all before him, marries Jezebel daughter of the king of the Zidonians, serves Baal and builds an altar for Baal in Samaria. The chapter ends with Hiel building Jericho at the cost of his sons.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what kind of king Ahab was and who his wife was?
ev: Name three things that made Ahab worse than earlier kings (16:30-33)
Say who Ahab married

nodes.t: Elijah announces drought and is fed by ravens
nodes.d: Elijah the Tishbite tells Ahab there will be neither dew nor rain except by his word, and the LORD sends him to hide by the brook Cherith, where ravens bring him bread and flesh until the brook dries up.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how God provided for Elijah by the brook Cherith?
ev: Say what Elijah told Ahab (17:1)
Explain how the LORD fed Elijah at Cherith

nodes.t: Elijah and the widow of Zarephath
nodes.d: The LORD sends Elijah to a widow at Zarephath with only a handful of meal and a little oil; at his word she feeds him first, and the barrel and cruse do not run out.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened to the widow's meal and oil, and why?
ev: Retell what the widow had and what happened to it
Say whose word the meal and oil followed (17:14, 16)

nodes.t: The widow's son is raised
nodes.d: The widow's son falls sick and dies; Elijah prays and stretches himself on the child, the LORD hears and the child revives. The woman says she now knows Elijah is a man of God and the LORD's word in his mouth is truth.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the widow's son was brought back to life and what she said?
ev: Retell what Elijah did and prayed
Say what the widow confessed at the end (17:24)

nodes.t: Elijah meets Obadiah and Ahab
nodes.d: In the third year of the famine the LORD sends Elijah to show himself to Ahab; Obadiah, who feared the LORD and hid a hundred prophets from Jezebel, brings word. Elijah tells Ahab that he and his father's house have troubled Israel by forsaking the LORD, and calls for a gathering on Carmel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Elijah told Ahab when they met?
ev: Say what Obadiah did for the LORD's prophets (18:4)
State who Elijah said had troubled Israel (18:17-18)

nodes.t: The LORD answers by fire on Mount Carmel
nodes.d: Elijah challenges the people to choose between the LORD and Baal and sets a test: the God who answers by fire is God. Baal's prophets cry out all day without answer; Elijah's drenched sacrifice is consumed by the fire of the LORD, and the people declare that the LORD is God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the contest on Carmel and what it proved?
ev: Retell the contest and its result
Say what the people cried when the fire fell (18:39)

nodes.t: The rain returns
nodes.d: Elijah tells Ahab to eat, because there is the sound of abundance of rain; after he prays and his servant looks seven times, a small cloud rises and heavy rain falls.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the drought ended in Elijah's day?
ev: Say what Elijah's servant saw on the seventh look (18:44)
Explain what this ended (compare 17:1)

nodes.t: Elijah flees from Jezebel
nodes.d: Jezebel vows to kill Elijah, and he flees to the wilderness and asks to die under a juniper tree; an angel touches him and feeds him, and he walks forty days and nights to Horeb.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell why Elijah ran away, and how God cared for him?
ev: Say what led Elijah to flee (19:1-3)
Describe how the LORD cared for him (19:5-8)

nodes.t: The LORD speaks to Elijah at Horeb
nodes.d: At Horeb Elijah complains that he alone is left; the LORD is not in the wind, earthquake or fire but in a still small voice, and sends him to anoint Hazael, Jehu and Elisha, saying he has left seven thousand who have not bowed to Baal.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD told Elijah at Horeb and how he spoke?
ev: Describe the wind, earthquake, fire and voice
State the three people Elijah was told to anoint and the number left in Israel

nodes.t: Elijah calls Elisha
nodes.d: Elijah finds Elisha son of Shaphat ploughing with twelve yoke of oxen and casts his mantle on him; Elisha slaughters a yoke of oxen, boils the flesh, takes leave of his parents and follows Elijah.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Elisha was called to follow Elijah?
ev: Say what Elijah did to call Elisha (19:19)
Say what Elisha did before following

nodes.t: Israel defeats Benhadad at Samaria
nodes.d: Benhadad of Syria and thirty-two kings demand Ahab's silver, gold and family; a prophet tells Ahab the LORD will deliver the host into his hand by the young men of the provincial princes, and Israel wins.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Israel beat the Syrian army at Samaria?
ev: Say what the prophet promised and why (20:13)
Describe how the battle went (20:15-21)

nodes.t: Aphek and Ahab spares Benhadad
nodes.d: The Syrians say the LORD is a god of the hills, so the LORD gives Israel victory on the plain at Aphek; Ahab then makes a covenant with Benhadad and lets him go. A prophet, disguised, tells Ahab that for letting go the man the LORD appointed to destruction, his life will go for Benhadad's life.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD was displeased when Ahab let Benhadad go?
ev: Say what the Syrians said about the LORD and what the LORD answered (20:23, 28)
Explain the prophet's message to Ahab (20:42)

nodes.t: Naboth's vineyard
nodes.d: Ahab wants Naboth's vineyard, but Naboth will not give his fathers' inheritance; Jezebel arranges false witnesses so Naboth is stoned and Ahab takes the vineyard.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how Ahab and Jezebel took Naboth's vineyard, and what was wrong with it?
ev: Say why Naboth refused (21:3)
Describe what Jezebel did to get the vineyard

nodes.t: Elijah pronounces judgment on Ahab
nodes.d: The LORD sends Elijah to Ahab in Naboth's vineyard: Ahab's house will be cut off like Jeroboam's and Baasha's and the dogs will eat Jezebel. Ahab tears his clothes and humbles himself, and the LORD says the evil will not come in his days but in his son's.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Elijah told Ahab about Naboth's vineyard and what happened when Ahab humbled himself?
ev: State the judgment on Ahab and on Jezebel (21:21-24)
Say how the LORD responded when Ahab humbled himself (21:27-29)

nodes.t: Micaiah prophesies against Ahab
nodes.d: Ahab asks Jehoshaphat to join him at Ramoth-gilead; four hundred prophets say go, but Micaiah, after saying the LORD's word, describes Israel scattered as sheep without a shepherd and a lying spirit in the prophets' mouths. Ahab puts Micaiah in prison.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Jehoshaphat wanted to hear a prophet of the LORD and what Micaiah said?
ev: Compare the four hundred prophets and Micaiah
Say what Ahab did with Micaiah (22:26-27)

nodes.t: Ahab dies at Ramoth-gilead
nodes.d: Ahab disguises himself in battle but a man draws a bow at random and strikes him; he dies, and the dogs lick his blood as the LORD had said.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Ahab died and how it matched what the LORD said?
ev: Say how Ahab tried to avoid Micaiah's word and what happened
Find the verse that says his death was according to the LORD's word (22:38)

nodes.t: Jehoshaphat of Judah and Ahaziah of Israel
nodes.d: Jehoshaphat walks in the ways of Asa and does right, though the high places remain; his ships to Ophir are broken. Ahaziah son of Ahab reigns in Israel, serving Baal as his father did.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} compare Jehoshaphat and Ahaziah as the book of 1 Kings ends?
ev: Say how Jehoshaphat is described (22:43)
Say how Ahaziah is described (22:52-53)

nodes.t: 2 Kings: overview
nodes.d: 2 Kings continues the divided kingdom from Ahaziah of Israel through Elijah and Elisha, the end of the house of Ahab, the fall of Samaria and the exile of Israel (ch. 17), the kings of Judah including Hezekiah and Josiah, and the exile of Judah to Babylon (ch. 25).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline 2 Kings in order, from Elijah's last days to the exile in Babylon?
ev: Name the two kingdoms and say how each ends (ch. 17 and ch. 25)
Name Elijah, Elisha, Hezekiah and Josiah and where they appear

nodes.t: Ahaziah consults Baal-zebub and fire falls
nodes.d: Ahaziah, hurt in a fall, sends to ask Baal-zebub god of Ekron whether he will recover; Elijah meets the messengers and says he will die because there is a God in Israel. Fire from heaven consumes two captains of fifty, and Elijah goes with the third.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell why Elijah sent Ahaziah this message and what happened to the soldiers?
ev: Say why Ahaziah was told he would die (1:3-4, 16)
Retell what happened to the captains of fifty

nodes.t: Elijah is taken up and Elisha receives his mantle
nodes.d: Elijah and Elisha cross Jordan, Elisha asks for a double portion of Elijah's spirit, and Elijah is taken up by a whirlwind with a chariot of fire. Elisha takes up the fallen mantle, strikes the Jordan and crosses, and the sons of the prophets say the spirit of Elijah rests on him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Elijah left the earth and who took up his work?
ev: Describe how Elijah left and what Elisha picked up
Say what the sons of the prophets recognised (2:15)

nodes.t: Elisha heals the spring and the boys mock him
nodes.d: At Jericho Elisha casts salt into the spring and the waters are healed, according to his word; going up to Bethel, small boys mock him and two she bears tear forty-two of them after he curses them in the LORD's name.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Elisha did at Jericho and what happened on the road to Bethel?
ev: Say what Elisha did to the waters at Jericho and by whose word
Describe what happened at Bethel (2:23-24)

nodes.t: Three kings and Moab: water in the valley
nodes.d: Jehoram of Israel, Jehoshaphat of Judah and the king of Edom march against rebel Moab and run out of water; Elisha, for Jehoshaphat's sake, says the LORD will fill the valley and give Moab into their hand. Water comes by morning and Moab is defeated, though the king of Moab offers his eldest son on the wall.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how the LORD provided for the three kings, and why Elisha helped?
ev: Say why Elisha agreed to inquire of the LORD (3:13-14)
Describe how the water came (3:16-20)

nodes.t: Elisha and the widow's oil
nodes.d: A prophet's widow cries to Elisha because a creditor will take her two sons; Elisha tells her to borrow empty vessels and pour from her small pot of oil, and the oil flows until all the vessels are full, so she sells it and pays her debt.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how Elisha helped the widow pay her debt?
ev: Say what the widow had in the house and what happened to it
Say what she did with the oil afterwards (4:7)

nodes.t: The Shunammite woman's son
nodes.d: A woman of Shunem builds a room for Elisha and, as he promised, bears a son; when the boy later dies, she goes to Elisha at Carmel, and Elisha prays, stretches himself on the child, and the boy sneezes and opens his eyes.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how the Shunammite's son was brought back to life?
ev: Say what the woman did for Elisha and what he promised her
Describe how Elisha restored the child

nodes.t: Death in the pot and the loaves
nodes.d: In a famine at Gilgal, wild gourds make the stew deadly and Elisha casts in meal so it is harmless; he then has a hundred men fed from twenty loaves, with some left, according to the LORD's word.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Elisha did for the sons of the prophets during the famine?
ev: Say how Elisha made the pottage safe
Say what the LORD said about the twenty loaves (4:43)

nodes.t: Naaman is healed of leprosy
nodes.d: Naaman, the Syrian commander, hears from an Israelite servant girl of the prophet in Samaria, goes to Elisha and is told to wash seven times in Jordan; he is angry but obeys and is healed, and confesses there is no God in all the earth but in Israel. Gehazi takes a reward by deceit and Naaman's leprosy comes on him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell the story of Naaman, the servant girl and Gehazi?
ev: Retell why Naaman was angry and what changed his mind
Say what happened to Gehazi and why (5:20-27)

nodes.t: The iron axe head floats
nodes.d: While the sons of the prophets cut beams at Jordan, a borrowed axe head falls into the water; Elisha casts in a stick and the iron swims, and the man takes it up.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell what happened to the borrowed axe head?
ev: Say what Elisha threw into the water and what happened
Say why the man was distressed (6:5)

nodes.t: Elisha and the Syrian army at Dothan
nodes.d: The king of Syria sends an army to take Elisha at Dothan; Elisha's servant sees them, Elisha prays and the servant sees chariots of fire around the mountain. The Syrians are struck blind, led to Samaria, given food and sent home, and the bands of Syria stop coming into Israel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Elisha's servant saw at Dothan and how the story ended?
ev: Say what the servant saw when his eyes were opened (6:17)
Explain how Elisha told the king of Israel to treat the Syrians (6:21-23)

nodes.t: Famine in besieged Samaria
nodes.d: Benhadad besieges Samaria, a great famine follows and the king of Israel, hearing a woman's terrible plea, tears his clothes and swears to take Elisha's head; Elisha tells the elders the king's messenger is coming.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the famine in Samaria and how the king reacted?
ev: Describe the state of the city (6:25)
Say what the king blamed and decided (6:31, 33)

nodes.t: The LORD lifts the siege of Samaria
nodes.d: Elisha says that by tomorrow fine flour will sell for a shekel at the gate; four lepers find the Syrian camp empty because the LORD made the Syrians hear the noise of a great host, and the city is plundered. The lord who doubted sees it but dies in the gate trampled by the crowd.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how the siege of Samaria ended and how Elisha's word came true?
ev: Say what Elisha prophesied (7:1) and how it happened
Say what happened to the doubting lord (7:17-20)

nodes.t: The Shunammite's land and Elisha at Damascus
nodes.d: Elisha warns the Shunammite of a seven-year famine; on her return the king hears about Elisha's deeds from Gehazi and restores her land. Elisha later tells Hazael he will be king of Syria and do great evil to Israel, and Hazael kills Benhadad.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened to the Shunammite woman after the famine, and what Elisha said to Hazael?
ev: Say what the king restored to the woman and why (8:4-6)
Say what Elisha told Hazael and how Elisha reacted (8:12)

nodes.t: Jehoram and Ahaziah of Judah
nodes.d: Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat marries a daughter of Ahab and does evil, yet the LORD will not destroy Judah for David's sake, as he promised David a light for his children. Edom revolts; his son Ahaziah walks in the way of Ahab's house and goes with Joram of Israel to fight Hazael at Ramoth-gilead.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why God spared Judah despite Jehoram's evil?
ev: Say why the LORD did not destroy Judah (8:19)
Say how Jehoram and Ahaziah are compared to the house of Ahab (8:18, 27)

nodes.t: Jehu is anointed king over Israel
nodes.d: Elisha sends a young prophet to Ramoth-gilead to pour oil on Jehu's head and announce that he will strike the house of Ahab, and that dogs will eat Jezebel; the captains acclaim Jehu king.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Jehu was anointed and what he was told to do?
ev: Say what Jehu was told to do (9:6-10)
Describe how the other captains responded (9:13)

nodes.t: Jehu strikes Joram and Ahaziah
nodes.d: Jehu drives to Jezreel and shoots Joram, throwing him into Naboth's field according to the LORD's word; Ahaziah of Judah flees and is killed too.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Joram and Ahaziah were killed?
ev: Say where Joram died and why Jehu cited Naboth (9:25-26)
Say what happened to Ahaziah of Judah

nodes.t: The death of Jezebel
nodes.d: Jehu enters Jezreel; Jezebel is thrown from the window, trampled, and the dogs eat her, so that Jehu says it is the word of the LORD spoken by Elijah.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Elijah's word about Jezebel came true?
ev: Say how Jezebel died and what remained
Find the verse that links her death to Elijah's word (9:36)

nodes.t: Jehu destroys the house of Ahab and the worship of Baal
nodes.d: Jehu has Ahab's seventy sons killed in Samaria, kills Ahaziah's brethren and the remainder of Ahab's house, then gathers the worshippers of Baal in the house of Baal and has them slain, destroying the house and image of Baal.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jehu did to Ahab's house and to Baal worship in Israel?
ev: Say how Jehu summoned the worshippers of Baal and what he did
Say whose word Jehu says is fulfilled (10:10)

nodes.t: Jehu's reign and its limits
nodes.d: The LORD tells Jehu that his sons to the fourth generation will sit on Israel's throne, but Jehu does not depart from Jeroboam's calves or walk in the law with all his heart, and the LORD begins to cut Israel short by Hazael.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain both the promise to Jehu and where he fell short?
ev: Say what the LORD promised Jehu and what Jehu failed to do (10:30-31)
Say who began to cut Israel short (10:32)

nodes.t: Athaliah and the hidden king Joash
nodes.d: After Ahaziah's death Athaliah destroys the royal seed and reigns six years; Jehosheba hides the baby Joash in the house of the LORD, and in the seventh year Jehoiada anoints him, Athaliah is put to death, and Jehoiada makes a covenant between the LORD, the king and the people.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how young Joash became king of Judah?
ev: Say how Joash was saved and for how long he was hidden
Say what the covenant of Jehoiada was (11:17)

nodes.t: Joash repairs the temple
nodes.d: Joash does right while Jehoiada instructs him, though the high places stay; when the priests have not repaired the house by his twenty-third year, a chest is placed at the altar and the money repairs it. Hazael threatens Jerusalem and Joash is killed by his servants.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Joash arranged the repair of the temple?
ev: Say how the temple money was collected and used (12:9-15)
Say how Joash's reign ended (12:17-21)

nodes.t: Jehoahaz and Joash of Israel
nodes.d: Jehoahaz of Israel follows Jeroboam's sins, so the LORD delivers Israel into Hazael's hand; when Jehoahaz seeks the LORD, he gives Israel a saviour, yet they do not depart from Jeroboam's sins. His son Joash reigns in the same way.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how the LORD treated Israel under Jehoahaz?
ev: Say what happened when Jehoahaz sought the LORD (13:4-5)
Say whether Israel turned from Jeroboam's sins (13:6)

nodes.t: Elisha's last word and death
nodes.d: The dying Elisha has King Joash shoot an arrow of the LORD's deliverance from Syria and strike the ground; Joash strikes only three times, so Elisha says he will defeat Syria only three times. After Elisha's death a dead man touches his bones and revives; the LORD is gracious to Israel because of his covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Elisha did on his deathbed and why the LORD still showed Israel compassion?
ev: Describe the arrows and why Elisha was angry (13:17-19)
Find the verse that names the covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob (13:23)

nodes.t: Amaziah of Judah
nodes.d: Amaziah does right, though not like David, kills the servants who killed his father but spares their children as the law of Moses says, defeats Edom, then challenges Joash of Israel and is beaten at Beth-shemesh, with Jerusalem's wall broken and the temple treasures taken. He is later killed in a conspiracy.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe Amaziah's reign, including his pride in challenging Israel?
ev: Say what Amaziah did and did not do with the children of the murderers (14:5-6)
Describe the result of his challenge to Israel (14:11-14)

nodes.t: Jeroboam II of Israel
nodes.d: Jeroboam son of Joash does evil like the earlier kings, yet restores Israel's border according to the word spoken by Jonah the prophet, because the LORD saw Israel's bitter affliction and had not said he would blot out Israel's name.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD helped Israel by Jeroboam II even though he did evil?
ev: Name the prophet mentioned in 14:25
Say why the LORD saved Israel by Jeroboam (14:26-27)

nodes.t: Azariah and Jotham of Judah
nodes.d: Azariah (Uzziah) does right, but the high places remain and the LORD smites him with leprosy until his death; his son Jotham does right in the same way. In Jotham's days the LORD begins to send Rezin of Syria and Pekah against Judah.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the reigns of Azariah and Jotham?
ev: Say what happened to Azariah and where he lived (15:5)
Say what remained in Judah despite the kings doing right (15:4, 35)

nodes.t: Israel's last kings: Zachariah to Pekah
nodes.d: Zachariah, Shallum, Menahem, Pekahiah and Pekah rule Israel in quick succession, mostly by conspiracy, all doing evil; Pul of Assyria is paid off by Menahem and Tiglath-pileser takes cities and carries people captive in Pekah's days. Hoshea then kills Pekah.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Assyria began to take Israel's land and people?
ev: Say how Zachariah's end fulfilled the word to Jehu (15:12)
Say how Assyria begins to affect Israel (15:19, 29)

nodes.t: Ahaz of Judah turns to Assyria
nodes.d: Ahaz walks in the way of Israel's kings, burns his son in the fire and sacrifices at the high places. Rezin and Pekah besiege Jerusalem, and Ahaz sends the temple silver and gold to Tiglath-pileser; he then copies a Damascus altar and moves the LORD's bronze altar aside.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Ahaz did instead of trusting the LORD when Syria and Israel attacked?
ev: Say who Ahaz asked for help and what he paid (16:7-8)
Describe what he did with the altar at the temple (16:10-16)

nodes.t: Samaria falls to Assyria
nodes.d: Hoshea becomes Assyria's servant, then conspires with Egypt; Shalmaneser besieges Samaria, takes it in Hoshea's ninth year and carries Israel into Assyria.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how and when the northern kingdom of Israel was taken captive?
ev: Say what Hoshea did that led to the siege (17:4)
Say where Israel was carried (17:6)

nodes.t: Why the LORD removed Israel
nodes.d: The writer explains that Israel sinned against the LORD who brought them from Egypt, walked in the nations' ways, ignored the prophets, rejected his covenant and statutes, and followed Jeroboam's sin, so the LORD removed them. Judah also did not keep his commandments.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} give the reasons 2 Kings 17 gives for Israel's exile?
ev: List several sins named in 17:7-17
Say how the LORD had warned them (17:13)

nodes.t: Foreign peoples settled in Samaria
nodes.d: The king of Assyria brings peoples from Babylon, Cuthah, Ava, Hamath and Sepharvaim to Samaria; lions come among them until a priest taught the manner of the God of the land, but each nation keeps its own gods while also fearing the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what happened in the land after Israel was taken away?
ev: Say how the settlers came to fear the LORD (17:25-28)
Say why the writer says they did not truly fear the LORD (17:34-41)

nodes.t: Hezekiah trusts the LORD
nodes.d: Hezekiah does right as David did, removes the high places and breaks the bronze serpent Moses made, which Israel had been burning incense to, and trusts the LORD like no king before or after him. He rebels against Assyria.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what made Hezekiah a good king?
ev: Say what Hezekiah removed and what he did to the bronze serpent (18:4)
Say what the writer says about his trust in the LORD (18:5-7)

nodes.t: Sennacherib's officer taunts Jerusalem
nodes.d: Sennacherib takes Judah's fortified cities and Hezekiah pays him; the king of Assyria still sends Rabshakeh, who mocks Hezekiah's trust in the LORD and Egypt and tells the people not to listen to him, asking which gods have delivered their land.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Rabshakeh said to shake Judah's trust in the LORD?
ev: Say what Rabshakeh told the people on the wall (18:28-35)
Say how the people responded (18:36)

nodes.t: The LORD delivers Jerusalem
nodes.d: Hezekiah spreads Sennacherib's letter before the LORD and prays; Isaiah says the LORD will defend the city for his own sake and David's sake, and that night the angel of the LORD strikes 185,000 in the Assyrian camp. Sennacherib returns to Nineveh and is killed by his sons.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how God answered Hezekiah's prayer against Sennacherib?
ev: Retell Hezekiah's prayer and what he asked (19:15-19)
Say what happened to the Assyrian army (19:35)

nodes.t: Hezekiah's illness and the Babylonian envoys
nodes.d: Hezekiah is told by Isaiah he will die, prays, and the LORD adds fifteen years, giving the shadow going back ten degrees as a sign. Afterward he shows Babylon's envoys all his treasures, and Isaiah tells him all will be carried to Babylon; Hezekiah says the word is good.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the LORD did when Hezekiah was sick, and what Isaiah said about Babylon?
ev: Say what sign the LORD gave and what he promised (20:5-11)
Say what Isaiah foretold about Babylon (20:16-18)

nodes.t: Manasseh and Amon
nodes.d: Manasseh rebuilds the high places, sets altars for the host of heaven in the LORD's house, passes his son through the fire and sheds much innocent blood; the LORD announces evil on Jerusalem like Samaria's. His son Amon does the same and is killed by his servants.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Manasseh led Judah further into sin, and what the LORD announced?
ev: List some of Manasseh's sins (21:3-6, 16)
Say what the LORD announced would happen to Jerusalem (21:12-15)

nodes.t: Josiah and the book of the law
nodes.d: In Josiah's eighteenth year, repairs to the temple turn up the book of the law; the king tears his clothes at its words, and Huldah the prophetess says the evil will come on Jerusalem but not in Josiah's days because his heart was tender.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what happened when the book of the law was found in the temple?
ev: Say what Hilkiah found and how Josiah reacted (22:8-11)
Say what Huldah told Josiah (22:16-20)

nodes.t: Josiah renews the covenant and cleanses the land
nodes.d: Josiah reads the book of the covenant to all the people and makes a covenant before the LORD to walk after him; he removes idols and high places in Judah, defiles Topheth, and at Bethel breaks Jeroboam's altar and burns bones on it according to the word of the man of God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Josiah renewed the covenant and what he removed?
ev: Say what Josiah covenanted (23:3)
Describe what he did at Bethel and which earlier prophecy it matched (23:15-18)

nodes.t: Josiah's Passover and the verdict on Judah
nodes.d: Josiah commands the people to keep the Passover as written; no such Passover had been held since the judges. No king before or after turned to the LORD as he did, yet the LORD did not turn from his wrath because of Manasseh, and says he will remove Judah as he removed Israel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD still would not turn from his anger after Josiah's reforms?
ev: Say how the Passover was different (23:22)
Say why the LORD did not turn from his wrath (23:26-27)

nodes.t: Josiah's death and Jehoahaz and Jehoiakim
nodes.d: Josiah dies at Megiddo when Pharaoh-nechoh goes up to Assyria; Jehoahaz reigns three months and is taken to Egypt, and Pharaoh makes Eliakim king as Jehoiakim, who taxes the land to pay him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened to Judah's kings right after Josiah?
ev: Say how Josiah died (23:29-30)
Say who appointed Jehoiakim (23:34)

nodes.t: Nebuchadnezzar takes Jehoiakim and Jehoiachin
nodes.d: Jehoiakim serves Nebuchadnezzar, then rebels, and the LORD sends bands against Judah as he said by the prophets because of Manasseh's sin; his son Jehoiachin surrenders to Babylon and Nebuchadnezzar carries off the temple treasures and about ten thousand captives. He appoints Zedekiah king.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Babylon took the first captives from Judah?
ev: Say why the LORD sent the invaders (24:2-4)
Say what Nebuchadnezzar took and who he made king (24:13-17)

nodes.t: The fall of Jerusalem
nodes.d: Zedekiah rebels and Nebuchadnezzar besieges Jerusalem; the city is broken up, Zedekiah is blinded after his sons are killed, and the Chaldeans burn the temple, palace and houses, break the walls and carry off the temple's bronze and the people.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how and why Jerusalem was destroyed?
ev: Describe what happened to Zedekiah and to the temple
Say how Judah's exile is summed up (25:21)

nodes.t: Gedaliah and Jehoiachin's release
nodes.d: Nebuchadnezzar appoints Gedaliah over the people left in Judah, but Ishmael kills him and the people flee to Egypt. The book ends with Evil-merodach lifting Jehoiachin out of prison in Babylon and giving him a daily allowance.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how 2 Kings ends and who was released from prison?
ev: Say what happened to Gedaliah (25:25)
Say how the book of 2 Kings ends (25:27-30)

nodes.t: 1 Chronicles: overview
nodes.d: 1 Chronicles opens with genealogies from Adam to the returned exiles (chs. 1-9), tells of Saul's death and David's reign (chs. 10-21), and then David's preparations for the temple, the organising of Levites and officers, and the accession of Solomon (chs. 22-29).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline 1 Chronicles in order, from the genealogies to David's death?
ev: Name the three parts: genealogies, David's reign, preparations for the temple
Say how the book begins (Adam) and ends (David's death and Solomon reigning)

nodes.t: Genealogies from Adam to Israel
nodes.d: 1 Chronicles 1 lists the line from Adam to Noah's sons, the nations from Japheth, Ham and Shem, the line to Abraham, Abraham's sons through Ishmael, Keturah and Isaac, and Esau's descendants and the kings of Edom.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say where 1 Chronicles begins its list of names and why a book of history might start there?
ev: Say whose name begins the list (1:1) and whose sons are named in 1:34
Say which sons of Isaac are traced (1:34)

nodes.t: The twelve sons of Israel and the line of Judah
nodes.d: Chapter 2 names the twelve sons of Israel and then follows Judah in detail through Hezron, Ram, Amminadab, Nahshon and Jesse to David, with other branches of Judah's families.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} follow the line from Judah to David in 1 Chronicles 2?
ev: List the twelve sons of Israel as named in 2:1-2
Say whose name ends the main line in 2:13-15

nodes.t: David's sons and the line of the kings of Judah
nodes.d: Chapter 3 lists David's sons born in Hebron and Jerusalem, then follows Solomon's line through the kings of Judah to the exile and the descendants of Jehoiachin.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what 1 Chronicles 3 traces from David to the exile?
ev: Say where David's sons were born and how long he reigned in each place (3:4)
Name some of the kings in the line from Solomon (3:10-16)

nodes.t: Other families of Judah and Simeon, and Jabez
nodes.d: Chapter 4 lists further families of Judah and Simeon. In the middle the text singles out Jabez, honoured above his brothers, who called on the God of Israel for blessing and was granted what he asked.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what is said about Jabez in 1 Chronicles 4?
ev: Say what Jabez asked of God and the result (4:10)
Name the two tribes whose families are listed

nodes.t: Reuben, Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh
nodes.d: Chapter 5 explains that Reuben lost the birthright to Joseph, lists Reuben, Gad and half Manasseh east of Jordan, notes that they cried to God and were helped in battle, and says they sinned by following other gods and were carried away by Assyria.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why 1 Chronicles 5 says the eastern tribes were taken captive?
ev: Say what happened to Reuben's birthright (5:1-2)
Say why the eastern tribes were carried away (5:25-26)

nodes.t: The tribe of Levi: priests and singers
nodes.d: Chapter 6 traces Levi through Gershon, Kohath and Merari, the line of the high priests, the Levitical towns, and the singers David set over the service of song, Heman, Asaph and Ethan.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say who the priests and singers were according to 1 Chronicles 6?
ev: Name the three sons of Levi (6:1)
Say what David set the singers over (6:31-32)

nodes.t: Issachar, Benjamin, Naphtali, Manasseh, Ephraim and Asher
nodes.d: Chapter 7 lists families of several tribes, noting their numbers of mighty men of valour, and ends with Asher.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name some of the tribes covered in 1 Chronicles 7?
ev: Name some tribes in the chapter
Say what the writer counts for several tribes

nodes.t: Benjamin and the house of Saul
nodes.d: Chapter 8 lists Benjamin's families, and 8:33-40 traces Saul and his sons; the same line is repeated in 9:35-44, where Saul's descendants are listed again.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} find where 1 Chronicles lists Saul's family?
ev: Say who is named as Saul's father and sons (8:33)
Say where else the line of Saul is listed (9:35-44)

nodes.t: Those who lived in Jerusalem after the captivity
nodes.d: Chapter 9:1-34 says all Israel was reckoned by genealogies, the people carried away to Babylon for their transgression, and lists those who first dwelt in their cities: Israelites, priests, Levites, temple servants, with the porters and singers and their duties.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what 1 Chronicles 9 says about the people who lived in Jerusalem?
ev: Say why Judah was carried to Babylon (9:1)
Name the groups who lived in Jerusalem (9:2-3)

nodes.t: Saul dies at Gilboa
nodes.d: The Philistines fight Israel, Saul and his sons die, and the Philistines strip Saul and fasten his head in the temple of Dagon; the men of Jabesh-gilead bury him. The text says Saul died for his transgression and for not enquiring of the LORD, and the kingdom was turned to David.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why 1 Chronicles says Saul died and what happened to the kingdom?
ev: Say why the writer says Saul died (10:13-14)
Say what happened to Saul's body and who buried it

nodes.t: David is made king and takes Jerusalem
nodes.d: All Israel gathers to David at Hebron and he makes a covenant with the elders before the LORD; David and Israel take Jebus (Jerusalem) from the Jebusites, Joab leading, and David dwells there; he grows greater because the LORD of hosts was with him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how David became king over all Israel and took Jerusalem?
ev: Say who came to Hebron and what they said (11:1-3)
Say who went up first against the Jebusites (11:6)

nodes.t: David's mighty men
nodes.d: The chief of David's mighty men are named with their deeds: Jashobeam, Eleazar, Abishai and Benaiah, three men who brought David water from the well of Bethlehem (which he poured out to the LORD), and a list of other valiant men.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell about David's mighty men and the water from Bethlehem?
ev: Say what David did with the water from Bethlehem and why (11:17-19)
Name two of the mighty men

nodes.t: Those who came to David at Ziklag and Hebron
nodes.d: Chapter 12 lists warriors from Benjamin, Gad, Judah, Manasseh and other tribes who joined David at Ziklag and in the wilderness, and then the tribal armies that came to Hebron with a perfect heart to make him king over all Israel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how all Israel came to support David as king?
ev: Say what Amasai told David (12:18)
Say why the tribes came to Hebron (12:38)

nodes.t: The ark moved on a cart and Uzza dies
nodes.d: David consults the leaders and all Israel to bring the ark of God from Kirjath-jearim; on the way Uzza puts out his hand to steady the ark and the LORD strikes him. David is afraid and leaves the ark with Obed-edom, whose house is blessed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what went wrong when David first tried to bring the ark to Jerusalem?
ev: Retell what happened to Uzza
Say where the ark was left and how the LORD treated that house (13:13-14)

nodes.t: David established at Jerusalem and the Philistines defeated
nodes.d: Hiram of Tyre sends cedar and craftsmen to David, who perceives that the LORD has confirmed him king; the Philistines come twice, David enquires of God each time, and God tells him the second time to wait for the sound in the mulberry trees, and the Philistines are beaten.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how David knew when to attack the Philistines?
ev: Say what David did before each battle (14:10, 14)
Say what sign God gave David (14:15)

nodes.t: The ark is brought up to Jerusalem
nodes.d: David prepares a place for the ark and says only Levites should carry it; the Levites sanctify themselves and bear it on their shoulders with the staves, singers and instruments appointed, and the ark comes to the city of David with shouting, though Michal despises David.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how David brought the ark up properly the second time?
ev: Say why David said only the Levites should carry the ark (15:2, 13)
Say how the ark was carried this time (15:15)

nodes.t: The ark in its tent and the worship appointed
nodes.d: The ark is set in the tent David pitched; burnt and peace offerings are made, bread is given to all Israel, and Levites are appointed to minister before the ark and praise the LORD, with Asaph and others, while Zadok and priests serve at Gibeon.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the worship David appointed once the ark was in Jerusalem?
ev: Say what David gave to the people (16:3)
Name the Levite chief appointed to sound the cymbals (16:5)

nodes.t: David's psalm of thanksgiving
nodes.d: David delivers to Asaph a psalm: give thanks to the LORD, seek his face, remember his marvellous works and his covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, declare his glory to the nations, for the LORD is great and above all gods, and his mercy endures for ever.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell some reasons David's psalm gives for thanking the LORD?
ev: Find the lines about the covenant with Abraham and the land of Canaan (16:15-18)
Say what the psalm says about the LORD and the gods of the peoples (16:25-26)

nodes.t: The LORD's promise to David's house
nodes.d: David wants to build a house for the ark but the LORD tells Nathan he will build David a house: he will raise up David's seed, who will build the LORD's house, whose throne will be established for ever and to whom the LORD will be a father. David sits before the LORD, praises him and asks that the word be established.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the LORD promised David in 1 Chronicles 17 and how David responded?
ev: State what the LORD promises about David's seed and throne (17:11-14)
Say how David responds in prayer (17:16-27)

nodes.t: David's victories and officers
nodes.d: David defeats the Philistines, Moab, Hadarezer of Zobah, the Syrians and Edom, and dedicates the spoil to the LORD; the text says the LORD preserved David whithersoever he went, and lists his officers.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} summarise David's victories in 1 Chronicles 18?
ev: Say who preserved David in battle (18:6, 13)
Say what David did with the silver and gold (18:11)

nodes.t: David and Ammon
nodes.d: David sends messengers to console Hanun king of Ammon, who shames them; Ammon hires Syrians and Joab and Abishai defeat them, and David then defeats Syria. In the next year Joab besieges Rabbah, and giants of the Philistines are killed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why David went to war with Ammon?
ev: Say how Hanun treated David's servants (19:4)
Say what Joab said to Abishai before the battle (19:13)

nodes.t: David numbers Israel and the plague
nodes.d: Satan provokes David to number Israel, Joab objects, and David confesses his sin; God sends a plague and 70,000 fall. When the angel stands over Jerusalem, David pleads to bear the punishment, buys Ornan's threshing floor, builds an altar and the LORD answers by fire.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell why David's census was sin and how the plague ended?
ev: Say what David chose among the three punishments and why (21:13)
Say what David bought and what he did there (21:24-26)

nodes.t: David prepares for the temple and charges Solomon
nodes.d: David declares the threshing floor the site of the LORD's house, gathers materials, and tells Solomon that though he himself shed much blood, a son of rest will build the house for the LORD's name and the LORD will establish his throne for ever; David commands the princes to help.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Solomon, not David, was to build the house, and what David prepared?
ev: Say why David himself could not build the house (22:8)
State what the LORD promised about Solomon (22:9-10)

nodes.t: The Levites' duties
nodes.d: Old David makes Solomon king, numbers the Levites from age twenty and above, and divides them into courses to assist the sons of Aaron, as porters, singers and in the temple service, now that the LORD has given his people rest.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the Levites were appointed to do under David?
ev: Name the Levite families (23:6) and some of their duties (23:28-31)
Say why they no longer carry the tabernacle (23:25-26)

nodes.t: The divisions of the priests
nodes.d: Chapter 24 lists the sons of Aaron, notes that Nadab and Abihu died childless, and divides the descendants of Eleazar and Ithamar into twenty-four courses by lot, with Zadok and Ahimelech, and lists remaining Levite heads.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say how David organised the priests?
ev: Say how the courses were assigned (24:5, 31)
Name the sons of Aaron who had no children (24:2)

nodes.t: The singers of the temple
nodes.d: David and the captains set apart the sons of Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun for the service of prophesying with harps, psalteries and cymbals, in twenty-four courses by lot.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain who the temple singers were and how they served?
ev: Name the three families of singers (25:1)
Say how their duties were assigned (25:8)

nodes.t: Gatekeepers and treasurers
nodes.d: Chapter 26 lists the courses of the porters at the gates of the house of the LORD, the Levites over its treasuries and dedicated things, and officers and judges for outward business.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the gatekeepers and treasurers David appointed?
ev: Say what the porters did (26:12-19)
Say what the treasurers kept (26:20-28)

nodes.t: The monthly army and tribal leaders
nodes.d: Chapter 27 lists the twelve divisions of 24,000 men that served the king by month, the tribal princes, David's stewards and counsellors, and notes that David did not number those under twenty because the LORD had said he would multiply Israel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how David's army and officers were organised?
ev: Say how the army was organised through the year (27:1)
Name the people who counselled David (27:32-34)

nodes.t: David's charge to Solomon and the assembly
nodes.d: David assembles Israel's leaders, says God did not let him build because he was a man of war, chose him as king for ever and Solomon as successor; he charges Solomon to know and serve God, and gives him the plans for the temple, telling him to be strong.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what David told Solomon and the leaders about the house of God?
ev: State what David says God chose (28:4-6) and the condition he gives (28:7-9)
Say what David gave to Solomon (28:11-19)

nodes.t: The offerings, David's prayer and Solomon enthroned
nodes.d: David gives his own treasure for the house, the leaders give willingly, and David blesses the LORD before the assembly, saying all things come of him, and prays for Solomon. Solomon is made king a second time and sits on the LORD's throne; David dies full of days, riches and honour after reigning forty years.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how David and the people gave to the house of the LORD, and how the book ends?
ev: Say what David says about giving (29:14-16)
Say how long David reigned (29:27) and who succeeded him

nodes.t: 2 Chronicles: overview
nodes.d: 2 Chronicles tells of Solomon's wisdom and the temple (chs. 1-9), then the kings of Judah from Rehoboam to Zedekiah, with attention to temple worship, reform and returning to the LORD, ending with the exile and Cyrus's decree to rebuild the house (ch. 36).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline 2 Chronicles in order, from Solomon's temple to Cyrus's decree?
ev: Say that the book follows Solomon's temple and then the kings of Judah
Say how it ends (36:22-23, Cyrus of Persia)

nodes.t: Solomon's wisdom and wealth
nodes.d: Solomon and the congregation go to the high place at Gibeon, where the LORD appears and tells him to ask; he asks for wisdom and knowledge to judge God's people and, because he did not ask for riches, God gives him wisdom, knowledge, riches, wealth and honour.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Solomon asked for at Gibeon and what God gave him?
ev: Say what Solomon asked and what God added (1:10-12)
Describe Solomon's wealth in 1:14-17

nodes.t: Solomon prepares to build the temple
nodes.d: Solomon determines to build a house for the LORD's name, numbers workmen, and asks Huram king of Tyre for timber and a skilled craftsman; Huram answers, blessing the LORD, and sends a cunning man and the timber.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Solomon arranged workers and timber for the temple?
ev: Say what Solomon asked from Huram (2:7-9)
Say how Huram responded (2:11-16)

nodes.t: Solomon builds the temple
nodes.d: Solomon begins to build on Mount Moriah, where the LORD appeared to David and on the threshing floor of Ornan, in his fourth year; the house is overlaid with gold, with two cherubim in the most holy place, a veil, and two pillars named Jachin and Boaz.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe where Solomon built the temple and what was inside?
ev: Say where the temple was built (3:1)
Say what stood in the most holy house (3:10-13)

nodes.t: The temple furnishings
nodes.d: Solomon makes the bronze altar, the molten sea on twelve oxen, ten lavers, golden lampstands and tables, and the courts; Huram makes the bronze pieces, and everything inside is of gold.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name some of the temple furnishings Solomon made?
ev: Name some of the furnishings and what the sea was used for (4:2-6)
Say what the vessels in the temple were made of (4:7-22)

nodes.t: The ark is brought in and the glory fills the house
nodes.d: At the feast the priests bring the ark of the covenant into the most holy place; when the singers and trumpeters praise the LORD, saying he is good and his mercy endures for ever, a cloud fills the house and the priests cannot minister because the glory of the LORD had filled it.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened when the ark was placed in the new temple?
ev: Say what was in the ark (5:10)
Describe what happened when the Levites praised the LORD (5:13-14)

nodes.t: Solomon blesses Israel and recalls the promise to David
nodes.d: Solomon says the LORD dwells in thick darkness, blesses the congregation, and says the LORD has performed his word to David: David's son has been set on the throne and built the house, in which the ark with the LORD's covenant is placed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Solomon says the LORD had promised David?
ev: Say what Solomon says the LORD promised David (6:5-9)
Say what Solomon says he has done (6:10-11)

nodes.t: Solomon's dedication prayer
nodes.d: Kneeling before the whole congregation, Solomon praises the LORD who keeps covenant and mercy, asks that the promise to David be kept, and prays for the LORD to hear and forgive when Israel sins, is defeated, is in drought, or in captivity, and when a stranger prays toward the house.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} summarise Solomon's prayer at the dedication of the temple?
ev: Say what Solomon asks for if Israel repents (6:24-25, 36-39)
Find the request about the throne and David (6:16-17, 42)

nodes.t: Fire from heaven and the feast of dedication
nodes.d: When Solomon finishes praying, fire comes down from heaven and consumes the sacrifices, and the glory of the LORD fills the house; the people bow and praise, great sacrifices are offered, and they keep the dedication for seven days.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened after Solomon prayed at the dedication?
ev: Describe what fell from heaven and how the people responded (7:1-3)
Say how many days they kept the feast (7:8-9)

nodes.t: The LORD answers Solomon
nodes.d: The LORD appears to Solomon by night and says that if his people humble themselves, pray, seek his face and turn from their wicked ways he will hear, forgive and heal their land; he will establish Solomon's throne as he covenanted with David, but if they forsake him he will pluck them out of the land and cast out the house.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD told Solomon about humbling themselves and about forsaking him?
ev: State the condition and promise of 7:14
Say what the LORD warns will happen if they serve other gods (7:19-22)

nodes.t: Solomon's cities, worship and ships
nodes.d: Solomon builds cities, sets forced labour on the remaining peoples, keeps the burnt offerings and feasts as appointed, and orders the priests and Levites as David commanded; ships brought gold from Ophir.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Solomon kept worship in order after the temple was built?
ev: Say how Solomon followed David's order for the priests and Levites (8:14-15)
Say what the ships brought (8:17-18)

nodes.t: The queen of Sheba and the end of Solomon's reign
nodes.d: The queen of Sheba tests Solomon with hard questions and blesses the LORD for setting him on the throne; the chapter describes his gold, throne, ships and wisdom, and ends with his forty-year reign and burial in the city of David.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell why the queen of Sheba came and how Solomon's reign ended?
ev: Say what the queen said about the LORD (9:8)
State how long Solomon reigned (9:30)

nodes.t: Israel rebels against Rehoboam
nodes.d: At Shechem Israel asks Rehoboam to lighten Solomon's yoke; he rejects the old men's counsel and answers roughly, and Israel rebels against the house of David, while Rehoboam reigns over the cities of Judah. The text says the cause was of God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the northern tribes broke from Rehoboam?
ev: Compare what the old men and the young men advised (10:7-11)
Say what Israel said when the king answered roughly (10:16)

nodes.t: Rehoboam strengthens Judah
nodes.d: Rehoboam gathers an army to fight Israel but obeys the word of Shemaiah and returns; he fortifies cities, and priests and Levites and those who set their hearts to seek the LORD come to Judah from Jeroboam's kingdom.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell why Rehoboam did not go to war and why the priests and Levites came to Judah?
ev: Say why Rehoboam did not fight Israel (11:2-4)
Say why the Levites came to Judah (11:13-16)

nodes.t: Shishak and Rehoboam humbles himself
nodes.d: When Rehoboam is strong he forsakes the law of the LORD, and in his fifth year Shishak of Egypt comes against Jerusalem; Shemaiah tells them the LORD has left them, and when they humble themselves the LORD grants some deliverance, though they become Shishak's servants.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Shishak came and how the LORD responded when Rehoboam humbled himself?
ev: Say what turned Judah to humility (12:5-7)
Say what Shishak took (12:9)

nodes.t: Abijah defeats Jeroboam
nodes.d: Abijah of Judah, standing on Mount Zemaraim, tells Jeroboam that the LORD gave the kingdom to David and his sons by a covenant of salt, that Judah has not forsaken the LORD while Israel has made golden calves; Judah cries to the LORD and Israel is defeated.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Abijah said about David and why Judah won?
ev: Find the phrase about the covenant of salt (13:5)
Say why Judah prevailed (13:18)

nodes.t: Asa removes idols and defeats Zerah
nodes.d: Asa does good and right in the LORD's eyes, removes altars and high places, builds fenced cities during ten years of quiet, and when Zerah the Ethiopian comes with a huge host he cries to the LORD, saying it is nothing with him to help, and the LORD smites the Ethiopians.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Asa prayed and what happened to Zerah's army?
ev: Say what Asa prayed before the battle (14:11)
Say what Asa removed from Judah (14:3-5)

nodes.t: Azariah's warning and Asa's covenant
nodes.d: The Spirit of God comes on Azariah, who tells Asa that the LORD is with them while they are with him; Asa removes the idols, renews the altar, and Judah enters a covenant to seek the LORD with all their heart and soul, and he removes his mother Maachah from being queen.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Azariah told Asa and what covenant Judah made?
ev: State Azariah's message (15:2)
Say what the covenant was and what it required (15:12-13)

nodes.t: Asa relies on Syria and not the LORD
nodes.d: In Asa's thirty-sixth year Baasha of Israel builds Ramah, and Asa takes treasures from the temple to hire Benhadad of Syria; Hanani the seer rebukes him for not relying on the LORD, and Asa imprisons him. In his illness he seeks physicians and not the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Asa's trust changed late in his reign?
ev: Say what Hanani told Asa (16:7-9)
Say how Asa responded to Hanani and in his disease (16:10, 12)

nodes.t: Jehoshaphat strengthens Judah
nodes.d: Jehoshaphat walks in the first ways of David and seeks the LORD, not Baalim; the LORD establishes his kingdom, and in the third year of his reign he sends princes, Levites and priests with the book of the law to teach through Judah's cities, so that fear of the LORD falls on the nations.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Jehoshaphat taught Judah the law of the LORD?
ev: Say what Jehoshaphat sent teachers to do (17:7-9)
Say what the LORD did for Jehoshaphat (17:5, 10)

nodes.t: Jehoshaphat joins Ahab and Micaiah warns
nodes.d: Jehoshaphat allies with Ahab and goes to Ramoth-gilead; four hundred prophets say go, but Micaiah, after saying he will speak what God says, shows a lying spirit sent into the prophets' mouths. Ahab disguises himself but is struck by a random arrow and dies, while Jehoshaphat cries out and God helps him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Jehoshaphat went with Ahab and what Micaiah said?
ev: Compare Micaiah with the four hundred prophets
Say how Ahab died and how Jehoshaphat was saved (18:30-34, 31)

nodes.t: Jehu's rebuke and Jehoshaphat's reforms
nodes.d: Jehu the seer rebukes Jehoshaphat for helping the ungodly yet notes the good in him; Jehoshaphat goes among the people turning them back to the LORD and sets judges in the fenced cities and in Jerusalem, telling them to judge for the LORD and fear him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Jehoshaphat set up judges and what he told them?
ev: Say what Jehoshaphat told the judges (19:6-7)
Say what Jehu the seer said was good in him (19:3)

nodes.t: The LORD fights for Judah against Moab and Ammon
nodes.d: A great multitude of Moab, Ammon and Mount Seir comes against Jehoshaphat, who proclaims a fast and prays that they have no might and their eyes are on God; Jahaziel says the battle is not theirs but God's, singers go before the army, and the LORD sets the enemy against each other.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Judah won the battle against Moab and Ammon without fighting?
ev: Quote the way Jahaziel describes the battle (20:15)
Describe how Judah went out to battle (20:20-22)

nodes.t: The end of Jehoshaphat's reign
nodes.d: Jehoshaphat walks in Asa's way, though the high places remain; he joins Ahaziah of Israel to build ships at Ezion-geber and Eliezer prophesies that the LORD has broken his works, and the ships do not sail.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell why Jehoshaphat's ships were broken?
ev: Say what remained despite his good reign (20:33)
Say why the ships were broken (20:37)

nodes.t: Jehoram of Judah
nodes.d: Jehoram kills his brothers, walks as the house of Ahab did (for Ahab's daughter is his wife), yet the LORD does not destroy David's house because of his covenant with David. Elijah writes warning of plague and a disease of his bowels, and Jehoram dies of it.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why God spared the house of David despite Jehoram?
ev: Say why the LORD did not destroy David's house (21:7)
Say what Elijah's writing announced (21:12-15)

nodes.t: Ahaziah, Athaliah and the hidden Joash
nodes.d: Ahaziah of Judah follows the counsel of Ahab's house and is killed with Joram of Israel by Jehu; Athaliah destroys the royal seed but Jehoshabeath hides the baby Joash in the house of God for six years.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Joash escaped Athaliah?
ev: Say who walked with Ahaziah and what happened to him (22:3-9)
Say who saved Joash and where he was hidden (22:11-12)

nodes.t: Jehoiada crowns Joash and Athaliah is slain
nodes.d: In the seventh year Jehoiada makes a covenant with the captains, brings out the king's son in the temple with guards and Levites, anoints him, and Athaliah is put to death; Jehoiada makes a covenant between the LORD, the people and the king, and the house of Baal is destroyed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how Joash became king and how the people renewed their covenant?
ev: Say how Joash was crowned and who protected him (23:1-11)
State what the king's son reigning is said to fulfil (23:3)

nodes.t: Joash repairs the temple, then turns away
nodes.d: Joash repairs the house of the LORD with money collected in a chest, but after Jehoiada dies the princes lead him to serve idols; when Zechariah the priest warns them, Joash has him stoned in the temple court, and Joash is later struck down by Syrians and conspirators.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Joash did well while Jehoiada lived and what changed after he died?
ev: Say how the temple was repaired (24:8-14)
Say what Joash did after Jehoiada's death (24:17-22)

nodes.t: Amaziah of Judah
nodes.d: Amaziah obeys the law about not killing children for fathers' sins, sends away hired Israelite troops at a prophet's word and defeats Edom, but then brings home Edom's gods and worships them. He ignores the prophet, challenges Joash of Israel and loses at Beth-shemesh, and is later killed in a conspiracy.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Amaziah went from obeying the LORD to worshipping idols?
ev: Say what Amaziah did after defeating Edom (25:14)
Say why God was angry and what resulted (25:15-24)

nodes.t: Uzziah's strength and pride
nodes.d: Uzziah seeks God while Zechariah teaches him, and God makes him prosper with victories, buildings and an army; when he is strong his heart is lifted up, he enters the temple to burn incense, and the LORD strikes him with leprosy until his death.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened to Uzziah when he became strong?
ev: Say what led to Uzziah's success (26:5)
Say what he did to bring leprosy on himself (26:16-21)

nodes.t: Jotham of Judah
nodes.d: Jotham does right as Uzziah did, but does not enter the temple; he builds in Jerusalem and Judah, conquers Ammon, and becomes mighty because he prepared his ways before the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what made Jotham a strong king?
ev: Say why Jotham became mighty (27:6)
Name something he built or won

nodes.t: Ahaz and Judah's defeat
nodes.d: Ahaz walks in the ways of Israel's kings, makes images for Baalim and burns his children; the LORD delivers him to Syria and Israel, where Pekah kills many in Judah in one day. In his distress he sends to Assyria, who does not help, and he closes the temple and sets up altars everywhere.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Ahaz responded to his troubles and what happened?
ev: List what Ahaz did instead of seeking the LORD (28:2-4, 22-25)
Say what happened when he turned to Assyria (28:20-21)

nodes.t: Oded and the captives sent home
nodes.d: When Israel brings home 200,000 captives from Judah, the prophet Oded meets the army and says they also have sins and must send them back; some Ephraimite leaders agree, and clothe, feed and carry the captives to Jericho.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Israelites showed kindness to the captives from Judah?
ev: Say what Oded told the army (28:9-11)
Describe how the leaders cared for the captives (28:15)

nodes.t: Hezekiah cleanses and reopens the temple
nodes.d: Hezekiah reopens the doors of the LORD's house in his first year, calls the priests and Levites to sanctify it and carry out the filth, and says he intends to make a covenant with the LORD; sin offerings are made for the kingdom and the sanctuary, and worship with singing and instruments resumes.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Hezekiah restored worship in the temple?
ev: Say what Hezekiah told the Levites (29:5-11)
Describe how worship was restored (29:25-30)

nodes.t: Hezekiah's Passover
nodes.d: Hezekiah sends letters to all Israel and Judah, including Ephraim and Manasseh, to come to Jerusalem and keep the Passover to the LORD, in the second month; some mock but many humble themselves and come, and the people keep the feast with great joy for fourteen days. Hezekiah prays for those who were not cleansed and the LORD heals the people.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Hezekiah invited all Israel to the Passover and how the people responded?
ev: Say whom Hezekiah invited (30:1-9)
Say what Hezekiah prayed for the uncleansed (30:18-20)

nodes.t: Hezekiah organises the offerings and priests
nodes.d: After the Passover Israel breaks down the idols, Hezekiah appoints the priests and Levites to their courses, and the people bring tithes and firstfruits in abundance; storerooms are prepared and men are appointed to distribute. The text says Hezekiah did this with all his heart and prospered.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Hezekiah arranged for the support of the priests and Levites?
ev: Say what the people brought (31:5-6)
Say how Hezekiah served God according to 31:20-21

nodes.t: Sennacherib threatens and the LORD delivers Jerusalem
nodes.d: Sennacherib invades Judah; Hezekiah strengthens Jerusalem and tells the people there is more with them than with the king of Assyria. Sennacherib's servants mock the LORD, Hezekiah and Isaiah pray, and the LORD sends an angel to cut off the Assyrian leaders; Sennacherib goes home and his sons kill him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Hezekiah and Isaiah prayed when Sennacherib threatened Jerusalem, and what God did?
ev: Say what Hezekiah told the people (32:7-8)
Say what the LORD did after Hezekiah and Isaiah prayed (32:20-22)

nodes.t: Hezekiah's illness, pride and death
nodes.d: Hezekiah is sick to death and prays and is given a sign, but his heart is lifted up and wrath falls on Judah until he and Jerusalem humble themselves. He prospers, stops the upper watercourse of Gihon, and when envoys come from Babylon God leaves him to test what was in his heart; he dies and is honoured in burial.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Hezekiah's heart was tested and what the LORD did?
ev: Say what happened because of Hezekiah's pride and how it was turned aside (32:25-26)
Name something Hezekiah built for Jerusalem (32:30)

nodes.t: Manasseh's repentance and Amon
nodes.d: Manasseh rebuilds the high places and sets idols in the house of God; the LORD brings Assyria's captains, who take him in fetters to Babylon, and there he humbles himself, prays and is restored to Jerusalem, where he removes the idols and repairs the altar. His son Amon does evil and does not humble himself, and is killed by his servants.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Manasseh turned back to the LORD and how Amon was different?
ev: Say what happened to Manasseh in affliction and what he did after returning (33:11-16)
Say how Amon differed from his father (33:23)

nodes.t: Josiah seeks God and purges the land
nodes.d: Josiah begins to seek the God of David in his eighth year, and in his twelfth year purges Judah and Jerusalem of high places, groves and images, and also in Manasseh, Ephraim, Simeon and Naphtali; in his eighteenth year he sends Shaphan and others to repair the house of the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Josiah did in the early years of his reign?
ev: Say when Josiah began to seek God and when he began to purge (34:3)
Say who oversaw the temple repair (34:8-13)

nodes.t: The book of the law found and the covenant renewed
nodes.d: Hilkiah finds the book of the law in the temple; Josiah tears his clothes, sends to Huldah the prophetess, who says the evil will come but not in his days because he humbled himself. Josiah reads the book to all the people and makes a covenant before the LORD to keep his commandments.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened when the book of the law was found and what Josiah did next?
ev: Say what Josiah did when the book was read (34:19)
Say what Huldah told him and what covenant he made (34:23-31)

nodes.t: Josiah's Passover
nodes.d: Josiah keeps the Passover in Jerusalem on the fourteenth of the first month, appointing priests and Levites to their duties, giving offerings to the people, with the singers in their places as David commanded; no Passover like it had been kept in Israel since Samuel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe Josiah's Passover and what made it special?
ev: Say how Josiah organised the Levites and priests (35:2-6)
Say how this Passover compared to earlier ones (35:18)

nodes.t: Josiah dies at Megiddo
nodes.d: Pharaoh Necho goes up to fight at Carchemish and warns Josiah not to meddle, saying God commanded him; Josiah does not heed and goes out to fight at Megiddo, where archers wound him, and he dies; all Judah mourns, and Jeremiah laments for him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Josiah died and who mourned for him?
ev: Say what Necho told Josiah (35:21)
Say what Josiah did and what happened (35:22-24)

nodes.t: Judah's last kings
nodes.d: Jehoahaz is deposed by the king of Egypt, Jehoiakim is bound by Nebuchadnezzar and temple vessels are taken to Babylon; Jehoiachin is taken to Babylon, and Zedekiah rebels, hardens his heart, and with the priests and people pollutes the house of the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name Judah's last kings in order and say what happened to each?
ev: Say what Nebuchadnezzar took to Babylon (36:7, 10)
Say how Zedekiah and the people sinned (36:12-14)

nodes.t: The LORD sends Judah into exile
nodes.d: The LORD sent messengers to his people because of his compassion, but they mocked the prophets until there was no remedy; the Chaldeans burn the house of God, break down Jerusalem's wall, and carry the survivors to Babylon until the land enjoyed its sabbaths, seventy years, as Jeremiah spoke.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Judah went into exile according to 2 Chronicles 36?
ev: Say why the LORD sent the messengers and how they were treated (36:15-16)
Say what the seventy years were to fulfil (36:21)

nodes.t: Cyrus's decree
nodes.d: In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia the LORD stirs up his spirit to proclaim that the LORD God of heaven has charged him to build him a house in Jerusalem, and invites any of his people to go up.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how 2 Chronicles closes and what Cyrus announced?
ev: Say whose spirit the LORD stirred up and what he proclaimed
Say how 2 Chronicles ends

nodes.t: Ezra: overview
nodes.d: Ezra reports the return from Babylon under Cyrus and Zerubbabel and the rebuilding of the temple despite opposition (chs. 1-6), then Ezra's own journey to Jerusalem, his prayer over intermarriage, and the people's covenant to put away foreign wives (chs. 7-10).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline Ezra, from Cyrus's decree to the people's confession?
ev: Name the two parts: the return and temple under Zerubbabel, and Ezra's mission
Say how the book begins (Cyrus) and ends (the list of those with foreign wives)

nodes.t: Cyrus's decree and the first return
nodes.d: In the first year of Cyrus the LORD stirs his spirit, and he proclaims that the LORD God of heaven charged him to build a house in Jerusalem and invites any of God's people to go up. Those whose spirit God raised go, neighbours help them, and Cyrus brings out the temple vessels to Sheshbazzar.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Cyrus decreed and who went up to Jerusalem?
ev: Say whose word was being fulfilled (1:1)
Say what Cyrus returned to Sheshbazzar (1:7-11)

nodes.t: The list of those who returned
nodes.d: Chapter 2 lists those who came up with Zerubbabel and Jeshua by family and town, then priests, Levites, singers, porters and temple servants, notes some who could not prove their ancestry, and gives the total and the freewill gifts for the house.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Ezra records the names and numbers of the returnees?
ev: Say who led the group (2:2)
Say what some of the chief fathers gave (2:68-69)

nodes.t: The altar is rebuilt and worship begins
nodes.d: In the seventh month the people gather at Jerusalem; Jeshua and Zerubbabel build the altar of the God of Israel, offer burnt offerings morning and evening as written in the law of Moses, and keep the feast of tabernacles, although fear was on them because of the people of the lands.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the returned exiles began by building the altar?
ev: Say what they built first and why (3:2-3)
Name the feast they kept (3:4)

nodes.t: The foundation of the temple is laid
nodes.d: In the second year the builders lay the foundation, with priests and Levites praising the LORD according to David's order; the people shout for joy, while many old men who had seen the first house weep, so that joy and weeping cannot be told apart.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell why some people shouted for joy and some wept when the foundation was laid?
ev: Describe what the people sang (3:11)
Say why some of the old men wept (3:12)

nodes.t: The adversaries offer to help and then oppose
nodes.d: The adversaries of Judah and Benjamin ask to build with Zerubbabel, claiming they seek his God; Zerubbabel and Jeshua refuse, saying they must build alone as Cyrus commanded, and the people of the land weaken their hands and hire counsellors against them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Zerubbabel refused the offer to help build the temple?
ev: Say what the adversaries asked and what the leaders answered (4:2-3)
Say how they opposed the work (4:4-5)

nodes.t: Letters to the king and the work stops
nodes.d: Later accusations are written against Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Ahasuerus and Artaxerxes; Rehum and Shimshai write to Artaxerxes that Jerusalem is a rebellious city, and the king orders the work stopped. The work on the house of God ceases until the second year of Darius.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the rebuilding was stopped and for how long?
ev: Say what the letter claimed about Jerusalem (4:12-16)
Say how long the work ceased (4:24)

nodes.t: Haggai and Zechariah and the resumed work
nodes.d: Haggai and Zechariah prophesy to the Jews in the name of the God of Israel, and Zerubbabel and Jeshua rise and begin to build again; when Tatnai the governor asks who commanded it, the text says the eye of their God was on the elders.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain who encouraged the Jews to start building again?
ev: Name the prophets and the leaders who began again (5:1-2)
Say what kept the work going when Tatnai questioned them (5:5)

nodes.t: Tatnai writes to Darius
nodes.d: Tatnai and his companions write to Darius reporting that the Jews are building the house of the great God, say they build as servants of the God of heaven and earth by Cyrus's decree, and ask the king to search the records.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the Jewish elders told Tatnai about Cyrus's decree?
ev: Say what the elders said about who commanded the building (5:11-16)
Say what Tatnai asked Darius to do (5:17)

nodes.t: Darius finds Cyrus's decree
nodes.d: A search in the house of the rolls finds Cyrus's decree about the house of God in Jerusalem; Darius orders Tatnai to let the work alone, give costs from the royal revenue, supply offerings, and punish anyone who changes the decree.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how the opposition to building the temple was ended?
ev: Say where the decree of Cyrus was found (6:1-2)
State what Darius commanded (6:6-12)

nodes.t: The temple is finished and dedicated
nodes.d: Tatnai carries out the decree, and the elders of the Jews build and prosper through the prophesying of Haggai and Zechariah; the house is finished on the third of Adar in Darius's sixth year, dedicated with joy, and the Passover is kept.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the second temple was completed and celebrated?
ev: Say when the house was finished (6:15)
Say what they kept after the dedication (6:19-22)

nodes.t: Ezra the scribe goes up to Jerusalem
nodes.d: In the reign of Artaxerxes, Ezra, a priest of the line of Aaron and a ready scribe in the law of Moses, goes up from Babylon with a company because the good hand of God was on him; the text says he prepared his heart to seek the law of the LORD, to do it, and to teach in Israel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain who Ezra was and why he went to Jerusalem?
ev: Say what Ezra had prepared his heart to do (7:10)
Say what is said about the hand of God on him (7:6, 9)

nodes.t: Artaxerxes' letter and Ezra's blessing
nodes.d: Artaxerxes' letter lets Ezra take volunteers, silver and gold and vessels to Jerusalem, orders treasurers to supply him, and tells Ezra to appoint judges to teach and enforce the law of God. Ezra blesses the LORD who put this in the king's heart.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what the king's letter gave Ezra and how Ezra responded?
ev: Say what the king authorised Ezra to do (7:13-26)
Say how Ezra responded (7:27-28)

nodes.t: The family heads who went up with Ezra
nodes.d: Ezra 8:1-14 lists the chief fathers and the number of men who went up with Ezra in the reign of Artaxerxes, by family.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Ezra 8:1-14 records?
ev: Say what the list records
Name at least one family that went up

nodes.t: Fasting at the river Ahava
nodes.d: At the river Ahava Ezra finds no Levites and sends for some; he proclaims a fast to seek a right way, being ashamed to ask the king for soldiers after saying God's hand is for good on those who seek him. They entrust the silver, gold and vessels to twelve priests, travel safely, and deliver the treasure in Jerusalem.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Ezra fasted instead of asking for an escort?
ev: Say why Ezra did not ask for soldiers (8:22)
Say how God answered the fast (8:23, 31)

nodes.t: Intermarriage reported to Ezra
nodes.d: The princes tell Ezra that the people, priests and Levites have not separated from the peoples of the lands and have taken their daughters as wives, the princes and rulers being chief in this trespass; Ezra tears his garment and hair and sits appalled.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the people had done that grieved Ezra?
ev: Say what the princes reported (9:1-2)
Say how Ezra reacted (9:3)

nodes.t: Ezra's confession
nodes.d: At the evening sacrifice Ezra falls on his knees and confesses the people's guilt from their fathers' days, remembers the mercy shown in giving a remnant and a little reviving, and says they have again broken God's commandments, and that the LORD is righteous.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} summarise how Ezra prayed over the people's sin?
ev: Say what mercy Ezra recalls (9:8-9)
