nodes.d: Psalm 127 says that unless the LORD builds the house those who build it labour in vain, and that children are a heritage from the LORD; Psalm 128 blesses the one who fears the LORD with the fruit of his labour, a fruitful wife and children, and the good of Jerusalem.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 127:1 teaches about work and the LORD?
ev: Read 127:1-2 and 128:1-4 and say what depends on the LORD.

nodes.t: Psalm 129: they have afflicted me from my youth, yet have not prevailed
nodes.d: Israel says they have often been afflicted from their youth yet not overcome, the LORD is righteous and has cut asunder the cords of the wicked, and those who hate Zion are compared to grass on the housetops that withers.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 129:2-4 says about the afflicted and the LORD?
ev: Read 129:1-4 and say why the afflicted have not been overcome.

nodes.t: Psalms 130-131: out of the depths; a weaned child
nodes.d: Psalm 130 cries to the LORD out of the depths, says that with him there is forgiveness and plenteous redemption, and waits for him more than watchmen for the morning; Psalm 131 says the speaker is not haughty and has quieted his soul like a weaned child, and both end by telling Israel to hope in the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 130:3-4 says about forgiveness and what 130:7 and 131:3 tell Israel to do?
ev: Read 130:3-8 and 131:1-3 and say what Israel is told to do.

nodes.t: Psalm 132: the LORD’s oath to David and his choice of Zion
nodes.d: The psalm recalls David’s vow to find a dwelling for the LORD and says the LORD swore to David that his seed would sit on his throne if his children keep his covenant; the LORD chose Zion for his rest and will make the horn of David to bud.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 132:11-12 says the LORD swore to David?
ev: Read 132:11-18 and say what the LORD swore and what he chose.

nodes.t: Psalms 133-134: brethren in unity; bless the LORD in the night
nodes.d: Psalm 133 says it is good and pleasant when brethren dwell together in unity, like precious ointment and the dew of Hermon, for there the LORD commands the blessing; Psalm 134 calls the LORD’s servants who stand in his house by night to lift up their hands and bless him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 133:1 says is good and what Psalm 134 calls the servants to do?
ev: Read 133:1-3 and 134:1-3 and say who is called to do what.

nodes.t: Psalm 135: praise the LORD who is great above all gods
nodes.d: The psalm calls the LORD’s servants to praise him, says he is above all gods and does whatever he pleases in heaven and earth, recalls Egypt’s firstborn and the defeat of Sihon and Og, and says those who make idols become like them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Psalm 135 contrasts the LORD with idols?
ev: Read 135:5-14 and 135:15-18 and list what the LORD does and what idols are.

nodes.t: Psalm 136: his mercy endureth for ever
nodes.d: Each verse tells a work of the LORD, from creation of the heavens and lights to the striking of Egypt’s firstborn, the dividing of the Red Sea and the giving of the land, and each is followed by the refrain that his mercy endures for ever.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list three works of the LORD in Psalm 136 and say the refrain?
ev: Read Psalm 136 and list the works named, noting the repeated refrain.

nodes.t: Psalm 137: by the rivers of Babylon
nodes.d: Exiles sit by the rivers of Babylon and weep when they remember Zion, hang up their harps when their captors ask for a song, and vow not to forget Jerusalem; the psalm ends with a plea against Babylon and Edom.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the exiles in Psalm 137 will not sing and what they vow about Jerusalem?
ev: Read 137:1-6 and say what the exiles refuse to do and what they promise.

nodes.t: Psalm 138: I will praise thee with my whole heart
nodes.d: The speaker praises the LORD for his lovingkindness and truth, for answering when he cried, says kings shall sing of the LORD and that though he is high he regards the lowly, and says the LORD will perfect that which concerns him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the speaker says in Psalm 138:6-8 about God and the lowly?
ev: Read 138:1-8 and say what the speaker praises God for.

nodes.t: Psalm 139: O LORD, thou hast searched me and known me
nodes.d: The speaker says the LORD knows his sitting and rising and thoughts, that he cannot flee from his presence in heaven, the depths or the uttermost sea, that God formed him in the womb so that he is fearfully and wonderfully made, and asks God to search him and lead him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 139 says about God’s knowledge of us and his presence?
ev: Read 139:1-6, 139:7-12 and 139:13-16 and say what each part says about God.
Read 139:23-24 as a prayer.

nodes.t: Psalms 140-142: deliver me from violent men; I cried unto the LORD
nodes.d: Psalm 140 asks the LORD to deliver the speaker from evil and violent men whose tongues are like serpents; Psalm 141 asks that his prayer be set before the LORD like incense and that he be kept from wickedness; Psalm 142 pours out his complaint, saying the LORD is his refuge and portion.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 141:2-4 and 142:5 say about the speaker’s prayer and refuge?
ev: Read 140:1-3, 141:1-4 and 142:1-7 and list what the speaker asks.

nodes.t: Psalm 143: enter not into judgment with thy servant
nodes.d: The speaker asks the LORD to hear and not to enter into judgment with him since in God’s sight no man living is righteous, remembers the days of old, spreads out his hands, and asks to be taught to do God’s will and led into the land of uprightness.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 143:2 says about being righteous in God’s sight?
ev: Read 143:1-2 and 143:8-10 and list what the speaker asks.

nodes.t: Psalm 144: blessed be the LORD my strength; happy is that people
nodes.d: The speaker blesses the LORD who teaches his hands to war and is his fortress and deliverer, asks what man is that God takes knowledge of him, asks for rescue from false and strange children, and describes the happy people whose God is the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 144:15 says makes a people happy?
ev: Read 144:1-4 and 144:12-15 and list the names for God and the picture of the happy people.

nodes.t: Psalm 145: I will extol thee, my God, O King
nodes.d: The speaker will bless the LORD every day and speak of his greatness, calls him gracious, full of compassion, slow to anger, good to all, near to all who call on him, upholding the fallen, and says his kingdom is an everlasting kingdom.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} read Psalm 145:8-9 and name three things it says about the LORD?
ev: Read 145:8-9 and 145:13-20 and list what is said about God’s character and care.

nodes.t: Psalms 146-148: praise the LORD from the heavens and the earth
nodes.d: Psalm 146 says to praise the LORD all one’s life and not to trust in princes, since the LORD gives justice and feeds the hungry; Psalm 147 praises him for rebuilding Jerusalem, healing the broken-hearted and his word on the earth; Psalm 148 calls angels, the sun, moon, stars, sea creatures, mountains and kings to praise him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list five things called to praise the LORD in Psalm 148?
ev: List what is called to praise the LORD in Psalm 148 and what the LORD does in 146:7-9.

nodes.t: Psalms 149-150: let every thing that hath breath praise the LORD
nodes.d: Psalm 149 calls the saints to sing a new song to the LORD with dancing and swords in their hands; Psalm 150 closes the book by calling for praise of God in his sanctuary and firmament with trumpet, harp, cymbals and all that has breath.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} read Psalm 150 and say who is to praise the LORD and with what?
ev: Read Psalm 150 and list where, why and with what God is to be praised.

nodes.t: Proverbs: overview
nodes.d: Proverbs begins with the proverbs of Solomon son of David (1:1), sets out a father’s teaching about wisdom and folly (1-9), gathers many short sayings (10-29), and ends with the words of Agur (30) and of king Lemuel (31).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name the main sections of Proverbs and who is named as the source of each?
ev: Describe the main sections of Proverbs: 1-9, 10-22, 22-24, 25-29, 30, 31.

nodes.t: The purpose of Proverbs and the fear of the LORD
nodes.d: Proverbs is given to know wisdom and instruction, to give prudence to the simple and knowledge to the young, and it names the fear of the LORD as the beginning of knowledge while fools despise wisdom.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} read Proverbs 1:7 and explain it in their own words?
ev: Name what Proverbs 1:2-4 says the book is for and what 1:7 calls the beginning of knowledge.

nodes.t: Do not follow sinners; wisdom cries out
nodes.d: A father urges his son to hear instruction and not consent when sinners entice him to join violence; Wisdom cries in the streets and warns those who hate knowledge and refuse her reproof.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the two warnings in Proverbs 1: the sinners’ enticing and Wisdom’s rebuke?
ev: Describe the enticement of 1:10-14 and the warning of 1:24-33.

nodes.t: Seeking wisdom: protection and the right path
nodes.d: The father says that if the son seeks wisdom like silver he will understand the fear of the LORD, and wisdom will deliver him from evil men and from the strange woman and keep him on the way of good men.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the son must do and what he will receive in Proverbs 2?
ev: List what Proverbs 2 says the LORD gives and what wisdom keeps the son from.

nodes.t: Trust in the LORD with all your heart
nodes.d: The father tells his son to keep his commandments, trust in the LORD and not lean on his own understanding, accept the LORD’s correction, value wisdom above silver and gold, and do good to his neighbour.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Proverbs 3:5-6 and give one example of leaning on one’s own understanding?
ev: Read 3:5-6 and say what the son is told to do and what the LORD does.
Find 3:11-12 and say what it says about correction.

nodes.t: Get wisdom; guard your heart
nodes.d: A father recalls the teaching he received, tells his son to get wisdom and understanding, to avoid the path of the wicked, and to keep his heart with all diligence since the issues of life flow from it.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain 4:23 and name the two paths described in chapter 4?
ev: Contrast the paths in 4:14-19 and 4:18.
Say what 4:23 tells the son to guard.

nodes.t: Warnings against the strange woman
nodes.d: The father warns his son against the strange woman whose lips drop honey but whose end is bitter and whose feet go down to death, and urges him to find joy in the wife of his youth.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the warning of Proverbs 5 and the counsel given in 5:15-19?
ev: Read Proverbs 5:3-6 and 5:15-19 and contrast the warning with the counsel.

nodes.t: Surety, sloth and seven abominations
nodes.d: Proverbs warns against becoming surety for a neighbour, sends the sluggard to the ant, describes the froward man who sows discord, and lists six things the LORD hates, even seven.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list some of the seven things the LORD hates in Proverbs 6:16-19?
ev: List the six things and the seventh named in 6:16-19.
Say what the ant teaches in 6:6-8.

nodes.t: Keep the commandment; the snare of adultery
nodes.d: The father says the commandment is a lamp and the law is light, warns that adultery brings ruin and burning that cannot be hidden, and in chapter 7 tells how a simple young man is lured by a woman and walks to her house like an ox to the slaughter.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the scene in Proverbs 7 and the warning it ends with?
ev: Describe the young man’s steps in 7:6-23 and the closing warning in 7:24-27.

nodes.t: Wisdom calls aloud and was there at creation
nodes.d: Wisdom cries out to the simple, says she is better than rubies, loves those who love her, and describes herself as brought forth by the LORD before the earth and rejoicing when he set the heavens and the foundations of the earth.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Wisdom says about herself in Proverbs 8:22-31?
ev: Read 8:22-31 and say what Wisdom says about her place before and during creation.
List what Wisdom offers in 8:12-21.

nodes.t: Two invitations: Wisdom’s house and Folly’s seat
nodes.d: Wisdom builds a house, prepares a feast and calls the simple to come, while a foolish woman sits at her door and calls them to stolen waters; the beginning of wisdom is the fear of the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} compare the invitation of Wisdom and the invitation of the foolish woman in Proverbs 9?
ev: Compare the two invitations in 9:1-6 and 9:13-18.
Read 9:10.

nodes.t: Proverbs of Solomon: the righteous, the wicked and words (10-11)
nodes.d: Short sayings contrast the righteous and the wicked, the diligent and the lazy, and the mouth that gives life with the mouth that harms; chapter 11 adds sayings on integrity, pride, surety and generosity.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} pick one saying from Proverbs 10 or 11 and explain what two ways of life it contrasts?
ev: Collect three contrasts between righteous and wicked from chapter 10 and chapter 11.

nodes.t: Fools, counsel, truth and diligence (12-13)
nodes.d: The sayings praise truthful lips over lying tongues, the one who hears counsel over the fool who is right in his own eyes, and diligent work over slothfulness; chapter 13 speaks about the mouth, wealth and discipline.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Proverbs 12:15 and give a saying from chapters 12-13 about work?
ev: Find a saying about speech, one about work, and one about counsel in chapters 12-13.

nodes.t: The fear of the LORD, the simple and the prudent (14-15)
nodes.d: The sayings contrast the simple who believe every word with the prudent who consider their steps, call the fear of the LORD a fountain of life, say that oppressing the poor insults their Maker, and teach that a soft answer turns away wrath.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Proverbs 15:1 and give an example from daily life?
ev: Read 14:27, 14:31 and 15:1 and say what each teaches.

nodes.t: The LORD directs; pride and strife (16-17)
nodes.d: The sayings say a man’s plans are before the LORD, that pride goes before destruction, that the LORD tries hearts as a furnace tries gold, and that justifying the wicked or condemning the just is an abomination to him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Proverbs 16:18 and name one saying about the LORD’s part in human plans in chapter 16?
ev: Read 16:3, 16:18 and 17:15 and state the lesson of each.

nodes.t: The tongue, friends, anger, rich and poor (18-19)
nodes.d: The sayings warn that a fool’s mouth is his destruction, that death and life are in the power of the tongue, that a brother offended is hard to win, that discretion defers anger, and that the poor are often forsaken while the fear of the LORD leads to life.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Proverbs 18:21 in their own words?
ev: Read 18:21 and 19:11 and say what each teaches.

nodes.t: Honest weights, justice and the safety of the LORD (20-21)
nodes.d: The sayings say wine is a mocker, that divers weights are an abomination to the LORD, that doing justice is more acceptable to him than sacrifice, and that the horse is prepared for battle but safety is of the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Proverbs 21:3 and say why it matters?
ev: Read 20:23, 21:3 and 21:31 and state what each says.

nodes.t: Good name, training a child, and the poor (22:1-16)
nodes.d: The sayings praise a good name over riches, say the rich and poor meet before their maker, tell parents to train up a child in his way, and say the rich rule over the poor while the borrower is servant to the lender.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Proverbs 22:6 and name something from 22:1-16 about the poor?
ev: Read 22:1, 22:2 and 22:6 and say what each teaches.

nodes.t: Sayings of the wise: do not rob the poor, do not envy sinners
nodes.d: The writer calls the reader to bow the ear to the words of the wise so that trust may be in the LORD, forbids robbing the poor, warns against greed for riches, correction of a child, the drunkard and the winebibber, and urges buying truth and not envying sinners.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the writer says is the reason for these sayings in Proverbs 22:17-21?
ev: Read 23:29-35 and describe the picture of strong drink.
Read 22:17-21 and say why the writer addresses the reader.

nodes.t: More sayings of the wise: wisdom, enemies and the sluggard’s field
nodes.d: The sayings say not to envy evil men, that wise men are strong, that respect of persons in judgment is not good, that one should not rejoice when an enemy falls or repay evil, and the writer learns a lesson from the field of the slothful man.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Proverbs 24:17 and 24:29 say about enemies?
ev: Read 24:17-18 and 24:29 and say what each commands.
Retell what the writer sees in 24:30-34.

nodes.t: More proverbs of Solomon: kings, neighbours and fitting words (25)
nodes.d: These proverbs, which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out, speak of the glory of God to conceal a thing and the honour of kings to search it out, a word fitly spoken, restraint with a neighbour, and kindness to an enemy.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what 25:1 says about the source of chapters 25-29 and give one saying from chapter 25?
ev: Read 25:1 and say who copied these proverbs.
Find the saying about a word fitly spoken (25:11).

nodes.t: Fools, sluggards and talebearers (26)
nodes.d: The proverbs liken honour for a fool to a stone bound in a sling, say a fool returns to his folly as a dog to its vomit, picture the slothful turning on his bed like a door on its hinges, and say strife ceases where there is no talebearer.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list two pictures Proverbs 26 uses for a fool or a sluggard?
ev: Find three images used for the fool and the sluggard in chapter 26.

nodes.t: Friends, boasting and tending flocks (27)
nodes.d: The proverbs say not to boast of tomorrow or of yourself, that open rebuke is better than secret love, that iron sharpens iron, and that a man should know the state of his flocks.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Proverbs 27:17 and name one other saying about friends or boasting in chapter 27?
ev: Read 27:5-6 and 27:17 and explain the lesson on friendship.

nodes.t: Rulers, justice and confessing sin (28-29)
nodes.d: The proverbs say the wicked flee when no man pursues while the righteous are bold as a lion, that confessing and forsaking sin brings mercy, that the poor and the oppressed matter to rulers, that when the righteous rule the people rejoice, and that he who trusts his own heart is a fool.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Proverbs 28:13 and give one saying about rulers from chapters 28-29?
ev: Read 28:13 and 29:2 and say what each teaches.
Contrast 28:26 with the proverbs on the fear of the LORD.

nodes.t: The words of Agur
nodes.d: Agur confesses he lacks understanding, asks who has ascended to heaven and gathered the wind, says every word of God is pure, asks for neither poverty nor riches, and lists things that are never satisfied or too wonderful and things that are small yet wise.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Agur prays for in Proverbs 30:7-9?
ev: Read 30:5-9 and state what Agur asks of God.

nodes.t: The words of king Lemuel
nodes.d: King Lemuel recounts what his mother taught him: not to give his strength to women or to strong drink, and to open his mouth for the dumb and to plead for the poor and needy.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Lemuel’s mother tells him about kings and the poor in Proverbs 31:1-9?
ev: Read 31:8-9 and say what the king is told to do for those who cannot speak for themselves.

nodes.t: The virtuous woman
nodes.d: A closing poem asks who can find a virtuous woman and describes her trust, work, care for her household and for the poor, and wise speech, concluding that a woman who fears the LORD shall be praised.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the woman of Proverbs 31 and read what 31:30 says is to be praised?
ev: List the works and character traits of the woman in 31:10-27.
Read 31:30 and say what is praised.

nodes.t: Ecclesiastes: overview
nodes.d: The Preacher, son of David, king in Jerusalem, examines life under the sun and declares that all is vanity, yet counsels the fear of God and keeping his commandments, for God will bring every work into judgment (12:13-14).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the Preacher’s repeated word “vanity” and his conclusion in chapter 12?
ev: Say who speaks in Ecclesiastes and state the closing conclusion in 12:13-14.

nodes.t: All is vanity: the weariness of life under the sun
nodes.d: The Preacher says all is vanity, that one generation goes and another comes while the earth abides, that the sun and wind keep returning, that there is nothing new, and that he gave his heart to know wisdom and found it vexation.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what the Preacher means by “under the sun” in chapter 1?
ev: Read 1:2-11 and list the cycles named.
Say what the Preacher concludes in 1:14.

nodes.t: Pleasure, wealth and labour are vanity
nodes.d: The Preacher tests pleasure, great works, gardens and riches, then sees that the wise and the fool share one event, that he must leave his labour to another, and says enjoying good in labour is from God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list what the Preacher tried in chapter 2 and what he concluded?
ev: List what the Preacher tried in 2:1-10 and his verdict in 2:11.
Read 2:24-26 and state what comes from the hand of God.

nodes.t: A time for everything
nodes.d: The Preacher says there is a season for every purpose, from birth and death to weeping and laughing, that God made everything beautiful in its time and put eternity in men’s hearts yet no man can find out his work, and that all go to the dust.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} read Ecclesiastes 3:1-8 and explain what 3:11 adds?
ev: Read 3:1-8 and list four pairs.
Read 3:11 and 3:14 and say what the Preacher says about God’s work.

nodes.t: Oppression, envy and two are better than one
nodes.d: The Preacher sees the tears of the oppressed with no comforter, that toil arises from envy, that a man alone has no second, and that two are better than one and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why two are better than one according to Ecclesiastes 4:9-12?
ev: Read 4:9-12 and list the reasons two are better than one.

nodes.t: Guard your step in God’s house; the vanity of riches
nodes.d: The Preacher says to keep your foot when going to the house of God, not to be hasty with the mouth or with vows, and that he who loves silver will not be satisfied with silver; enjoying one’s labour is a gift of God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Ecclesiastes 5:1-7 says about speaking to God?
ev: Read 5:1-7 and list the instructions about worship and vows.
Read 5:10-15 and state what is said about loving riches.

nodes.t: Wealth without enjoyment; what is man the better?
nodes.d: The Preacher describes a man to whom God gives riches but not the power to eat of them, says a stillborn child has more rest, and asks who knows what is good for man.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} summarize the “evil” the Preacher sees in Ecclesiastes 6:1-2?
ev: Say what evil the Preacher describes in 6:1-2 and what question he asks in 6:11-12.

nodes.t: Better is the house of mourning; wisdom and its limits
nodes.d: The Preacher gathers sayings that the house of mourning is better than feasting, the rebuke of the wise better than the song of fools, and the end of a thing better than its beginning, notes there is not a just man who sins not, and says wisdom is far from him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list three “better” sayings from Ecclesiastes 7 and read what 7:20 says?
ev: Find the “better than” sayings in chapter 7 and say what each prefers.
Read 7:20 and 7:29.

nodes.t: Obey the king; the work of God cannot be found out
nodes.d: The Preacher counsels keeping the king’s commandment, observes that sentence against evil is not carried out speedily, that the righteous sometimes get what the wicked deserve, and that man cannot find out the work of God under the sun.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what troubles the Preacher in Ecclesiastes 8:14?
ev: Read 8:11-14 and state what puzzles the Preacher.
Read 8:17.

nodes.t: One event comes to all; enjoy life; time and chance
nodes.d: The Preacher says the same event comes to the righteous and the wicked, that the living know they shall die, tells his reader to eat and drink with joy and enjoy life with the wife he loves, and says the race is not always to the swift and wisdom is better than weapons.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Ecclesiastes 9:11 says about outcomes?
ev: Read 9:7-10 and list the counsel given.
Read 9:11-12 and say what the Preacher observes.

nodes.t: Dead flies and fools: sayings on folly and wisdom
nodes.d: Sayings say dead flies spoil ointment, that he who digs a pit may fall into it, that a fool is full of words, and that one should not curse the king, even in thought.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain one saying about folly from Ecclesiastes 10?
ev: Find three sayings in chapter 10 about the fool and say what harm each describes.

nodes.t: Cast your bread on the waters; remember your Creator
nodes.d: The Preacher tells men to give a portion and sow in the morning since they cannot know the work of God, to rejoice in their youth yet know that God will bring them to judgment, and to remember their Creator before the evil days come.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} read Ecclesiastes 12:1 and explain what it tells the young to do?
ev: Read 11:9-12:1 and say what is said about youth.
List the images of old age in 12:1-7.

nodes.t: The conclusion: fear God and keep his commandments
nodes.d: The Preacher sought out acceptable words, says the words of the wise are as goads and nails given by one Shepherd, warns that of making many books there is no end, and concludes that the whole duty of man is to fear God and keep his commandments, for God will bring every work into judgment.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} state the conclusion of Ecclesiastes in 12:13-14 in their own words?
ev: Read 12:13-14 and state the conclusion.

nodes.t: Song of Solomon: overview
nodes.d: The Song of songs, which is Solomon’s (1:1), is a poem of dialogue between a bride, her beloved and the daughters of Jerusalem, praising mutual love from first longing to its strength (8:6-7).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the speakers in the Song of Solomon and the theme of the poem?
ev: Name the speakers in the Song and the main settings (gardens, vineyards, the city, the wilderness).

nodes.t: Longing and praise: the first meeting
nodes.d: The bride longs for her beloved and speaks of him as a bundle of myrrh; he praises her as a lily among thorns, and she says she is sick of love, charging the daughters of Jerusalem not to awaken love before it pleases.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} identify who is speaking in Song of Solomon 1-2:7 and what they say about each other?
ev: Find the speakers in 1:2-4 and 2:1-7 and list the images used for love.

nodes.t: Arise, my love: the voice of the beloved in spring
nodes.d: The bride hears her beloved coming over the mountains and he calls her to arise and come away because the winter is past and flowers appear; she asks for the little foxes to be caught, and says my beloved is mine and I am his.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the invitation in Song of Solomon 2:10-13 and the bride’s answer in 2:16?
ev: Read 2:10-13 and list the signs of spring.
Read 2:16 and say what the bride says of the two of them.

nodes.t: Seeking him whom my soul loves
nodes.d: By night the bride seeks her beloved in the city, is found by the watchmen, and then finds him and holds him until she brings him to her mother’s house; she again charges the daughters of Jerusalem.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the search in Song of Solomon 3:1-4?
ev: Retell the bride’s search in 3:1-4.

nodes.t: Solomon’s bed and the daughters of Zion
nodes.d: A procession is described coming out of the wilderness with smoke of myrrh and frankincense around the bed of Solomon with sixty valiant men, and the daughters of Zion are called to behold king Solomon with his crown on his wedding day.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the scene of 3:6-11 and name who is being looked at?
ev: Read 3:6-11 and list what is carried and who accompanies it.

nodes.t: A garden enclosed
nodes.d: The beloved praises his bride at length, calls her my spouse, his garden enclosed and a spring shut up; she invites him to come into his garden, and he says he has come into his garden.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the garden images in Song of Solomon 4:12-5:1?
ev: Read 4:12-5:1 and list the images of the garden and what the bride and groom say.

nodes.t: I opened to my beloved, but he was gone
nodes.d: The bride hears her beloved knocking at night, hesitates, and opens to find him gone; the watchmen strike her, and she asks the daughters of Jerusalem to tell him she is sick of love; they ask what is her beloved, and she describes him, saying he is hers.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the events of Song of Solomon 5:2-8 and what the bride says in 6:3?
ev: Retell 5:2-8 and read 6:3.

nodes.t: Praise of her beauty
nodes.d: The beloved praises his bride as beautiful as Tirzah and comely as Jerusalem, says there are many queens and concubines but she alone is his dove, and in chapter 7 admires her form and desires her; she says I am my beloved’s and his desire is toward me.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the bride says of herself and her beloved in Song of Solomon 7:10?
ev: Find 6:8-10 and 7:10 and say what is said of the bride.

nodes.t: Come, let us go forth into the field
nodes.d: The bride invites her beloved to go forth into the field and lodge in the villages and give him her love there; she wishes he were as her brother, and charges the daughters of Jerusalem once more not to awaken love before it pleases.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the bride invites her beloved to do in Song of Solomon 7:10-13?
ev: Read 7:10-8:4 and list what the bride offers.

nodes.t: Love is strong as death
nodes.d: The bride asks to be set as a seal upon his heart, saying love is strong as death and many waters cannot quench it; the closing verses speak of a little sister, Solomon’s vineyard, and the bride calling her beloved to come quickly.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} read Song of Solomon 8:6-7 and explain what it says about love?
ev: Read 8:6-7 and list the images used for the strength of love.

nodes.t: Matthew: overview
nodes.d: The gospel of Matthew, from the genealogy of Jesus Christ, son of David and son of Abraham (1:1), through the five great discourses, the passion and the resurrection, to the closing commission (28:16-20).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what Matthew is about and how it begins and ends?
ev: Describe the movement of the book: birth and preparation (1-4), the Sermon on the Mount (5-7), miracles and mission (8-12), parables of the kingdom (13), teaching on the way to Jerusalem (14-23), the coming kingdom (24-25), the passion and resurrection (26-28)
Name where the book starts and ends

nodes.t: Mark: overview
nodes.d: The gospel of Mark, from “the beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God” (1:1) through Jesus’ ministry in Galilee, the road to Jerusalem and his death, to the empty tomb and commission.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what Mark is about and where it begins and ends?
ev: Describe the movement of the book: John and the start of ministry (1), Galilee (1-8), the way to Jerusalem (8-10), the last week and passion (11-15), the empty tomb (16)
Say what Mark calls the book in 1:1

nodes.t: Matthew opens with Jesus’ genealogy
nodes.d: Matthew begins by tracing Jesus Christ as son of David and son of Abraham through three sets of fourteen generations, naming Tamar, Rahab, Ruth and Bathsheba along the way.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Matthew starts with Abraham and David?
ev: Say whose son Jesus is called in 1:1
Name the three groups of fourteen generations (1:17)

nodes.t: The birth of Jesus announced to Joseph
nodes.d: Joseph finds Mary with child by the Holy Ghost, and an angel tells him in a dream to take her as wife and name the child Jesus, who will save his people from their sins.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Joseph was told in his dream and why the child was named Jesus?
ev: Retell what the angel told Joseph
Say what the name Jesus is linked to in 1:21

nodes.t: The wise men and Herod
nodes.d: Wise men from the east come to Jerusalem to worship the newborn King of the Jews, and Herod learns from the scribes that Bethlehem is the place; the star leads them to the child and they bring gifts.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell the story of the wise men and name their gifts?
ev: Retell why the wise men came and where they found Jesus
Describe Herod’s reaction

nodes.t: Flight to Egypt and return to Nazareth
nodes.d: Warned in dreams, Joseph takes the child to Egypt away from Herod, who has the children of Bethlehem killed; after Herod dies the family returns and settles in Nazareth.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the escape from Herod and where the family finally lived?
ev: Trace the family’s journey: Bethlehem, Egypt, Nazareth
Name the three places where Matthew says a prophecy was fulfilled (2:15, 17-18, 23)

nodes.t: John the Baptist prepares the way
nodes.d: John preaches repentance in the wilderness, baptizes in the Jordan, warns Pharisees and Sadducees to bear fruit, and says one mightier will baptize with the Holy Ghost and fire.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what John the Baptist told people to do and who he said was coming?
ev: Say what John preached
Explain the difference John draws between his baptism and the coming one’s

nodes.t: The baptism of Jesus
nodes.d: Jesus comes from Galilee to be baptized by John to fulfil all righteousness; the heavens open, the Spirit descends like a dove and a voice calls him beloved Son.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened when Jesus was baptized?
ev: Describe what was seen and heard at the Jordan
Say what Jesus told John in 3:15

nodes.t: The temptation in the wilderness
nodes.d: After forty days of fasting Jesus is tempted three times by the devil and answers each with “it is written”; the devil leaves and angels minister to him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the devil offered Jesus and how Jesus replied?
ev: List the three temptations
Say what Jesus answered each time

nodes.t: Jesus begins in Galilee and calls fishermen
nodes.d: Hearing John is imprisoned, Jesus moves to Capernaum, preaches repentance for the kingdom of heaven, calls Peter, Andrew, James and John from their nets, and heals great crowds.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Jesus called his first disciples?
ev: Name the four fishermen Jesus called
Summarise what Jesus did throughout Galilee (4:23-25)

nodes.t: The Beatitudes and salt and light
nodes.d: Seated on a mountain, Jesus pronounces blessings on the poor in spirit, mourners, meek, merciful and others, then calls his disciples the salt of the earth and light of the world.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain two of the blessings and what it means to be light of the world?
ev: Recite or paraphrase several Beatitudes
Explain the images of salt and light

nodes.t: Jesus and the law and the prophets
nodes.d: Jesus says he has not come to destroy the law or the prophets but to fulfil them, that not a jot or tittle will pass, and that righteousness must exceed that of the scribes and Pharisees.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus says about the law in 5:17-20?
ev: State what Jesus says he came to do with the law
Explain what is required for entering the kingdom (5:20)

nodes.t: Murder, anger, adultery and lust
nodes.d: Jesus takes the commandments against killing and adultery to the heart: anger and contempt, and lustful looks, are judged, and reconciliation and cutting off sin are urged.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Jesus deepens the commands about murder and adultery?
ev: Contrast “ye have heard” with “I say unto you” in 5:21-22 and 27-28
Describe what Jesus says to do before offering a gift at the altar

nodes.t: Divorce, oaths, retaliation and love for enemies
nodes.d: Jesus teaches on divorce, on plain speech instead of oaths, on not resisting evil with evil, and on loving and praying for enemies, as the Father gives sun and rain to evil and good.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus says about loving enemies and why?
ev: Say what Jesus teaches about oaths (5:33-37)
Explain the command about enemies and the reason given in 5:45

nodes.t: Giving and prayer in secret
nodes.d: Jesus warns against giving, praying and fasting to be seen by people and tells his hearers to do these before the Father who sees in secret.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Jesus says to give and pray in secret?
ev: Name the three practices Jesus mentions
Explain what Jesus says about those who do them to be seen

nodes.t: The Lord’s Prayer
nodes.d: Jesus gives a pattern for prayer addressed to “Our Father which art in heaven”, with petitions for his name, kingdom and will, daily bread, forgiveness and deliverance from evil, and adds a saying on forgiving others.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say the Lord’s Prayer and explain one petition?
ev: Recite the prayer or list its petitions
Say what 6:14-15 teaches about forgiveness

nodes.t: Treasure in heaven and not being anxious
nodes.d: Jesus contrasts earthly and heavenly treasure, says no one can serve God and mammon, and tells disciples not to be anxious since the Father feeds the birds and clothes the lilies; seek first his kingdom.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Jesus says not to worry and what to seek first?
ev: Explain the two kinds of treasure
Use the birds and lilies to say why not to worry

nodes.t: Judging, asking and the golden rule
nodes.d: Jesus warns against judging while a beam is in one’s own eye, urges asking, seeking and knocking since the Father gives good gifts, and sums up the law and prophets in doing to others as you would have done to you.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain 7:1-5 and 7:12 in their own words?
ev: Retell the beam and the mote
State the golden rule from 7:12

nodes.t: The two ways, false prophets and the two builders
nodes.d: Jesus calls hearers to the narrow gate, warns of false prophets known by fruit, says not everyone who says “Lord, Lord” enters, and closes with the wise man on rock and the foolish man on sand; the crowds are astonished.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell the story of the two builders and what it teaches?
ev: Contrast the two gates and the two houses
Say how the crowds responded (7:28-29)

nodes.t: Healing a leper and the centurion’s servant
nodes.d: Coming down from the mountain, Jesus cleanses a leper by a touch and heals a centurion’s servant with a word, marvelling at the centurion’s faith and saying many will come from east and west to the kingdom.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the centurion said and how Jesus responded?
ev: Describe the two healings
Say what Jesus said about the centurion’s faith

nodes.t: Healing Peter’s mother-in-law and many others
nodes.d: Jesus heals Peter’s wife’s mother of a fever and, that evening, casts out spirits and heals all who are brought; Matthew links this to a word of Isaiah.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Jesus did in Peter’s house and that evening?
ev: Retell the healing in Peter’s house
Say what Matthew says was fulfilled in 8:17

nodes.t: The cost of following Jesus
nodes.d: Two would-be followers hear that the Son of man has nowhere to lay his head and that following him comes before burying one’s father.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus told the scribe and the other disciple?
ev: Summarise what Jesus says to each man
Explain what these sayings show about discipleship

nodes.t: Jesus calms the storm
nodes.d: A great tempest swamps the boat while Jesus sleeps; the disciples wake him, he rebukes winds and sea, and they marvel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened on the boat and what the disciples wondered?
ev: Retell the storm in order
Say what the disciples asked in 8:27

nodes.t: The two demon-possessed men and the swine
nodes.d: On the far shore two fierce men from the tombs meet Jesus; the demons ask to enter a herd of swine, which run into the sea, and the city begs Jesus to leave.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the demons asked and how the townspeople responded?
ev: Retell what happened to the swine
Describe the town’s response

nodes.t: Forgiving and healing the paralytic
nodes.d: Seeing faith, Jesus tells a paralysed man his sins are forgiven; when scribes call it blasphemy, he heals the man to show the Son of man has power on earth to forgive sins.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the healing and what Jesus said about forgiving sins?
ev: Explain why the scribes objected
Say how Jesus showed his authority

nodes.t: Matthew called and eating with sinners
nodes.d: Jesus calls Matthew the tax collector, eats with publicans and sinners, and answers the Pharisees that the sick need a physician and that he came to call sinners.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Jesus ate with publicans and sinners?
ev: Say who Jesus called and where he found him
Explain the “physician” saying

nodes.t: The bridegroom and new wine
nodes.d: Asked why his disciples do not fast, Jesus speaks of the bridegroom being taken away, and of new cloth on old garments and new wine in old bottles.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Jesus’ answer about fasting?
ev: State the question from John’s disciples
Explain one of the two pictures in 9:16-17

nodes.t: The ruler’s daughter and the woman with the issue of blood
nodes.d: On his way to a ruler’s dead daughter, Jesus is touched by a woman with a twelve-year bleeding, whom he calls daughter and heals; then he raises the girl.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Jesus helped the woman and the ruler’s daughter?
ev: Retell both healings in order
Say what Jesus told the woman

nodes.t: Two blind men and a mute man
nodes.d: Two blind men call him Son of David and are healed according to their faith; a mute demoniac speaks, and the Pharisees say he casts out devils by the prince of devils.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the blind men asked and how the Pharisees reacted to the mute man?
ev: Describe the two healings
Say what the Pharisees claimed

nodes.t: The plenteous harvest
nodes.d: Seeing the multitudes like sheep without a shepherd, Jesus is moved with compassion and tells his disciples to pray that the Lord of the harvest send labourers.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus asked his disciples to pray for?
ev: Say what moved Jesus to compassion
Explain the harvest saying

nodes.t: The twelve named and sent out
nodes.d: Jesus gives the twelve authority to heal and cast out spirits, names them, and sends them to the lost sheep of Israel to preach the kingdom, with instructions about provision and receiving.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell who Jesus sent and what he told them to do?
ev: Name several of the twelve
List the instructions about what to take and what to say

nodes.t: Warnings of persecution and the Spirit’s help
nodes.d: Jesus sends the twelve as sheep among wolves, warns of courts and family betrayal, promises the Spirit of the Father will speak in them, and says he who endures to the end is saved.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus said disciples should expect and what help they would have?
ev: List the troubles Jesus foretells
Say what promise he gives about what to speak

nodes.t: Fear not, confess Christ, and the cost
nodes.d: Jesus tells his disciples to fear God not men, notes the Father’s care for sparrows, says to confess him before men, that he brings a sword that divides households, and that those who lose their life for him will find it.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus says about fear, confessing him, and taking up the cross?
ev: Explain why disciples need not fear (10:29-31)
Describe what confessing and denying him leads to

nodes.t: John’s question and Jesus’ witness to John
nodes.d: John in prison sends disciples to ask whether Jesus is the one to come; Jesus points to the works done and then speaks of John as more than a prophet, the messenger of whom it is written “I send my messenger before thy face”, and of an unresponsive generation.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Jesus answered John’s question and what he said about John?
ev: Say what Jesus told John’s disciples to report
Explain how Jesus describes John

nodes.t: Woes on the unrepentant cities
nodes.d: Jesus denounces Chorazin, Bethsaida and Capernaum for not repenting despite his mighty works and says it will be more tolerable for Tyre, Sidon and Sodom in the day of judgment.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Jesus rebuked those cities?
ev: Name the three cities
Explain why judgment is greater on them

nodes.t: The Father’s revelation and “Come unto me”
nodes.d: Jesus thanks the Father for revealing these things to babes, says no one knows the Son but the Father and those to whom the Son reveals him, and invites the weary to take his yoke and find rest.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus invites the weary to do and what he promises?
ev: Say who Jesus says he is known by
Explain the invitation of 11:28-30

nodes.t: Plucking grain on the sabbath
nodes.d: Pharisees object that the disciples pluck grain on the sabbath; Jesus cites David eating the shewbread and the priests in the temple, and says the Son of man is Lord of the sabbath.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Jesus said about David and the sabbath?
ev: Explain the Pharisees’ objection
Say what examples Jesus gave

nodes.t: Healing the withered hand and the chosen servant
nodes.d: In the synagogue Jesus heals a man’s withered hand on the sabbath after saying it is lawful to do good; the Pharisees plot, and Matthew says his gentle ministry fulfils Isaiah’s word of the chosen servant.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Jesus healed on the sabbath and what the Pharisees planned?
ev: Retell the healing and the reason Jesus gave
Say what the Pharisees did next

nodes.t: The Beelzebub accusation and the unpardonable word
nodes.d: After a blind and mute man is healed, the Pharisees say Jesus casts out devils by Beelzebub; he answers that a divided kingdom falls, that he casts out by the Spirit of God, and warns of blasphemy against the Holy Ghost and of the words people speak.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the Pharisees claimed and how Jesus answered?
ev: Summarise Jesus’ reply about a divided kingdom
Say what he teaches about the heart and words

nodes.t: The sign of Jonah
nodes.d: Asked for a sign, Jesus says only the sign of Jonah will be given, the three days in the whale, and that Nineveh and the queen of the south will condemn that generation; he adds a saying about an unclean spirit returning.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus meant by the sign of Jonah?
ev: State the one sign Jesus promises
Explain why Nineveh and the queen of the south are mentioned

nodes.t: Jesus’ true family
nodes.d: When his mother and brothers wait outside, Jesus points to his disciples and says whoever does the will of his Father in heaven is his brother, sister and mother.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain who Jesus calls his mother and brothers?
ev: Retell the scene
Say who Jesus names as his family

nodes.t: The parable of the sower
nodes.d: Jesus tells of seed falling on the path, stony ground, thorns and good ground, explains why he speaks in parables, and interprets the sower for his disciples.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what each soil in the parable stands for?
ev: Retell the four soils
Give the explanation Jesus gave for each

nodes.t: The parable of the wheat and tares
nodes.d: An enemy sows tares among wheat; the householder lets both grow until harvest, and Jesus explains the field is the world and the reapers are angels at the end of the world.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the parable of the tares and what happens at harvest?
ev: Retell the parable
Give Jesus’ interpretation of the field, seed, enemy and harvest

nodes.t: The mustard seed and the leaven
nodes.d: Jesus compares the kingdom of heaven to a tiny mustard seed that becomes a tree and to leaven hidden in three measures of meal, and Matthew says he spoke only in parables to the crowd.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell the mustard seed and leaven parables and what they say about the kingdom?
ev: Retell the two parables
Say what Matthew says in 13:34-35

nodes.t: Hidden treasure, the pearl and the net
nodes.d: Jesus likens the kingdom to treasure in a field, a pearl of great price and a net gathering good and bad fish, and tells the scribe instructed in the kingdom to bring out things new and old.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the treasure and pearl parables?
ev: Describe what each man did on finding what he sought
Explain the net parable’s picture of the end

nodes.t: Rejected in his own country
nodes.d: In his home synagogue Jesus is questioned as the carpenter’s son whose family they know; they are offended, and he does few mighty works there because of unbelief.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Jesus was not honoured in his own country?
ev: Say why the people were offended
Explain Jesus’ saying about a prophet’s honour

nodes.t: The death of John the Baptist
nodes.d: Herod, hearing of Jesus, thinks John is risen; Matthew recounts how Herod imprisoned John over Herodias and, because of an oath at his birthday, had him beheaded; John’s disciples bury him and tell Jesus.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened to John the Baptist?
ev: Retell why John was imprisoned
Describe how Herod came to order the execution

nodes.t: Feeding the five thousand
nodes.d: Hearing of John, Jesus withdraws; the crowds follow, he heals them, and with five loaves and two fishes he feeds about five thousand men with twelve baskets left over.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how Jesus fed the crowd?
ev: Say how much food there was and how much remained
Describe what Jesus did with the loaves

nodes.t: Jesus walks on the sea and Peter sinks
nodes.d: Jesus comes to the disciples on the sea in the fourth watch; Peter walks toward him, fears the wind and begins to sink, and Jesus saves him, after which they worship him and he heals at Gennesaret.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell the story of Jesus and Peter on the water?
ev: Retell what Peter did and why he sank
Say what the disciples said when the wind ceased

nodes.t: Tradition and what defiles
nodes.d: Pharisees accuse the disciples of breaking the tradition of the elders; Jesus charges them with voiding God’s commandment by tradition and says what comes out of the heart, not what goes into the mouth, defiles.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus said defiles a person?
ev: Give Jesus’ example of tradition overriding a commandment
List what comes out of the heart (15:19)

nodes.t: The Canaanite woman’s faith
nodes.d: Near Tyre and Sidon a woman of Canaan begs for her daughter; Jesus is at first silent and speaks of the children’s bread, but she answers about crumbs and he praises her faith and heals the girl.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the woman asked and how Jesus responded?
ev: Retell the conversation
Say what Jesus said about her faith

nodes.t: Feeding the four thousand
nodes.d: After healing many at the Galilee mountain, Jesus has compassion on a crowd that has been with him three days and feeds four thousand with seven loaves and a few fishes, with seven baskets left.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell this feeding and say how it differs from the five thousand?
ev: Compare this feeding with the earlier one (14:13-21)
Give the numbers of loaves, fishes and baskets

nodes.t: The demand for a sign and the leaven of the Pharisees
nodes.d: Pharisees and Sadducees seek a sign from heaven and Jesus again points to Jonah; he then warns his disciples against the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees, which they take to mean bread but he says is their doctrine.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees is?
ev: Explain what Jesus meant by leaven
Recall the feedings he reminds them of

nodes.t: Peter’s confession at Caesarea Philippi
nodes.d: Asked who they say he is, Peter answers that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of the living God; Jesus calls him blessed, speaks of building his church on this rock, and gives the keys of the kingdom.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell who Peter said Jesus is and how Jesus replied?
ev: State what the people said and what Peter said
Say what Jesus told Peter in 16:17-19

nodes.t: The Son of man must suffer; take up your cross
nodes.d: Jesus begins to tell the disciples he must go to Jerusalem, suffer, be killed and raised the third day; Peter rebukes him and is rebuked, and Jesus calls his followers to deny themselves and take up the cross.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus said following him costs?
ev: State what Jesus foretold about himself
Explain the call to deny oneself

nodes.t: The transfiguration
nodes.d: On a high mountain Jesus is transfigured before Peter, James and John, Moses and Elias appear, and a voice from the cloud says to hear his beloved Son; coming down he speaks of Elias as already come.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the transfiguration and what the voice said?
ev: Describe what the three disciples saw and heard
Say what Jesus told them to keep silent

nodes.t: The boy with a demon, a second prediction and the temple tax
nodes.d: Jesus heals a boy the disciples could not heal, saying unbelief is the reason and faith like a mustard seed can move mountains; he again foretells his betrayal and resurrection and arranges payment of the tribute through a coin in a fish.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus said about faith like a mustard seed?
ev: Say why the disciples could not cast the spirit out
Retell the coin in the fish

nodes.t: Who is greatest, offences and the lost sheep
nodes.d: Asked who is greatest, Jesus sets a child in their midst and calls for conversion and humility, warns against causing little ones to stumble, and tells of the shepherd seeking one lost sheep.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus said makes someone greatest in the kingdom?
ev: Explain what Jesus says about becoming like a child
Retell the lost sheep

nodes.t: Reproving a brother and agreeing in prayer
nodes.d: Jesus gives steps for a brother who sins: tell him alone, then with witnesses, then the church; he speaks of binding and loosing and of his presence where two or three gather in his name.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the steps Jesus gives for a brother who sins?
ev: List the steps in 18:15-17
Say what Jesus promises in 18:20

nodes.t: The unforgiving servant
nodes.d: Peter asks how often to forgive; Jesus says seventy times seven and tells of a servant forgiven a huge debt who refuses to forgive a fellow servant a small one, so is delivered to the tormentors.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell this parable and what Jesus says it means for forgiving others?
ev: Compare the two debts
Explain the final verse (18:35)

nodes.t: Jesus on marriage and divorce
nodes.d: Tested by Pharisees, Jesus points back to male and female at the beginning and “one flesh”, says what God joined man must not separate, speaks of Moses’ allowance because of hard hearts, and says not all can receive the saying about eunuchs.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus teaches about marriage and why?
ev: Say what Jesus cites from the beginning
Explain why Moses allowed divorce according to 19:8

nodes.t: Jesus blesses the little children
nodes.d: People bring children for Jesus to lay hands on and pray; the disciples rebuke them, but Jesus says to let them come, for the kingdom of heaven belongs to such.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Jesus said about children coming to him?
ev: Retell what the disciples did and Jesus said
Say whose is the kingdom of heaven

nodes.t: The rich young man and rewards of following
nodes.d: A young man asks what good thing earns eternal life; told to keep the commandments and then to sell all and follow, he goes away sorrowful; Jesus speaks of the camel and needle and promises rewards to those who left all.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Jesus asked the young man to do and why it was hard?
ev: Say why the young man left sorrowful
Explain “with God all things are possible”

nodes.t: The labourers in the vineyard
nodes.d: A householder hires workers at different hours and pays all the same; the first complain, and he answers that he does no wrong and may be generous with his own; the last will be first and the first last.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the householder’s answer and Jesus’ closing line?
ev: Retell the parable
Say what the householder answered the complaint

nodes.t: Third prediction and the call to serve
nodes.d: Going up to Jerusalem Jesus again foretells his betrayal, mockery, crucifixion and rising; the mother of Zebedee’s sons asks for places for them, and Jesus teaches that the great must serve, for the Son of man came to give his life a ransom for many.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus said it means to be great among his followers?
ev: Describe what Jesus foretold
Explain what he says about greatness and the ransom

nodes.t: Two blind men near Jericho
nodes.d: Leaving Jericho, two blind men cry out “Lord, thou son of David”; the crowd tells them to be quiet, but Jesus stops, touches their eyes and they see and follow him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the blind men asked and what happened?
ev: Retell what the blind men cried and Jesus did
Say what they did after receiving sight

nodes.t: Jesus enters Jerusalem
nodes.d: Jesus sends two disciples for an ass and colt, and rides toward Jerusalem while crowds spread garments and branches and cry Hosanna to the son of David; Matthew says this fulfils a word about the King coming meek on an ass.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how Jesus came into Jerusalem and what the crowds said?
ev: Describe the entry
Say what the crowds shouted

nodes.t: Cleansing the temple
nodes.d: Jesus drives out the buyers and sellers, overturns tables and seats, says the house of prayer has become a den of thieves, heals the blind and lame, and answers the priests about children’s praise.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Jesus overturned the tables?
ev: Say what Jesus did and quoted
Describe what the children cried and the priests’ reaction

nodes.t: The withered fig tree
nodes.d: Hungry, Jesus finds only leaves on a fig tree and it withers; he tells the astonished disciples that faith without doubt can even move a mountain and that believing prayer receives.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened to the fig tree and what Jesus taught?
ev: Retell what happened to the tree
Say what Jesus taught about faith and prayer

nodes.t: By what authority?
nodes.d: Priests and elders ask by what authority Jesus acts; he asks whether John’s baptism was from heaven or men, and when they will not answer he will not answer them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Jesus replied to the question about his authority?
ev: State their question and Jesus’ counter-question
Explain why they would not answer

nodes.t: The parable of the two sons
nodes.d: A father tells two sons to work in his vineyard; the one who refused repents and goes, the one who agreed does not. Jesus says tax collectors and harlots go into the kingdom before the priests because they believed John.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain which son did his father’s will?
ev: Retell the parable
Say whom Jesus compares to each son

nodes.t: The parable of the wicked tenants
nodes.d: Tenants of a vineyard beat and kill the owner’s servants and then his son; Jesus cites the rejected stone made head of the corner, says the kingdom will be taken from them, and the priests perceive he speaks of them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain who the servants, son and tenants stand for in the parable?
ev: Retell the parable
Say what the priests understood

nodes.t: The wedding feast and the man without a garment
nodes.d: A king prepares a wedding for his son; invited guests refuse and are destroyed, others from the highways are gathered, and a man without a wedding garment is cast into outer darkness; many are called, few chosen.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened to those invited and the man without a garment?
ev: Retell the parable
Explain the closing line, “many are called, but few are chosen”

nodes.t: Tribute to Caesar
nodes.d: Pharisees and Herodians ask whether it is lawful to pay tribute to Caesar; Jesus asks for a coin, asks whose image is on it, and says to render to Caesar what is Caesar’s and to God what is God’s.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Jesus’ reply about the coin?
ev: Say why they asked
Explain Jesus’ answer

nodes.t: The Sadducees and the resurrection
nodes.d: Sadducees pose a puzzle about a woman married to seven brothers; Jesus says they err not knowing the scriptures or God’s power, that in the resurrection they are as angels, and that God is God of the living.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Jesus’ answer about the resurrection?
ev: Say what the Sadducees denied
Explain how Jesus uses the words about Abraham, Isaac and Jacob

nodes.t: The great commandment
nodes.d: Asked which is the great commandment, Jesus answers love the Lord with all heart, soul and mind, and love your neighbour as yourself, and says all the law and the prophets hang on these two.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say the two great commandments and what they cover?
ev: State the two commandments
Explain “on these two hang all the law and the prophets”

nodes.t: David’s son and David’s Lord
nodes.d: Jesus asks the Pharisees whose son Christ is; they say David’s, and he asks how David in spirit calls him Lord; no one can answer.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the puzzle Jesus raised about David and the Christ?
ev: Retell the question Jesus asked
Say what the Pharisees could not answer

nodes.t: Woes on the scribes and Pharisees
nodes.d: Jesus tells the crowds to do what the scribes and Pharisees say but not what they do, warns against titles and pride, pronounces seven woes for hypocrisy, and laments over Jerusalem.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus criticised in the scribes and Pharisees?
ev: List several hypocrisies Jesus names
Describe the lament over Jerusalem (23:37-39)

nodes.t: The Olivet discourse: signs and persecution
nodes.d: Leaving the temple, Jesus foretells its destruction; on the Mount of Olives he warns of deceivers, wars, famines and persecution, and says the gospel of the kingdom will be preached to all nations before the end.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list the warnings Jesus gave in 24:4-14?
ev: State what the disciples asked in 24:3
Name the events Jesus says are not yet the end

nodes.t: The abomination of desolation and the great tribulation
nodes.d: Jesus tells those in Judaea to flee when they see the abomination of desolation spoken of by Daniel, describes great tribulation and warns against false Christs.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus told his disciples to do when they see the abomination of desolation?
ev: Say what Jesus tells those in Judaea to do
Explain the warning about false Christs

nodes.t: The coming of the Son of man
nodes.d: Jesus says after the tribulation the sun will darken and the Son of man will appear in the clouds and send angels to gather the elect; he gives the fig tree parable and says his words will not pass away.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Jesus said will happen when the Son of man comes?
ev: Describe the signs and the coming
Explain the fig tree lesson

nodes.t: Watch, for no one knows the day
nodes.d: Jesus says no one but the Father knows the day, compares the coming to the days of Noah, and tells disciples to watch and be ready, with the picture of the faithful and evil servant.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Jesus told his disciples to be ready?
ev: State who knows the day and hour
Contrast the faithful and the evil servant

nodes.t: The parable of the ten virgins
nodes.d: Five wise and five foolish virgins await the bridegroom; the foolish lack oil, are away when he comes, and find the door shut. Jesus concludes: watch.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what made five virgins wise and five foolish?
ev: Retell the parable
State the lesson in 25:13

nodes.t: The parable of the talents
nodes.d: A man entrusts talents to three servants; two trade and double them and are praised, but the one who hid his talent is called wicked and slothful and cast out.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the master said to each servant?
ev: Retell the three servants’ responses
Say what the master told each

nodes.t: The judgment of the sheep and the goats
nodes.d: The Son of man sits on his throne and separates the nations as sheep and goats; the King says what was done to the least of his brethren was done to him, and the two groups go to life eternal and everlasting punishment.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain on what basis the sheep and goats are separated?
ev: List the deeds named
Say what the King says about “the least of these”

nodes.t: The plot, the anointing at Bethany and Judas’ bargain
nodes.d: Two days before Passover the rulers plot to kill Jesus; a woman anoints him at Simon the leper’s house and Jesus calls it for his burial; Judas goes to the chief priests for thirty pieces of silver.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the woman did and what Judas agreed to do?
ev: Retell the anointing and the disciples’ objection
Say what Judas did

nodes.t: The Passover and the Lord’s Supper
nodes.d: At the Passover meal Jesus says one of the twelve will betray him; he gives the bread as his body and the cup as his blood of the new testament shed for many for the remission of sins.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus said at the Passover meal about the cup and bread?
ev: Describe what Jesus said over the bread and the cup
Explain “blood of the new testament” in 26:28

nodes.t: Peter’s boast and Gethsemane
nodes.d: Jesus foretells that the disciples will scatter and Peter will deny him; in Gethsemane he prays three times that the cup may pass but not his will, while the disciples sleep.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Jesus prayed in Gethsemane?
ev: Retell what Jesus prayed
Say what happened to the disciples in the garden

nodes.t: Jesus is arrested
nodes.d: Judas arrives with a crowd and betrays Jesus with a kiss; a disciple cuts off an ear, Jesus tells him to put up the sword and says the scriptures must be fulfilled, and the disciples flee.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what happened in the garden when Jesus was arrested?
ev: Describe the betrayal
Say what Jesus said about the sword

nodes.t: Jesus before Caiaphas and the council
nodes.d: False witnesses speak against Jesus about the temple; asked if he is the Christ the Son of God he answers and speaks of the Son of man sitting on the right hand of power; the high priest cries blasphemy and they condemn him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the council asked Jesus and what they decided?
ev: Say what the false witnesses claimed
Explain the charge of blasphemy

nodes.t: Peter denies Jesus
nodes.d: Peter follows to the high priest’s palace and, challenged three times, denies knowing Jesus; the cock crows, he remembers Jesus’ word and weeps bitterly.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Peter denied Jesus and what he did afterwards?
ev: Retell the three denials
Say what Peter did when the cock crew

nodes.t: Judas repents and the field of blood
nodes.d: Seeing Jesus condemned, Judas returns the thirty silver pieces, confesses innocent blood and hangs himself; the priests buy the potter’s field, and Matthew links this to a word of Jeremy.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what happened to Judas and the silver?
ev: Say what Judas did with the money
Say what the priests did with it

nodes.t: Jesus before Pilate and Barabbas
nodes.d: Pilate asks if Jesus is King of the Jews; Jesus answers little; offered the choice, the crowd demands Barabbas and calls for Jesus to be crucified, and Pilate washes his hands.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell Pilate’s trial and the choice of Barabbas?
ev: Say who the crowd chose
Describe what Pilate and his wife said about Jesus

nodes.t: The mocking and crucifixion
nodes.d: Soldiers mock Jesus with a robe and thorns, Simon of Cyrene carries his cross, he is crucified at Golgotha with two thieves under the title King of the Jews, and passers-by taunt him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Jesus was mocked and crucified?
ev: Describe the mocking
List the details of the crucifixion

nodes.t: The death of Jesus
nodes.d: Darkness covers the land, Jesus cries “My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?” and yields up the ghost; the temple veil tears, the earth quakes, graves open, and the centurion says truly this was the Son of God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what happened when Jesus died?
ev: List the signs at his death
Say what the centurion said

nodes.t: The burial and the guard at the tomb
nodes.d: Joseph of Arimathaea buries Jesus in his new rock tomb; the next day the chief priests ask Pilate to make the tomb secure and set a sealed stone and a watch.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell where Jesus was buried and what the priests did about the tomb?
ev: Say who buried Jesus and where
Explain why the priests wanted a guard

nodes.t: The resurrection and the guards’ report
nodes.d: At dawn an angel rolls back the stone and tells the women Jesus is risen and will meet his disciples in Galilee; Jesus meets the women, and the guards are paid to say the disciples stole the body.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened at the tomb on the first day of the week?
ev: Retell what the angel said
Describe what the guards were told to say

nodes.t: The Great Commission
nodes.d: On a mountain in Galilee the eleven see the risen Jesus, some doubt, and he says all power is given to him and tells them to make disciples of all nations, baptizing in the name of the Father, Son and Holy Ghost, with his presence always.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus told his disciples to do and what he promised?
ev: Say what Jesus commanded in 28:19-20
Say what he promises

nodes.t: John prepares the way
nodes.d: Mark opens with the beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God; John baptizes in the wilderness for repentance and says one mightier will baptize with the Holy Ghost.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain who John was and what he said about the one coming after him?
ev: Say how Mark begins his book
Describe John’s message and appearance

nodes.t: The baptism and temptation of Jesus
nodes.d: Jesus is baptized by John, the Spirit descends like a dove and a voice calls him beloved Son; the Spirit then drives him into the wilderness, where he is tempted forty days by Satan.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened at Jesus’ baptism and in the wilderness?
ev: Describe what happened at the Jordan
Say where Jesus went next and for how long

nodes.t: Jesus preaches the kingdom and calls four fishermen
nodes.d: After John is imprisoned Jesus preaches in Galilee that the time is fulfilled and the kingdom of God is at hand, and calls Simon, Andrew, James and John from their nets.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Jesus called his first disciples?
ev: Say what Jesus preached
Name the four fishermen

nodes.t: The man with an unclean spirit in the synagogue
nodes.d: At Capernaum Jesus teaches with authority and commands an unclean spirit, which cries that he is the Holy One of God, to come out, and the people are amazed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Jesus did in the Capernaum synagogue?
ev: Retell what the unclean spirit said
Say how the people responded

nodes.t: Healing Peter’s mother-in-law and the crowds
nodes.d: Jesus heals Simon’s wife’s mother, then at evening heals many and casts out devils; before dawn he prays alone in a solitary place and says he must preach in other towns.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus did that evening and next morning?
ev: Retell the evening at the door
Say why Jesus left Capernaum

nodes.t: Jesus cleanses a leper
nodes.d: A leper kneels and asks to be made clean; Jesus, moved with compassion, touches him and heals him, telling him to show himself to the priest, but the man spreads the news.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the leper asked and what Jesus did?
ev: Retell the healing
Say what happened after the man disobeyed

nodes.t: The paralytic let down through the roof
nodes.d: Four men break through a roof to lower a paralysed man to Jesus, who forgives his sins; when scribes call it blasphemy he heals the man to show that the Son of man has power on earth to forgive sins.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Jesus did for the man lowered through the roof?
ev: Retell how the man reached Jesus
Say why the scribes objected

nodes.t: Levi called and the question about fasting
nodes.d: Jesus calls Levi the tax collector and eats with publicans and sinners, saying he came to call sinners; asked about fasting, he speaks of the bridegroom, new cloth and new wine.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Jesus ate with sinners and what he said about fasting?
ev: Say whom Jesus called and what Pharisees objected to
Explain the bridegroom saying

nodes.t: Lord of the sabbath: the grainfield
nodes.d: When disciples pluck grain on the sabbath, Jesus cites David eating the shewbread and says the sabbath was made for man and the Son of man is Lord of it.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus said about the sabbath?
ev: State the objection and Jesus’ example
Explain “the sabbath was made for man”

nodes.t: Healing the withered hand
nodes.d: In the synagogue Jesus asks whether it is lawful to do good or evil on the sabbath, heals a man’s withered hand, and the Pharisees and Herodians plot to destroy him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the Pharisees plotted against Jesus after this healing?
ev: Retell the healing and Jesus’ question
Say what the Pharisees did

nodes.t: The multitudes and the appointing of the twelve
nodes.d: Crowds from many regions come to Jesus; he goes up a mountain and appoints twelve to be with him, to preach and to have power to heal and cast out devils, and Mark names them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Jesus appointed the twelve for?
ev: Name several of the twelve
Say what the twelve were appointed to do

nodes.t: The Beelzebub charge and Jesus’ family
nodes.d: Scribes from Jerusalem say Jesus casts out devils by the prince of devils; he answers that a divided kingdom cannot stand, warns of blaspheming the Holy Ghost, and says whoever does God’s will is his brother, sister and mother.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the scribes said and how Jesus answered?
ev: Summarise Jesus’ reply about a divided house
Say who Jesus calls his family

nodes.t: The parable of the sower
nodes.d: Teaching from a boat, Jesus tells the parable of the sower and explains it privately to his disciples: the word sown on the path, stony ground, thorns and good ground.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the four soils stand for?
ev: Retell the four soils
Give Jesus’ explanation of each

nodes.t: The lamp, the growing seed and the mustard seed
nodes.d: Jesus says what is hidden will be made known, speaks of the measure you give, tells of seed growing by itself until harvest and of the mustard seed, and explains all things privately to his disciples.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Jesus says the kingdom of God is like in 4:26-32?
ev: Explain the lamp saying
Compare the growing seed and the mustard seed

nodes.t: Jesus stills the storm
nodes.d: Crossing the sea in the evening, the disciples are swamped by a storm while Jesus sleeps; he rebukes the wind and says to the sea “Peace, be still”, and they ask what manner of man this is.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Jesus did in the storm?
ev: Retell the storm
State the disciples’ question in 4:41

nodes.t: The man called Legion
nodes.d: Jesus meets a man living among tombs with an unclean spirit; the many spirits (Legion) are sent into two thousand swine, and the healed man is told to tell his friends what the Lord has done and proclaims it in Decapolis.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened to the man called Legion?
ev: Describe the man’s condition
Say what Jesus told him to do after healing

nodes.t: Jairus’ daughter and the woman who touched his garment
nodes.d: Jairus begs Jesus to heal his dying daughter; on the way a woman bleeding for twelve years touches his garment and is healed; Jesus then raises the girl, telling Jairus not to fear but to believe.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Jesus did for the woman and for Jairus’ daughter?
ev: Retell both healings
Say what Jesus said to Jairus when news came the girl was dead

nodes.t: Rejected at Nazareth
nodes.d: Jesus teaches in his home synagogue; people are offended that he is the carpenter, Mary’s son, and he can do few mighty works there, marvelling at their unbelief.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what happened when Jesus taught at Nazareth?
ev: Say why they took offence
Quote or paraphrase the saying about a prophet’s honour

nodes.t: The twelve sent out two by two
nodes.d: Jesus sends the twelve out in pairs with power over unclean spirits and instructions to take little; they preach repentance, cast out devils and anoint many sick with oil.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Jesus sent out the twelve?
ev: List the instructions about what to take
Say what the twelve did

nodes.t: Herod and the death of John the Baptist
nodes.d: Hearing of Jesus, Herod fears John has risen; Mark recounts John’s imprisonment for rebuking Herod over Herodias, and how Herod’s oath at his birthday supper led to John’s beheading.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how John the Baptist died?
ev: Retell why John was imprisoned
Describe the oath and its result

nodes.t: Feeding the five thousand
nodes.d: The apostles return and Jesus takes them apart, but crowds follow; Jesus teaches them, then feeds about five thousand with five loaves and two fishes, with twelve baskets of fragments.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the feeding of the five thousand?
ev: Say what Jesus did with the loaves and fishes
Give the numbers fed and left over

nodes.t: Jesus walks on the sea
nodes.d: Jesus sends the disciples by ship while he prays on the mountain; in the fourth watch he comes to them walking on the sea, tells them not to be afraid, and the wind ceases; Mark says their hearts were hardened about the loaves.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell the story of Jesus walking on the sea?
ev: Retell what Jesus did and said
Say what Mark says the disciples had not understood

nodes.t: Tradition of the elders and what defiles
nodes.d: Pharisees fault the disciples for eating with unwashed hands; Jesus quotes Isaiah on lip service, charges them with setting aside God’s commandment through Corban, and says what comes out of the heart defiles.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus says defiles a person?
ev: Explain Jesus’ Corban example
List what proceeds from the heart (7:21-22)

nodes.t: The Syrophenician woman
nodes.d: In the region of Tyre a Greek woman begs Jesus to cast a spirit out of her daughter; after his word about the children’s bread she replies about crumbs, and he tells her the devil has gone out.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the woman said and what Jesus did?
ev: Retell the conversation
Say how the daughter was healed

nodes.t: Healing the deaf man
nodes.d: In Decapolis people bring a deaf man with a speech impediment; Jesus takes him aside, touches his ears and tongue, says “Ephphatha”, and he hears and speaks.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the healing of the deaf man?
ev: Describe what Jesus did and said
Say what the crowd said (7:37)

nodes.t: Feeding the four thousand
nodes.d: Jesus has compassion on a crowd three days without food and feeds about four thousand with seven loaves and a few fishes, leaving seven baskets.
