nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the feeding of the four thousand?
ev: Give the numbers of loaves and baskets
Compare with the five thousand

nodes.t: Seeking a sign and the leaven of the Pharisees and Herod
nodes.d: Pharisees seek a sign from heaven and Jesus refuses; in the boat he warns against the leaven of the Pharisees and Herod and reminds the disciples of the loaves and baskets in the two feedings.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Jesus asked the disciples to remember the baskets?
ev: Say what Jesus refused to give
Recall the numbers Jesus asked the disciples about

nodes.t: The blind man of Bethsaida
nodes.d: At Bethsaida Jesus leads a blind man outside the town, lays hands on him twice, and he sees clearly.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Jesus healed the blind man at Bethsaida?
ev: Describe the two stages of the healing
Say what Jesus told the man afterwards

nodes.t: Peter’s confession and the first prediction of the cross
nodes.d: At Caesarea Philippi Peter says Jesus is the Christ; Jesus begins to teach that the Son of man must suffer, be killed and rise after three days, rebukes Peter, and calls followers to deny themselves and take up the cross.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain who Peter said Jesus is and what Jesus said must happen?
ev: State what the people and Peter said of Jesus
Explain the call to take up the cross

nodes.t: The transfiguration
nodes.d: Jesus is transfigured before Peter, James and John on a high mountain with Elias and Moses; a voice from the cloud calls him beloved Son and says hear him; he tells them not to speak of it until he rises.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the transfiguration?
ev: Describe what the disciples saw and heard
Say what Jesus said about Elias

nodes.t: The boy with a dumb spirit
nodes.d: A father brings his son tormented by a spirit; Jesus says all things are possible to him that believes, the father cries “Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief”, and Jesus casts the spirit out, saying this kind comes out by prayer.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the father said and how Jesus helped the boy?
ev: Retell the father’s plea and Jesus’ answer
Say what Jesus told the disciples about prayer

nodes.t: Second prediction, who is greatest and stumbling blocks
nodes.d: Jesus again foretells his death and rising; the disciples argue who is greatest, and he sets a child among them, says whoever is not against them is for them, warns against offending little ones and speaks of the fire that is not quenched and having salt.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus said about greatness and little ones?
ev: Say what Jesus taught about being first
Explain the warning about offences

nodes.t: Marriage and divorce, and blessing the children
nodes.d: Tested about divorce, Jesus points to creation: male and female, leaving father and mother and becoming one flesh; later he welcomes children, saying the kingdom of God belongs to such and must be received as a child.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus taught about marriage and about children?
ev: Say what Jesus cites from creation about marriage
Explain what he says about the children

nodes.t: The rich man who went away sorrowful
nodes.d: A man runs to ask what he must do to inherit eternal life; Jesus loves him and tells him to sell all and follow, and he leaves sad; Jesus teaches about the difficulty of riches and what God can do and promises to those who leave all.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Jesus asked of the rich man and why he left sad?
ev: Say what Jesus lists and then asks of the man
Explain “with God all things are possible”

nodes.t: Third prediction, James and John, and the ransom
nodes.d: On the way to Jerusalem Jesus foretells his betrayal, mocking and rising; James and John ask for seats at his right and left, and Jesus says whoever would be great must serve, for the Son of man came to give his life a ransom for many.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus said about serving and about his life as a ransom?
ev: Describe what Jesus foretold
Explain 10:45

nodes.t: Blind Bartimaeus
nodes.d: Leaving Jericho, blind Bartimaeus cries out to Jesus as son of David; told to be silent he cries more, Jesus calls him, asks what he wants, and he receives his sight and follows Jesus.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Bartimaeus was healed?
ev: Retell what Bartimaeus said and did
Say what Jesus told him

nodes.t: The entry into Jerusalem
nodes.d: Jesus sends two disciples for a colt that no one has ridden; he rides it as people spread garments and branches and shout Hosanna, blessing him that comes in the name of the Lord and the kingdom of David.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Jesus entered Jerusalem?
ev: Retell how the colt was found
Say what the people shouted

nodes.t: The fig tree and the cleansing of the temple
nodes.d: Jesus curses a leafy fig tree without fruit, drives out sellers and moneychangers saying the house is for prayer for all nations, and next day the disciples see the fig tree withered; he teaches faith and forgiving when praying.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus did in the temple and what he taught about prayer?
ev: Retell the order of events
Say what Jesus taught about prayer

nodes.t: The question about Jesus’ authority
nodes.d: Chief priests, scribes and elders ask by what authority Jesus acts; he asks them whether John’s baptism was from heaven or of men, and when they will not answer he declines to answer them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Jesus answered the authority question?
ev: State the question and counter-question
Explain why they would not answer

nodes.t: The parable of the vineyard tenants
nodes.d: A man plants a vineyard and lets it to husbandmen who beat and kill his servants and then his beloved son; Jesus cites the rejected stone that became head of the corner, and the rulers know the parable is against them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain who the servants, son and husbandmen stand for?
ev: Retell the parable
Say what the rulers understood

nodes.t: Render to Caesar
nodes.d: Pharisees and Herodians ask if tribute to Caesar is lawful; Jesus asks for a penny, asks whose image it bears, and says to render to Caesar what is Caesar’s and to God what is God’s.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus said about the coin?
ev: Say why they asked
Explain Jesus’ answer

nodes.t: The Sadducees and the resurrection
nodes.d: Sadducees who deny the resurrection ask about a woman married to seven brothers; Jesus says they err not knowing the scriptures or God’s power, that the risen are as angels, and that God is God of the living, citing the bush.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Jesus’ answer about the resurrection?
ev: Say what the Sadducees asked
Explain Jesus’ use of the words from the bush

nodes.t: The first commandment
nodes.d: A scribe asks which commandment is first; Jesus answers the Lord is one and to love him with all heart, soul, mind and strength, and second to love your neighbour as yourself; the scribe agrees and Jesus says he is not far from the kingdom.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say the two great commandments?
ev: State the two commandments
Say what the scribe added and what Jesus replied

nodes.t: David’s Lord and warning against the scribes
nodes.d: Teaching in the temple, Jesus asks how the Christ can be David’s son when David calls him Lord, and warns the people against scribes who love honour and devour widows’ houses.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus asked about David and the Christ?
ev: State the puzzle Jesus raised about David
List what he warns about the scribes

nodes.t: The widow’s two mites
nodes.d: Sitting by the treasury, Jesus sees rich people give much and a poor widow give two mites, and says she has given more than all because she gave all her living.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Jesus praised the widow?
ev: Describe what the widow gave
Explain why Jesus said she gave more

nodes.t: The Olivet discourse: signs and the abomination
nodes.d: Leaving the temple, Jesus foretells the buildings’ destruction and on the Mount of Olives warns of deceivers, wars, persecution and the gospel preached to all nations; he warns of the abomination of desolation, great affliction and false Christs.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list what Jesus said to watch for?
ev: State the disciples’ question (13:4)
List the warnings Jesus gave

nodes.t: The coming of the Son of man and the call to watch
nodes.d: After the tribulation the Son of man will be seen coming in clouds and gather the elect; Jesus gives the fig tree parable, says no one but the Father knows the day, and tells everyone to watch.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Jesus told his disciples to watch?
ev: Describe the coming of the Son of man
Say what Jesus commands in 13:37

nodes.t: The plot, the anointing at Bethany and Judas’ offer
nodes.d: Two days before Passover the priests seek to take Jesus; a woman pours spikenard on his head at Simon the leper’s house and Jesus says she anointed his body for burial; Judas goes to the chief priests.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the woman did and what Jesus said about it?
ev: Retell the anointing and the objection
Say what Judas offered

nodes.t: The Passover meal and the Lord’s Supper
nodes.d: Disciples prepare the Passover in an upper room; Jesus says one of the twelve will betray him, gives them bread as his body and the cup as his blood of the new testament shed for many, and says he will drink new in the kingdom of God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus did with the bread and cup at the Passover?
ev: Describe what Jesus said over the bread and cup
Say what he said about the new testament

nodes.t: Peter’s boast and Gethsemane
nodes.d: Jesus foretells that the sheep will be scattered and Peter will deny him; in Gethsemane he prays “Abba, Father” that the cup might pass yet not his will, and finds the disciples asleep.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Jesus prayed in Gethsemane?
ev: Retell Jesus’ prayer
Say what Peter said and what Jesus answered

nodes.t: Jesus is betrayed and arrested
nodes.d: Judas comes with a crowd and betrays Jesus with a kiss; one drawn sword cuts off a servant’s ear; Jesus says the scriptures must be fulfilled, all the disciples flee, and a young man runs away leaving a linen cloth.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Jesus was arrested?
ev: Describe the betrayal
Say what the disciples did

nodes.t: Jesus before the council
nodes.d: False witnesses disagree; asked if he is the Christ the Son of the Blessed, Jesus says “I am” and speaks of the Son of man at the right hand of power; the high priest charges blasphemy and they condemn him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the high priest asked and the council decided?
ev: Say what Jesus answered the high priest
Describe how the council treated him

nodes.t: Peter’s denial
nodes.d: In the high priest’s courtyard Peter denies Jesus three times; the cock crows twice, he remembers Jesus’ word and weeps.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Peter denied Jesus?
ev: Retell the three denials
Say what Peter did when he remembered

nodes.t: Jesus before Pilate and Barabbas
nodes.d: The council delivers Jesus to Pilate, who asks if he is King of the Jews; the crowd, moved by the priests, asks for Barabbas and cries for Jesus to be crucified; Pilate scourges Jesus and delivers him to be crucified.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the trial before Pilate?
ev: Say who was released
Say why Pilate gave in

nodes.t: The mocking and crucifixion
nodes.d: Soldiers dress Jesus in purple and a crown of thorns and mock him; Simon of Cyrene carries his cross; he is crucified at Golgotha between two thieves under the title King of the Jews while others mock.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Jesus was crucified?
ev: Describe the mockery
List what is said of the crucifixion

nodes.t: The death of Jesus
nodes.d: Darkness covers the land; Jesus cries “My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?” and dies; the temple veil tears, and the centurion says truly this man was the Son of God; women watch from afar.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what happened when Jesus died?
ev: List the signs and the centurion’s words
Name the women who watched

nodes.t: The burial of Jesus
nodes.d: Joseph of Arimathaea asks Pilate for the body, wraps it in fine linen, lays it in a rock tomb and rolls a stone to the door; Mary Magdalene and Mary see where he is laid.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Jesus was buried?
ev: Say who buried Jesus and where
Say who saw where he was laid

nodes.t: The empty tomb
nodes.d: Early on the first day the women find the stone rolled away and a young man in white tells them Jesus is risen, and that he goes before them into Galilee; they flee in fear and say nothing to anyone.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the women found at the tomb?
ev: Retell what the women found and were told
Say how they responded

nodes.t: The appearances and commission (longer ending)
nodes.d: The longer ending tells that Jesus appeared first to Mary Magdalene, then to two and then to the eleven, rebuking their unbelief; he sends them to preach the gospel to every creature and is received up to the right hand of God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus told the eleven to do and what happened to him afterwards?
ev: List those to whom Jesus appeared
State the commission in 16:15-16

nodes.t: Isaiah: overview
nodes.d: Isaiah son of Amoz sees visions concerning Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah; the book moves from indictment and judgment to comfort, a servant, and new heavens and a new earth.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say who Isaiah was and describe, using Isaiah 1:1 and 40:1-2, how the book moves from rebuke to comfort?
ev: Name the four kings of Judah named in Isaiah 1:1
Describe the shift in tone between chapters 1-39 and chapter 40 using the texts

nodes.t: The Lord charges his rebellious children
nodes.d: The LORD calls heaven and earth to witness that the children he raised have rebelled, rejects their empty sacrifices, and offers cleansing if they are willing and obedient.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD says he is weary of sacrifices in Isaiah 1 and what he commands instead?
ev: Retell the charge of Isaiah 1:2-4
Explain why God rejects the sacrifices in 1:11-15 and what he asks instead in 1:16-17
Quote the offer in 1:18-20

nodes.t: The mountain of the Lord in the last days
nodes.d: Isaiah sees the mountain of the LORD's house raised up, nations streaming to learn his ways, and weapons turned into farming tools; the house of Jacob is called to walk in his light.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Isaiah 2:2-4 says will happen to the nations and to weapons in the last days?
ev: Describe what the nations say and do in Isaiah 2:2-4
Explain the image of swords into plowshares from the text

nodes.t: The day of the Lord humbles the proud
nodes.d: Judah is full of silver, horses and idols, and a day of the LORD is coming on everything lofty so that he alone is exalted and men are told to cease trusting in man.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the day of the LORD brings against the proud in Isaiah 2:12-17?
ev: List what Judah is full of in Isaiah 2:7-8
Say what the day of the LORD comes against (2:12-17)
Explain the command in 2:22

nodes.t: Jerusalem stripped of support
nodes.d: The Lord takes away Jerusalem's leaders and supplies, the people oppress one another, the elders and the proud daughters of Zion are charged, and the city is left desolate.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the LORD takes from Jerusalem in Isaiah 3 and why?
ev: Name the supports taken away in Isaiah 3:1-3
Describe the LORD's charge against the elders in 3:14-15
Describe the fate of the haughty daughters of Zion (3:16-26)

nodes.t: The Branch of the Lord and the cleansed remnant
nodes.d: After judgment, the Branch of the LORD is beautiful and glorious, those left in Zion are called holy, and the LORD covers Zion with cloud by day and fire by night as a shelter.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what the LORD does for Zion in Isaiah 4:2-6 after washing away her filth?
ev: Say who is called holy in Isaiah 4:3
Describe the cloud, fire and shelter over Zion in 4:5-6

nodes.t: The song of the vineyard
nodes.d: Isaiah sings of a beloved's well-tended vineyard that yields wild grapes, and the LORD explains that the vineyard is the house of Israel, for which he looked for justice and righteousness.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the song of the vineyard and say what Isaiah 5:7 says it means?
ev: Retell what the owner did for the vineyard (5:1-2)
Say what he will do to it (5:5-6)
Explain who the vineyard is according to 5:7

nodes.t: Six woes and the distant nation
nodes.d: Isaiah pronounces woes on land-grabbers, drunkards, those who call evil good and those who pervert justice, and says the LORD will summon a swift nation from afar against his people.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name at least three of the woes in Isaiah 5 and the reason given for judgment in 5:24?
ev: List the woes of Isaiah 5:8, 11, 18, 20, 21 and 22
Explain why the LORD's anger is not turned away (5:24-25)

nodes.t: Isaiah sees the Lord and is sent
nodes.d: In the year King Uzziah died Isaiah sees the LORD enthroned with seraphim crying holy, is cleansed by a coal from the altar, volunteers, and is told to preach to a people who will not understand until a stump remains.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell Isaiah's vision in chapter 6, including what the seraphim cry and how Isaiah is cleansed?
ev: Retell what the seraphim say and do (6:2-7)
Explain Isaiah's response in 6:5 and 6:8
Describe the message he is given and the "holy seed" in 6:9-13

nodes.t: The sign of Immanuel to Ahaz
nodes.d: When Syria and Ephraim threaten Judah, Isaiah tells Ahaz to trust the LORD, Ahaz refuses to ask a sign, and the Lord gives a sign of a son called Immanuel, with Assyria coming on the land.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the setting of Isaiah 7:14 and what Ahaz was told to do in 7:4-9?
ev: Explain what Rezin and Pekah plan against Judah (7:1-6)
Quote the sign in 7:14 and say to whom the word is addressed (7:13)
Describe the coming of the king of Assyria (7:17-20)

nodes.t: Maher-shalal-hash-baz and the Assyrian flood
nodes.d: Isaiah writes a name-sign for a son, the LORD warns that the king of Assyria will flood Judah, tells Isaiah not to fear what the people fear, and calls him to the law and testimony instead of mediums.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD says to sanctify him rather than fear what the people fear in Isaiah 8:11-13?
ev: Explain the meaning of the child's name sign in 8:1-4
Say whom Isaiah is told to fear and sanctify (8:12-13)
Explain the contrast between the law and testimony and consulting the dead (8:19-20)

nodes.t: Light for the people in darkness and the child born
nodes.d: Light shines on the people in darkness in Zebulun and Naphtali, the yoke is broken, and a child is born whose government, names and everlasting reign are on the throne of David.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Isaiah 9:6-7 says about the child and the throne of David?
ev: Name the regions mentioned in Isaiah 9:1
List the names given to the child in 9:6
Explain what 9:7 says about his throne and kingdom

nodes.t: His hand is stretched out still
nodes.d: A refrain runs through four stanzas: Ephraim's pride, unrepentant people, false leaders and civil strife bring judgment, and the LORD's anger is not turned away; woe is also pronounced on unjust decrees.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} find the refrain repeated in Isaiah 9:8-10:4 and explain why the people are judged?
ev: Find the repeated refrain in Isaiah 9:12, 17, 21 and 10:4
Say what Ephraim's boast in 9:10 shows about the people's attitude

nodes.t: Assyria the rod, then judged
nodes.d: The LORD sends Assyria as the rod of his anger against a hypocritical nation, but punishes the king of Assyria for his boasting; a remnant will return and Zion is told not to fear.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the picture of the axe boasting against the one who swings it in Isaiah 10:15?
ev: Explain how Assyria is both used and judged (10:5-7, 12-15)
Say what is promised to the remnant (10:20-23)
Describe the comfort given to Zion in 10:24-27

nodes.t: The shoot from the stem of Jesse
nodes.d: A shoot from Jesse's stem, endowed with the Spirit of the LORD, judges the poor with righteousness; peace reaches even the animals, the earth is full of the knowledge of the LORD, and the remnant is gathered.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the one who comes from the stem of Jesse and the peace of his kingdom in Isaiah 11?
ev: List the gifts of the Spirit resting on him in Isaiah 11:2
Describe how he judges (11:3-5)
Describe the peaceful creation in 11:6-9 and the gathering in 11:10-12

nodes.t: A song of salvation
nodes.d: In that day the redeemed will praise the LORD, saying God is their salvation and strength, draw water from the wells of salvation, and call all the earth to sing.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the people sing in Isaiah 12 and why they can praise the LORD?
ev: Quote the declaration of trust in Isaiah 12:2
Say what the people are told to do in 12:4-6

nodes.t: The burden of Babylon and the fallen king
nodes.d: The LORD musters an army against Babylon, a day of the LORD brings desolation by the Medes, and a taunt song mocks the king of Babylon who said he would ascend and be like the Most High.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the proverb against the king of Babylon in Isaiah 14:4-20?
ev: Name the people the LORD stirs up against Babylon (13:17)
Describe the king's boast and his fall in 14:12-15
Say what mercy the LORD shows Jacob in 14:1-3

nodes.t: The LORD's purpose against Assyria and Philistia
nodes.d: The LORD swears to break Assyria on his mountains, declares his purpose stretched over all nations, and tells Philistia not to rejoice, since Zion is founded by the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the LORD says in Isaiah 14:24-27 about his purpose?
ev: Say what the LORD has sworn about Assyria (14:24-25)
Quote the answer to the messengers in 14:32

nodes.t: The burden of Moab
nodes.d: Moab is laid waste in a night and mourns, a request is made for Moab's outcasts to find shelter in Judah where a throne is established in mercy, and Moab's pride is judged with a time limit.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Isaiah 15-16 portrays Moab's fall and the grief it causes?
ev: Describe the mourning of Moab (15:2-5)
Say what is said of the throne in 16:5
Identify the time limit given in 16:14

nodes.t: Damascus, Israel and the land beyond Ethiopia
nodes.d: Damascus becomes a ruin and Ephraim's fortress ceases, a remnant turns to its Maker, and the roaring nations are rebuked; Ethiopia is addressed and a gift is brought to the LORD at Zion.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the burden of Damascus and the reason given in Isaiah 17:10?
ev: Say why Ephraim is judged according to Isaiah 17:10
Describe the fate of the roaring nations (17:12-14)
Say what happens to Ethiopia's people in 18:7

nodes.t: The burden of Egypt and Isaiah's sign
nodes.d: The LORD comes against Egypt, whose counsel fails; yet he promises that Egypt will know and serve him, and that Egypt, Assyria and Israel will be a blessing; Isaiah walks barefoot as a sign against trusting Egypt and Ethiopia.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Isaiah 19:19-25 says will happen to Egypt and what Isaiah's sign in chapter 20 means?
ev: Describe the judgment on Egypt (19:1-15)
Describe the blessing on Egypt, Assyria and Israel (19:23-25)
Explain what Isaiah's walking naked and barefoot signifies (20:2-6)

nodes.t: Babylon's fall, Dumah and Arabia
nodes.d: Isaiah watches in fear at a grievous vision, the watchman announces that Babylon is fallen, Seir asks the watchman what remains of the night, and Arabia's glory is to fail within a year.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the watchman's report in Isaiah 21:6-9?
ev: Describe what the watchman reports in Isaiah 21:6-9
Say what the watchman answers in 21:11-12

nodes.t: The valley of vision and Shebna
nodes.d: Jerusalem is distressed by a day of trouble; the people prepare defenses but do not look to the LORD and say let us eat and drink; Shebna is removed and Eliakim receives the key of the house of David.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jerusalem does in Isaiah 22:8-13 and what the LORD says about it?
ev: Say what the people do and fail to do in Isaiah 22:8-13
Explain what happens to Shebna and Eliakim (22:15-25)

nodes.t: The burden of Tyre
nodes.d: Tyre, the merchant city, is laid waste by the LORD's purpose, forgotten seventy years, and afterward returns to her trade, which will be holy to the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Isaiah 23 says about Tyre's fall and her trade after seventy years?
ev: Say who purposed Tyre's fall and why (23:9)
Describe what happens after seventy years (23:15-18)

nodes.t: The LORD lays waste the earth
nodes.d: The LORD empties the earth because its people broke the laws and the everlasting covenant; joy ceases, the earth reels, the host on high and kings below are punished, and the LORD reigns in Zion.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the earth is emptied in Isaiah 24 and who reigns at the end?
ev: Say why the earth is defiled (24:5)
Describe the punishment of the host on high and the kings of the earth (24:21-22)
Say where the LORD reigns (24:23)

nodes.t: A feast on the mountain and death swallowed up
nodes.d: The LORD makes a feast for all peoples on his mountain, removes the veil over all nations, swallows up death, wipes away tears, and the redeemed say they waited for him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the LORD does for all peoples on his mountain in Isaiah 25:6-9?
ev: Describe the feast and the veil (25:6-7)
Quote what the LORD does to death and tears (25:8)
Say what the people say in 25:9

nodes.t: A song in Judah: perfect peace and the dead who live
nodes.d: Judah sings of a strong city and perfect peace for those who trust the LORD, laments that they have brought no deliverance, and hears that the LORD's dead shall live and the earth will disclose her slain.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Isaiah 26:3 and 26:19 promise?
ev: Quote the promise of peace in Isaiah 26:3
Say what is promised about the dead in 26:19
Describe the call to hide until the indignation is past (26:20-21)

nodes.t: Leviathan punished and the vineyard of red wine
nodes.d: The LORD punishes leviathan, the vineyard he guards will fill the world with fruit, Jacob's iniquity is purged, and the scattered are gathered with a great trumpet to worship at Jerusalem.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the vineyard of Isaiah 27 and compare it with the vineyard in Isaiah 5?
ev: Say what the LORD does to leviathan (27:1)
Describe the vineyard and its keeper (27:2-6)
Describe the gathering in 27:12-13

nodes.t: Woe to Ephraim's drunkards and the scoffers in Jerusalem
nodes.d: Isaiah rebukes the drunken leaders, who mock his teaching, boast of a covenant with death, and are promised a tested cornerstone laid in Zion; the farmer's patient work illustrates God's wise ways.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the scoffers in Isaiah 28:15 relied on and what the LORD lays in Zion in 28:16?
ev: Describe the scoffers' covenant with death (28:15)
Quote what the LORD lays in Zion (28:16)
Explain the farmer illustration in 28:23-29

nodes.t: Woe to Ariel: a sealed vision and a marvellous work
nodes.d: The LORD besieges Ariel, the city where David dwelt, then saves it from the nations; the people honour him with lips but not hearts, the vision is like a sealed book, and the deaf will hear and the blind see.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what 29:13 says about the people's worship?
ev: Describe the siege and sudden deliverance of Ariel (29:1-8)
Explain the charge in 29:13
Describe the change promised in 29:17-24

nodes.t: Rebellious children and trust in Egypt
nodes.d: Judah sends to Egypt for help instead of asking the LORD, refuses to hear true prophecy, and is told that in returning and rest is salvation; the LORD will wait to be gracious and will beat down Assyria.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the people were told in Isaiah 30:15 and how they answered?
ev: Say why the LORD calls the people rebellious (30:1-2, 9-11)
Quote 30:15 and the people's answer in 30:16
Describe the grace promised in 30:18-26

nodes.t: Woe to those who trust in horses
nodes.d: Those who go to Egypt for help trust in chariots rather than the LORD, who is wise and will protect Jerusalem like birds flying; Assyria will fall by a sword not of man.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} contrast Egypt's horses with the LORD's help in Isaiah 31:1-3?
ev: Say what the people trust instead of the LORD (31:1)
Quote the contrast in 31:3
Describe how the LORD defends Jerusalem (31:4-5)

nodes.t: A king reigns in righteousness; the Spirit is poured out
nodes.d: A king and princes will reign in righteousness, careless women are warned of coming desolation, until the Spirit is poured from on high and righteousness and peace dwell in the land.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what 32:15-17 says happens when the Spirit is poured out?
ev: Describe the king and the changes in 32:1-8
Say what ends the desolation (32:15)
Say what the work of righteousness is (32:17)

nodes.t: The destroyer destroyed and the LORD our king
nodes.d: The spoiler is warned, the people pray for grace, the LORD rises to be exalted, sinners in Zion fear the devouring fire, and the righteous see the king; the LORD is judge, lawgiver and king.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say the three roles given to the LORD in Isaiah 33:22?
ev: Say who asks, "Who among us shall dwell with the devouring fire?" and the answer (33:14-16)
Quote 33:22
Describe Jerusalem as a quiet habitation (33:20)

nodes.t: The day of vengeance on the nations and Edom
nodes.d: The LORD's indignation is on all nations; his sword comes down on Edom for the controversy of Zion, and the land becomes a lasting wasteland inhabited by wild creatures.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Edom is singled out in Isaiah 34:5-8?
ev: Say what the LORD does to the host of heaven and the nations (34:2-4)
Say which land receives the sword (34:5-6)
Describe Edom after judgment (34:9-15)

nodes.t: The desert blooms and the way of holiness
nodes.d: The wilderness blossoms, the weak are strengthened, the blind see and the lame leap, and a highway of holiness leads the ransomed to Zion with everlasting joy.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the way of holiness and the people who walk it in Isaiah 35?
ev: Describe the healings in Isaiah 35:5-6
Say who walks the way of holiness (35:8-10)

nodes.t: Sennacherib's envoy mocks Jerusalem
nodes.d: In Hezekiah's fourteenth year Sennacherib's envoy Rabshakeh stands by Jerusalem's conduit and tries to turn the people from trusting Hezekiah and the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell what Rabshakeh says to Jerusalem's people in Isaiah 36 and how they answer?
ev: Retell the arguments Rabshakeh uses (36:4-10, 14-20)
Say how Hezekiah's officers respond (36:21-22)

nodes.t: Hezekiah prays and the angel strikes the Assyrian camp
nodes.d: Hezekiah takes the letter to the LORD's house and prays; Isaiah answers that the LORD will defend Jerusalem, and the angel of the LORD strikes the Assyrian camp so that Sennacherib returns to Nineveh.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how the LORD answered Hezekiah's prayer in Isaiah 37?
ev: Retell Hezekiah's prayer (37:14-20)
Say what Isaiah's answer promises (37:21-35)
Retell what happens to Sennacherib (37:36-38)

nodes.t: Hezekiah's sickness and recovery
nodes.d: Hezekiah, told he will die, prays and weeps; the LORD adds fifteen years, promises to deliver the city from Assyria, and gives a sign with the shadow on the sundial; Hezekiah writes a thanksgiving.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how the LORD answered Hezekiah when he was sick in Isaiah 38?
ev: Retell what Isaiah first says to Hezekiah and how Hezekiah responds (38:1-3)
Say what the LORD adds and the sign given (38:5-8)
Describe the lesson of the writing in 38:17-20

nodes.t: Envoys from Babylon
nodes.d: Merodach-baladan sends letters to Hezekiah, who shows them all his treasures; Isaiah tells him everything will be carried to Babylon, and Hezekiah calls the word good because there will be peace in his days.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Isaiah told Hezekiah about Babylon and how Hezekiah answered?
ev: Say what Hezekiah shows the envoys (39:2)
Say what Isaiah foretells (39:5-7)
Describe Hezekiah's response (39:8)

nodes.t: Comfort my people: the incomparable God
nodes.d: God tells his prophets to comfort Jerusalem because her iniquity is pardoned, a voice prepares the way of the LORD, the LORD comes as shepherd, and no one compares to him who gives strength to the weary.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD comforts Jerusalem in Isaiah 40:1-2 and who the LORD is compared to in 40:12-26?
ev: Quote the command and reason in Isaiah 40:1-2
Describe the voice crying in the wilderness (40:3-5)
Explain what 40:28-31 says about those who wait on the LORD

nodes.t: The LORD chose Israel; idols have no answer
nodes.d: The LORD calls Israel his servant, the seed of Abraham his friend, and tells them not to fear; he challenges the idols to declare the future and raises up one from the north and east.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD tells Israel in Isaiah 41:8-10 and how he challenges the idols?
ev: Quote the promise in Isaiah 41:10
Say how Israel is addressed in 41:8-14
Describe the challenge to the idols (41:21-29)

nodes.t: Behold my servant
nodes.d: The LORD presents his chosen servant, on whom he puts his Spirit, who brings justice to the nations gently and is given as a covenant and a light to the Gentiles to open blind eyes.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the servant and his work in Isaiah 42:1-7?
ev: List what the LORD says of the servant (42:1-4)
Say what the servant is given for (42:6-7)
Explain 42:8 about the LORD's glory

nodes.t: A new song and the blind servant
nodes.d: The LORD is called to be praised to the ends of the earth and goes forth as a warrior, but his servant is blind and deaf; Jacob was given to plunder because they would not walk in his ways.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD calls his servant blind and deaf in Isaiah 42:18-25?
ev: Describe the new song and the LORD as a warrior (42:10-13)
Explain what is said of the blind and deaf servant (42:18-20)
Say why Jacob was given to spoil (42:24-25)

nodes.t: I have redeemed you; I am the LORD, your Saviour
nodes.d: The LORD redeems and calls Jacob by name, will be with them through waters and fire, gathers sons from the ends of the earth, calls Israel his witnesses, does a new thing, and blots out their transgressions for his own sake.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the LORD promises in Isaiah 43:1-2 and 43:25?
ev: Quote the promise in Isaiah 43:1-2
Say what Israel is called in 43:10-12
Explain the "new thing" (43:18-19) and the forgiveness in 43:25

nodes.t: The folly of idols and the Spirit poured out
nodes.d: The LORD pours his Spirit on Jacob's seed and declares he is first and last with no God beside him, while the idol-maker's craft is shown to be foolish; the LORD blots out transgressions.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Isaiah 44:9-20 calls idol-making foolish?
ev: Quote 44:6
Describe how the idol is made and used (44:12-17)
Say what the LORD says to Israel in 44:21-22

nodes.t: Cyrus, the LORD's shepherd and anointed
nodes.d: The LORD names Cyrus, by name before his time, as his shepherd and anointed who will let Jerusalem and the temple be rebuilt, so that all will know there is none else.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the LORD says Cyrus will do and why in Isaiah 44:28-45:6?
ev: Say what the LORD says of Cyrus (44:28, 45:1)
Explain why the LORD calls Cyrus by name (45:4-6)
Quote the invitation in 45:22-23

nodes.t: Babylon's gods carried, Israel carried by God
nodes.d: Bel and Nebo are carried off as burdens while the LORD has carried Israel from birth and to old age; he declares the end from the beginning.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} contrast the gods of Babylon with the LORD in Isaiah 46:1-4?
ev: Contrast who carries whom in Isaiah 46:1-4
Say what the LORD declares in 46:9-10

nodes.t: The fall of Babylon the lady of kingdoms
nodes.d: The virgin daughter of Babylon is brought down from her throne, for she showed the LORD's people no mercy and trusted in sorceries and in saying "I am, and none else"; her counsellors cannot save her.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Babylon is brought low in Isaiah 47?
ev: Say why Babylon is judged (47:6-8)
Describe what her sorceries and astrologers cannot do (47:12-15)

nodes.t: The obstinate house of Jacob and the furnace of affliction
nodes.d: The LORD tells Jacob he foretold things because they were obstinate, delays his anger for his name's sake, calls them out of Babylon, and says had they heeded his commandments their peace would be like a river.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD says he tested Israel in the furnace of affliction in Isaiah 48:10-11?
ev: Say why the LORD declared things beforehand (48:3-7)
Describe the call to leave Babylon (48:20-21)
Quote 48:22

nodes.t: The servant, a light to the nations
nodes.d: The servant called from the womb, whose mouth is like a sharp sword, says he has laboured in vain; the LORD says it is too light a thing to restore Israel and gives him as a light to the Gentiles, and promises Zion she is not forgotten.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the LORD says is "too light a thing" for his servant in Isaiah 49:6?
ev: Describe how the servant is called (49:1-3)
Quote the LORD's answer in 49:6
Say what the LORD says to Zion in 49:14-16

nodes.t: The servant who gives his back to the smiters
nodes.d: The servant says the Lord GOD opened his ear and he was not rebellious, gave his back to those who struck him, and sets his face like flint trusting the Lord's help; those who walk in darkness are urged to trust the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what the servant says he will endure and why he is not put to shame in Isaiah 50:4-9?
ev: Describe what the servant endures (50:5-6)
Say why he is not ashamed (50:7-9)

nodes.t: Awake, arm of the LORD
nodes.d: Those who pursue righteousness are told to look to Abraham and Sarah, the LORD promises comfort and a law going forth, the arm of the LORD is called to awake as in ancient days, and Jerusalem is told the cup of fury is taken from her.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say who the people are told to look to in Isaiah 51:1-2 and why?
ev: Say whom they are told to look to (51:1-2)
Describe the cry to the arm of the LORD (51:9-11)
Say what happens to the cup of trembling (51:22-23)

nodes.t: Awake, Zion: good tidings of peace
nodes.d: Jerusalem is told to put on strength, she is redeemed without money, the feet of the one who brings good tidings are beautiful, and the LORD has bared his arm before the nations.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what 52:7 describes about the one who brings good tidings?
ev: Quote 52:7
Say what the watchmen see (52:8)
Describe the command to depart in 52:11-12

nodes.t: The servant exalted, despised and bearing iniquity
nodes.d: The servant is high, yet marred; despised and rejected, he bears griefs and iniquities of others, is wounded for transgressions and led like a lamb, is cut off and buried with the rich, and after his soul's travail justifies many.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what the servant suffers and for whose sake according to Isaiah 53:4-6?
ev: Describe what Isaiah 53:4-6 says he bears and for whom
Describe how he is treated (53:3, 7-9)
Say what the LORD says follows in 53:10-12

nodes.t: Sing, barren one: the covenant of peace
nodes.d: The barren woman is told to sing and enlarge her tent, the LORD her husband has called her back with mercy, swears as with the waters of Noah, and promises a covenant of peace that will not be removed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how the LORD compares his promise in Isaiah 54:9-10 to the waters of Noah?
ev: Describe the call to the barren woman (54:1-3)
Say what the LORD compares his oath to (54:9)
Quote the promise in 54:10

nodes.t: Come, buy without money: the sure mercies of David
nodes.d: The LORD invites the thirsty to come without money, promises an everlasting covenant, the sure mercies of David, calls the wicked to return, and says his word will accomplish what he pleases.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say who is invited and what is promised in Isaiah 55:1-7?
ev: Quote the invitation in Isaiah 55:1-3
Say what is promised to those who return (55:7)
Explain 55:10-11

nodes.t: Foreigners and eunuchs welcomed; blind watchmen
nodes.d: The LORD says foreigners and eunuchs who hold to his covenant and keep sabbaths will be joyful in his house of prayer for all peoples, while blind watchmen and greedy shepherds are condemned.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say who the LORD welcomes in Isaiah 56:3-8 and what his house is called?
ev: Say who is welcomed in Isaiah 56:3-7
Quote what the house is called (56:7)
Describe the charge against the watchmen (56:10-12)

nodes.t: Idolatry condemned; the LORD revives the contrite
nodes.d: The perishing of the righteous goes unnoticed, the idolatrous are condemned, and the high and lofty One who inhabits eternity dwells with the contrite and heals; there is no peace for the wicked.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say with whom the LORD dwells in Isaiah 57:15?
ev: Describe the idolatry condemned in Isaiah 57:3-10
Say whom the LORD dwells with in 57:15
Quote 57:21

nodes.t: The fast the LORD chooses
nodes.d: The people fast yet oppress, and the LORD says the fast he chooses is to loose bonds, share bread with the hungry and clothe the naked, promising light and healing; he also promises delight to those who honour the sabbath.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the fast the LORD chooses in Isaiah 58:6-7?
ev: Explain what is wrong with the people's fast (58:3-5)
List the fast the LORD chooses (58:6-7)
Describe the promises that follow (58:8-12)

nodes.t: Your iniquities have separated; the Redeemer comes
nodes.d: The LORD's hand is not short, but iniquities separate the people from God; he sees no intercessor, so his own arm brings salvation, and the Redeemer comes to Zion with a covenant that his Spirit and words will not depart.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what has separated the people from God in Isaiah 59:1-2 and how the LORD responds?
ev: Quote Isaiah 59:1-2
List sins in 59:3-8
Say what the LORD does when he sees no intercessor (59:16-17) and the covenant of 59:21

nodes.t: Arise, shine: the glory of Zion
nodes.d: Zion's light has come and nations and kings come to her brightness with gifts, her walls are Salvation and her gates Praise, and the LORD himself is her everlasting light.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what happens to Zion and what her light is in Isaiah 60?
ev: Say what comes to Zion (60:3-9)
Say what replaces sun and moon (60:19-20)
Describe the people (60:21)

nodes.t: The Spirit is upon me: good tidings to the meek
nodes.d: A speaker anointed by the Spirit proclaims good tidings to the poor and release for captives, the year of the LORD's favour and a day of vengeance, and the mourners are given beauty for ashes.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list what the one anointed by the Spirit proclaims in Isaiah 61:1-3?
ev: List what the anointed one announces in Isaiah 61:1-3
Say what the people are called in 61:6
Describe the everlasting covenant in 61:8-9

nodes.t: A new name for Zion
nodes.d: The LORD will not rest until Zion's righteousness shines, calls her by a new name, rejoices over her like a bridegroom, sets watchmen on her walls, and calls her people the holy people and the redeemed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Zion is called and how the LORD feels about her in Isaiah 62?
ev: Describe the new names (62:2-4, 12)
Quote the picture in 62:5
Say what the watchmen do (62:6-7)

nodes.t: One comes from Edom with red garments
nodes.d: A glorious figure from Edom with garments stained from the winepress declares he trod the peoples alone in anger, for the day of vengeance and the year of his redeemed has come.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the figure in Isaiah 63:1-6 and what he has done?
ev: Describe the figure and his garments (63:1-3)
Say why he acts alone (63:5)

nodes.t: A prayer of remembrance and lament
nodes.d: The prophet recalls the LORD's kindnesses and how Israel rebelled and he became their enemy, then prays for him to look down and come down, confessing sin, and says "we are the clay and thou our potter."
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the prayer of Isaiah 63:15-64:12 and what the people confess?
ev: Recall what the LORD did for his people (63:7-14)
Quote the confession in 64:6
Quote 64:8

nodes.t: New heavens and a new earth
nodes.d: The LORD answers a rebellious people, saves a remnant of his servants, and creates new heavens and a new earth and Jerusalem a joy where weeping is no more and the wolf and lamb feed together.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what the LORD says he will create in Isaiah 65:17-25?
ev: Say who the LORD preserves and who he judges (65:8-15)
Describe the new heavens and new earth (65:17-25)

nodes.t: Heaven my throne: the final word
nodes.d: The LORD asks where a house can be built for him who made all things and looks to the humble and contrite; he comforts Jerusalem, comes with fire, gathers all nations to see his glory, and the new heavens and earth remain.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say whom the LORD looks to in Isaiah 66:2 and how the book ends?
ev: Say whom the LORD looks to (66:2)
Describe the gathering of the nations (66:18-21)
Describe the end in 66:22-24

nodes.t: Jeremiah: overview
nodes.d: Jeremiah son of Hilkiah, a priest of Anathoth, receives the word of the LORD from the thirteenth year of Josiah to the exile after Zedekiah's eleventh year, warning Judah of judgment from the north and promising restoration and a new covenant.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say who Jeremiah was and during whose reigns the word of the LORD came to him according to Jeremiah 1:1-3?
ev: Name the kings during whose reigns the word came (Jeremiah 1:1-3)
Explain that the book is not arranged only in the order of the events it describes, using examples from its dates

nodes.t: The call of Jeremiah
nodes.d: The LORD tells Jeremiah he knew and set him apart before birth as a prophet to the nations; Jeremiah protests he is a child, the LORD touches his mouth and gives visions of an almond rod and a boiling pot from the north.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how Jeremiah was called and how the LORD answered his fear in Jeremiah 1:6-8?
ev: Retell what the LORD says before Jeremiah's birth (1:5)
Describe how the LORD answers Jeremiah's objection (1:6-9)
Explain the two visions of 1:11-16

nodes.t: Israel forsakes the fountain of living waters
nodes.d: The LORD remembers Israel's devotion in the wilderness, charges that the fathers and leaders went after vanity, and says his people committed two evils: forsaking him and digging broken cisterns.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the picture of the fountain and the broken cisterns in Jeremiah 2:13?
ev: Say what the LORD remembers in Jeremiah 2:2-3
Explain the two evils of 2:13
List the people the LORD charges in 2:8, 26

nodes.t: Return, backsliding Israel
nodes.d: Using the image of an unfaithful wife, the LORD calls faithless Israel and Judah to return, promises shepherds after his heart and a gathering to Jerusalem, and calls Judah to circumcise their hearts.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the LORD's call to return in Jeremiah 3:12-14, 3:22 and 4:1-4?
ev: Say what happened to backsliding Israel and what Judah did (3:6-11)
Quote the invitation in 3:12-14
Explain the call to circumcise the heart in 4:4

nodes.t: Disaster from the north
nodes.d: A trumpet is blown for a destroyer coming from the north; Jeremiah laments over the false peace and sees the earth returned to emptiness, though the LORD says he will not make a full end.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Jeremiah sees in Jeremiah 4:23-26 and what the LORD says in 4:27?
ev: Describe the warning given in Jeremiah 4:5-8
Describe Jeremiah's vision of 4:23-26
Say what the LORD says in 4:27

nodes.t: Not one to be found: Jerusalem's guilt
nodes.d: The LORD asks whether a single just person can be found in Jerusalem, charges leaders and people with false oaths, deceit and ignoring the poor, and says a distant nation will come, yet he will not make a full end.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the LORD asks Jeremiah to look for in Jerusalem in chapter 5 and what he finds?
ev: Say what is asked in Jeremiah 5:1
Describe the charges in 5:26-28
Describe the coming nation (5:15-17) and what remains true (5:18)

nodes.t: Jerusalem besieged: peace, peace, when there is no peace
nodes.d: The LORD calls for a siege against Jerusalem, whose people reject his word; prophets and priests heal the wound lightly, saying peace, and the people refuse the old paths; Jeremiah is set as an assayer of metal.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the people answer when the LORD points them to the old paths in Jeremiah 6:16?
ev: Quote the false message in Jeremiah 6:14
Say what the LORD invites in 6:16 and the people's reply
Describe the assayer image (6:27-30)

nodes.t: The temple sermon
nodes.d: At the gate of the LORD's house Jeremiah says not to trust "the temple of the LORD"; the LORD cites Shiloh, forbids Jeremiah to pray for the people, and condemns worship of the queen of heaven and child burning in Tophet.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Jeremiah told the people not to trust in the temple of the LORD in Jeremiah 7:1-15?
ev: Explain what the people trusted and what the LORD required (7:3-7)
Say how the LORD compares the temple to Shiloh (7:12-14)
Describe the sins at Tophet (7:30-34)

nodes.t: Is there no balm in Gilead?
nodes.d: The people hold to deceit and refuse to return; wise men have rejected the LORD's word; the harvest is past and they are not saved, and Jeremiah weeps asking whether there is no balm in Gilead.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the question Jeremiah asks in 8:22 and why he asks it?
ev: Describe how even the stork knows her times (8:7)
Quote the question of 8:22
Describe the people's complaint in 8:20

nodes.t: Weeping prophet; let him glory that he knows me
nodes.d: Jeremiah longs to weep for the slain of his people, who speak deceit; the LORD announces desolation and says the wise, mighty and rich should not glory in those things but in knowing him as one who exercises lovingkindness, judgment and righteousness.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the LORD says a person should glory in according to Jeremiah 9:23-24?
ev: Quote Jeremiah 9:1
Say what the LORD says to glory in (9:23-24)
Explain 9:25-26

nodes.t: The living God and the idols of the nations
nodes.d: The LORD says not to learn the way of the nations; idols made by craftsmen cannot speak or move, while the LORD is the true, living God and everlasting king who made the earth by his power.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} contrast the idols of the nations with the LORD in Jeremiah 10:3-16?
ev: Describe how the idol is made (10:3-5)
Contrast the LORD and the idols (10:10-16)
Describe Jeremiah's prayer in 10:23-25

nodes.t: The words of this covenant and the plot at Anathoth
nodes.d: Jeremiah is told to proclaim the words of the covenant commanded when Israel left Egypt; Judah has broken it and the LORD forbids prayer for them; Jeremiah learns the men of Anathoth plot against his life.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what covenant Jeremiah 11:1-8 refers to and why Judah is said to have broken it?
ev: Say what covenant the LORD refers to and when it was given (11:3-5)
Describe how Judah broke it (11:9-10)
Describe the plot against Jeremiah and the LORD's answer (11:18-23)

nodes.t: Why does the way of the wicked prosper?
nodes.d: Jeremiah asks why the wicked prosper; the LORD says his trouble will grow, grieves over forsaking his heritage, judges Judah's neighbours, and promises compassion and return if the nations learn his ways.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jeremiah asks the LORD in 12:1 and how the LORD answers in 12:5?
ev: Quote Jeremiah's question (12:1)
Describe the LORD's reply (12:5)
Say what is promised for the nations after plucking out (12:14-17)

nodes.t: The ruined linen belt
nodes.d: Jeremiah buys a linen belt, hides it by the Euphrates, and finds it ruined; the LORD says he will ruin the pride of Judah, warns of exile, and asks whether a leopard can change its spots.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the sign of the linen belt and say what it stood for in Jeremiah 13?
ev: Retell what Jeremiah does with the belt (13:1-7)
Explain what the belt represents (13:9-11)
Quote the question in 13:23

nodes.t: Drought, false prophets and intercession refused
nodes.d: During a drought Jeremiah prays for Judah and the people confess sin, but the LORD says not to pray for them; he denounces prophets who promise peace and Jeremiah weeps for the slain.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say why the LORD tells Jeremiah not to pray for the people in Jeremiah 14:10-12?
ev: Describe the drought and the people's prayer (14:1-9, 19-22)
Say what the LORD says about the prophets (14:13-16)

nodes.t: Though Moses and Samuel stood before me
nodes.d: The LORD says even Moses and Samuel could not turn him from Judah; he appoints four kinds of destroyers, Jeremiah complains of his pain, and the LORD tells him to return and promises he will be a bronze wall.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jeremiah says about the LORD's words in 15:16 and what the LORD promises him in 15:19-21?
ev: Say whom the LORD names in Jeremiah 15:1
Quote Jeremiah's words about God's words in 15:16
Say what the LORD promises Jeremiah in 15:19-21

nodes.t: A prophet forbidden to marry or mourn
nodes.d: Jeremiah is told not to marry, mourn or feast because the LORD will remove peace from the land; the LORD says the people forsook him, promises a return from the north greater than the exodus, and sends fishers and hunters.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Jeremiah is forbidden to marry or join mourners in Jeremiah 16?
ev: Say what Jeremiah is told not to do and why (16:2-9)
Describe the promise in 16:14-15

nodes.t: Cursed is the man who trusts in man
nodes.d: The LORD contrasts the person who trusts in man with the one who trusts in the LORD, says the heart is deceitful, and Jeremiah prays for healing; the LORD adds a call to keep the sabbath, promising kings on David's throne if they obey.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} contrast the person who trusts in man with the one who trusts in the LORD in Jeremiah 17:5-8?
ev: Contrast the two people and their trees (17:5-8)
Quote 17:9-10
Say what is promised and warned about the sabbath (17:19-27)

nodes.t: The potter and the clay
nodes.d: Jeremiah watches a potter remake a spoiled vessel; the LORD says he can do the same with Israel and will relent of judgment or blessing depending on how a nation responds; the people say there is no hope and plot against Jeremiah.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the potter and clay story and say what the LORD says he does when a nation turns from evil in Jeremiah 18:7-8?
ev: Retell what Jeremiah sees at the potter's house (18:1-4)
Explain the message of 18:7-10
Describe the people's reaction (18:12, 18)

nodes.t: The broken jar in the valley of Hinnom
nodes.d: Jeremiah breaks a potter's flask in the valley of Hinnom before elders as a sign the LORD will break the city for idolatry and child sacrifice, and then repeats the warning in the temple court.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell what Jeremiah does with the flask in Jeremiah 19 and what it means?
ev: Retell the sign Jeremiah performs (19:1-2, 10-11)
Say why the LORD judges (19:4-5)

nodes.t: Pashur strikes Jeremiah; Jeremiah's complaint
nodes.d: Pashur the priest beats Jeremiah and puts him in stocks; Jeremiah names him Terror on every side and tells of exile to Babylon, then complains that the word is like fire in his bones and curses the day of his birth.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Jeremiah responds to Pashur and what Jeremiah says about holding back the word in 20:9?
ev: Retell what Pashur does and what Jeremiah says (20:1-6)
Describe the fire in Jeremiah's bones (20:9)
Compare the praise of 20:11-13 with the lament of 20:14-18

nodes.t: Zedekiah asks Jeremiah to enquire of the LORD
nodes.d: When Nebuchadnezzar attacks, King Zedekiah sends to Jeremiah, who answers that the LORD himself will fight against the city and sets before the people the way of life, which is to go out to the Chaldeans, and the way of death.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say how the LORD answers Zedekiah in Jeremiah 21 and what choice the people are given?
ev: Say who sends to Jeremiah and why (21:1-2)
Describe the LORD's answer (21:4-7)
Describe the two ways set before the people (21:8-9)

nodes.t: Judgment on the sons of Josiah and Coniah
nodes.d: The house of David is told to do justice or the palace will be desolate; Jehoiakim, who built his house by unrighteousness, and Coniah are condemned, with Shallum's exile also announced.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} contrast what the LORD says of Josiah and of Jehoiakim in Jeremiah 22:13-17?
ev: Say what the king is told to do (22:3)
Contrast Jehoiakim with his father Josiah (22:13-17)
Describe what is said of Coniah (22:24-30)

nodes.t: A righteous Branch raised up to David
nodes.d: The LORD condemns the shepherds who scatter his flock, promises to gather the remnant and set shepherds over them, and says he will raise to David a righteous Branch, a king named The LORD our righteousness.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the LORD promises to raise up for David in Jeremiah 23:5-6?
ev: Describe what the LORD promises in Jeremiah 23:3-4
Quote the promise of 23:5-6
Compare 23:7-8 with the exodus

nodes.t: Against the prophets who speak their own dreams
nodes.d: The LORD says the prophets of Samaria and Jerusalem are profane, speak visions of their own heart and dreams without being sent, while his word is like fire and a hammer, and mocks use of "the burden of the LORD."
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how the LORD says to tell a true prophet from a false one in Jeremiah 23:16-32?
ev: Say what the LORD says false prophets lack (23:18, 21-22)
Contrast the chaff and the wheat (23:28)
Quote 23:29

nodes.t: Two baskets of figs
nodes.d: After Nebuchadnezzar carries off Jeconiah, Jeremiah is shown a basket of good figs and a basket of bad figs; the LORD says the exiles are the good figs he will return and plant, while Zedekiah and the rest are the bad.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the vision of the two baskets of figs in Jeremiah 24 and what each stands for?
ev: Retell the vision (24:1-3)
Say what the LORD promises the good figs (24:5-7)
Say who the bad figs are (24:8-10)

nodes.t: Seventy years and the cup of wrath
nodes.d: In Jehoiakim's fourth year Jeremiah reminds Judah of twenty-three years of unheeded warnings; Babylon will rule seventy years and then be punished, and the nations are made to drink the cup of the LORD's fury.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jeremiah 25:11-12 says about seventy years and what happens to Babylon afterward?
ev: Say how long Jeremiah had spoken (25:3)
Say what the LORD says about the seventy years (25:11-12)
Describe the cup the nations drink (25:15-29)

nodes.t: Jeremiah on trial
nodes.d: Jeremiah's warning at the temple that the house will become like Shiloh leads priests and prophets to demand his death; the princes and elders spare him, citing Micah in Hezekiah's day, while Urijah is killed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell why Jeremiah was not put to death in Jeremiah 26?
ev: Say what Jeremiah says in the temple court (26:2-6)
Retell the argument for sparing him (26:16-19)
Say what happened to Urijah (26:20-23)

nodes.t: The yoke and the king of Babylon
nodes.d: Jeremiah wears wooden yokes and sends word to the kings of Edom, Moab, Ammon, Tyre and Zidon and to Zedekiah that the LORD has given the lands to Nebuchadnezzar; they are not to heed prophets who say otherwise.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jeremiah told the kings and Zedekiah to do in Jeremiah 27 and why he said not to listen to the other prophets?
ev: Describe the sign Jeremiah is told to make (27:2)
Say what the LORD says about serving the king of Babylon (27:6-8, 11-12)
Say what happens to the temple vessels (27:19-22)

nodes.t: Hananiah breaks the yoke
nodes.d: The prophet Hananiah says in the LORD's name that Babylon's yoke will be broken within two years and breaks Jeremiah's yoke; Jeremiah answers that the LORD has made a yoke of iron, and Hananiah dies that year.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the confrontation between Jeremiah and Hananiah and how it ended in Jeremiah 28?
ev: Retell Hananiah's prophecy and what he does to the yoke (28:1-4, 10-11)
Say how Jeremiah says a prophet of peace is known (28:9)
Say what happens to Hananiah (28:15-17)

nodes.t: Jeremiah's letter to the exiles
nodes.d: Jeremiah writes to those carried to Babylon to build houses, plant gardens, seek the city's peace, and wait seventy years, promising thoughts of peace and that they will find the LORD if they seek him with all their heart; false prophets among them are condemned.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jeremiah told the exiles to do in Babylon and what the LORD promised in Jeremiah 29:10-14?
ev: List what the exiles are told to do (29:5-7)
Say what is promised after seventy years (29:10-14)
Describe the warning about false prophets (29:8-9, 21-32)

nodes.t: The time of Jacob's trouble and restoration
nodes.d: The LORD tells Jeremiah to write in a book that he will bring Israel and Judah back; though their wound is incurable because of their sins, he will heal them, break the yoke, and raise up David their king.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the LORD promises Israel and Judah in Jeremiah 30:3, 10 and 17?
ev: Say what Jeremiah is told to write (30:2-3)
Describe the time of Jacob's trouble and the promise (30:7-11)
Quote the covenant words in 30:22

nodes.t: Everlasting love: Israel gathered and Rachel comforted
nodes.d: The LORD loves Israel with an everlasting love and will gather them from the north, redeem them and turn mourning to joy; Rachel weeps for her children but the LORD promises they will return, and the new thing and the sour grape saying are addressed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the LORD promises in Jeremiah 31:3 and 31:15-17?
ev: Quote Jeremiah 31:3
Describe Rachel's weeping and the promise (31:15-17)
Explain the saying about the sour grape that will no longer be used (31:29-30)

nodes.t: The new covenant
nodes.d: The LORD promises a new covenant with Israel and Judah, unlike the one broken after the exodus: he will write his law on their hearts, they will all know him, and he will forgive their iniquity and remember their sin no more.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what is new about the covenant promised in Jeremiah 31:31-34?
ev: Say whom the covenant is made with and what it is unlike (31:31-32)
Describe what the LORD does in 31:33
Quote the promise of forgiveness in 31:34

nodes.t: As sure as the sun and moon: Israel's future and the city rebuilt
nodes.d: The LORD says Israel would cease only if the fixed order of sun, moon and stars departed, and that he will not cast off Israel for their sin; Jerusalem will be rebuilt and holy to the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the comparison the LORD makes in Jeremiah 31:35-37?
ev: Say the comparisons the LORD makes in Jeremiah 31:35-37
Describe the rebuilt city (31:38-40)

nodes.t: Jeremiah buys a field at Anathoth
nodes.d: With Jerusalem besieged and Jeremiah imprisoned, the LORD has him buy his cousin's field as a sign that fields will again be bought in the land; Jeremiah prays, and the LORD promises an everlasting covenant and return.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell why Jeremiah bought a field in Anathoth during the siege and what the LORD said about it in Jeremiah 32?
ev: Retell how Jeremiah buys the field and seals the deed (32:6-15)
Quote the LORD's question in 32:27
Describe the promise in 32:37-44

nodes.t: The Branch of righteousness and the covenant with David and the Levites
nodes.d: The LORD promises healing, cleansing and rejoicing, and that a Branch of righteousness will grow up for David; he compares his covenant with David and the Levites to his covenant of day and night.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the LORD promises about David and the Levites in Jeremiah 33:17-22?
ev: Say what the LORD promises in Jeremiah 33:6-11
Describe the Branch and the name given in 33:15-16
Explain the comparison in 33:20-22

nodes.t: Zedekiah's covenant to free slaves is broken
nodes.d: During the siege Zedekiah and the people covenant to free Hebrew servants, then take them back; the LORD recalls the covenant at the exodus and says that those who passed between the parts of the calf will be given to their enemies.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the people did wrong with their servants in Jeremiah 34 and why the LORD judged them?
ev: Say what the king and people covenanted and what they did next (34:8-11)
Say what law the LORD cites from the time of the exodus (34:13-14)
Describe the judgment (34:17-22)

nodes.t: The Rechabites' obedience
nodes.d: In Jehoiakim's days Jeremiah offers wine to the Rechabites, who refuse because their father Jonadab commanded them; the LORD contrasts their obedience to a human father with Judah's refusal to hear him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the story of the Rechabites and say what the LORD teaches through them in Jeremiah 35?
ev: Retell what Jeremiah does and what the Rechabites say (35:5-10)
Explain the LORD's lesson from them (35:13-16)
Say what is promised to the Rechabites (35:18-19)

nodes.t: The scroll burned by Jehoiakim
nodes.d: The LORD has Jeremiah dictate all his words to Baruch, who reads them in the temple and to the princes; King Jehoiakim cuts and burns the scroll piece by piece, and the LORD has Jeremiah write it again with more added.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how Jeremiah's scroll was written, burned and written again in Jeremiah 36?
ev: Retell how the scroll is written and read (36:1-10)
Describe the king's response (36:21-26)
Say what the LORD commands next (36:27-32)

nodes.t: Jeremiah imprisoned during the siege
nodes.d: When the Chaldeans withdraw briefly because of Pharaoh's army, Jeremiah says they will return and burn the city; he is arrested, accused of deserting, beaten and imprisoned, then secretly questioned by Zedekiah and moved to the court of the prison.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell why Jeremiah was arrested in Jeremiah 37 and what he said to Zedekiah?
ev: Say what Jeremiah says about the Chaldeans' withdrawal (37:7-10)
Describe his arrest (37:11-15)
Say what he asks Zedekiah (37:17-21)

nodes.t: Jeremiah in the cistern and Ebed-melech
nodes.d: The princes lower Jeremiah into a muddy cistern to die; Ebed-melech the Ethiopian pleads with the king and lifts him out with ropes and rags; Zedekiah again questions Jeremiah, who urges him to surrender, and later the LORD promises Ebed-melech deliverance.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how Ebed-melech helped Jeremiah and what the LORD said to him in Jeremiah 39:15-18?
ev: Retell why the princes put Jeremiah in the cistern (38:1-6)
Retell how Ebed-melech rescues him (38:7-13)
Say what the LORD promises Ebed-melech (39:15-18)

nodes.t: The fall of Jerusalem and Jeremiah freed
nodes.d: In Zedekiah's eleventh year the city is breached; Zedekiah flees, is caught, sees his sons killed and is blinded and taken to Babylon; the city is burned, and Nebuchadnezzar orders that Jeremiah be treated well.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell what happened to Zedekiah and Jerusalem in Jeremiah 39:1-10 and what happened to Jeremiah?
ev: Retell what happens to Zedekiah (39:4-7)
Say what happens to the city and to the poor (39:8-10)
Say how Jeremiah is treated (39:11-14)

nodes.t: Gedaliah governor and his murder
nodes.d: Nebuzaradan releases Jeremiah, who joins Gedaliah at Mizpah; Jews return and gather harvest, but Ishmael murders Gedaliah and others and Johanan and the captains flee toward Egypt.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell what happened to Gedaliah and the people at Mizpah in Jeremiah 40-41?
ev: Say what Nebuzaradan says to Jeremiah (40:2-5)
Describe the warning Gedaliah ignores (40:13-16)
Retell what Ishmael does (41:1-10)

nodes.t: Do not go down to Egypt
nodes.d: The remnant asks Jeremiah to pray for guidance and promises to obey, but when the LORD says to stay and he will build them up, and that going to Egypt means the sword and famine, they accuse Jeremiah of lying and go to Egypt.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell what the remnant asked Jeremiah and how they responded to the LORD's answer in Jeremiah 42-43?
ev: Say what the people promise and what the LORD answers (42:5-12)
Say what the LORD warns about Egypt (42:13-22)
Describe the people's reaction (43:1-7)

nodes.t: Nebuchadnezzar and the stones at Tahpanhes
nodes.d: In Tahpanhes in Egypt Jeremiah hides great stones in the brickwork at Pharaoh's house as a sign that Nebuchadnezzar will set his throne there and strike Egypt and burn the Egyptian gods' temples.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the sign with the stones at Tahpanhes and what it means in Jeremiah 43:8-13?
ev: Describe the sign Jeremiah performs (43:9)
Say what it signifies (43:10-13)

nodes.t: The Jews in Egypt and the queen of heaven
nodes.d: Jeremiah warns the Jews in Egypt that idolatry caused the fall of Jerusalem; the people reply they will keep burning incense to the queen of heaven, and the LORD declares he will watch over them for evil and gives a sign concerning Pharaoh Hophra.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the Jews in Egypt answered Jeremiah in 44:15-19 and how Jeremiah replied?
ev: Say what the people answer Jeremiah (44:15-19)
Say how Jeremiah replies (44:21-23)
Describe the sign in 44:29-30

nodes.t: A word to Baruch
nodes.d: In the fourth year of Jehoiakim the LORD answers Baruch's complaint of sorrow by saying he will break down what he has built, and tells Baruch not to seek great things, promising his life as a prize.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the LORD told Baruch in Jeremiah 45:4-5?
ev: Say what Baruch complained of (45:3)
Say what the LORD tells him to stop seeking and promises (45:5)

nodes.t: Oracles against Egypt and the Philistines
nodes.d: The LORD announces defeat of Pharaoh Necho's army at Carchemish and later Nebuchadnezzar's attack on Egypt, while Jacob is told not to fear; waters from the north overflow the Philistines.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the LORD announces against Egypt in Jeremiah 46 and what comfort he gives Israel?
ev: Describe the defeat of Egypt's army (46:2-12)
Say what the LORD tells Jacob (46:27-28)
Describe the flood from the north against the Philistines (47:2-7)

nodes.t: The oracle against Moab
nodes.d: Moab is to be destroyed because it trusted in its works and treasures and magnified itself against the LORD; Jeremiah mourns for Moab, yet the LORD says he will restore Moab's captivity in the latter days.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say why Moab is judged in Jeremiah 48 and what is promised at the end?
ev: Say why Moab is judged (48:7, 26, 42)
Describe the mourning (48:31-36)
Say what is promised in 48:47

nodes.t: Oracles against Ammon, Edom, Damascus, Kedar and Elam
nodes.d: The LORD judges Ammon, Edom, Damascus, Kedar and Hazor and Elam; Edom's pride and refuge in the rocks will not save it, orphans and widows of Edom are told to trust him, and captivity of Ammon and Elam will later be restored.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name the nations judged in Jeremiah 49 and describe Edom's fate?
ev: Describe the charge against Edom (49:7-16)
Say what happens to Kedar and Hazor (49:28-33)
Say what is promised for Ammon and Elam (49:6, 39)

nodes.t: The fall of Babylon and the return of Israel
nodes.d: The LORD declares through Jeremiah that Babylon will fall to a nation from the north, that Israel and Judah will return weeping and join themselves to the LORD in a perpetual covenant, and that Babylon will be destroyed as Sodom was.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Jeremiah 50-51 says will happen to Babylon and to Israel?
ev: Describe how Babylon falls (50:2-3, 51:30-32)
Describe the return of Israel and Judah (50:4-5, 19-20)
Say why the LORD judges Babylon (50:11, 24, 51:24)

nodes.t: The Babylon scroll sunk in the Euphrates
nodes.d: Jeremiah writes all the evil coming on Babylon in a book and tells Seraiah to read it in Babylon, then tie a stone to it and sink it in the Euphrates, saying Babylon shall sink and not rise.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell what Seraiah was to do with the book in Babylon and what the act meant?
ev: Retell what Seraiah is told to do with the book (51:61-64)

nodes.t: The fall of Jerusalem and the exiles recounted
nodes.d: The book closes with Zedekiah's rebellion, the siege, the burning of the temple, the stripping of the bronze pillars and vessels, the executions at Riblah, the numbers carried to Babylon, and Jehoiachin's release and honour in Babylon.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the fall of Jerusalem in Jeremiah 52 and how the chapter ends with Jehoiachin?
ev: Retell the fall of Jerusalem (52:4-14)
Say what is taken from the temple (52:17-23)
Describe what happens to Jehoiachin (52:31-34)

nodes.t: Lamentations: overview
nodes.d: Five poems mourn the desolation of Jerusalem, confess that the LORD afflicted her for her transgressions, and in the middle chapter turn to hope in the LORD's mercies, ending with a prayer for restoration.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Lamentations mourns and which verses in chapter 3 express hope?
ev: Say what the five chapters of Lamentations are about
Name the hopeful turning point in the book (3:21-26)

nodes.t: How the city sits solitary
nodes.d: Jerusalem is pictured as a widow weeping with none to comfort her; her adversaries prevail because of her many transgressions, and she cries to the LORD, confessing that he is righteous.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Lamentations 1 pictures Jerusalem and what she confesses?
ev: Describe how the city is pictured in Lamentations 1:1-2
Say why the LORD has afflicted her (1:5, 8)
Quote the confession in 1:18

nodes.t: The LORD has done what he planned
nodes.d: The poet describes the LORD acting like an enemy in anger, overthrowing the stronghold, altar and sanctuary, with children dying in the streets; the prophets failed to reveal the iniquity, and the people are urged to pour out their hearts to the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Lamentations 2 describes the LORD's anger and what the people are urged to do?
ev: Describe what the LORD has done to Zion (2:1-8)
Say what is said of the prophets (2:14)
Describe the call to pray in 2:18-19

nodes.t: I am the man who has seen affliction
nodes.d: The speaker describes his affliction under the rod of the LORD's wrath as darkness, walls and arrows, remembering the wormwood and the gall.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name some of the images the speaker uses for his affliction in Lamentations 3:1-18?
ev: List the images of affliction used in Lamentations 3:1-18
Quote the speaker's state of mind in 3:18-20

nodes.t: Great is thy faithfulness
nodes.d: In the middle of suffering the speaker recalls that the LORD's mercies never fail, are new every morning, and that it is good to wait for him, because he will not cast off for ever and does not afflict willingly.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} quote Lamentations 3:22-23 and say why the speaker has hope?
ev: Quote Lamentations 3:22-23
Explain what he says to do in 3:25-30
Say what 3:31-33 says about the LORD's compassion

nodes.t: Let us search our ways and turn again
nodes.d: The people call each other to examine their ways and return to the LORD, confess rebellion, and the speaker recalls calling from the dungeon, being heard, and asks the LORD to judge his enemies.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the call to search our ways in Lamentations 3:40 and what the speaker recalls about calling on the LORD?
ev: Quote the call in Lamentations 3:40-41
Describe the speaker's deliverance in 3:55-58
Describe his prayer against enemies (3:64-66)

nodes.t: The gold grown dim: famine and the sins of priests and prophets
nodes.d: The sanctuary stones lie in the streets, children starve, the sins of prophets and priests who shed blood are named as the cause, and Edom is told its cup is coming while Zion's punishment is accomplished.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Lamentations 4 says caused the city's suffering and what it says at the end about Edom and Zion?
ev: Describe the famine (4:3-10)
Say who is blamed (4:13)
Say what is said of Edom and of Zion (4:21-22)

nodes.t: Remember, O LORD, what is come upon us
nodes.d: The people ask the LORD to remember their reproach and the loss of everything, acknowledge that the crown has fallen because they sinned, affirm his throne is for ever, and pray that he turn them and renew their days.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the people ask in Lamentations 5:19-22 and what they confess about themselves?
ev: List what the people have lost (5:2-14)
Quote the confession and the prayer (5:16, 19-21)

nodes.t: Ezekiel: overview
nodes.d: Ezekiel the priest, among the captives by the river Chebar in the fifth year of Jehoiachin's captivity, sees the glory of the LORD, announces the fall of Jerusalem, speaks against the nations, and sees promises of restoration and a new temple.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say where Ezekiel was and what the first chapter says happened to him?
ev: Say where and when Ezekiel received the word (1:1-3)
Describe the main movement of the book from judgment to restoration using the texts

nodes.t: Ezekiel's vision of the glory of the LORD
nodes.d: By the river Chebar Ezekiel sees a storm cloud with four living creatures, wheels full of eyes, a firmament, and above it a throne with a figure like a man in brightness; he falls on his face.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Ezekiel saw by the river Chebar and how he responded in Ezekiel 1:28?
ev: Describe the four living creatures and the wheels (1:5-21)
Describe the throne and what is on it (1:26-28)
Say how Ezekiel responds (1:28)

nodes.t: Ezekiel is sent to a rebellious house and eats a scroll
nodes.d: The Spirit raises Ezekiel, calls him "son of man", and sends him to a rebellious house with a scroll of lament, mourning and woe, which he eats, tasting sweet as honey; he is told Israel will not listen, and sits astonished among the exiles.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how Ezekiel was commissioned and what he did with the scroll in Ezekiel 2-3?
ev: Describe what Ezekiel is sent to do (2:3-7)
Describe the scroll and what he does with it (2:9-3:3)
Say what the LORD says about Israel's hearing (3:7-9)

nodes.t: Ezekiel the watchman
nodes.d: After seven days the LORD makes Ezekiel a watchman for Israel, responsible to warn the wicked and the righteous; he is then told to shut himself in his house and made mute except when the LORD gives him words.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the duty of a watchman and what happens if he warns or does not warn in Ezekiel 3:17-21?
ev: Explain what the watchman is responsible for (3:17-21)
Describe what happens to Ezekiel's speech (3:26-27)

nodes.t: Signs of the siege of Jerusalem
nodes.d: Ezekiel draws Jerusalem on a tile with a siege against it, lies on his side for days bearing the iniquity of Israel and Judah, and eats rationed bread baked over dung as a sign of the famine and defiled bread to come.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the signs Ezekiel acts out in chapter 4 and what they stood for?
ev: Describe the tile and iron pan (4:1-3)
Describe the days he lies on each side (4:4-8)
Explain the bread and water (4:9-17)

nodes.t: The razor and the three parts
nodes.d: Ezekiel shaves his head and beard and divides the hair into thirds, burned, struck with a sword and scattered, as a sign of what the LORD will do in Jerusalem, set in the midst of the nations but worse than them in rejecting his statutes.
